The next obstruction and its filler are \[ \begin{aligned} \Omega_{c,b,a} &=L(c)H_{b,a}-H_{cb,a}+H_{c,ba}-H_{c,b}L(a),\\ d\Omega_{c,b,a}&=0, \qquad \Omega_{c,b,a}\in\ker\pi, \qquad dT_{c,b,a}=\Omega_{c,b,a},\quad |T_{c,b,a}|=-2. \end{aligned} \tag{B.ND10} \] Expanding the four differentials cancels the two copies of each composite by associativity. The image vanishes because the lower witnesses are in the kernel. This is the three-input instance of (B.ND9). A diagram with more cells is handled by the same well-founded induction after its boundary differential has been specified and checked to square to zero. An arbitrary chosen family of homotopies has not been declared coherent merely because the first composition defects vanish.

The whole-diagram resolutions and relative natural lifting constructions apply over the coefficient rings specified in B.1t. For the geometric consumer, the fixed strict square and folding-roof module comparisons have natural witnesses, and prescribed free higher diagrams can be lifted with their boundaries retained. The remaining assembly must still specify the actual joint compactification, base-change and composition parameter diagrams, account for changes of their module-variable index, and verify the simultaneous unit, counit and triangle boundaries there. The general nearby attaching, multiplicative descent and normalized coefficient comparisons are not established by this construction. \(\square\)

Joint transport diagrams and changes of index

Proposition B.1v (resolve the square, retaining its transport). The two mate squares of (B.SM3) can be resolved as entire diagrams over their four different module categories. Their counit comparisons are then equalities on the joint models, with the specified induction-composition isomorphism, not just independently chosen homotopies at the four corners. There is also a transport-labelled resolution graph for changes of these indexing categories. It supplies coherent comparison maps for every supplied strict target diagram of index changes. Neither assertion requires restriction to preserve h-projectivity. We give the constructions and identify the geometric input, while keeping the remaining unit/triangle assembly separate.

A category that records varying coefficients. Let \(I\) be a small ordinary category and \(\mathcal C:I\to\mathrm{dgCat}_k\) a strict diagram, writing \(F_a:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j\) for \(a:i\to j\). Define its transport category \(\mathcal T\) to have objects \((i,X)\), and \[ \mathcal T((j,Y),(i,X)) =\bigoplus_{a:i\to j}\mathcal C_j(Y,F_aX). \tag{B.TD1} \] The direction is important: the indexing arrow goes from \(i\) to \(j\), whereas its transport morphism goes from the \(j\)-fibre to the \(i\)-fibre. For \(u:Y\to F_aX\) and \(v:Z\to F_bY\), composition in \(\mathcal T\) is \[ (a,u)\circ(b,v)=(ba,F_b(u)v). \tag{B.TD2} \] The differential is the differential of each summand. The arrows of \(I\) have degree zero, so the Leibniz sign in the right side is exactly \((-1)^{|u|}\). Associativity is the equality \(F_c(F_b(u)v)w=F_{cb}(u)F_c(v)w\), and the identity is \((1_i,1_X)\). This verifies a dg category over the original ring without any flatness assumption on the fibre Hom complexes.

A right \(\mathcal T\)-module is equivalent to right modules \(M_i\) and closed structure maps \[ s_a:M_i\longrightarrow F_a^*M_j, \qquad s_{ba}=F_a^*(s_b)s_a,\quad s_{1_i}=1. \tag{B.TD3} \] Indeed \(m\in M_i(X)\) acts on \((a,u)\) by \(s_a(m)u\). The module identity is precisely (B.TD3) and (B.TD2). Conversely use the action on \((a,1_{F_aX})\). Equivalently the adjoints \(t_a:F_{a!}M_i\to M_j\) compose using the explicit balanced-tensor associator. This correspondence also identifies all homogeneous maps and their differentials: the structure maps have degree zero, so the required naturality is ordinary equality, with the usual Hom differential supplying its degree signs.

Resolve this one \(\mathcal T\)-module by the many-object semifree construction, obtaining \(r:P\to M\). Its evaluations \(P_i\) are h-projective over \(\mathcal C_i\). To prove this rather than assume it, evaluate a representable cell: \[ \mathcal T(-,(i,X))|_{\mathcal C_j} =\bigoplus_{a:i\to j}\mathcal C_j(-,F_aX). \tag{B.TD4} \] Each is a sum of representables. Every stage of the evaluated semifree filtration has graded-split attachments of their shifts, and the differential of a new generator lands in earlier stages. Thus the generatorwise acyclic-target Hom argument of B.1l applies. For arbitrary h-projective \(P\), first take a semifree replacement; its quasi-isomorphism is a homotopy equivalence over \(\mathcal T\), and evaluation preserves that equivalence. In particular no restriction along a general functor was claimed to preserve h-projectivity: it is this specific representable calculation that proves it. The map \(r\) respects every structure map exactly.

The actual first mate square. In (B.SM3) put \(M\) h-projective over \(\mathcal B\). Use the commutative-square category for \(I\), including its relation \(p\beta=F\alpha\). The following four modules, with the listed induction structure maps, form a right transport module: \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{fibre}&\text{module}\\\hline \mathcal A&\alpha^*M\\ \mathcal B&M\\ \mathcal C&p^*F_!M\\ \mathcal D&F_!M \end{array} \qquad \begin{array}{c|c} \text{edge}&t_a\\\hline \alpha&\epsilon^\alpha_M\\ F&1_{F_!M}\\ \beta&b_M\\ p&\epsilon^p_{F_!M} \end{array} \tag{B.TD5} \] The only nontrivial path relation is the second identity of (B.SM6), which was proved by tensor evaluation. Hence this is a module on the commutative square, not just on its free edge graph. Resolve it over \(\mathcal T\). Write \(P_A,P_B,P_C,P_D\) for the four h-projective values, \(r_A,r_B,r_C,r_D\) for the replacements, and \(t_\alpha,t_F,t_\beta,t_p\) for the new induction structure maps. Naturality of \(r\) and the path relation give \[ \begin{aligned} r_Ct_\beta&=b_M\beta_!r_A,\\ r_Bt_\alpha&=\epsilon^\alpha_M\alpha_!r_A,\\ r_Dt_F&=F_!r_B,\qquad r_Dt_p=\epsilon^p_{F_!M}p_!r_C,\\ t_p\,p_!t_\beta &=t_F\,F_!t_\alpha\,C_{P_A}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.TD6} \] All four new structure maps are homotopy equivalences in this particular module square. For \(t_\alpha\) and \(t_p\), (B.SM2) makes the respective right sides quasi-isomorphisms. For \(t_\beta\), use (B.SM8) with the actual replacement \(r_A\). For \(t_F\), both ends of \(r_B\) are h-projective, so \(r_B\) is a homotopy equivalence and \(F_!\) preserves it. In every case the receiving \(r\) is a quasi-isomorphism, and both ends of the structure map are h-projective. These conclusions do not assert that the horizontal functor \(F\) itself is a quasi-equivalence.

Thus (B.SM10)'s comparison has a joint choice with zero defect in its first line: the equality is the first line of (B.TD6). The final line supplies its compatible counit square on the same joint resolution. Here is that square, entirely in h-projective modules over \(\mathcal D\): \[ \begin{array}{ccc} p_!\beta_!P_A&\xrightarrow{\ p_!t_\beta\ }&p_!P_C\\ {C_{P_A}}\downarrow&&\downarrow{t_p}\\ F_!\alpha_!P_A&\xrightarrow{\ t_F\,F_!t_\alpha\ }&P_D. \end{array} \] The lower arrow is the displayed composite, and the left arrow is the balanced-tensor isomorphism (B.SM4); neither is an unnamed identification. This diagram also displays (B.TD8)'s equality below, but its horizontal arrows are not then asserted to be equivalences. The construction does not replace the original counit by a bare isomorphism class.

The other mate, with different equivalence claims. For h-projective \(N\) over \(\mathcal C\), the second transport module is \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \mathcal A&\beta^*N\\ \mathcal B&F^*p_!N\\ \mathcal C&N\\ \mathcal D&p_!N \end{array} \qquad \begin{array}{c|c} \alpha&d_N\\ \beta&\epsilon^\beta_N\\ p&1_{p_!N}\\ F&\epsilon^F_{p_!N} \end{array} \tag{B.TD7} \] Its path relation is exactly the second identity of (B.SM7). On its joint resolution, \[ \begin{aligned} r_Bt_\alpha&=d_N\alpha_!r_A,\\ r_Ct_\beta&=\epsilon^\beta_N\beta_!r_A,\\ r_Dt_p&=p_!r_C,\qquad r_Dt_F=\epsilon^F_{p_!N}F_!r_B,\\ t_F\,F_!t_\alpha\,C_{P_A} &=t_p\,p_!t_\beta. \end{aligned} \tag{B.TD8} \] Here \(t_\alpha\) is a homotopy equivalence by (B.SM9), and \(t_p\) is one because \(r_C\) is a homotopy equivalence. No equivalence claim is made for \(t_\beta\) or \(t_F\): they represent counits of horizontal adjunctions, which need not be invertible. The last line is the joint resolved form of (B.SM11), retaining those actual counits.

Both constructions are natural in a whole dg-indexed parameter family. First use \(\mathcal J=Q\mathcal I\), and replace the input family by an h-projective module over \(\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes\mathcal B\), or over \(\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes\mathcal C\) in the second construction. Use these product categories as the fibres in (B.TD1). The vertical quasi-equivalences survive by (B.ND3), and the preceding proofs apply to the whole parameter family. By (B.ND6), evaluating it gives admissible h-projective modules. Resolving only the individual inputs would not justify this natural-family assertion.

Changes of the indexing category. A strict morphism of fibre diagrams consists of \(u:I\to I'\) and functors \(A_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C'_{ui}\) with \(A_jF_a=F'_{ua}A_i\). It induces a strict dg functor \[ \tau:\mathcal T\longrightarrow\mathcal T', \quad (i,X)\longmapsto(ui,A_iX), \quad(a,v)\longmapsto(ua,A_jv). \tag{B.TD9} \] The composition check is \(A_k(F_b(v)w)=F'_{ub}(A_jv)A_kw\). Distinct summands can map to the same summand; extend linearly, without asserting injectivity. Restriction \(\tau^*\) preserves objectwise quasi-isomorphisms, since it evaluates at the displayed objects. It need not preserve h-projectivity, and \(\tau\) is not assumed to be a quasi-equivalence. This avoids the invalid inference that tensoring an original-index quasi-equivalence with a nonflat fibre always preserves it.

We now construct higher comparisons, not just separate first lifts. Let \(K\) be an ordinary indexing category, \(s\mapsto\mathcal T_s\) a strict diagram with functors \(\tau_u\), and let \(M_s\) be modules with specified closed maps \(b_u:M_s\to\tau_u^*M_t\) satisfying the strict path and unit relations. Choose whole-module resolutions \(r_s:P_s\to M_s\), with \(P_s\) h-projective over \(\mathcal T_s\). For a fixed transport \(u:s\to t\), a degree-\(n\) resolution-graph arrow is \((v,a,h)\), with \[ \begin{aligned} v&:M_s\to\tau_u^*M_t,& |v|&=n,\\ a&:P_s\to\tau_u^*P_t,& |a|&=n,\\ h&:P_s\to\tau_u^*M_t,& |h|&=n-1,\\ D(v,a,h)&=(dv,da,(\tau_u^*r_t)a-vr_s-dh). \end{aligned} \tag{B.TD10} \] Take the direct sum of these complexes over transports with the same endpoints. If \((w,c,k)\) has degree \(m\) over \(z:t\to q\), composition is \[ \begin{aligned} (w,c,k)\circ(v,a,h) =\bigl(&\tau_u^*(w)v,\ \tau_u^*(c)a,\\ &\tau_u^*(k)a+(-1)^m\tau_u^*(w)h\bigr) \end{aligned} \tag{B.TD11} \] over \(zu\). Strict pullback composition and (B.DA7)'s signed graph calculation prove \(D^2=0\), the graded Leibniz rule and associativity; all pullbacks here are degree-zero dg functors. Units are \((1,1,0)\).

Projection onto \(v\) is degreewise surjective, even in a fixed transport summand. Its kernel is the shifted cone of \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_s}(P_s,\tau_u^*P_t)\to \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_s}(P_s,\tau_u^*M_t)\). This map is a quasi-isomorphism: \(\tau_u^*r_t\) is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism and \(P_s\) is h-projective. Thus the kernel is acyclic for each transport, without requiring \(\tau_u^*P_t\) to be h-projective. Direct sums retain acyclicity.

To retain the index labels when lifting, use the normalized word category \(U(kK)\), not an unlabelled free replacement that could mix transports. Its generator \([u_n|\cdots|u_1]\) has degree \(1-n\) and label \(u_n\cdots u_1\). For degree-zero arrows (B.SF3) has only the split and merge terms. Both preserve this composite label, and every term involves generators of smaller word length. Identities are normalized as in B.1t. The strict target functor sends a one-letter generator to \(b_u\) and longer generators to zero; its chain property is precisely the strict composition law for \(b\). Lift inductively by (B.ND9), within the fixed-label acyclic kernel. This gives a strict graph-valued functor on \(U(kK)\), hence the entire strictly unital higher comparison system. Its first and second components satisfy \[ \begin{aligned} (\tau_u^*r_t)a_u-b_ur_s&=dh_u,\qquad da_u=0,\\ d a_{z,u}&=\tau_u^*(a_z)a_u-a_{zu}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.TD12} \] The second equation is the \(a\)-component of the graph differential, and the corresponding \(h\)-component is retained by the same lift. Higher word boundaries and all unit relations hold because the lift is a dg functor, not because an arbitrary collection of homotopies was declared coherent. Previously fixed lifts on a relative free dg subdiagram remain fixed by the relative form of (B.ND9); a subdiagram with additional relations needs those relations checked separately.

If \(b_u\) is a quasi-isomorphism, then \(a_u\) is one by the first equation and two-out-of-three. It is not automatically a homotopy equivalence over \(\mathcal T_s\), because its pulled-back target need not be h-projective there. In particular applying an induction functor to that comparison still requires the h-projective or homotopy-equivalence hypotheses used in B.1s. This distinction is essential for subsequent unit and triangle constructions.

The geometric composition square. For the actual two-morphism composition, use B.1r's strict square \(\alpha:\mathcal L_{g,f}\to\mathcal G_J\), \(\beta:\mathcal L_{g,f}\to\mathcal G_L\), \(p=\pi_g\), \(F=F_f\), with \(p\beta=F\alpha\). Its \(\alpha,p\) are the already-proved quasi-equivalences; no unresolved proper image replaces \(\mathcal L_{g,f}\). Equations (B.TD5)–(B.TD8) therefore supply joint natural resolved models of both of its mates and their counit squares. The strict arrows of the folding roof (B.SF7) may be used as fibre functors as well. Each specified strict refinement map and strict outer map (B.SF9) induces (B.TD9); composition is retained by (B.TD11)–(B.TD12). Canonical proper-image isomorphisms are not silently treated as equalities: work with the formal paths of their strict maps and retain each specified isomorphism and coherence cell when presenting the target diagram.

The remaining task is to supply the joint geometric unit and triangle boundaries, with their changes of compactification and base, and apply the relative construction to those actual target cells. The fact that every supplied strict index-change diagram has coherent lifts does not manufacture missing target-side cells. Both natural mate/counit squares and the index-change lifting obstruction have been handled here; full enhanced geometric adjunction, nearby attaching, normalized coefficient transport are not asserted. \(\square\)

Joint unit and paired triangle diagrams

Proposition B.1w (retain both triangles in the same target). The common-span square of (B.SM3) has joint h-projective models of both unit comparisons as well as its two counit comparisons. For each strict fibre functor, both triangle boundaries can be included in one target diagram before taking its resolution. We construct the diagrams and their relations explicitly. In particular the second triangle uses a replacement of the restricted input, not an unresolved induction of that input. This supplies the fixed-square adjunction boundary diagrams needed after B.1v; it does not assert the remaining global geometric comparison cells.

The unit-mate diagram. Temporarily write a strict square as \[ \begin{matrix} \mathcal A&\xrightarrow{H}&\mathcal C\\ K\downarrow&&J\downarrow\\ \mathcal B&\xrightarrow{V}&\mathcal D, \end{matrix} \quad JH=VK, \qquad b_{K_!L}H_!(\eta^K_L)=J^*(C_L)\eta^J_{H_!L}. \tag{B.JT1} \] Here \(C_L:J_!H_!L\longrightarrow V_!K_!L\) is the balanced-tensor isomorphism and \(b:H_!K^*\longrightarrow J^*V_!\) its first mate. We use only the two substitutions below, for which (B.JT1) is the already checked first line of (B.SM6) or (B.SM7). Let \(L\) be h-projective over \(\mathcal A\). Take the following five labelled vertices: \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{vertex}&\text{fibre}&\text{target module}\\\hline 0&\mathcal A&L\\ 1&\mathcal A&K^*K_!L\\ 2&\mathcal C&H_!L\\ 3&\mathcal C&J^*J_!H_!L\\ 4&\mathcal C&J^*V_!K_!L. \end{array} \tag{B.JT2} \] There are edges \(0\to1\), \(0\to2\), \(1\to4\), \(2\to3\), \(3\to4\). Their fibre functors are respectively \(1,H,H,1,1\); their induction structure maps are \(\eta^K_L,1_{H_!L},b_{K_!L},\eta^J_{H_!L},J^*C_L\). Impose the path relation \((0\to1\to4)=(0\to2\to3\to4)\). Both paths have fibre functor \(H\), and (B.JT1) proves their equality on the target modules. Consequently this is a genuine module over B.1v's transport category with that relation, not just a collection of maps on its free edge graph.

Resolve the whole transport module, with values \(Q_i\) and quasi-isomorphisms \(r_i\) to (B.JT2). All \(Q_i\) are h-projective in their respective fibres by (B.TD4). Name the new structure maps \(u:Q_0\to Q_1\), \(\mu:H_!Q_0\to Q_2\), \(\nu:H_!Q_1\to Q_4\), \(v:Q_2\to Q_3\), \(w:Q_3\to Q_4\). The single resolution gives \[ \begin{aligned} r_1u&=\eta^K_Lr_0,&r_2\mu&=H_!r_0,\\ r_4\nu&=b_{K_!L}H_!r_1,\\ r_3v&=\eta^J_{H_!L}r_2,&r_4w&=J^*(C_L)r_3,\\ \nu H_!u&=wv\mu. \end{aligned} \tag{B.JT3} \] Thus the actual unit comparison is the commutative diagram \[ \begin{array}{ccc} H_!Q_0&\xrightarrow{H_!u}&H_!Q_1\\ {\mu}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\nu}\\ Q_2&\xrightarrow{\ wv\ }&Q_4. \end{array} \] The lower arrow still factors through \(Q_3\): it is the resolved unit followed by the specified induction-composition isomorphism, not an unspecified comparison. The map \(r_0\) is a homotopy equivalence since \(L,Q_0\) are h-projective. Hence \(H_!r_0\), and then \(\mu\), are homotopy equivalences. Also \(w\) is a homotopy equivalence, because \(J^*C_L\) is an actual isomorphism and \(r_3,r_4\) are quasi-isomorphisms. These arguments do not apply induction to an arbitrary quasi-isomorphism.

The two required specializations are \[ \begin{array}{c|cccc|cc} &K&H&J&V&\text{mate}&\text{associator}\\\hline \text{first unit}&\alpha&\beta&p&F&b&C\\ \text{other unit}&\beta&\alpha&F&p&d&C^{-1}. \end{array} \tag{B.JT4} \] In the first row, (B.SM8), applied to the replacement \(r_1\) and the h-projective module \(\alpha_!L\), proves that \(\nu\) is a homotopy equivalence. The units for \(\alpha,p\) are quasi-isomorphisms by (B.SM1), so \(u,v\) are homotopy equivalences too. In the other row, (B.SM9), with h-projective input \(\beta_!L\), proves the same assertion for \(\nu\). However \(\eta^\beta\) and \(\eta^F\) need not be quasi-isomorphisms: no equivalence claim is made for \(u,v\) in that row. Both rows retain the full unit equations.

A paired triangle target. Let \(F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D\) be any strict dg functor, \(T=F_!\), \(U=F^*\). For h-projective \(N\) over \(\mathcal D\), first choose an h-projective replacement \(q:P\to UN\), and put \[ e=\epsilon_N Tq:TP\longrightarrow N, \qquad \begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{vertex}&\text{fibre}&\text{target module}\\\hline a&\mathcal C&P\\ b&\mathcal C&UTP\\ c&\mathcal C&UN\\ d&\mathcal D&TP\\ n&\mathcal D&N. \end{array} \tag{B.JT5} \] The edges within the \(\mathcal C\)-fibre carry \(\eta_P\) on \(a\to b\), \(Ue\) on \(b\to c\), and \(q\) on \(a\to c\). The three edges with fibre functor \(F\) have induction structure maps \(1_{TP}\) on \(a\to d\), \(\epsilon_{TP}\) on \(b\to d\), and \(\epsilon_N\) on \(c\to n\). Finally \(d\to n\) has fibre functor \(1_{\mathcal D}\) and map \(e\). Impose these four relations, with the unit induction identifications retained: \[ \begin{aligned} Ue\,\eta_P&=q,\\ \epsilon_{TP}T\eta_P&=1_{TP},\\ e&=\epsilon_N Tq,\\ e\,\epsilon_{TP}&=\epsilon_N T(Ue). \end{aligned} \tag{B.JT6} \] The first follows from naturality \(UTq\,\eta_P=\eta_{UN}q\) and the second strict triangle \(U\epsilon_N\eta_{UN}=1_{UN}\). The second is the first strict triangle. The third is the definition of \(e\), and the fourth is counit naturality for the closed map \(e:TP\to N\). These identities can also be checked on the tensors of (B.DA3)–(B.DA5); no permutation of homogeneous factors occurs. The corresponding index paths have identical fibre functors: either \(1_{\mathcal C}\) or \(F\). Thus quotienting the path category by these relations defines a strict fibre diagram and a target transport module. An unresolved \(TUN\) occurs only inside the strict identity proving the first relation; it is never substituted for the derived input \(TP\).

Resolve this entire target. Denote its five h-projective values by \(Q_a,Q_b,Q_c,Q_d,Q_n\), and replacements by \(r_a,r_b,r_c,r_d,r_n\). Name the lifted structure maps \(u:Q_a\to Q_b\), \(b:Q_b\to Q_c\), \(c:Q_a\to Q_c\), \(\ell:TQ_a\to Q_d\), \(h:TQ_b\to Q_d\), \(d:TQ_c\to Q_n\), and \(e':Q_d\to Q_n\). Here the roman edge name \(d\) is a closed degree-zero map, not the differential, which below is written \(\partial\). The four relations are now exact on these common models: \[ bu=c,\qquad hTu=\ell,\qquad e'\ell=dTc,\qquad e'h=dTb. \tag{B.JT7} \] The following diagram displays both squares of the counit compatibility; the separate relation \(bu=c\) retains the other triangle on the \(\mathcal C\)-side: \[ \begin{array}{ccccc} TQ_a&\xrightarrow{Tu}&TQ_b&\xrightarrow{Tb}&TQ_c\\ {\ell}\downarrow&&\downarrow{h}&&\downarrow{d}\\ Q_d&\xrightarrow{1}&Q_d&\xrightarrow{e'}&Q_n. \end{array} \] These are not new arbitrary maps satisfying the same abstract relations. Naturality of the replacement binds them to the actual unit and counit: \[ \begin{aligned} r_bu&=\eta_Pr_a,&r_cb&=Ue\,r_b,&r_cc&=qr_a,\\ r_d\ell&=Tr_a,&r_dh&=\epsilon_{TP}Tr_b,\\ r_nd&=\epsilon_NTr_c,&r_ne'&=er_d. \end{aligned} \tag{B.JT8} \] The map \(c\) is a quasi-isomorphism by its displayed equation, since \(q,r_a,r_c\) are. It is therefore a homotopy equivalence between h-projectives. The map \(r_a:Q_a\to P\) is likewise a homotopy equivalence, so \(Tr_a\) is one. Its equation and \(r_d\) show that \(\ell\) is a homotopy equivalence as well. Neither \(d\) nor \(e'\) is generally invertible. The argument has not required \(UTP\) or \(UN\) to be h-projective.

Equations (B.JT7)–(B.JT8), with the explicit equivalence legs \(c,\ell\), represent the two derived triangle boundaries on one diagram. To see concrete homotopies after transporting the legs, choose inverses \(\iota:Q_c\to Q_a\), \(j:Q_d\to TQ_a\), and degree-minus-one maps \(s_c,s_\ell\) such that \(c\iota-1=\partial s_c\), \(j\ell-1=\partial s_\ell\). Then \[ bu\iota-1_{Q_c}=\partial s_c, \qquad jhTu-1_{TQ_a}=\partial s_\ell. \tag{B.JT9} \] The first is the right triangle after identifying the replacement of \(UN\) by \(c\); the second is the left triangle at \(Q_a\) after identifying \(Q_d\) with \(TQ_a\). The other two relations in (B.JT7) identify their counit maps with the same resolved \(e\). More explicitly \(r_ne'\ell=\epsilon_NT(qr_a)\) and \(r_nd=\epsilon_NTr_c\), so \(e'\ell=dTc\) is exactly the change of restricted-input model from \(Q_a\) to \(Q_c\). The two sides of (B.JT9) must not be called strict identities before the inverse homotopies are chosen. This is consistent with, and supplies common models for, the earlier fixed-choice formulas (B.DA11)–(B.DA12).

One joint presentation, not independent corner replacements. For the fixed common-span square, take the two unit diagrams (B.JT2), the two counit diagrams (B.TD5), (B.TD7), and the paired triangle diagrams (B.JT5) for the fibre functors at the required inputs. Choose the finitely many input replacements \(q\) first. Form the category generated by all these labelled diagrams. Whenever an input is shared, use one vertex if the fibre and module are literally the same; otherwise keep the two vertices and the specified identity or closed isomorphism between their target modules. Identify only equal fibre functors, and impose only the checked relations (B.SM6)–(B.SM7), (B.JT6) and those of the counit diagrams. Each generator has its displayed target map, and every imposed relation has just been proved. This constructs a single target transport module. Its one semifree resolution supplies all these equations simultaneously; the proof of (B.TD4) still applies if gluing introduces further index paths. Direct sums over those paths cause no finiteness or flatness assumption.

This procedure need not preserve an earlier choice of replacement literally. It does preserve the earlier counit target and its relation, and has controlled comparisons with those choices. For an old subdiagram with transport category \(\mathcal T_s\), let \(\tau:\mathcal T_s\to\mathcal T\) be its inclusion, and let \(\rho_s:P_s\to M_s\), \(\rho:Q\to M\) be its old and the new whole resolutions. By construction \(M_s=\tau^*M\). Since \(P_s\) is h-projective, the graph lift of the identity target map yields \[ A:P_s\longrightarrow\tau^*Q,\qquad (\tau^*\rho)A-\rho_s=\partial H, \qquad \partial A=0. \tag{B.JT10} \] The map \(A\) is a quasi-isomorphism. For these inclusions the fibre functors are identities, so its value at each fibre is between h-projectives by (B.TD4), and is a homotopy equivalence. Applying an induction functor to such a fibrewise comparison is justified. We have not claimed that \(\tau^*Q\) is h-projective over the whole subdiagram category. For the strict diagram of inclusions, (B.TD10)–(B.TD12) supply the labelled higher comparison maps and their witnesses. Earlier specified lifts can be kept on a relative free dg subdiagram as in (B.ND9); extra relations are not made automatic by that relative lifting assertion.

For a dg-indexed family, first use the free index \(\mathcal J=Q\mathcal I\) of B.1u, and choose the initial \(L,N,P,q\) over the appropriate product categories \(\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes\mathcal C_i\). The entire construction then takes place over those fibres. Equations (B.JT1) and (B.JT6) are strict natural identities there, with the homogeneous naturality convention (B.ND4); evaluating after the joint resolution gives h-projective values by (B.ND6). In particular \(q\) is a single natural replacement of the whole input family, not a list of unrelated pointwise replacements. This proves family naturality in the stated free-index model. It does not turn a resolution-graph arrow whose compatibility holds only up to its recorded homotopy into a strictly commuting map of the target presentations.

Exact geometric application and remaining boundary. For \(f,g\), substitute \(\mathcal A=\mathcal L_{g,f}\), \(\mathcal B=\mathcal G_J\), \(\mathcal C=\mathcal G_L\), \(\mathcal D=\mathcal I_Y\), \(K=\alpha\), \(H=\beta\), \(J=\pi_g\), \(V=F_f\) from (B.GC2)–(B.GC6). Their equation \(\pi_g\beta=F_f\alpha\) is strict and their vertical functors are the proved quasi-equivalences, so both rows of (B.JT4) apply. The paired triangle construction applies to each strict functor in this common span and the strict folding roof (B.SF7). Thus the fixed common-span unit, counit and paired triangle targets are now supplied with common resolved models and explicit comparison legs.

What remains is the actual map of these target presentations for every geometric refinement and base-change/composition array, including their specified proper-image isomorphisms and higher fold cells. A strict fibre-diagram map alone does not assert compatibility of an arbitrarily chosen \(q\); its target comparison must be supplied, or its resolution-graph homotopy retained. General fibre pullback still need not preserve h-projectivity. The inclusion argument above has identity fibres and must not be used to erase this distinction for geometric maps. Full global enhanced adjunction, nearby attaching, normalized coefficient transport are not established by this fixed-fibre comparison. \(\square\)

The joint left triangle at every input

Proposition B.1x (do not restrict the first triangle to right inputs). For every h-projective left input \(A\), the first triangle of \(T=F_!\dashv U=F^*\) has a joint resolved target diagram. It joins the paired right-input construction of B.1w along its actual three-vertex subdiagram. Thus the common presentation covers the first triangle at arbitrary \(A\) and the second triangle at arbitrary h-projective \(N\), without requiring \(A\) to be equivalent to a replacement of some \(UN\).

The additional target. For a strict dg functor \(F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D\), take the three vertices \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} \text{vertex}&\text{fibre}&\text{target module}\\\hline 0&\mathcal C&A\\ 1&\mathcal C&UTA\\ 2&\mathcal D&TA. \end{array} \tag{B.LA1} \] The edge \(0\to1\) has identity fibre functor and map \(\eta_A\). The edges \(1\to2\) and \(0\to2\) both have fibre functor \(F\), with induction structure maps \(\epsilon_{TA}\) and \(1_{TA}\), respectively. Impose the relation that the two paths from \(0\) to \(2\) agree. Their fibre functors agree, and their target maps agree by the strict triangle \(\epsilon_{TA}T\eta_A=1_{TA}\) proved in (B.DA5). This is a transport module on the triangle category with its relation. The target \(UTA\) is not assumed h-projective, and the unit \(\eta_A\) is not assumed a quasi-isomorphism.

Resolve this one transport module. Its values \(R_0,R_1,R_2\) are h-projective in their fibres by (B.TD4). Write \(r_0:R_0\to A\), \(r_1:R_1\to UTA\), \(r_2:R_2\to TA\) for the replacements, and \(u:R_0\to R_1\), \(v:TR_1\to R_2\), \(\lambda:TR_0\to R_2\) for its structure maps. All are closed and \[ \begin{aligned} r_1u&=\eta_A r_0,\\ r_2v&=\epsilon_{TA}Tr_1,\qquad r_2\lambda=Tr_0,\\ vTu&=\lambda. \end{aligned} \tag{B.LA2} \] The equation is visible as a triangle, with the comparison leg labelled rather than erased: \[ \begin{array}{ccc} TR_0&\xrightarrow{Tu}&TR_1\\ {\lambda}\downarrow&&\downarrow{v}\\ R_2&\xrightarrow{1}&R_2. \end{array} \] Since \(A,R_0\) are h-projective, \(r_0\) is a homotopy equivalence. Induction preserves that equivalence, so \(Tr_0\) is one; its equality with \(r_2\lambda\) implies that \(\lambda\) is a quasi-isomorphism. Its two ends are h-projective, so \(\lambda\) is a homotopy equivalence. Equivalently \(r_2\) is itself between h-projectives, because \(T\) preserves h-projectivity and \(A\) is h-projective. This proof never applies \(T\) to the unresolved quasi-isomorphism \(r_1\) as though it preserved all quasi-isomorphisms.

Choose a homotopy inverse \(j:R_2\to TR_0\) and a degree-minus-one map \(s\) on \(TR_0\) with \(j\lambda-1=\partial s\). Then the actual transported counit \(jv\) and the unit \(u\) have first triangle \[ (jv)Tu-1_{TR_0}=\partial s. \tag{B.LA3} \] It is a homotopy identity, not a claim that the comparison leg is literally an identity. Naturality in (B.LA2) binds it to the original strict adjunction. Indeed \(r_1u=\eta_A r_0=UT(r_0)\eta_{R_0}\), while \(r_2v=\epsilon_{TA}Tr_1\). Thus the diagram represents the unit at \(R_0\) and the counit at \(TR_0\) after the explicit equivalences \(r_0\), \(Tr_0\) and \(\lambda\). Formula (B.DA11) supplies the earlier fixed-choice witness, and this construction supplies compatible choices on the whole target triangle.

The overlap is exact. In (B.JT5) the left input happens to be \(P\), a replacement of \(UN\). When \(A=P\), the target (B.LA1) is exactly the subdiagram on vertices \(a,b,d\) of that paired target: \[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} \text{left target vertex}&0&1&2\\\hline \text{paired target vertex}&a&b&d\\ \text{target module}&P&UTP&TP. \end{array} \qquad (u,v,\lambda)=(u,h,\ell) \text{ on a common resolution}. \tag{B.LA4} \] Here the equality of lifted maps is asserted only after taking one resolution of the combined presentation and restricting its structure maps; independently chosen earlier resolutions need not agree literally. The target relation in (B.LA2) is the second relation in (B.JT6), and the resolved relation is \(hTu=\ell\) in (B.JT7). Consequently the first witness in (B.LA3) agrees with the left-triangle witness in (B.JT9) on that shared model if the same inverse and homotopy are chosen. No additional target relation is being postulated on the overlap.

For other \(A\), attach (B.LA1) as an additional three-vertex diagram to B.1w's common presentation. Use the same target modules whenever they are shared and the explicit closed comparison maps otherwise. Only the proved strict triangle and the existing checked relations are imposed. One transport-module resolution then handles these triangles, both unit-mate squares, both counit squares and the paired right-input triangles. Comparison with an earlier separate triangle or paired resolution uses (B.JT10): the inclusion has identity fibre functors, its evaluated comparison is a homotopy equivalence, and its higher inclusion comparisons retain the graph witnesses of (B.TD10)–(B.TD12). Literal preservation of arbitrary old replacement choices is not claimed.

The distinction between arbitrary \(A\) and the chosen \(P\) matters. Already for scalar extension \(k\to M_2(k)\), \(A=k\) has one-dimensional cohomology, whereas the underlying vector-space cohomology of a right \(M_2(k)\)-module has even dimension when finite. The latter assertion follows directly from the two diagonal matrix idempotents: they split the module into two summands, and the off-diagonal matrix units give inverse isomorphisms between those summands. The same identities hold on cohomology. Thus an arbitrary left input need not be covered by calling it a replacement of a restricted right input. The three-vertex construction does not make that assumption.

Whole dg-indexed families are handled before evaluation over \(\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes\mathcal C\) and \(\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes\mathcal D\), with \(\mathcal J=Q\mathcal I\) and \(A\) h-projective over the product. The unit and counit are natural on that product category, and (B.ND6) gives h-projective evaluations. This is the same family convention as B.1w, so the overlap and the inclusions remain compatible there.

Apply the construction to every strict functor in the geometric common span of (B.GC2)–(B.GC6) and to the strict folding roofs (B.SF7). Together with B.1w, this gives the fixed-input unit, counit and two-triangle target diagrams at the stated h-projective module scope. Geometric refinements, compositions and base changes require comparisons of these target presentations that preserve the proper-image isomorphisms and higher fold cells. The identity-fibre inclusion argument proves neither general pullback preservation of h-projectivity nor global geometric coherence. It also does not construct nearby attaching maps or normalized coefficient transport. \(\square\)

Refinement maps of the joint adjunction targets

Proposition B.1y (compare the actual targets across a refinement). The proper refinements of B.1m admit compatible resolutions of their restricted target modules. Their unit and counit comparisons then have joint models, and there are actual maps of both the paired triangle target of B.1w and the arbitrary left-input target of B.1x. These maps retain the canonical direct-image isomorphisms rather than replacing them by equalities. Their resolution comparisons have the labelled higher coherence described below. This assertion concerns the refinement diagram at fixed geometric endpoints; compatibility with the full composition and base-change arrays is a further stated obligation.

Transport with specified associators. Let \(K\) be a small category of refinements, with dg categories \(\mathcal C_i\), strict dg functors \(G_g:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j\), and closed natural isomorphisms \(m_{h,g}:G_hG_g\to G_{hg}\). Require the pentagon and unit identities. Use normalized identities \(G_1=1\), retaining the given unit identifications when comparing to an unnormalized model. Concretely replace only the identity-arrow functors and conjugate the composition maps by their given unit isomorphisms; the unit identities make the new unit maps identities, and conjugation preserves the pentagon. For the actual refinements these data and their identities are (B.CR2)–(B.CR4). The transport construction becomes \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal T((j,Y),(i,X))&=\bigoplus_{g:i\to j}\mathcal C_j(Y,G_gX),\\ (g,u)\circ(h,v)&=(hg,m_{h,g,X}G_h(u)v). \end{aligned} \tag{B.RT1} \] Naturality of \(m\) moves it through the homogeneous morphism \(u\) without a sign, since \(m\) has degree zero. The two triple composites are equal by its pentagon; its unit identities give identities in \(\mathcal T\). Closedness of \(m\) gives the same differential and Leibniz rule as (B.TD2). This proves the dg-category axioms with the original associators present.

A right module consists of \(M_i\) and closed maps \(s_g:M_i\to G_g^*M_j\) satisfying \[ m_{h,g}^*s_{hg}=G_g^*(s_h)s_g. \tag{B.RT2} \] Here \(m_{h,g}^*:G_{hg}^*M\to G_g^*G_h^*M\) is induced by the contravariant module action on \(m\). The action is still \(x(g,u)=s_g(x)u\); its associativity is precisely (B.RT2). Evaluating a representable gives the same sum \(\bigoplus_g\mathcal C_j(-,G_gX)\) as (B.TD4). Thus one semifree resolution over \(\mathcal T\) has h-projective values in every fibre. No flatness or projectivity-preserving general restriction is assumed.

Resolve the refinement inputs together. Write \(F_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D\) for the fixed-endpoint output functors and \(\beta_g:F_jG_g\xrightarrow{\sim}F_i\) for (B.CR5). Their compatibility is \(\beta_{hg}F_k(m_{h,g})=\beta_g(\beta_hG_g)\). Put \(S_g=G_{g!}\), \(T_i=F_{i!}\), \(U_i=F_i^*\), and use the actual maps \(\chi_g,c_g,k_g\) of (B.CR6)–(B.CR8). For h-projective \(N\) over \(\mathcal D\), the modules \(M_i=U_iN\) with \(s_g=\chi_{g,N}\) satisfy (B.RT2): both sides act on \(n\) by the displayed composite of \(\beta\)'s. Resolve this single module. Its values \(q_i:P_i\to U_iN\) and induction structure maps \(a_g:S_gP_i\to P_j\) obey \[ \begin{aligned} q_ja_g&=k_{g,N}S_gq_i,\\ a_hS_ha_g&=a_{hg}\,\widehat m_{h,g,P_i}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.RT3} \] The isomorphism \(\widehat m:S_hS_g\to S_{hg}\) combines balanced-tensor associativity and induction along \(m\); it is specified, not suppressed. The second equation is the induction form of the module relation. Each \(a_g\) is a homotopy equivalence when \(G_g\) is a quasi-equivalence. Indeed the adjoint of its first equation is \(G_g^*(q_j)G_g^*(a_g)\eta^{G_g}_{P_i}=\chi_{g,N}q_i\). The units are quasi-isomorphisms by (B.SM1), while \(q_i,q_j\) are quasi-isomorphisms and \(\chi\) is an isomorphism. Two-out-of-three and the detection argument of (B.SM2) show that \(a_g\) is a quasi-isomorphism; its two ends are h-projective. This does not presume that \(S_gq_i\) is a quasi-isomorphism.

Set \(e_i=\epsilon^i_NT_iq_i\), the actual resolved counit. Equations (B.CR8), (B.RT3) and naturality of \(c\) give \[ \begin{aligned} e_jT_ja_g&=e_i c_{g,P_i},\\ t_g&=T_ja_g\,c_{g,P_i}^{-1}:T_iP_i\longrightarrow T_jP_j,\\ e_jt_g&=e_i,\qquad t_ht_g=t_{hg}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.RT4} \] The maps \(t_g\) are homotopy equivalences. For their composition, naturality moves \(T_ja_g\) through \(c_h^{-1}\); then use \(a_hS_ha_g=a_{hg}\widehat m\) and \(c_g c_{h,S_gP_i}=c_{hg}T_k\widehat m\). The two factors \(T_k\widehat m\) cancel. This proves the last equality with its canonical identifications accounted for, rather than choosing a separate direct comparison. The units are identities. Diagrammatically the exact counit comparison is \[ \begin{array}{ccc} T_jS_gP_i&\xrightarrow{T_ja_g}&T_jP_j\\ {c_{g,P_i}}\downarrow&&\downarrow{e_j}\\ T_iP_i&\xrightarrow{e_i}&N. \end{array} \]

The induced map on transport categories. A change of a strict fibre diagram need only commute through specified isomorphisms. More precisely, let \(u:I\to I'\), let \(A_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C'_{ui}\), and give closed natural isomorphisms \(\theta_a:A_jF_a\to F'_{ua}A_i\), compatible with composition and identities. Then \[ \tau(i,X)=(ui,A_iX),\qquad \tau(a,v)=(ua,\theta_{a,X}A_j(v)) \tag{B.RT5} \] is a strict functor between the transport categories. For \(a:i\to j\), \(b:j\to k\), compatibility means \(\theta_{ba}=F'_{ub}(\theta_a)(\theta_bF_a)\). Naturality of \(\theta_b\) moves \(A_kF_b(v)\) to \(F'_{ub}A_j(v)\), and this compatibility makes (B.TD2) agree on both sides. Differentials and units are preserved because \(\theta\) is closed and unital. This is a direct verification, not an identification of \(A_jF_a\) with \(F'_{ua}A_i\).

For the paired triangle shape, take \(A_i=G_g\) on its three \(\mathcal C\)-vertices and the identity on its two \(\mathcal D\)-vertices. On each crossing edge use \(\theta=\beta_g^{-1}:F_i\to F_jG_g\); on the other edges use identities. Every path relation in (B.JT6) crosses at most once, so the required compatibility is the same \(\beta_g^{-1}\) on both paths. This defines an actual functor \(\tau_g\) between the two paired-target transport categories.

All seven edges of the paired target. Use the \(q_i,P_i,a_g\) of (B.RT3), not independently chosen replacements. On the five vertices \((P_i,U_iT_iP_i,U_iN,T_iP_i,N)\) of (B.JT5), specify the following induction-side comparison maps: \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{vertex}&\text{comparison}\\\hline a&a_g:S_gP_i\to P_j\\ b&B_g=U_j(t_g)k_{g,T_iP_i}:S_gU_iT_iP_i\to U_jT_jP_j\\ c&k_{g,N}:S_gU_iN\to U_jN\\ d&t_g:T_iP_i\to T_jP_j\\ n&1_N. \end{array} \tag{B.RT6} \] After adjunction on the first three vertices, these are a map of modules over \(\tau_g\). Here are the checks, including the unit, not only the terminal counit: \[ \begin{aligned} B_gS_g\eta^i_{P_i}&=\eta^j_{P_j}a_g,\\ k_{g,N}S_g(U_ie_i)&=U_je_j B_g,\\ k_{g,N}S_gq_i&=q_ja_g. \end{aligned} \tag{B.RT7} \] For the first, (B.CR9) changes the left side to \(U_j(t_gc_{g,P_i})\eta^j_{S_gP_i}\); use \(t_gc_{g,P_i}=T_ja_g\) and unit naturality. For the second use naturality of \(k\) and \(e_jt_g=e_i\). The third is (B.RT3). The remaining four edges satisfy \[ \begin{aligned} t_gc_{g,P_i}&=T_ja_g,\\ t_g\epsilon^i_{T_iP_i}c_{g,U_iT_iP_i} &=\epsilon^j_{T_jP_j}T_jB_g,\\ \epsilon^i_Nc_{g,U_iN}&=\epsilon^j_NT_jk_{g,N},\\ e_jt_g&=e_i. \end{aligned} \tag{B.RT8} \] The middle two are (B.CR8), with counit naturality for \(t_g\) in the second line. The first and last are (B.RT4). These are precisely the crossing-edge conditions for (B.RT5); the factors \(c_g\) encode the specified \(\beta_g\). Thus all seven edges and the four target relations are respected. The triangle comparisons have not been inferred from a bare equivalence of adjoints.

Every component of this target-module map is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism after taking its restriction-side form. At \(a\) it is \(G_g^*a_g\,\eta^{G_g}_{P_i}\). At \(b\) it is \(G_g^*U_j(t_g)\chi_{g,T_iP_i}\); at \(c\) it is \(\chi_{g,N}\). The last two are \(t_g,1\). These assertions follow from (B.SM1), the actual isomorphisms \(\chi\), and preservation of homotopy equivalences by dg functors. No projectivity of an unresolved restricted module is used.

Arbitrary left inputs and the unit square. More generally, let h-projective \(A_i\) have coherent homotopy equivalences \(a_g:S_gA_i\to A_j\) satisfying (B.RT3)'s composition equation, without any \(q_i\). Set \(t_g=T_ja_g c_{g,A_i}^{-1}\) and \(B_g=U_j(t_g)k_{g,T_iA_i}\). The three vertices of (B.LA1) have comparisons \((a_g,B_g,t_g)\). The first equation of (B.RT7) and first two of (B.RT8), with \(P_i\) replaced by \(A_i\), verify all three edges. No replacement of a restricted right input is required. For a single refinement, take \(A_j=S_gA_i\) and \(a_g=1\); for all refinements of an arbitrary initial \(A\) simultaneously, use the coslice category \(i/K\). Its object \(g:i\to j\) has input \(A_g=S_gA\), and an arrow \(h\) has comparison \(\widehat m_{h,g,A}:S_hS_gA\to S_{hg}A\). Their coherence is the pentagon already checked. Thus no existence of an unrelated global family of \(A_i\)'s is assumed. For \(A_i=P_i\), this is exactly the \(a,b,d\) subdiagram of (B.RT6). The arbitrary left triangle and the paired triangles agree on their actual overlap.

For completeness the refinement unit comparison itself has a joint target, not just its edge calculation. Fix h-projective \(L\) over \(\mathcal C_i\), put \(N_1=T_iL\), \(N_2=T_jS_gL\), and retain \(c_{g,L}:N_2\to N_1\). Use the five vertices \(L,U_iN_1,S_gL,U_jN_2,U_jN_1\), in fibres \(\mathcal C_i,\mathcal C_i,\mathcal C_j,\mathcal C_j,\mathcal C_j\). Their edges are the unit \(\eta^i\), the induction identity, \(k_{g,N_1}\), \(\eta^j\), and \(U_jc_{g,L}\), exactly as in (B.JT2). The two paths have fibre functor \(G_g\), and their target relation is (B.CR9); it does not require \(F_jG_g=F_i\). Include the two input rows \(U_iN_r,U_jN_r\), their \(k_{g,N_r}\) edges and the maps induced by \(c_{g,L}\). Naturality of \(k\) proves the additional square relation. One resolution of this combined presentation gives \[ a_1S_gu_i=z_j u_j\lambda, \qquad z_ja_2=a_1S_gz_i. \tag{B.RT9} \] Here \(u_i:R_L\to P_i(N_1)\), \(u_j:R_{S_gL}\to P_j(N_2)\), \(\lambda:S_gR_L\to R_{S_gL}\) is the induction-identity comparison, and \(z_i,z_j\) lift the maps induced by \(c_{g,L}\). All domains are thereby fixed. The maps \(\lambda,z_i,z_j,a_1,a_2\) are homotopy equivalences by the same arguments as (B.JT3), (B.RT3), and two-out-of-three for the isomorphism \(c\). The units themselves need not be equivalences. If these \(q_i\)'s are used as the initial inputs of the paired targets, keep their now-exact \(u,a,z,\lambda\) maps as target maps before forming the combined presentation. This gives an explicit two-stage construction, with comparison to the first stage by (B.JT10), not a circular choice of replacements. The unit target and the paired/left targets can then be included in one presentation as in B.1w; only the displayed checked relations are imposed.

Coherent comparisons of the resolved targets. Successive \(\tau_g\)'s above compose through a natural isomorphism \(\gamma_{h,g}:\tau_h\tau_g\to\tau_{hg}\). Its components are \(m_{h,g}\) on the \(\mathcal C\)-fibres and identities on the \(\mathcal D\)-fibres. Naturality on the crossing edges is the stated compatibility of \(\beta\) with \(m\); the pentagon is that of \(m\). The target maps of (B.RT6) satisfy (B.RT2) for this \(\gamma\), by (B.RT3), (B.RT4) and naturality of \(k\). The left-target maps do also. Hence these are supplied coherent target diagrams, with their actual comparison isomorphisms.

Here is the precise extension of the graph lift when the index composition is not literal. For a resolution \(\rho_s:Q_s\to M_s\) of each whole transport module, use (B.TD10)'s triples \((v,a,H)\) over \(g:s\to t\). Their differential is unchanged. For a degree-\(m\) triple \((w,b,K)\) over \(h:t\to r\), the composite over \(hg\) is \[ \left( (\gamma^*_{M_r})^{-1}\tau_g^*(w)v, (\gamma^*_{Q_r})^{-1}\tau_g^*(b)a, (\gamma^*_{M_r})^{-1} \bigl(\tau_g^*(K)a+(-1)^m\tau_g^*(w)H\bigr) \right). \tag{B.RT10} \] The inverse occurs because \(\gamma^*\) goes from \(\tau_{hg}^*\) to \(\tau_g^*\tau_h^*\). Its naturality with \(\rho_r\), closedness, and the pentagon reduce the differential, Leibniz and associativity checks to those of (B.TD10)–(B.TD11). Projection to \(v\) is degreewise surjective and has, in each fixed label, the same acyclic shifted-cone kernel as before: \(Q_s\) is h-projective and \(\tau_g^*\rho_t\) is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism. No preservation of h-projectivity by \(\tau_g^*\) enters.

The supplied target maps give a strict functor from \(kK\) into this isomorphism-corrected target category. Lift its normalized word category \(U(kK)\) within each transport label, as in (B.ND9). Every differential has only shorter-word split and merge terms with the same composite label. Thus the lift exists in all lengths, respects units, and has, for example, \[ \begin{aligned} \tau_g^*(\rho_t)A_g-b_g\rho_s&=\partial H_g,\qquad \partial A_g=0,\\ \partial A_{h,g} &=(\gamma^*_{Q_r})^{-1}\tau_g^*(A_h)A_g-A_{hg}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.RT11} \] Higher identities follow from the same dg functor, not from independent choices of homotopies. The relative free-subdiagram form preserves earlier specified lifts where its hypotheses hold. Additional quotient relations require their checked target relations; none are inferred from acyclicity alone.

The maps \(A_g\) are objectwise quasi-isomorphisms since their target maps \(b_g\) are. On a \(\mathcal C\)-fibre their pulled-back targets may fail to be h-projective, so it would be wrong to call those components homotopy equivalences before changing fibres. Instead take the actual induction adjoint \[ \overline A_g=\epsilon^{G_g}_{Q_t}S_gA_g:S_gQ_s\longrightarrow Q_t, \qquad G_g^*\overline A_g\,\eta^{G_g}_{Q_s}=A_g. \tag{B.RT12} \] Equation (B.SM2), or its displayed unit/detection proof, makes \(\overline A_g\) a quasi-isomorphism between h-projectives, hence a homotopy equivalence. On identity \(\mathcal D\)-fibres the same conclusion is immediate. It is these adjoint fibre comparisons to which further induction may safely be applied. The higher equations are retained under this adjunction: balanced-tensor associativity identifies the adjoint of \(\tau_g^*A_h A_g\), with its \(\gamma\) correction, with the composite of the induction adjoints and the specified induction associator. Adjunction is an isomorphism of Hom complexes, so it preserves their differentials and the signs in (B.RT11). This resolves the projectivity issue without assuming that arbitrary restriction preserves it.

The natural-family version uses the product fibres of B.1u and makes the initial family h-projective there before evaluation. Quasi-equivalence of the refinement functors survives those products by (B.ND3). The whole-module resolutions, target relations and graph kernels above then apply to that family, including its homogeneous maps. This is not a pointwise choice promoted to strict naturality.

Geometric binding and limit. For actual compactifications use \(G_h\) of (B.CR2), \(m\) of (B.CR4), and \(\beta_h\) of (B.CR5). Their quasi-equivalence, closedness and canonical coherences were proved there; all hypotheses used above are present. The same argument applies to each fixed-endpoint strict model in the refinement arrays (B.GC5)–(B.GC6) when its specified output isomorphism is retained. It supplies the actual adjunction-target comparisons for those refinements, not merely fixed-choice homotopies. The remaining work is to place these maps together with the two-morphism common-span mate diagrams, the higher folding roofs and the geometric base-change/composition interchange cells. Those additional maps need not be quasi-equivalences of the fibres, so (B.RT12) is not a blanket assertion about them. Full enhanced geometric coherence, nearby attaching, normalized coefficient transport remain open. \(\square\)

Normalize the refinement array before folding

Proposition B.1z (one model for the refinement and fold roof). The proper-refinement array of the two-open composition model (B.GC4) admits a simultaneous normalization in which the refinement arrows and the strict folding roofs commute strictly. Evaluation returns the original models together with their specified canonical isomorphisms. All higher folding coefficients and the original source and proper-output functors are retained. This fills the strict-outer-diagram hypothesis of (B.SF9) for this array; it does not yet identify the entire geometric composition/base-change adjunction diagram.

Objects remember their origin. Use the normalized pseudofunctor data \((\mathcal C_i,G_g,m_{h,g})\) of (B.RT1), indexed by a small category \(K\). Define a dg category \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_i\) whose objects are pairs \((u,X)\), where \(u:a\to i\) is an arrow of \(K\) and \(X\in\mathcal C_a\). Different pairs remain different objects, even when their evaluations agree. Put \[ \begin{aligned} \widehat{\mathcal C}_i((u,X),(v,Y)) &=\mathcal C_i(G_uX,G_vY),\\ E_i(u,X)&=G_uX. \end{aligned} \tag{B.SN1} \] Differentials and composition are exactly those on the right. Evaluation \(E_i\) is an isomorphism on every Hom complex. It is essentially surjective, since \((1_i,X)\) evaluates to \(X\); hence it is a quasi-equivalence. This is not a restriction of objects to a selected refinement image.

For \(g:i\to j\), define \[ \widehat G_g(u,X)=(gu,X),\qquad \widehat G_g(f)=m_{g,v,Y}G_g(f)m_{g,u,X}^{-1}. \tag{B.SN2} \] Every factor \(m\) is closed of degree zero. Thus the formula preserves differentials, units and composition. For successive \(g,h\), the pentagon says \[ m_{h,gv}G_h(m_{g,v}) =m_{hg,v}(m_{h,g}G_v). \tag{B.SN3} \] Insert this equality at both ends of \(\widehat G_h\widehat G_g(f)\), and use naturality of \(m_{h,g}\) on \(f\). The middle expression becomes \(G_{hg}(f)\), proving \(\widehat G_h\widehat G_g=\widehat G_{hg}\) on objects and all homogeneous maps. The identity functor is literal. The maps \(m_{g,u,X}\) give the closed natural isomorphism \(G_gE_i\to E_j\widehat G_g\); (B.SN3) is precisely its composition coherence. In particular, if \(G_g\) is a quasi-equivalence, so is \(\widehat G_g\), by evaluation and Hom two-out-of-three. No inverse to \(G_g\) was selected.

Normalize the fixed output at the same time. Suppose \(F_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D\) and \(\beta_g:F_jG_g\to F_i\) satisfy (B.RT3)'s stated output coherence. On the same origin-labelled objects define \[ \widehat F_i(u,X)=F_aX,\qquad \widehat F_i(f)=\beta_{v,Y}F_i(f)\beta_{u,X}^{-1}. \tag{B.SN4} \] This is a dg functor by cancellation of the middle inverse factors. The components \(\beta_{u,X}:F_iE_i(u,X)\to\widehat F_i(u,X)\) are a closed natural isomorphism. The actual identity

\[ \beta_{gu}F_j(m_{g,u})=\beta_u(\beta_gG_u) \tag{B.SN5} \]

makes \(\widehat F_j\widehat G_g=\widehat F_i\) strictly: substitute (B.SN2) in (B.SN4), use (B.SN5) at both ends, and move \(\beta_g\) across \(F_jG_g(f)\) by naturality. The output of an object is its original \(F_aX\), so object equality also holds. One may do this for several fixed endpoint outputs at once. These are conjugated models, not declarations that the original direct-image isomorphisms were identities.

Horizontal maps and the extra requirement for a higher map. Let a second pseudofunctor have fibres \(\mathcal D_i\), refinement functors \(H_g\), and associators \(n_{h,g}\). For strict dg functors \(P_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D_i\), suppose the specified closed natural isomorphisms \(\alpha_g:P_jG_g\to H_gP_i\) obey \[ \alpha_{hg}P_k(m_{h,g}) =(n_{h,g}P_i)(H_h\alpha_g)(\alpha_hG_g). \tag{B.SN6} \] Define \(\widehat P_i(u,X)=(u,P_aX)\) and \(\widehat P_i(f)=\alpha_vP_i(f)\alpha_u^{-1}\). Equation (B.SN6) and naturality give \(\widehat P_j\widehat G_g=\widehat H_g\widehat P_i\) strictly, by the same two-end cancellation. This construction preserves a composite \(QP\) exactly when its comparison is the specified composite \(\alpha^Q_uP_a\circ Q_i\alpha^P_u\). Consequently a strictly commuting horizontal square with equal composite comparisons remains a strictly commuting square. An arbitrary incoherent choice of four comparisons is not enough.

For a strictly unital higher functor \(L_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal D_i\), replace naturality by the actual all-arity identities \[ \alpha_{g,X_r}L_{j,r}(G_gf_r,\ldots,G_gf_1) =H_gL_{i,r}(f_r,\ldots,f_1)\alpha_{g,X_0}. \tag{B.SN7} \] Here the object components of \(\alpha_g\) are actual closed invertible arrows, and (B.SN6) uses \(L_{k,1}(m_{h,g})\). There is one more condition: for the designated closed object isomorphisms \(\sigma_b\) occurring in the associators, their images must be closed invertible arrows and \[ L_r(\sigma_r f_r\sigma_{r-1}^{-1},\ldots, \sigma_1f_1\sigma_0^{-1}) =L_1(\sigma_r)L_r(f_r,\ldots,f_1)L_1(\sigma_0)^{-1}. \tag{B.SN8} \] This equivariance is automatic for a strict functor but is not inferred for an arbitrary higher functor. In particular it is not a new assertion that \(Q\) acts functorially on arbitrary higher maps or natural transformations.

Under these hypotheses the normalized higher functor is given in every arity by \[ \begin{aligned} \widehat L_i(u,X)&=(u,L_aX),\\ \widehat L_{i,r}(f_r,\ldots,f_1) &=\alpha_{u_r,X_r}L_{i,r}(f_r,\ldots,f_1) \alpha_{u_0,X_0}^{-1}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.SN9} \] It has degree \(1-r\). Closedness of the outer factors preserves internal differential terms of (B.RS8); in split terms the two factors at the intermediate object cancel; merge terms retain the original composition of \(f\)'s. This proves all higher identities with the same signs. Strict units are preserved. To check strict refinement compatibility, substitute (B.SN2) in (B.SN9). First apply (B.SN8) to the \(m_{g,u_b}\), then (B.SN7), and finally (B.SN6) for the pair \(g,u_b\). The resulting outer factors are \(n_{g,u_r}H_g(\alpha_{u_r})\) and its initial-end inverse. They are exactly the formula for \(\widehat H_g\widehat L_{i,r}\). Thus \[ \widehat L_{j,r}(\widehat G_gf_r,\ldots,\widehat G_gf_1) =\widehat H_g\widehat L_{i,r}(f_r,\ldots,f_1) \tag{B.SN10} \] is equality for every arity, not only for \(r=1\). Evaluation compares \(\widehat L\) with \(L\) through the displayed \(\alpha_u\), retaining (B.SN7). If \(L_1\) is Hom-quasi-isomorphic and essentially surjective on \(H^0\), the same is true of \(\widehat L_1\): its Hom maps are conjugates of those of \(L_1\); essential surjectivity follows using \(E_i\), \((1_i,X)\), and the isomorphisms \(\alpha_u\).

Why the actual folding coefficients satisfy the extra condition. An isomorphism of resolution strings with closed invertible vertex maps \(\sigma_b\) and zero edge homotopies sends a homogeneous edge homotopy \(h_b\) to

\[ h_b\longmapsto\sigma'_b h_b J_b(\sigma_{b-1}^{-1}), \qquad q_b\longmapsto\sigma_b q_b J_b(\sigma_{b-1}^{-1}). \tag{B.SN11} \]

The endpoint maps transform by ordinary conjugation. The zero edge homotopies and the string equations prove this by the signed composition rule of B.1o. In every selected-edge word defining \(W_r\), adjacent \(\sigma^{-1}\sigma\) cancel, also after transport by the exact \(J_b\)'s. What remains is the final vertex factor and the transported inverse initial factor. This proves (B.SN8) for each word separately, hence their sum, for all string lengths and arities. The factors have degree zero, so no bar sign changes. The first folding coefficient includes the two transformed endpoint maps; higher coefficients have zero endpoints. Folding a designated zero-homotopy isomorphism gives the graph isomorphism with these endpoints and zero homotopy, whose inverse is the fold of the inverse. This verifies the invertibility requirement as well.

Apply this to the actual proper-image associators of (B.CR4) in the string transfers (B.GC6). Their graph components have zero edge homotopies. The ordered-exchange identity (B.RS12) supplies (B.SN7) for every coefficient; (B.GC5) identifies the exchange edges, and the canonical proper-image pentagon and exchange pasting supply (B.SN6). The strict exchange functor \(E\) of (B.GC3) satisfies the strict-functor version; the equality with refinement on its second edge and its homogeneous homotopy component was checked explicitly after (B.GC6). Thus the hypotheses are checked on the actual composition roof, rather than postulated for an unrelated higher functor.

A strict roof of the whole normalized refinement diagram. At refinement index \(i\), write \(\widehat{\mathcal R}_i\) for the normalized two-open string category, \(\widehat{\mathcal L}_i\) for the normalized iterated-composition graph, and \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_i\) for the normalized single-open graph. Let \(\widehat C_i\) be the normalized higher fold and \(\widehat E_i:\widehat{\mathcal R}_i\to\widehat{\mathcal L}_i\) the normalized strict exchange. Form \[ \begin{array}{ccccc} &&UQ\widehat{\mathcal R}_i&&\\ &{\scriptstyle e_i}\swarrow&&\searrow{\scriptstyle h_{\widehat C_i}}&\\ \widehat{\mathcal R}_i&&&&\widehat{\mathcal G}_i\\ {\scriptstyle\widehat E_i}\downarrow&&&&\\ \widehat{\mathcal L}_i.&&&& \end{array} \tag{B.SN12} \] All three arrows are strict quasi-equivalences: evaluation proves the claim for \(\widehat E_i\), and (B.SF7) proves it for \(e_i\) and \(h_{\widehat C_i}\). Refinement on the upper vertex is \(UQ\widehat G_g\), using only a strict dg functor. Equations (B.SN10) and (B.SF9) prove that both slanted edges commute with it strictly; the strict-functor case proves the same for \(\widehat E_i\). The upper refinement is a quasi-equivalence by two-out-of-three in its commuting square with \(e_i,e_j\) and \(\widehat G_g\). Refinement composition on the upper vertex is literal by functoriality of \(UQ\). No lift of an original \(m_{h,g}\) through \(Q\) is required: those maps have already been accounted for by (B.SN2)–(B.SN3) before \(Q\) is applied.

There are fixed endpoint outputs to the original source enhancement and to the final proper-target enhancement. Here is the required compatibility explicitly. Write \(O_i:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal E\) and \(V_i:\mathcal D_i\to\mathcal E\), with \(V_iL_{i,1}=O_i\), \(V_iL_{i,r}=0\) for \(r>1\), and output comparisons \(b_g:O_jG_g\to O_i\), \(c_g:V_jH_g\to V_i\). The condition and its normalized consequence are \[ \begin{aligned} b_g&=(c_gL_i)V_j(\alpha_g),\\ \widehat V_i\widehat L_{i,1}&=\widehat O_i,\qquad \widehat V_i\widehat L_{i,r}=0\quad(r>1). \end{aligned} \tag{B.SN13} \] Indeed, substitute (B.SN9) in (B.SN4). Its value on an \(r\)-tuple is \(b_{u_r}V_iL_{i,r}(f_r,\ldots,f_1)b_{u_0}^{-1}\). This is the required normalized output for \(r=1\) and is zero for \(r>1\); object equality is \(V_aL_aX=O_aX\). In the actual composition array the outputs are the first and final vertex projections followed, for the latter, by the specified proper direct images. The first-component comparison is the identity at the protected original source. At the proper output, the first line of (B.SN13) equates the two canonical reassociations of the same ordered proper images; it is their composition pentagon from (B.CR4)–(B.CR5), used in (B.GC4)–(B.GC6). The designated graph comparisons have zero edge homotopies, and the higher folding components have zero endpoints. This verifies all the stated output hypotheses. Equation (B.SF8) now makes both paths through (B.SN12) have literally equal fixed endpoint outputs. Evaluation back to the geometric models retains, rather than erases, the original proper-image comparison maps.

This gives a concrete simultaneous adjunction target model for this roof and its refinements. Take the category presented by the refinement arrows, the three arrows in (B.SN12), and their checked commuting faces. Its fibre categories and functors form a strict diagram; all its arrows are quasi-equivalences, and the normalized final output is constant along them. Apply (B.RT1)–(B.RT4) with \(m=\beta=1\) to a right input \(N\). A single module resolution supplies all \(q\)'s and all comparison maps, with the exact counit identities simultaneously. Equations (B.RT5)–(B.RT12) then supply the paired triangles, arbitrary left-input triangles along each coslice, the unit target and their labelled higher resolution comparisons. Include the checked boundary presentations before resolving, as in B.1w and (B.RT9); do not choose incompatible lifts separately for the two slanted legs. The induction adjoints are homotopy equivalences because every fibre arrow of this roof/refinement diagram is a quasi-equivalence. This claim does not extend to arbitrary horizontal geometric or base-change functors.

The construction is not yet the comparison with the two-stage adjunction on the intermediate category. That requires the actual common-span mate targets of B.1s and B.1w, their intermediate input modules, and the base-change/interchange maps. Nearby attaching, multiplicative descent, normalized coefficient transport also remain open. The normalization just proved removes the roof-level strictness gap without treating these further statements as automatic. \(\square\)

Join the intermediate adjunction to the composition roof

Proposition B.1aa (the actual two-stage adjunction). The common-span square in (B.SM13) identifies the two-stage adjunction with the common-span adjunction, including their mapping complexes, actual units and counits, and both triangle homotopies. This comparison joins the fixed composition roof of (B.SN12); it is not merely an isomorphism of the resulting objects. The construction works over an arbitrary commutative coefficient ring with possibly unbounded dg modules. Horizontal functors are not assumed to be quasi-equivalences.

Use the notation \[ \begin{array}{ccccc} \mathcal A&\xrightarrow{\ \beta\ }&\mathcal C& \xrightarrow{\ G\ }&\mathcal E\\ {\scriptstyle\alpha}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle p}&&\\ \mathcal B&\xrightarrow{\ F\ }&\mathcal D,&& \end{array} \qquad p\beta=F\alpha . \tag{B.IA1} \] Only \(\alpha,p\) are required to be quasi-equivalences. The arrows depict the actual functors, not inverses chosen in a derived category. Write \(C_Q:p_!\beta_!Q\to F_!\alpha_!Q\) for (B.SM4)'s balanced induction isomorphism and \(b,d\) for (B.SM5)'s two mates. Keep the right-module conventions and the induction/restriction units and counits of B.1l.

Synchronized models cover every source object. For an h-projective \(\mathcal A\)-module \(Q\), put \(M=\alpha_!Q\), \(P=\beta_!Q\), and \(L=G_!P\). These are h-projective. The particular replacement needed by the second stage is \[ \begin{aligned} r_Q&=p^*C_Q\,\eta^p_P: P\longrightarrow p^*F_!M,\\ r_Q&=b_M\beta_!\eta^\alpha_Q . \end{aligned} \tag{B.IA2} \] The second equality is (B.SM6); the first makes \(r_Q\) a quasi-isomorphism by (B.SM1). Thus the two-stage left object is literally \(G_!\beta_!Q\), canonically identified by balanced tensors with \((G\beta)_!Q\). This is not an assumption that the unresolved \(b_M\) is invertible.

There is no loss of source scope in using \(M=\alpha_!Q\). For h-projective \(Q,Q'\), adjunction identifies the map on Hom complexes induced by \(\alpha_!\) with \(\operatorname{Hom}(Q,\eta^\alpha_{Q'})\), a quasi-isomorphism. For arbitrary h-projective \(M_0\), choose \(Q\to\alpha^*M_0\); its adjoint \(\alpha_!Q\to M_0\) is a homotopy equivalence by (B.SM2). Consequently \(\alpha_!:\operatorname{HP}(\mathcal A)\to\operatorname{HP}(\mathcal B)\) is a quasi-equivalence. This proves coverage of all h-projective source modules, not just modules already in a selected right-adjoint image.

For an h-projective \(\mathcal E\)-module \(Y\), choose h-projective replacements \(r:R\to G^*Y\) over \(\mathcal C\) and \(t:Z\to\beta^*R\) over \(\mathcal A\). Set \[ \begin{aligned} q_Y&=\beta^*r\,t:Z\longrightarrow(G\beta)^*Y,\\ W_Y&=\alpha_!Z,\\ s_Y&=d_R\alpha_!t:W_Y\longrightarrow F^*p_!R . \end{aligned} \tag{B.IA3} \] Both \(q_Y\) and \(s_Y\) are quasi-isomorphisms, the latter by (B.SM9), not by assuming \(d_R\) invertible. Thus \(W_Y\) is simultaneously the common-span right model and an actual replacement in the sequential right model. No restriction functor is claimed to preserve h-projectivity.

The pairing agrees as a map of complexes. For every homogeneous \(a:P=\beta_!Q\to R\), its adjoint is \(a^\flat=\beta^*a\,\eta^\beta_Q\). Naturality of \(d\) and the first identity of (B.SM7) give the exact equality \[ \begin{aligned} d_R\alpha_!(a^\flat) &=F^*(p_!a\,C_Q^{-1})\,\eta^F_M,\\ \operatorname{Adj}_F\!\left(d_R\alpha_!(a^\flat)\right) &=p_!a\,C_Q^{-1}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.IA4} \] All displayed structural maps have degree zero, so this equality holds for arbitrary homogeneous \(a\), with no additional degree sign. In particular, if \(f:Q\to Z\), apply it to \(a=\operatorname{Adj}_\beta(tf)\).

Here are the two mapping-complex routes. They share \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E}(G_!P,Y) \cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(P,G^*Y) \longleftarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(P,R)\). The common-span route then uses \[ \begin{array}{ccccc} \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(P,R)&\cong& \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(Q,\beta^*R)& \longleftarrow&\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(Q,Z)\\ &&&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle\alpha_!}\\ &&&&\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(M,W_Y). \end{array} \tag{B.IA5} \] The sequential route sends \(a\) to \(p_!a\,C_Q^{-1}\) in \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(F_!M,p_!R)\), uses the \(F\)-adjunction, and compares with \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(M,W_Y)\) by postcomposition with \(s_Y\). Equation (B.IA4) makes the resulting comparison square commute on the nose. Every arrow in these zigzags is a quasi-isomorphism: use h-projectivity for \(r,t,s_Y\), and the just-proved Hom assertion for the quasi-equivalences \(p_!,\alpha_!\). This establishes the same mapping-complex pairing, rather than appealing to uniqueness of adjoints only on \(H^0\).

Unit and its actual witnesses. At \(Y=L=G_!P\), choose closed maps \(u:P\to R_L\), \(a:Q\to Z_L\), and degree-minus-one maps \(k,h\) with \[ \begin{aligned} r_Lu-\eta^G_P&=dk,\\ t_La-\beta^*u\,\eta^\beta_Q&=dh . \end{aligned} \tag{B.IA6} \] The Hom quasi-isomorphisms out of \(P,Q\) supply these choices. The shared unit on the \(\mathcal B\)-model is \(\alpha_!a:M\to W_L\). Define \(\omega_Q=F^*(p_!u\,C_Q^{-1})\eta^F_M\). Equations (B.IA4) and (B.IA6) give \[ \begin{aligned} s_L\alpha_!a-\omega_Q &=d\!\left(d_{R_L}\alpha_!h\right),\\ q_La-\eta^{G\beta}_Q&=d\ell_Q,\\ \ell_Q&=\beta^*r_L\,h+\beta^*k\,\eta^\beta_Q . \end{aligned} \tag{B.IA7} \] Here \(\eta^{G\beta}_Q=\beta^*\eta^G_{\beta_!Q}\eta^\beta_Q\), with the balanced induction identification retained. The first line is the sequential unit witness; the other lines are the common-span unit witness. Units need not be quasi-isomorphisms.

Counit, including the intermediate map. Put \(v_Y=\varepsilon^\beta_R\beta_!t:\beta_!Z\to R\). Then both counits are represented by the same map \[ \begin{aligned} e_Y&=\varepsilon^G_Y\,G_!r\,G_!v_Y: G_!\beta_!Z\longrightarrow Y,\\ e_Y&=\varepsilon^{G\beta}_Y(G\beta)_!q_Y,\\ \varepsilon^F_{p_!R}F_!s_Y\,C_Z&=p_!v_Y . \end{aligned} \tag{B.IA8} \] The last line follows from the second identity of (B.SM7) and naturality of \(C\). It identifies the actual intermediate counit, before passing through the \(p\)-equivalence. Thus that passage is represented by \(v_Y\) itself, not by an unspecified inverse on cohomology. The first two lines follow by composing the two ordinary induction/restriction counits. There is no claim that \(v_Y\) or \(e_Y\) is invertible.

For the left triangle, put \(w=\varepsilon^\beta_{R_L}\beta_!h\). Naturality and the ordinary \(\beta\)-triangle give \(v_L\beta_!a-u=dw\). Applying the \(G\)-triangle yields the full witness \[ e_L\,G_!\beta_!a-1_L =d\!\left(\varepsilon^G_L\,G_!(r_Lw+k)\right). \tag{B.IA9} \] This is a triangle at arbitrary \(Q\); the coverage argument above transports it to every source object. Neither induction of an arbitrary quasi-isomorphism nor contractibility of an arbitrary acyclic module was used.

The nested right-resolution graph is not strictly folded. Retain the objects \((Y,R,Z;r,t)\) of (B.IA3). A degree-\(n\) map has vertex maps \((f,\rho,z)\) and edge maps \(k,h\) of degree \(n-1\). Its differential on the edges is \[ \begin{aligned} Dk&=r'\rho-G^*f\,r-dk,\\ Dh&=t'z-\beta^*\rho\,t-dh . \end{aligned} \tag{B.IA10} \] Vertex differentials are ordinary Hom differentials. For a degree-\(m\) map \(S\) after \(T\), the edge components of their composite are \(k_S\rho_T+(-1)^mG^*f_Sk_T\) and \(h_Sz_T+(-1)^m\beta^*\rho_Sh_T\). Associativity, the Leibniz rule and \(D^2=0\) follow from these formulas as in (B.RS2).

The sequential right-resolution map is a strict dg functor: \[ (f,\rho,z;k,h)\longmapsto (p_!\rho,\alpha_!z,d_{R'}\alpha_!h) \tag{B.IA11} \] to the graph of \(s_Y:W_Y\to F^*p_!R\). For example, its differential identity is \(s_{Y'}\alpha_!z-F^*p_!\rho\,s_Y =d_{R'}\alpha_!(t'z-\beta^*\rho\,t)\); its signed composition identity follows by homogeneous naturality of \(d\). Thus the strict claim has been checked, not inferred from a commutative square on objects.

In contrast, the comparison with the graph of \(q_Y:Z\to(G\beta)^*Y\) is the higher fold of the two-edge string \(Z\to\beta^*R\to\beta^*G^*Y\). In exactly the suspended convention of (B.RS7), its coefficients are \[ \begin{aligned} K_1(T)&=(f_T,z_T,H_T),& H_T&=\beta^*r'\,h_T+\beta^*k_T\,t,\\ K_2(S,T)&=(0,0,\beta^*k_S\,h_T),& K_j&=0\quad(j>2). \end{aligned} \tag{B.IA12} \] The triples here are ordered as (target vertex, replacement vertex, witness), as in B.1l. The selected-edge proof of (B.RS8) applies purely algebraically; its cancellation does not require the intermediate module \(\beta^*R\) to be h-projective. It proves all higher identities, including the three-input identity involving \(K_2\). The ordinary multiplicativity homotopy has the sign \((-1)^{|S|+1}K_2(S,T)\). Omitting \(K_2\) is generally false. Inserting an identity makes every higher coefficient vanish, since its edge witnesses are zero.

Projection of the nested graph to \(\operatorname{HP}(\mathcal E)\) is a Hom-surjective quasi-isomorphism. To prove it, forget the \(Z,t,h,z\) data first. The kernel on Hom complexes is the shifted cone of \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(Z,Z')\to \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(Z,\beta^*R')\), induced by \(t'\), hence acyclic. The remaining projection has kernel the analogous cone induced by \(r'\), with h-projective source \(R\). Both projections are surjective on graded Hom groups, and replacements exist for every object. The common graph projects to the same category by the same argument with \(q_Y\). Since \(K_1\) commutes with projection, it is a Hom quasi-isomorphism. Every common-graph object is isomorphic in \(H^0\) to the image of a nested object over the same \(Y\): lift \(1_Y\) through the common graph's Hom quasi-isomorphism and lift its inverse in the reverse direction. Thus \(K\) is essentially surjective as well.

Apply (B.SF7) to obtain a strict quasi-equivalence roof from \(UQ\) of the nested graph to the nested and common graphs. Both the input \(Y\) and right output \(\alpha_!Z\) commute strictly along this roof: their projections send \(K_2\) to zero and have the same \(K_1\) values. This supplies the coherent comparison for homogeneous parameter maps; independent pairwise choices of \(k,h\) would not do so.

Right triangle on the same models. At \(Y\), apply the unit construction to \(Q=Z_Y\), so its source is \(L_W=G_!\beta_!Z_Y\). Lift the closed counit \(e_Y:L_W\to Y\) through the nested graph, obtaining \((e_Y,\rho_e,z_e;k_e,h_e)\); the preceding Hom quasi-isomorphism supplies the lift. Put \(H_e=\beta^*r_Yh_e+\beta^*k_e t_{L_W}\). The common graph equation and (B.IA7) give \[ q_Y(z_ea_{Z_Y}-1_{Z_Y}) =d\!\left(H_ea_{Z_Y}+(G\beta)^*e_Y\,\ell_{Z_Y}\right). \tag{B.IA13} \] In deriving this identity use \((G\beta)^*e_Y\,\eta^{G\beta}_{Z_Y}=q_Y\), the ordinary counit identity for the adjoint of \(q_Y\). The defect \(z_ea_{Z_Y}-1\) is closed. Since \(\operatorname{Hom}(Z_Y,q_Y)\) is a quasi-isomorphism, that defect equals \(dJ\) for some degree-minus-one \(J\). Then \(\alpha_!J\) proves the sequential and common right triangle on \(W_Y\). This argument asserts a boundary, not the unjustified stronger equation that \(q_YJ\) equals the displayed witness.

For parameter diagrams, use the whole-diagram resolutions of B.1v before evaluation. Include (B.IA4), (B.IA8), the unit equations and the two displayed triangle witnesses in their actual target presentation. They are checked relations, not new relations imposed without proof. The Hom-surjective acyclic-kernel argument of (B.ND9) lifts a free dg indexing resolution relative to already chosen faces; the strict roof just constructed retains (B.IA12) on its free words. It does not turn arbitrary higher coherence relations into consequences of separately chosen homotopies.

Insert the actual geometric intermediate category. For (B.GC2), take \[ \begin{aligned} (\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C,\mathcal D) &=(\mathcal L_{g,f},\mathcal C_f,\mathcal C_g,\mathcal I_Y),\\ (\alpha,\beta,p,F,G) &=(\alpha,\beta,\pi_g,F_f,F_g),\\ \pi&=\pi_f:\mathcal C_f\longrightarrow\mathcal I_X . \end{aligned} \tag{B.IA14} \] Here \(\alpha(c,N,t)=c\) and \(\beta(c,N,t)=(F_fc,N,t)\); hence \(p\beta=F\alpha\) literally. The actual two-stage left functor is \(LG_!\,p^*\,LF_!\,\pi^*\), and the common-span functor is \(L(G\beta)_!(\pi\alpha)^*\), with h-projective replacements understood as above. On the full family of source models \(\pi_!\alpha_!Q\), use \(\eta^\pi_{\alpha_!Q}\) for the first inverse-equivalence replacement and (B.IA2) for the second. The two left models are then \(G_!\beta_!Q\). Their right model is \(\pi_!\alpha_!Z_Y\), their unit is \(\pi_!\alpha_!a\), and their counit is (B.IA8). Induction by \(\pi\) transports the right-triangle witness; the left witness remains (B.IA9). Since \((\pi\alpha)_!\) is a quasi-equivalence on h-projectives, these source models cover every object of the original source enhancement.

Join, rather than replace, the strict composition roof. A leg of (B.SN12), followed by evaluation, gives a strict quasi-equivalence \(j:\mathcal V\to\mathcal A\). Its endpoint outputs are \((\pi\alpha)j,(G\beta)j\), after inserting the specified closed evaluation isomorphisms of (B.SN13). Their induction maps are the canonical balanced-tensor maps of (B.CR6)–(B.CR9), not discarded identifications. For fixed \(j\), use \(Q=j_!Q_0\) in the preceding construction. On the right choose \(\zeta:Z_0\to j^*Z_Y\), and write \(e_j=\varepsilon^j_{Z_Y}j_!\zeta:j_!Z_0\to Z_Y\). This is a homotopy equivalence by (B.SM2). If \(a:j_!Q_0\to Z_Y\) is the unit lift, lift its adjoint to \(a_0:Q_0\to Z_0\), with \(\zeta a_0-j^*a\,\eta^j_{Q_0}=dh_0\). The actual comparison identities are \[ \begin{aligned} e_jj_!a_0-a &=d\!\left(\varepsilon^j_{Z_Y}j_!h_0\right),\\ \varepsilon^{G\beta}_Y(G\beta)_!q_Y\,(G\beta)_!e_j &=\varepsilon^{(G\beta)j}_Y ((G\beta)j)_!(j^*q_Y\,\zeta). \end{aligned} \tag{B.IA15} \] The first follows by counit naturality and the \(j\)-triangle; the second is the composed-counit identity on balanced tensors. Apply \((\pi\alpha)_!\) to the first line for the source unit. The right output comparison is \((\pi\alpha)_!e_j\). These are the concrete maps that attach the intermediate adjunction to each roof leg. The joint unit, paired and arbitrary-left-triangle target constructions of B.1w–B.1y retain these maps and their witnesses across that roof; they induce only homotopy equivalences between h-projective replacements. The nested right comparison continues to use its \(K_2\) term.

The fixed intermediate-square comparison attaches to the normalized composition roof as above. It does not establish the geometric base-change/interchange target maps, compatibility of the entire intermediate square with every proper refinement, geometric nearby-cycle multiplicative descent, or completed coefficient transport. Those remaining arguments must use the actual maps above; they cannot be replaced by uniqueness of an ordinary adjoint or by declaring all horizontal functors equivalences.

Transpose the actual base-change cells

Proposition B.1ab (base-change mates and their resolved pasting). The actual left-hand comparison in a strict common model determines a right-adjoint comparison with explicit unit, counit and composition witnesses. The construction does not require the vertical functors to be equivalences. An invertible left comparison does not imply that its right mate is invertible. We give the maps before and after h-projective replacement, and identify the precise cellwise input supplied by (B.GC12)–(B.GC13). Global descent across every change of geometric model is distinguished at the end.

Work over an arbitrary commutative coefficient ring with possibly unbounded modules.
