Let \(L_i:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C_i)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal D_i)\) be balanced induction by a dg functor \(F_i\), with right adjoint \(U_i=F_i^*\). Let \(S,V\) be induction functors between the source and target module categories, respectively. In particular, they preserve h-projectives and homotopy equivalences, not necessarily arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms. Suppose a closed dg-natural map has been specified: \[ \begin{array}{ccc} \operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C_0)&\xrightarrow{\ L_0\ }& \operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal D_0)\\ {\scriptstyle S}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle V}\\ \operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal C_1)&\xrightarrow{\ L_1\ }& \operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal D_1), \end{array} \qquad \theta:L_1S\longrightarrow VL_0 . \tag{B.BM1} \] The arrow direction of \(\theta\) is part of the data. For geometric compact-support base change the usual comparison points the other way; its inverse in a common resolved model is the input here, with its homotopies retained. No inverse to a general vertical functor is being chosen.

Transpose on the actual module categories. Denote the ordinary units and counits of \(L_i\dashv U_i\) by \(\eta^i,\varepsilon^i\). Define \[ \begin{aligned} \mu_N:S U_0N&\longrightarrow U_1VN,\\ \mu_N &=U_1(V\varepsilon^0_N\,\theta_{U_0N})\, \eta^1_{S U_0N}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.BM2} \] This is a closed dg-natural map, since every factor is closed of degree zero. Its defining transposition and its unit identity are \[ \begin{aligned} \varepsilon^1_{VN}L_1\mu_N &=V\varepsilon^0_N\,\theta_{U_0N},\\ \mu_{L_0A}S\eta^0_A &=U_1\theta_A\,\eta^1_{SA}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.BM3} \] The first equality is the induction/restriction Hom-complex adjunction. For the second, move \(S\eta^0_A\) through \(\eta^1\), then move \(L_1S\eta^0_A\) through \(\theta\). The remaining middle product is \(V(\varepsilon^0_{L_0A}L_0\eta^0_A)=1\). This proves the identity as a module map. Homogeneous naturality follows by the same adjunction isomorphism; no homogeneous factor has been permuted.

Conversely, a closed natural \(\mu:SU_0\to U_1V\) has left mate \(\varepsilon^1_{VL_0A}L_1(\mu_{L_0A}S\eta^0_A)\). Inserting (B.BM2), using naturality and the two ordinary triangle identities, gives \(\theta_A\). In the reverse direction the same calculation gives \(\mu_N\). Thus an equality between actual left cells gives an equality between their actual right mates. This is a concrete transposition, not an inference from the dimensions of mapping spaces.

Why invertibility must be checked separately. Over a field \(k\), use the algebra square with \(F_0:k\to k\times k\) diagonal, \(F_1:k\to k\) the identity, \(S\) the identity, and \(V\) induction along the first projection \(k\times k\to k\). Then \(VL_0=L_1S=1\), so \(\theta=1\) is invertible. A right \(k\times k\)-module is a pair \((N_1,N_2)\), and the mate is \[ \mu_{(N_1,N_2)}: N_1\oplus N_2\longrightarrow N_1,\qquad (x,y)\longmapsto x . \tag{B.BM4} \] For \((N_1,N_2)=(0,k)\) it is \(k\to0\), not a quasi-isomorphism. All these modules are projective. The failure is therefore not caused by unresolved replacements or unboundedness. A geometric right-exchange isomorphism needs its own hypotheses; ordinary compact-support base change alone does not establish it.

Resolve the right mate without inducing an unresolved quasi-isomorphism. For h-projective \(N\), choose \(r_0:P_0\to U_0N\) and \(r_1:P_1\to U_1VN\) with h-projective sources. Since \(SP_0\) is h-projective, there are a closed \(c_N:SP_0\to P_1\) and a degree-minus-one \(b_N\) with \[ \begin{aligned} r_1c_N-\mu_N S r_0&=db_N,\\ e^1_{VN}L_1c_N-Ve^0_N\,\theta_{P_0} &=d\!\left(\varepsilon^1_{VN}L_1b_N\right),\\ e^0_N&=\varepsilon^0_NL_0r_0,\qquad e^1_{VN}=\varepsilon^1_{VN}L_1r_1 . \end{aligned} \tag{B.BM5} \] Existence uses \(\operatorname{Hom}(SP_0,r_1)\), a quasi-isomorphism, not any assertion that \(Sr_0\) is one. The second line follows by applying \(L_1\), then the first identity in (B.BM3) and naturality of \(\theta\). It compares the actual counits, with the actual witness. The resulting \(c_N\) need not be a homotopy equivalence.

For the unit comparison, take \(N=L_0A\), with \(A\) h-projective. Choose \(u_0:A\to P_0\) and \(k_0\) with \(r_0u_0-\eta^0_A=dk_0\). To represent the other unit, first choose a replacement \(r':P'\to U_1L_1SA\) and a unit lift \(u':SA\to P'\) with \(r'u'-\eta^1_{SA}=dk'\). Lift the map \(\theta_A:L_1SA\to VL_0A\) through the right-resolution graph to \((\theta_A,z,h)\), so \(r_1z-U_1\theta_A\,r'=dh\). Then \[ \begin{aligned} u_1&=zu',& k_1&=hu'+U_1\theta_A\,k',\\ r_1u_1-U_1\theta_A\,\eta^1_{SA}&=dk_1,\\ r_1(c_{L_0A}Su_0-u_1) &=d\!\left(b_{L_0A}Su_0+\mu_{L_0A}Sk_0-k_1\right). \end{aligned} \tag{B.BM6} \] The last identity uses the second line of (B.BM3). Its closed defect is a boundary because \(\operatorname{Hom}(SA,r_1)\) is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus this is the unit followed by the actual lifted \(\theta_A\), not a replacement chosen merely to make a desired diagram commute.

The underlying triangle faces also agree before replacement. Two useful explicit forms are \[ \begin{aligned} V\varepsilon^0_{L_0A}\,\theta_{U_0L_0A}\,L_1S\eta^0_A &=\theta_A =\varepsilon^1_{VL_0A}L_1U_1\theta_A\,L_1\eta^1_{SA},\\ U_1V\varepsilon^0_N\,\mu_{L_0U_0N}\,S\eta^0_{U_0N} &=\mu_N =U_1\varepsilon^1_{VN}\,\eta^1_{U_1VN}\,\mu_N . \end{aligned} \tag{B.BM7} \] For the first line use naturality of \(\theta,\varepsilon^1\) and the left triangles. For the second use naturality of \(\mu\), the right triangle for \(L_0\), and then the right triangle for \(L_1\). The resolved witnesses (B.BM5)–(B.BM6), together with (B.IA9) and (B.IA13), are the corresponding triangle target data. A Hom quasi-isomorphism gives a boundary lift of a closed defect; it does not assert equality with a prescribed primitive after applying \(r_1\).

Successive changes of base: actual vertical pasting. Add a second square \(\theta_2:L_2S_2\to V_2L_1\), and write \(\theta_1,\mu_1\) for the first. With the balanced induction associators inserted, the composite left and right maps are \[ \begin{aligned} \theta_{21}&=(V_2\theta_1)(\theta_2S_1),\\ \mu_{21,N}&=\mu_{2,V_1N}\,S_2\mu_{1,N}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.BM8} \] To prove the second formula, transpose it under \(L_2\dashv U_2\). The first identity of (B.BM3) gives \(V_2\varepsilon^1\,\theta_{2,U_1V_1N}\,L_2S_2\mu_{1,N}\). Naturality of \(\theta_2\) moves \(L_2S_2\mu_1\) to the left. Apply (B.BM3) for \(\mu_1\); the result is \(V_2V_1\varepsilon^0_N\,\theta_{21,U_0N}\). This is exactly the defining transpose of \(\mu_{21}\).

For compatible replacements \(P_0,P_1,P_2\), suppose \(c_1,b_1\) and \(c_2,b_2\) are the two lifts in (B.BM5). A lift of the composite, with no new choice, is \[ \begin{aligned} c_{21}&=c_2S_2c_1,\\ b_{21}&=b_2S_2c_1+\mu_{2,V_1N}S_2b_1,\\ r_2c_{21}-\mu_{21,N}S_2S_1r_0&=db_{21}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.BM9} \] Expand the left side, substitute both lift equations, and use closedness of \(c_1,\mu_2\). For three successive squares the witness is \[ b_3S_3c_2\,S_3S_2c_1+ \mu_3S_3b_2\,S_3S_2c_1+ \mu_3S_3\mu_2\,S_3S_2b_1 . \tag{B.BM10} \] Both parenthesizations give this ordered sum by (B.BM8). Induction gives the analogous finite sum for any length. No factors are permuted. If a separately chosen composite lift is retained, subtract its witness from (B.BM9); the Hom quasi-isomorphism out of \(S_2S_1P_0\) supplies the comparison homotopy. Identity squares use \(c=1,b=0\).

Composition of geometric operations: horizontal pasting. Let \(M_i\dashv W_i\) be a second pair of induction/restriction adjunctions after \(L_i\dashv U_i\). Write the vertical functors as \(S,T,V\), and the cells as \(\theta:L_1S\to TL_0\), \(\phi:M_1T\to VM_0\). Their mates are \(\mu:SU_0\to U_1T\) and \(\nu:TW_0\to W_1V\). For the composite adjunction \(M_iL_i\dashv U_iW_i\), the formulas are \[ \begin{aligned} \Xi&=(\phi L_0)(M_1\theta),\\ \psi_N&=U_1\nu_N\,\mu_{W_0N}: SU_0W_0N\longrightarrow U_1W_1VN . \end{aligned} \tag{B.BM11} \] For a direct check, transpose \(\psi_N\) first under \(L_1\). Naturality of \(\varepsilon^1\) turns its transpose into \(\nu_N\,T\varepsilon^0_{W_0N}\,\theta_{U_0W_0N}\). Now transpose under \(M_1\). Naturality of \(\phi\) and the defining transpose of \(\nu\) give \[ V\!\left(\varepsilon^{M_0}_N M_0\varepsilon^0_{W_0N}\right) \phi_{L_0U_0W_0N}\,M_1\theta_{U_0W_0N}. \tag{B.BM12} \] The first parenthesis is the composite counit and the final factors are \(\Xi_{U_0W_0N}\). This proves (B.BM11), including its direction and factor order. Together (B.BM8) and (B.BM11) prove raw interchange: both orders transpose the same pasted left cell. The ordinary unit and counit identifications used here are exactly those retained in (B.IA7)–(B.IA8).

Here is the horizontal resolved witness, where the intermediate replacement cannot be omitted. Choose \(r:R\to W_0N\), \(t:Z\to U_0R\), \(r':R'\to W_1VN\), \(t':Z'\to U_1R'\), all with h-projective sources. Lift the second mate to \(c_\nu:TR\to R'\), with \(r'c_\nu-\nu_NTr=db_\nu\). Then lift the closed map \(U_1c_\nu\,\mu_R\,St\) through \(t'\) to \(c_\psi:SZ\to Z'\), with witness \(b_\psi\). The complete equation is \[ \begin{aligned} t'c_\psi-U_1c_\nu\,\mu_R\,St&=db_\psi,\\ (U_1r'\,t')c_\psi-\psi_N\,S(U_0r\,t) &=d\!\left(U_1r'\,b_\psi+ U_1b_\nu\,\mu_R\,St\right). \end{aligned} \tag{B.BM13} \] Expand the left side using the first line, substitute the equation for \(b_\nu\), and use homogeneous naturality of \(\mu\) on the closed \(r\). Every lift exists because its source is h-projective and its target replacement is a quasi-isomorphism. No induction of an unresolved quasi-isomorphism is asserted.

For homogeneous parameter maps, the two replacements \(r,t\) have the nested graph of (B.IA10). Its passage to the composite replacement retains \[ K_1(f,\rho,z;k,h) =(f,z,U_0r'\,h+U_0k\,t),\qquad K_2(B,A)=(0,0,U_0k_Bh_A). \tag{B.BM14} \] These are exactly (B.IA12), with \(G=M_0,\beta=F_0\); the target route has the same formula with subscript \(1\). The signs are those of (B.RS7)–(B.RS8), not signs deduced from the degree-zero witness alone. Thus (B.BM13) is attached to the same nested models as the intermediate adjunction, not an incompatible third selection of replacements.

Whole parameter diagrams, rather than independent pointwise choices. Suppose the strict source/target functors and \(\theta,\phi\) are given over a specified free dg parameter index \(J\). Resolve the full modules over \(J^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes\mathcal C_i\) and \(J^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes\mathcal D_i\) before evaluation, as in B.1u–B.1v. The induced \(S,V,L_i\) preserve h-projectivity in these whole categories by their actual induction/restriction adjunctions. The Hom quasi-isomorphisms used in (B.BM5), (B.BM6), (B.BM9) and (B.BM13) therefore hold for whole diagrams. Their lifts and witnesses are graded-natural, not independently chosen at each vertex.

For already specified faces, use the graph form of these lifts: its kernel is the shifted cone of the relevant Hom quasi-isomorphism, and projection is surjective on graded maps. The relative free-index lifting argument (B.ND9) extends the lifts while retaining those faces. Include the checked unit, counit and triangle relations (B.BM3), (B.BM7), and their displayed witnesses in the target presentation. Include the nested comparison through its strict roof, so its free words retain (B.BM14). This supplies coherent lifts for the specified strict parameter diagram. It does not assert that an arbitrary geometric changing-model diagram has already been made strict, or that adding an unchecked relation to a quotient presentation is harmless.

When the left inverse is available only on resolved inputs. This distinction matters geometrically. A homotopy inverse of a left base-change comparison on h-projective models is not automatically a natural transformation on every unresolved module. In particular, one may not evaluate that inverse at \(U_0N\) without further evidence. There is a direct resolved construction that needs only its values on the h-projective inputs.

Retain \(P_0,r_0,e^0_N\) from (B.BM5). Suppose the specified closed left comparison \(\theta\) is natural on the h-projective inputs and maps of the whole parameter diagram under consideration. Define its resolved transpose by \[ \begin{aligned} \zeta_N&=\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1} (Ve^0_N\,\theta_{P_0}): SP_0\longrightarrow U_1VN,\\ r_1c_N-\zeta_N&=db_N,\\ \ell_0&=\varepsilon^0_{L_0A}L_0k_0,\\ r_1(c_{L_0A}Su_0-u_1) &=d\!\left(b_{L_0A}Su_0+ \operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}(V\ell_0\,\theta_A)-k_1\right). \end{aligned} \tag{B.BM16} \] The notation \(\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}\) denotes the full Hom-complex adjunction in every degree, so the transpose of the degree-minus-one map in the last line is defined. The counit equation in (B.BM5) is unchanged, by definition of \(\zeta_N\). For the last line, \(e^0_{L_0A}L_0u_0-1=d\ell_0\) by (B.DA11). Naturality of \(\theta\) on the map \(u_0:A\to P_0\), whose ends are h-projective, gives \(\zeta_{L_0A}Su_0-U_1\theta_A\eta^1_{SA} =d\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}(V\ell_0\theta_A)\). This proves the displayed unit witness. If the full unresolved \(\mu\) exists, naturality identifies \(\zeta_N=\mu_NSr_0\), so this retains rather than changes the earlier construction.

There are equally direct pasting formulas. Set \(D_1=\varepsilon^1_{V_1N}L_1b_1\). With the ordered composite \(\theta_{21}\) from (B.BM8), a vertical witness is \[ \begin{aligned} b_{21}^{\mathrm{res}} &=b_2S_2c_1+ \operatorname{Adj}_{L_2} \!\left(V_2D_1\,\theta_{2,S_1P_0}\right),\\ r_2c_2S_2c_1-\zeta_{21,N} &=db_{21}^{\mathrm{res}} . \end{aligned} \tag{B.BM17} \] Indeed, transpose the second term in the difference under \(L_2\), move \(c_1\) through \(\theta_2\), and use \(e^1L_1c_1-V_1e^0\theta_1=dD_1\). All values of \(\theta_2\) are at h-projectives. When the full unresolved mate exists, its naturality identifies the second term with \(\mu_2S_2b_1\) in (B.BM9). Without it, (B.BM17) is the formula to use. Repeated pasting is defined by these transposed counit witnesses; associativity follows by expanding them in their original order and using the same balanced associators.

For horizontal composition retain \(R,Z,R',Z'\) of (B.BM13), and put \(e_L=\varepsilon^0_RL_0t:L_0Z\to R\), \(e_M=\varepsilon^{M_0}_NM_0r:M_0R\to N\). Define and lift \[ \begin{aligned} \zeta_\nu&=\operatorname{Adj}_{M_1}(Ve_M\,\phi_R), &r'c_\nu-\zeta_\nu&=db_\nu,\\ \kappa&=\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1} (c_\nu\,Te_L\,\theta_Z), &t'c_\psi-\kappa&=db_\psi,\\ \zeta_\Xi&=\operatorname{Adj}_{M_1L_1} \!\left(V(e_M M_0e_L)\,\Xi_Z\right),\\ (U_1r'\,t')c_\psi-\zeta_\Xi &=d\!\left(U_1r'\,b_\psi+ \operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}(b_\nu\,Te_L\,\theta_Z)\right). \end{aligned} \tag{B.BM18} \] Transpose the last equation first under \(L_1\), substitute the equation for \(c_\nu\), and then transpose under \(M_1\). Naturality of \(\phi\) on the h-projective map \(e_L:L_0Z\to R\) gives (B.BM12)'s ordered composite, while the remaining differential is exactly the displayed witness. No value \(\theta_{U_0R}\) or \(\phi_{W_0N}\) is used. Thus the resolved-only construction covers the geometric input actually supplied, even when an unresolved inverse is unavailable. Its parameter lifts still use whole modules and the nested coefficient (B.BM14).

Bind the formulas to the actual geometric cube. In a common strict module model of the compact-support square, use \[ L_0=Rf_!,\qquad L_1=Rf'_!,\qquad S=u^*,\qquad V=g^*,\qquad \theta=(g^*Rf_!\longrightarrow Rf'_!u^*)^{-1}. \tag{B.BM15} \] These symbols mean the functors represented by the common resolved model, with their induction descriptions and specified endpoint comparisons inserted; inverse image is not being asserted to preserve K-injectives. The usual left base-change map comes from (B.CB2)–(B.CB6). Its proper/open mixed cell is the actual sheaf-map cube (B.GC12), and (B.GC13) gives its resolved edge \(z=t(A_Cs)\theta_k^{-1}\). Those paragraphs compare all selected-edge coefficients, including the second coefficient.

On a specified whole strict parameter model, the left comparison on representable cells is the resolved geometric comparison just cited. Both sides are induction functors and preserve sums and graded-split cell attachments. The split semifree filtration, exact filtered unions and passage along homotopy-equivalent h-projective replacements, as in (B.SM1), extend its quasi-isomorphism assertion to the whole h-projective module. Thus the left comparison is a quasi-isomorphism between h-projective whole-module representatives. Its cone is acyclic and h-projective, hence contractible; choose its chain-homotopy inverse there, retaining both inverse homotopies. That is the \(\theta\) in (B.BM15). It need not be a literal inverse on the original K-injective models. In particular, the present construction never applies a proper direct image to an unresolved quasi-isomorphism.

Use (B.BM16) for the actual exchange map \(u^*f^!\to f'^!g^*\) in this common model; an unresolved inverse is not assumed. Its counit face is (B.BM5), and its unit face is the resolved-only witness in (B.BM16). For a composition \(gf\), use (B.BM18) and the actual replacements of (B.IA14), comparing with the common-span right target. Successive base changes use (B.BM17). Where a full unresolved comparison is already supplied, these reduce to (B.BM2), (B.BM9) and (B.BM13). The supplied geometric mixed cube therefore has the indicated cellwise right-adjoint mate and pasted witnesses. No general right-exchange isomorphism follows: (B.BM4) explains the logical obstruction.

The remaining geometric step is to join these whole-parameter constructions across the entire varying-refinement and changing-model array. B.1z normalizes the fixed-endpoint refinement/fold roof; it does not by itself supply that larger parameter model. Its source/target model-change maps and higher components must be explicitly joined to define the global enhanced operation system. Geometric nearby attaching and multiplicative descent, normalized coefficient transport and strict-heart higher effacement are not established by this construction. \(\square\)

Resolve inverse-image transport over the geometric index

Proposition B.1ac (one parameter category for inverse images). In the ordinary coefficient setting, let \(K\) be any small category of geometric changes of base: an arrow \(g:i\to j\) denotes a scheme map \(X_j\to X_i\), with its actual étale inverse-image/direct-image adjunction. There is a single labelled dg category of mapping kernels for all these inverse images. Its composition is strictly associative and retains the actual geometric adjunction maps. A relative-free resolution of the whole category makes every labelled kernel h-projective separately in either module variable. Its compositors induce homotopy equivalences on h-projective modules. This supplies the changing-base parameter input; joining the compact-support cells and their exceptional-adjunction targets to this input remains a separate, explicit step below.

No map \(g\) is assumed proper, an equivalence, or a map whose inverse image preserves K-injectives. Complexes may be unbounded and the coefficient ring need not be a field. Categories and modules are taken in successively larger universes as in B.1k.

Start with the right adjoints, not a choice of inverse-image replacements. Put \(\mathcal C_i=\mathcal I(X_{i,\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)\). Exactness of \(g^*\) gives, for an acyclic complex \(A\) and K-injective \(J\), \[ \operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(A,g_*J) \cong\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(g^*A,J). \tag{B.IP1} \] The right side is acyclic. Thus \(g_*\) restricts to an actual dg functor \(\mathcal C_j\to\mathcal C_i\), without a properness hypothesis. The adjunction isomorphism respects all homogeneous maps. The canonical comparisons \(g_*h_*\cong(hg)_*\) and the unit comparisons satisfy the composition pentagon: their sections identify the same iterated direct image, with the same restriction maps.

Apply (B.SN1)–(B.SN3) to this contravariant system, that is, on \(K^{\mathrm{op}}\). Write \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_i\) for its origin-labelled fibres. Their evaluation maps are quasi-equivalences; the normalized functors \(\widehat G_g:\widehat{\mathcal C}_j\to\widehat{\mathcal C}_i\) compose literally. Now, and only now, apply the strict-functorial free replacement \(Q\) of B.1t: \[ \mathcal E_i=Q\widehat{\mathcal C}_i,\qquad D_g=Q\widehat G_g,\qquad D_gD_h=D_{hg},\qquad D_{1_i}=1. \tag{B.IP2} \] Let \(e_i:\mathcal E_i\to\mathcal C_i\) be augmentation followed by evaluation. It is a quasi-equivalence, with specified closed natural isomorphisms \(e_iD_g\cong g_*e_j\). These comparisons retain their pentagon. We have not applied \(Q\) to a natural transformation. The Hom complexes of \(\mathcal E_i\) are semifree over \(\Lambda\): in the free-word construction of \(Q\), filter by the ordered cell generators and then their finite words; the differential of each generator uses earlier cells. This also makes them h-projective and K-flat over \(\Lambda\). It does not say that \(g_*\) itself is a quasi-equivalence.

For \(I\in\mathcal E_i\), \(J\in\mathcal E_j\), define \[ \begin{aligned} B_g(J,I)&=\mathcal E_i(I,D_gJ),\\ a\cdot u\cdot b&=D_g(a)\,u\,b. \end{aligned} \tag{B.IP3} \] Here \(a:J\to J'\), \(b:I'\to I\); the order of the factors is part of the formula. This is covariant in \(J\) and contravariant in \(I\). Evaluation and (B.IP1) give the natural quasi-isomorphism \[ B_g(J,I)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(e_iI,g_*e_jJ) \cong\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(g^*e_iI,e_jJ). \tag{B.IP4} \] The second complex computes the derived Hom with the actual inverse image, because its target is K-injective. There is no unresolved direct image being applied to a quasi-isomorphism in this assertion.

The composition is a co-Yoneda isomorphism. For successive \(g:i\to j\), \(h:j\to k\), use the usual balanced tensor, with no permutation of homogeneous factors: \[ \begin{aligned} B_h(K,-)\otimes_{\mathcal E_j}B_g(-,I) &\xrightarrow{\ \mu_{h,g}\ }B_{hg}(K,I),\\ v\otimes u&\longmapsto D_g(v)u,\\ w&\longmapsto 1_{D_hK}\otimes w. \end{aligned} \tag{B.IP5} \] The last line is its inverse. Indeed \(B_h(K,-)=\mathcal E_j(-,D_hK)\) is a representable right module. The balancing relation turns \(v\otimes u\) into \(1_{D_hK}\otimes D_g(v)u\), while the forward map sends the latter to \(D_g(v)u\). This verifies both inverses, not merely equality of cohomology dimensions. The differential is respected since \(d(D_g(v)u)=D_g(dv)u+(-1)^{|v|}D_g(v)du\). Representable tensor is evaluation, so the same tensor already computes the derived tensor in this variable, over an arbitrary \(\Lambda\).

For three changes and arbitrary homogeneous \(u,v,w\), both associations give \[ D_gD_h(w)\,D_g(v)\,u =D_{hg}(w)\,D_g(v)\,u. \tag{B.IP6} \] The units are the identity kernels. Thus every finite parenthesization gives exactly the same ordered expression. Under (B.IP4), this is the usual successive inverse-image adjunction, with the canonical inverse-image composition isomorphism retained. It is not a statement that inverse images themselves were chosen as strict functors on K-injective objects.

Here is that geometric interpretation on representatives. Choose a quasi-isomorphism \(q:g^*e_iI\to J_0\), with \(J_0\) K-injective, and a fibre object representing \(J_0\). Full faithfulness on cohomology of \(e_i\) lifts the adjoint of \(q\) to a closed \(u\in B_g(J_0,I)\), after inserting the chosen fibre equivalence. Then \[ \mathcal E_j(J_0,J)\longrightarrow B_g(J,I), \qquad a\longmapsto D_g(a)u \tag{B.IP7} \] is a quasi-isomorphism for every \(J\). To prove it, evaluate, apply (B.IP1), and precompose with \(q\). Precomposition is a quasi-isomorphism because the target \(e_jJ\) is K-injective. A homotopic lift of the adjoint gives the same conclusion. This proves quasi-corepresentability of the entire left module \(B_g(-,I)\).

If \(q_h:h^*J_0\to J_1\) is a second such replacement, the element \(D_g(u_h)u\) represents \(q_hh^*q\), with the inverse-image associator inserted. This follows by applying the two actual adjunction bijections in succession; their unit/counit triangles cancel the middle pair. Exactness of \(h^*\) makes this composite a quasi-isomorphism. More generally, precomposition by \(u\) on every subsequent labelled Hom is a quasi-isomorphism, since it becomes precomposition by the quasi-isomorphism \(b^*q\) into a K-injective target. This is the homotopical universal property of the transported object, not a claim that \(g\) is invertible.

Put all labels in one category. Define \(\mathcal T\) with objects \((i,I)\) and \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal T((i,I),(j,J)) &=\bigoplus_{g:i\to j}B_g(J,I),\\ (h,v)\circ(g,u)&=(hg,D_g(v)u). \end{aligned} \tag{B.IP8} \] Its differential preserves labels. Equations (B.IP5)–(B.IP6) prove the dg axioms, including the signed Leibniz identity, for the whole category. Parallel arrows of \(K\) remain distinct summands. A nonidentity endomorphism is not merged with the identity sector. Direct sums are exact for modules, so evaluation gives a quasi-isomorphism on each labelled Hom and on their sums. The identity-labelled sectors are the \(\mathcal E_i\); their disjoint union \(\mathcal E=\coprod_i\mathcal E_i\) is a dg subcategory with all the same objects.

The kernel composition is already strict, but its left modules need not yet be h-projective. Resolve this defect once over \(\mathcal E\), rather than replacing the arrows independently. Construct \[ \mathcal E\ \hookrightarrow\ \mathcal R \xrightarrow{\ p\ }\mathcal T, \qquad p|_{\mathcal E}=1. \tag{B.IP9} \] Start with \(\mathcal E\), and freely adjoin closed generators mapping to every closed homogeneous element of every labelled Hom of \(\mathcal T\). At each following stage, for every closed \(z\) in a labelled Hom of the current category and every \(a\) of the same label with \(p(z)=da\), adjoin \(t\) of degree \(|z|-1\), with \(dt=z\), \(p(t)=a\). Iterate through the countable stages and take their union. Every word is finite. Consequently every kernel cohomology class appears at some stage and is killed at the next one; every target class was hit at the first stage. Thus \(p\) is a quasi-isomorphism on each labelled Hom. It is the identity on objects and fixes every original fibre arrow. No relation between labels is imposed by deleting a generator; its specified boundary is retained.

We justify the required module property, including the identity sector. Fix \(I\), \(g:i\to j\). In a relative free word with at least one newly adjoined generator, separate its last fibre arrow. As a left \(\mathcal E_j\)-module its resulting graded summand has form \(\mathcal E_j(B,-)\otimes_\Lambda V\), where \(V\) consists of earlier fibre Hom factors, finitely many shifted new generators and the first fibre factor from \(I\). The intervening fibre Homs are semifree over \(\Lambda\), by (B.IP2); their finite tensors and direct sums are semifree. Filter the relative words by the ordered new cells, refining by these coefficient filtrations. The differential of a new cell lowers this filtration, since its specified boundary uses earlier cells; the fibre differentials lower the coefficient filtration. Thus the summands give a semifree filtration of the left module. The zero-new-generator summand exists only for \(i=j,g=1_i\), and is the representable \(\mathcal E_i(I,-)\). It is included at the initial stage. Separating the first fibre arrow gives the dual argument for a fixed target and a right \(\mathcal E_i\)-module. Therefore \[ C_g(J,I)=\mathcal R((i,I),(j,J))_g \longrightarrow B_g(J,I) \tag{B.IP10} \] is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism, with \(C_g\) h-projective and K-flat separately in either module variable. This assertion does not require the diagonal bimodule itself to be h-projective as a module on the tensor-product category.

Composition in \(\mathcal R\) supplies one associative system, with the canonical balanced-tensor associators inserted: \[ \begin{array}{ccc} C_h(K,-)\otimes_{\mathcal E_j}C_g(-,I) &\xrightarrow{\ c_{h,g}\ }&C_{hg}(K,I)\\ {\scriptstyle p\otimes p}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle p}\\ B_h(K,-)\otimes_{\mathcal E_j}B_g(-,I) &\xrightarrow[\ \cong\ ]{\ \mu_{h,g}\ }&B_{hg}(K,I). \end{array} \tag{B.IP11} \] Every such map is a quasi-isomorphism. Compare it with (B.IP5). First replace \(C_h(K,-)\) by \(B_h(K,-)\); tensoring this quasi-isomorphism with the K-flat left module \(C_g(-,I)\) preserves it. Then replace \(C_g(-,I)\) by \(B_g(-,I)\); the right module \(B_h(K,-)\) is representable, so this second tensor also preserves the quasi-isomorphism. The bottom map (B.IP5) is an isomorphism and the right vertical map (B.IP10) is a quasi-isomorphism. Two-out-of-three proves the assertion. Omitting either flatness justification would not be valid for arbitrary coefficients.

For clarity, on left modules use \[ \begin{aligned} \mathsf A_g(N)(J)&=C_g(J,-)\otimes_{\mathcal E_i}N,\\ \mathsf A_h\mathsf A_g(N)&\xrightarrow{\ c_{h,g}\ } \mathsf A_{hg}(N),\qquad N\xrightarrow{\ \iota_i\ }\mathsf A_{1_i}(N). \end{aligned} \tag{B.IP12} \] Equivalently these are right modules on \(\mathcal E_i^{\mathrm{op}}\), with the standard Koszul convention. Each \(\mathsf A_g\) sends h-projectives to h-projectives: apply it to a semifree filtration of \(N\); its representable cells become the h-projective left modules \(C_g(-,I)\), and refine by their just-proved semifree filtrations. Retracts and homotopy equivalences are retained. For h-projective \(N\), tensoring (B.IP11) with \(N\) is a quasi-isomorphism, and both resulting left modules are h-projective. Its cone is therefore acyclic and h-projective, so it is contractible; the compositor is a homotopy equivalence. The same argument applies to the unit \(\iota_i\), induced by the protected inclusion \(\mathcal E_i\subset\mathcal R\): its composite with augmentation is the ordinary Yoneda identity of \(N\). Composition and the two unit diagrams commute exactly, because they are the composition and identity laws of the one category \(\mathcal R\). No separately chosen inverses enter those diagrams.

Before resolution, the corresponding tensor functor is simply \(N\mapsto N\circ D_g\), by co-Yoneda. For h-projective \(N\), augmentation gives a quasi-isomorphism from \(\mathsf A_g(N)\) to this restriction: tensor (B.IP10), in its right \(\mathcal E_i\)-variable, with the K-flat left module \(N\). Restriction preserves objectwise quasi-isomorphisms. Thus on a h-projective replacement of a corepresentable, (B.IP7) identifies the result with the opposite of the actual geometric inverse-image functor. Taking opposites returns its original variance. This identifies the parameter action; it is not the right adjoint of \(g_*\) obtained by using representable right modules in place of these left modules.

What has been joined, and what has not. The index \(K\) can contain the entire chosen family of geometric base changes and their compositions, not only one square or a finite sample. The same normalization and relative-free category treats every label and every composition. Proper compactification refinements remain the distinct fixed-endpoint equivalences of B.1z; the inverse-image arrows here are not promoted to equivalences. In (B.GC12), the four symbols \(A_D,A_Y,A_C,A_U\) now have these actual mapping-kernel models. Equation (B.GC13) still supplies their mixed compact-support cell, with the original edge \(t(A_Cs)\theta_k^{-1}\) and its higher coefficients. Those existing coefficients must be included when attaching that cell and the compact-support operation kernels to this parameter category.

In particular, (B.IP11)–(B.IP12) give strictly associative compositor maps which become homotopy equivalences on h-projective inputs. They are not literal isomorphisms and have not been replaced by pointwise inverses to claim a strictly commuting exceptional-operation system. The remaining join must use the common strict roof and whole-diagram lifts of B.1t–B.1aa, retaining the resolved-only transposes (B.BM16)–(B.BM18). That join, geometric nearby attaching and multiplicative descent, coefficient completion/rationalization and strict-heart higher effacement are not established by this construction. \(\square\)

Join the geometric kernels in right-module variance

Proposition B.1ad (the module side of the compact-support join). The inverse-image kernels of B.1ac admit actual right-module models and natural composition roofs. The fixed-compactification functor of (B.RG9) admits a right-module kernel over the same source and target models. Both constructions preserve h-projectives and homotopy-representable right modules. The compact-support kernel has a strict tensor–Hom adjunction, whose resolved unit and counit represent the ordinary exceptional adjunction. We construct these maps, including the bar and dual-evaluation signs.

This addresses a variance issue in joining the preceding constructions. The left-module functor of (B.IP12) models the opposite inverse image; it cannot simply be substituted for the right-module functors in (B.BM15). The construction below supplies the correctly directed functors. It does not assert that their geometric mixed-cell diagrams have already been assembled or that an objectwise homotopy inverse is a natural inverse of bimodules.

All models are over the original commutative \(\Lambda\). Compact support retains the full Noetherian, separated finite-type, unbounded ordinary torsion scope of (B.RG9); inverse images have the scope of B.1ac. Keep its chosen locally semifree models \(\mathcal E_i\), their evaluations \(e_i\), and the label-preserving kernels \(C_g\). For left modules a homogeneous degree-\(r\) map satisfies \(u(ax)=(-1)^{r|a|}a\,u(x)\). For right modules use exactly (B.DA1)'s convention \(u(xa)=u(x)a\).

Dualize the quasi-corepresentable kernel, not its variance label. For \(g:i\to j\), define \[ P_g(J,I)= \operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal E_j\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}} \bigl(C_g(-,I),\mathcal E_j(J,-)\bigr). \tag{B.RK1} \] This is contravariant in \(J\), covariant in \(I\), hence a kernel for right-module transport from \(\mathcal E_i\) to \(\mathcal E_j\). The Hom is the ordinary full complex of graded module maps. No extra derived-Hom replacement is needed: \(C_g(-,I)\) is h-projective by (B.IP10).

Here is why its columns have the required properties. Equations (B.IP4) and (B.IP7), together with the augmentation from (B.IP10), give a zigzag from \(C_g(-,I)\) to a left corepresentable \(\mathcal E_j(J_0,-)\), where \(e_jJ_0\) represents \(g^*e_iI\). Lift the corepresentable's quasi-isomorphism through that zigzag by Hom from a corepresentable, as in B.1l. The resulting quasi-isomorphism between h-projectives is a homotopy equivalence. Applying the contravariant Hom functor in (B.RK1) carries this homotopy equivalence to one of right modules. On the corepresentable the enriched Yoneda map gives exactly \(\mathcal E_j(-,J_0)\). Therefore \(P_g(-,I)\) is h-projective and homotopy representable, with the actual inverse image as its representing object. Tensoring a right module with \(P_g\) sends representable cells to these columns. The cell-filtration proof of B.1l then proves preservation of h-projectives and homotopy representables. This is not the generally different right adjoint of \(g_*\).

Composition has a canonical roof, not an inverted arrow by fiat. Set \(R_{h,g}(-,I)=C_h(-,-)\otimes_{\mathcal E_j}C_g(-,I)\), with the factor order of (B.IP11). Write \(D R(K,I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E_k\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}}^\bullet(R(-,I),\mathcal E_k(K,-))\). The common right-module kernel is \[ P_g\otimes_{\mathcal E_j}P_h \xrightarrow{\ \nu_{h,g}\ }D R_{h,g} \xleftarrow{\ D c_{h,g}\ }P_{hg}. \tag{B.RK2} \] Here the first tensor is ordered as right-module transport: \(g\) first, then \(h\). The arrow on the right points from \(P_{hg}\), because Hom dualization reverses the compositor. At \(K,I\), the first arrow is balanced evaluation. For homogeneous \(u\in P_g(J,I)\), \(v\in P_h(K,J)\), \(x\in C_h(L,J')\) and \(y\in C_g(J',I)\), it is \[ \nu_{h,g}(u\otimes v)(x\otimes y) =(-1)^{|u|(|v|+|x|)}\,v\bigl(x\,u(y)\bigr). \tag{B.RK3} \] This sign moves \(u\) past \(v,x\) before evaluation on \(y\); no other factor is permuted. In these conventions \((u a)(y)=(-1)^{|a||y|}u(y)a\) and \((a v)(x)=(-1)^{|a|(|v|+|x|)}v(xa)\). Substitution verifies the balancing relation in the first tensor. The relation \((xa)\otimes y=x\otimes ay\) in the second tensor uses the left-linearity rule for \(u\) and gives the same sign. Evaluation, tensor symmetry with its Koszul sign, and the module action are chain maps; thus (B.RK3) is a chain map and has the indicated right and left kernel actions.

Both arrows of (B.RK2) are objectwise homotopy equivalences of right modules for every fixed \(I\). Indeed, \(R_{h,g}(-,I)\) is h-projective: resolve the left \(\mathcal E_j\)-module \(C_g(-,I)\) by its semifree filtration, and its cells become the h-projective columns of \(C_h\). The compositor \(c_{h,g}\) is a quasi-isomorphism between these h-projectives by (B.IP11), hence a homotopy equivalence. Its dual is a homotopy equivalence. To check \(\nu\), replace \(C_g(-,I)\), by a homotopy equivalence, with \(\mathcal E_j(J_0,-)\). Both the tensor and the Hom constructions preserve such homotopies, without a flatness assumption. The resulting map is precisely the co-Yoneda isomorphism onto \(P_h(-,J_0)\). Also \(P_g(-,I)\otimes P_h\) is h-projective by its representable-cell filtration. Thus all columns in the displayed roof are legitimate h-projective representatives.

There is an all-length compatibility already at the common kernels. For three arrows, the two evaluation routes to the dual of \(C_\ell\otimes C_h\otimes C_g\) both send \(u\otimes v\otimes w\), evaluated on \(x\otimes y\otimes z\), to \[ (-1)^{\,|u|(|v|+|w|+|x|+|y|) +|v|(|w|+|x|)} w\bigl(x\,v(y\,u(z))\bigr). \tag{B.RK4} \] Here \(x,y,z\) belong respectively to the \(\ell,h,g\) kernels. The sign is the permutation moving each evaluator next to its argument. The same ordered evaluation and its permutation sign prove the assertion for every finite length, with the usual tensor associators. Precomposition with \(c\) respects these comparisons because the \(c\)'s come from the associative category \(\mathcal R\) of B.1ac. Identity evaluations give the unit comparisons. These are compatible roofs; no choice of pointwise inverse is promoted to a strict natural composition map.

Put the actual compactification roof over these same endpoint models. The diagram to be used is \[ \mathcal E_X\xleftarrow{\ p\ }\mathcal A_f \xrightarrow{\ q\ }\mathcal E_Y, \qquad p\text{ a quasi-equivalence}. \tag{B.RK5} \] We construct it from (B.RG9), not from a new compactification theorem. First pull its graph back along \(e_X:\mathcal E_X\to\mathcal I(X)\). Projection of (B.RG9) is surjective on graded Homs with acyclic kernel, and a replacement exists over every object. Its strict pullback therefore has the same properties and is a quasi-equivalence onto \(\mathcal E_X\). Its proper-output functor still lands in \(\mathcal I(Y)\).

To lift this output to \(\mathcal E_Y\), use objects \((a,J,t)\), where \(a\) is in that pullback, \(J\in\mathcal E_Y\), and \(t:F(a)\to e_YJ\) is a closed homotopy equivalence. Such objects exist: the identity-origin objects in (B.SN1) include every K-injective target. A degree-\(n\) map has components \((b,c,k)\) with \(k:F(a)\to e_YJ'\) of degree \(n-1\), and its third differential is \(t'F(b)-e_Y(c)t-dk\). Use exactly the graph composition (B.RG3). Projection to \(a\) is graded-Hom-surjective. Its kernel is the shifted cone of \(\mathcal E_Y(J,J')\to\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(F(a),e_YJ')\), \(c\mapsto e_Y(c)t\). This map is a quasi-isomorphism, because \(e_Y\) is one on Homs and \(t\) is a homotopy equivalence. Thus this projection is also a quasi-equivalence; projection to \(J\) is a strict dg functor. Finally apply the free replacement \(Q\) of B.1t to this source and compose its augmentation with the two projections. This gives (B.RK5) with semifree Hom complexes in \(\mathcal A_f\). The endpoint categories have not been replaced. In degree-zero derived categories the roof is still exactly \(Rf_!\), and \(p\) remains surjective on objects. No functorial choice of a K-injective resolution has been asserted.

One bar kernel retains all source-module actions. For a right \(\mathcal A_f\)-module \(M\), let \(P_{\mathcal A_f}M\) be its unnormalized augmented bar resolution. Its length-\(n\) terms are \(M(a_n)\otimes\mathcal A_f(a_{n-1},a_n)\otimes\cdots\otimes \mathcal A_f(a_0,a_1)\otimes\mathcal A_f(-,a_0)\), summed over all \(a_0,\ldots,a_n\). Set \[ \begin{aligned} H_f(J,I)&=q_!P_{\mathcal A_f}\bigl(p^*\mathcal E_X(-,I)\bigr)(J),\\ H_f^{[n]}(J,I)&= \bigoplus_{a_0,\ldots,a_n} \mathcal E_X(pa_n,I)\otimes \mathcal A_f(a_{n-1},a_n)\\ &\qquad\otimes\cdots\otimes \mathcal A_f(a_0,a_1)\otimes\mathcal E_Y(J,qa_0). \end{aligned} \tag{B.RK6} \] Every \(n\geq0\) is included, by direct-sum totalization. No truncation or product completion is implicit. Give an element of internal degree \(r\) in length \(n\) total degree \(r-n\). The faces, from left to right, first act on \(M\), then compose adjacent arrows, and finally act on the last representable. With the ordinary internal tensor differential, use \[ d_{\mathrm{tot}}\big|_{[n]} =(-1)^n d_{\mathrm{int}}+\sum_{s=0}^{n}(-1)^s d_s, \qquad P(\phi)\big|_{[n]}=(-1)^{n|\phi|}\phi \tag{B.RK7} \] for a homogeneous module map \(\phi\); the face sum is zero at length zero in the unaugmented complex. In the last formula \(\phi\) acts on the first factor. Simplicial face identities give \(\delta^2=0\), internal differentials commute with faces, and the factor \((-1)^n\) reverses when a face lowers length. Hence \(d_{\mathrm{tot}}^2=0\). The second sign makes \(P\) an actual dg functor, also for odd homogeneous maps. Right actions on the last factor are unaltered; their Leibniz exponent is the total degree \(r-n\). Source \(I\)-actions in (B.RK6) use the second sign in (B.RK7).

At each test object \(a\), augment \(P M(a)\) by module composition. The section is \(m\mapsto m\otimes1_a\). On an unaugmented word, append its last representable factor as a new bar arrow and put \(1_a\) in the new last position; denote this insertion by \(s_{\mathrm{end}}\). Then \[ h_n=(-1)^{n+1}s_{\mathrm{end}},\qquad d_{\mathrm{tot}}h+h\,d_{\mathrm{tot}} =1-\mathrm{section}\,\mathrm{augmentation}. \tag{B.RK8} \] To verify it, the last face after insertion is the original word, while every other face pairs with insertion after that face with the opposite sign. Internal terms cancel because insertion commutes with the internal differential and changes the length by one. This contraction is objectwise; it is not asserted to be a right-module-linear contraction of the augmentation. It proves the needed quasi-isomorphism for unbounded complexes without a convergence argument.

For \(M=p^*\mathcal E_X(-,I)\), all coefficient complexes in the length filtration are h-projective over \(\Lambda\): the endpoint and source Hom complexes are semifree. Finite tensors of such semifree complexes remain semifree. Each successive bar quotient is a sum of those coefficient complexes tensored with right representables. It is h-projective as a module: Hom into an acyclic module is Hom from the coefficient complex into its acyclic value. The length filtration is split on graded modules. The recursive primitive construction from (B.DA2) applies to these quotients as well: at each length the defect is a closed map into an acyclic Hom complex, and can be filled while preserving all previous lengths. Thus \(P M\) is h-projective, including its infinite union. Induction \(q_!\) preserves h-projectivity by (B.DA4), so every column \(H_f(-,I)\) is h-projective.

Choose an object \(a\) of (B.RK5) with \(pa=I\). Quasi-full faithfulness of \(p\) gives a quasi-isomorphism \(\mathcal A_f(-,a)\to p^*\mathcal E_X(-,I)\). Lift this through the bar augmentation using Hom from the representable. The lift is a quasi-isomorphism between h-projectives, hence a homotopy equivalence. Induction sends it to a homotopy equivalence between \(H_f(-,I)\) and \(\mathcal E_Y(-,qa)\). Under the graph above, \(e_Yqa\) is precisely a representative of \(Rf_!e_XI\). This proves the required geometric identification, not merely abstract quasi-representability.

For any right module \(N\), co-Yoneda in the \(I\)-variable gives an actual natural isomorphism of complexes \[ \begin{aligned} N\otimes_{\mathcal E_X}H_f &\cong q_!P_{\mathcal A_f}(p^*N),\\ m\otimes(e\otimes f_n\otimes\cdots\otimes f_1\otimes v) &\longmapsto (-1)^{n|m|}(me)\otimes f_n\otimes\cdots\otimes f_1\otimes v . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RK9} \] There are \(n\) internal bar arrows in the second line. Its sign is the tensor–totalization sign. It agrees with the source-action sign in (B.RK7), so the formula is balanced. For the internal differential the exponent on \(dm\) changes by \(n\); for a face it changes by \(|m|\), precisely compensating the tensor differential. This verifies the chain identity. For h-projective \(N\), its values are h-projective over \(\Lambda\), by a representable-cell resolution and the locally semifree Hom complexes of \(\mathcal E_X\). The preceding bar argument therefore still applies. Alternatively, the h-projective columns of \(H_f\) and a cell resolution of \(N\) prove that \(N\otimes H_f\) is h-projective directly. Homotopy representables are sent to homotopy representables.

The common right-module adjunction has actual units and counits. For either right kernel \(K=P_g\) or \(K=H_f\), write \[ \begin{aligned} T_K M&=M\otimes_{\mathcal E_X}K,\\ (U_KN)(I)&=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Mod}\text{-}\mathcal E_Y}^\bullet (K(-,I),N),\\ \operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(T_KM,N) &\cong\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(M,U_KN),\\ \eta_M(m)(k)&=m\otimes k,\\ \varepsilon_N(\phi\otimes k)&=\phi(k). \end{aligned} \tag{B.RK10} \] The Hom-complex bijection sends \(b\) to \(m\mapsto(k\mapsto b(m\otimes k))\). Its inverse is evaluation. The balancing relation is exactly right-module linearity. Differentiating this formula cancels the terms containing \(dk\), with exponent \(|b|+|m|\); hence it holds in every degree. The two triangle identities follow on \(m\otimes k\) and on \(\phi\) by evaluation, before passing to cohomology. Since the columns of \(K\) are h-projective, \(U_K\) preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Its adjunction therefore also proves that \(T_K\) preserves h-projectives.

For \(H_f\), the ordinary exceptional adjoint in B.1e identifies \(U_{H_f}\) on represented targets. More explicitly, choose the representing source object for \(f^!Y\), and represent the ordinary counit by a closed map from its image under \(T_{H_f}\) to \(h_Y\). Its transpose under (B.RK10) gives a right-module map from that representable to \(U_{H_f}h_Y\). On every shifted input its cohomology is the ordinary adjunction bijection, with this very counit, so it is a quasi-isomorphism in every degree. This is the same argument as (B.RG11), now over the common endpoint models. No claim that \(U_{H_f}h_Y\) itself is h-projective is needed.

Use the resolution graph of (B.DA7), now with this \(T_K,U_K\). Its Hom-kernel argument uses only h-projectivity of the resolved source and the target replacement, so is unchanged. If \(r:P\to U_KN\) is the chosen graph object, the maps are \[ e_N=\varepsilon_NT_Kr,\qquad r_{T_KA}u_A-\eta_A=dk_A. \tag{B.RK11} \] Their actual triangle witnesses are \[ \begin{aligned} e_{T_KA}T_Ku_A-1&=d(\varepsilon_{T_KA}T_Kk_A),\\ r(r_eu_P-1)&=d(h_eu_P+U_Ke_N\,k_P). \end{aligned} \tag{B.RK12} \] Here \((e_N,r_e,h_e)\) is a closed lift of the counit through the graph. The second equation and the Hom quasi-isomorphism imply that \(r_eu_P-1\) is a boundary; they do not require a prescribed primitive upstairs to map to that particular primitive downstairs. For compact support the resolved right modules are homotopy representable by the counit argument just given. These formulas thus supply the ordinary exceptional adjunction in the common right-module variance.

The remaining geometric join is now a map problem with specified endpoints. In (B.BM15) use \(L_0=T_{H_f}\), \(L_1=T_{H_{f'}}\), \(S=T_{P_u}\), and \(V=T_{P_g}\). All four are now actual dg functors on right modules that preserve h-projectives. The inverse-image composition comparisons are the natural roofs (B.RK2), not nonexistent inverses of the left-module compositors. The compactification and folding comparisons retain the existing spans and all coefficients of B.1s–B.1aa.

It remains to present the actual mixed cell (B.GC12)–(B.GC13) as a whole-diagram map between these kernels, including \(t(A_Cs)\theta_k^{-1}\), the nested second coefficient (B.IA12), and the common composition roofs. A comparison merely identifying each represented object, or merely identifying functors on \(H^0\), would not do this. Only after that whole map and its relative faces are supplied may its homotopy inverse be used in (B.BM16)–(B.BM18). The right mate is not thereby an isomorphism. This module-side join does not establish the full exceptional-operation system or coefficient completion. \(\square\)

Construct the whole-bimodule compact-support base-change cell

Proposition B.1ae (an actual cell over the common endpoints). For one cartesian compactification diagram, the proper and open base-change maps define a homotopy equivalence of whole bimodule models. Their composite represents the canonical compact-support base-change map. A signed bar construction compares this model with the actual compactification-roof kernel \(H_f\) of (B.RK6), retaining the replacement edges and their homotopies. Its inverse therefore supplies the resolved input to (B.BM16), not just an isomorphism of functors on \(H^0\).

This statement is about the specified diagram and its recorded faces. It does not declare that all changing compactifications, iterated compositions and base changes have already been assembled into one coherent parameter diagram. The geometric hypotheses remain those of (B.RG9), (B.BC3) and (B.CB6): Noetherian separated finite-type compactifications and the stated unbounded ordinary torsion scope, with the common annihilator required by the proper-base-change provider. The algebra below works over the original arbitrary commutative \(\Lambda\); this does not extend the geometric theorem to arbitrary coefficients.

Use the locally semifree endpoint categories \(\mathcal E_T\), with evaluations \(e_T\), from B.1ac. Consider \[ \begin{array}{ccccc} X'&\xrightarrow{\ j'\ }&U'&\xrightarrow{\ h'\ }&Y'\\ {\scriptstyle u}\downarrow&&{\scriptstyle v}\downarrow&& \downarrow{\scriptstyle g}\\ X&\xrightarrow{\ j\ }&U&\xrightarrow{\ h\ }&Y . \end{array} \qquad f=hj,\quad f'=h'j'. \tag{B.KC1} \] Both squares are cartesian; \(j,j'\) are open immersions and \(h,h'\) are proper. This is a diagram of the actual schemes and maps, not a claim that inverse image preserves K-injective complexes. Every unnamed tensor associator and direct-image comparison below is its canonical one.

Choose resolutions in both variables at once. For an inverse image \(a^*:D(T)\to D(T')\), an open extension \(j_!:D(X)\to D(U)\), and a proper image \(h_*:D(U)\to D(Y)\), the raw left kernels are \[ \begin{aligned} B_a(J,I)&=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(e_TI,a_*e_{T'}J),\\ B_j(J,I)&=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(e_XI,j^*e_UJ),\\ B_h(J,I)&=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(h_*e_UI,e_YJ). \end{aligned} \tag{B.KC2} \] They are covariant in \(J\) and contravariant in \(I\). The first two formulas are the actual complex-level adjunctions. The functors \(a_*\), \(j^*\) and \(h_*\) occurring here preserve K-injectives: each has the appropriate exact left adjoint. Proper direct image is not being called exact.

Resolve each kernel as a left module over \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{target}}\otimes\mathcal E_{\mathrm{source}}^{\mathrm{op}}\). For an inverse image, take a whole semifree replacement \(L_a\to C_a\) of the existing kernel (B.IP10), and then its augmentation to \(B_a\). For the open and proper kernels take whole semifree replacements \(L_j\to B_j\) and \(L_h\to B_h\). The many-object construction (B.DA2), applied to these product categories, supplies these maps.

These are stronger replacements than separate columnwise choices. An exterior representable cell, evaluated in either variable, is a representable module tensored with a semifree endpoint Hom complex. The filtration proof (B.ND2), (B.ND6) therefore makes every row and column h-projective and K-flat. A tensor of two whole semifree kernels is again whole h-projective: tensor two exterior cells over the middle category and apply co-Yoneda. The resulting exterior cell has as its coefficient a middle Hom complex, which is semifree over \(\Lambda\). Filter first by the two cell stages and then by that coefficient's path filtration. Differentials decrease this order. The recursive primitive argument of B.1u proves h-projectivity into every objectwise acyclic bimodule; the corresponding split filtration proves K-flatness. Direct sums and limit stages cause no convergence problem.

Each \(L_F(-,I)\) is homotopy corepresentable by the actual derived image of \(eI\). For \(a,j\), choose a K-injective replacement of the exact image and use adjunction. For \(h\), the object \(h_*e_UI\) is already K-injective. The evaluation quasi-equivalence and a lift from a corepresentable give a quasi-isomorphism between h-projectives, hence a homotopy equivalence. This argument also proves that \(L_h\otimes L_j\) is homotopy corepresentable by \(h_*B\) when \(j_!e_XI\to B\) is a K-injective replacement. It does not identify this composite with the unresolved expression \(h_*j_!e_XI\).

The proper cell before any inverse is chosen. Put \[ \begin{aligned} M(Q,I)&=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_Y(h_*e_UI,g_*e_{Y'}Q),\\ \chi_{\mathrm{raw}}(w\otimes z) &=g_*(w)\,\kappa_K\,h_*(z),\\ \kappa_K:\ h_*v_*e_{U'}K&\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }g_*h'_*e_{U'}K . \end{aligned} \tag{B.KC3} \] Here \(z:e_UI\to v_*e_{U'}K\) and \(w:h'_*e_{U'}K\to e_{Y'}Q\). Thus \(\chi_{\mathrm{raw}}\) is defined on \(B_{h'}\otimes_{\mathcal E_{U'}}B_v\). The square of direct images supplies the closed canonical \(\kappa\). Composition and its homogeneous naturality prove the balancing relation and the chain-map identity. No homogeneous factors are interchanged.

If \(q_z:v^*e_UI\to e_{U'}K\) is the adjoint of \(z\), transposing the output of (B.KC3) under \(g^*\dashv g_*\) gives \[ \operatorname{Adj}_g\bigl(\chi_{\mathrm{raw}}(w,z)\bigr) =w\,h'_*(q_z)\,\beta_{h,e_UI}. \tag{B.KC4} \] Indeed substitute the unit-and-counit definition (B.BC2) of \(\beta\). Naturality moves the units past \(z,w\); the two adjunction triangles cancel the inserted counits and units. What remains is exactly \(g_*w\,\kappa_Kh_*z\). This proves equality for every homogeneous \(z,w\), not merely for cohomology classes.

Let \(A=L_{h'}\otimes L_v\) and \(B=L_g\otimes L_h\). Augment the first word and apply (B.KC3), giving \(\chi:A\to M\). Augment the second word and compose maps \(h_*e_UI\to e_YK\to g_*e_{Y'}Q\), giving \(\pi:B\to M\). Both maps are quasi-isomorphisms. For \(\pi\), fix \(I\), replace \(L_h(-,I)\) by its homotopy-corepresentable model and apply co-Yoneda; the remaining map is the inverse-image kernel augmentation. For \(\chi\), replace \(L_v(-,I)\) by a corepresentable associated to \(q:v^*e_UI\to e_{U'}K_0\). Under this comparison, (B.KC4) is precomposition by \((h'_*q)\beta_{h,e_UI}\). This is the exact quasi-isomorphism of (B.BC3). Hom into the K-injective \(e_{Y'}Q\) preserves that quasi-isomorphism. This proof does not apply \(h'_*\) to an arbitrary quasi-isomorphism.

Since \(A\) is whole h-projective, (B.ND7) gives closed \(\lambda_h\) and degree-minus-one \(\omega_h\), in the whole bimodule Hom complex, with \[ \lambda_h:A\longrightarrow B,\qquad \pi\lambda_h-\chi=d\omega_h. \tag{B.KC5} \] The map \(\lambda_h\) is a quasi-isomorphism between whole h-projectives, hence a bimodule-linear homotopy equivalence. To see the last assertion directly, lift the identity of the target through the Hom quasi-isomorphism induced by \(\lambda_h\). This gives a closed inverse with one composite homotopic to the identity. Applying the other Hom quasi-isomorphism makes the second composite a boundary as well. Both witnesses are bimodule-linear; no family of pointwise inverses has been promoted to a natural inverse.

The open cell uses its actual right-adjoint mate. The exact open-base-change isomorphism and its right-adjoint mate are \[ \theta:v^*j_!\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j'_!u^*, \qquad \theta^R:u_*j'^*\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }j^*v_* . \tag{B.KC6} \] For the mate, evaluate a sheaf on an open of \(X\): both sides restrict the direct image of the same sheaf on its inverse image in \(U'\). The maps agree with the adjunction units and restrictions. Thus this is the canonical isomorphism on complexes and all homogeneous maps, not an arbitrary identification.

Set \(A_o=L_{j'}\otimes L_u\), \(B_o=L_v\otimes L_j\). Composition after the augmentations gives \[ \begin{aligned} A_o(J,I)&\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_X(e_XI,u_*j'^*e_{U'}J),\\ B_o(J,I)&\xrightarrow{\ \pi_o\ } \operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_X(e_XI,j^*v_*e_{U'}J)=M_o(J,I). \end{aligned} \tag{B.KC7} \] These maps are quasi-isomorphisms. Reduce the first exact operation to its corepresentable replacement, then use co-Yoneda; exactness of the second operation preserves the chosen replacement. Composing the first line with \(\theta^R\) gives \(\chi_o:A_o\to M_o\). Whole h-projectivity gives a closed \(\lambda_j:A_o\to B_o\) and a whole witness \(\pi_o\lambda_j-\chi_o=d\omega_o\), exactly as in (B.KC5). It is again a whole-bimodule homotopy equivalence.

With \(W_f=L_h\otimes L_j\), the resulting left-kernel comparison is the explicit two-step map \[ \begin{aligned} W_{f'}\otimes L_u &\xrightarrow{\ 1\otimes\lambda_j\ } L_{h'}\otimes L_v\otimes L_j\\ &\xrightarrow{\ \lambda_h\otimes1\ } L_g\otimes W_f . \end{aligned} \tag{B.KC8} \] The indicated factors fix the variance and order. Tensoring preserves the actual inverse maps and homotopies, so (B.KC8) is a whole homotopy equivalence. It is the left-module, hence opposite, version of \(g^*Rf_!\to Rf'_!u^*\). To use it with (B.RK10), we still have to connect \(W_f\) to the existing right-roof kernel; agreement on represented objects alone is not sufficient.

A signed bar map carries the graph homotopies. We give that connection rather than appeal to uniqueness on \(H^0\). Let \(N_0,N_1\) be left modules on a dg category \(\mathcal A\), possibly also carrying a commuting target-module structure. Suppose there are closed degree-zero object maps \(\alpha_a\) and degree-\((|t|-1)\) maps \(k_t\) such that \[ \begin{aligned} dk_t+k_{dt}&=\alpha_bN_0(t)-N_1(t)\alpha_a,\\ k_{st}&=k_sN_0(t)+(-1)^{|s|}N_1(s)k_t,\qquad k_{1_a}=0 . \end{aligned} \tag{B.KC9} \] These are the differential, composition and unit relations in the actual resolution graph (B.RG2)–(B.RG3). For a right module \(M\), use the direct-sum two-sided bar with total degree internal degree minus length, and differential (B.RK7). There is a map to the ordinary balanced tensor \(M\otimes_{\mathcal A}N_1\): \[ \begin{aligned} \Psi(m\otimes x)&=m\otimes\alpha_a x&&(\text{length }0),\\ \Psi(m\otimes t\otimes x) &=(-1)^{|m|+1}m\otimes k_t x&&(\text{length }1),\\ \Psi\big|_{[n]}&=0&& (n\geq2). \end{aligned} \tag{B.KC10} \] For length one the chain defect is minus \(m\otimes(dk_t+k_{dt})x\); the two face terms are \(m\otimes(N_1(t)\alpha-\alpha N_0(t))x\). For length two the remaining expression, after factoring \((-1)^{|m|+1}\), is \((-1)^{|s|}N_1(s)k_t-k_{st}+k_sN_0(t)\), which is zero by (B.KC9). Higher lengths give zero. Length zero uses \(d\alpha=0\). This verifies every bar length, including the internal differential.

The map is natural for homogeneous maps of \(M\), with the factor \((-1)^{n|\phi|}\) of (B.RK7) on length \(n\); the degree of \(m\) in the second line makes the two routes agree. It is also natural in any commuting target variable, using the ordinary Koszul interchange. If \(M\) is h-projective and every \(\alpha_a\) is a quasi-isomorphism, then \(\Psi\) is a quasi-isomorphism. For \(M=\mathcal A(-,a)\), the endpoint insertion contraction of (B.RK8) identifies the source with \(N_0(a)\); its section followed by \(\Psi\) is exactly \(\alpha_a\). For a semifree \(M\), use its graded-split cell filtration: the assertion holds on each shifted representable quotient, then on the successive extensions and their unions. A general h-projective is homotopy equivalent to its semifree replacement, and both constructions preserve the homotopies with the same length signs. No flatness of the \(N_i(a)\), finite bar truncation, or module-linear endpoint contraction is assumed.

Here is the opposite convention needed for the geometric graph. If \(s_a:F_0a\to F_1a\), with graph homotopies \(h_t\), apply \(\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(-,J)\). On \(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{op}}\) the two left modules are \(N_0(a)=\operatorname{Hom}(F_1a,J)\) and \(N_1(a)=\operatorname{Hom}(F_0a,J)\). For \(t:a\to b\) and homogeneous \(\phi:F_1b\to J\), their comparison is \[ \alpha_a(\psi)=\psi s_a,\qquad \widehat h_{t^{\mathrm{op}}}(\phi) =(-1)^{(|t|-1)|\phi|+1}\phi h_t . \tag{B.KC11} \] Here \(\psi:F_1a\to J\). The action of \(t^{\mathrm{op}}\) is \(\phi\mapsto(-1)^{|t||\phi|}\phi F_i(t)\). Differentiating the second formula cancels its two \(d\phi\) terms; the remaining terms are \(-(-1)^{|t||\phi|}\phi(dh_t+h_{dt})\), precisely \(\alpha N_0(t^{\mathrm{op}})-N_1(t^{\mathrm{op}})\alpha\). Composition follows by inserting the graph composition and the dg-opposite sign \((-1)^{|s||t|}\). Thus (B.KC10) applies with its signs specified, rather than with an unspecified “opposite homotopy.”

Compare the actual compactification graph. Refine (B.RK5) by also lifting its middle K-injective to \(\mathcal E_U\). Before the free replacement its objects are \((I,K,J;s,t)\), with \(s:j_!e_XI\to e_UK\) a quasi-isomorphism and \(t:h_*e_UK\to e_YJ\) a homotopy equivalence. Its morphisms retain the two graph homotopies for \(s,t\). Forgetting \(K\) by evaluation gives a strict map to the raw graph used in (B.RK5). Both graphs project quasi-equivalently to \(\mathcal E_X\): the new middle Hom kernel is the shifted cone of \(\mathcal E_U(K,K')\to\operatorname{Hom}(j_!e_XI,e_UK')\); it is acyclic by evaluation and the replacement \(s\). The output kernel is the one already checked in B.1ad. Therefore the forgetful map is also a quasi-equivalence.

The construction \(Q\) in (B.SF1) is functorial on these strict maps. Send \(c_z\) to \(c_{Fz}\), and at each later stage send \(e_{n,z,m}\) to \(e_{n,QF(z),F(m)}\). The defining differential and augmentation equations are preserved, including the formally labelled zero cycles. Hence we obtain a commuting diagram \[ \begin{array}{ccc} \mathcal A_f^+&\xrightarrow{\ \rho\ }&\mathcal A_f\\ {\scriptstyle p^+}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle p}\\ \mathcal E_X&=&\mathcal E_X, \end{array} \qquad q^+=q\rho . \tag{B.KC12} \] All three source Hom complexes are in the stated semifree models, and \(\rho\) is a quasi-equivalence. This use of \(Q\) on strict functors does not apply it directly to an \(A_\infty\) map.

The replacement \(s\) gives the objectwise quasi-isomorphism \(\mathcal E_U(K,-)\to B_j(-,p^+a)\), \(z\mapsto e_U(z)s\). Its homotopy is obtained from the \(s\)-edge by (B.KC11). After tensoring with the K-flat row \(L_h(J,-)\), co-Yoneda gives the comparison from \(L_h(J,K)\) to \((L_h\otimes B_j)(J,p^+a)\). The augmentation \(W_f\to L_h\otimes B_j\) is a quasi-isomorphism. The second edge \(t\) gives \(\mathcal E_Y(q^+a,J)\to B_h(J,K)\), \(z\mapsto e_Y(z)t\), with its recorded \(t\)-homotopy; insert also the augmentation \(L_h(J,K)\to B_h(J,K)\). For the intermediate raw Hom functors, evaluation from the endpoint representables is a quasi-isomorphism. All these arrows are thus justified in their actual directions.

Apply (B.KC10) to each of these graph comparisons over \((\mathcal A_f^+)^{\mathrm{op}}\), retaining a bar source and its augmentation for each arrow. Resolve the whole parameter modules before tensoring. It gives a zigzag of actual bimodule quasi-isomorphisms, natural in both \(I,J\), between \(W_f(J,I)\) and the derived coend \(\mathcal E_Y(q^+-,J)\otimes_{\mathcal A_f^+}^{\mathbb L} \mathcal E_X(I,p^+-)\). Indeed induction along the quasi-equivalence \(p^+\) identifies the coend with the original left \(\mathcal E_X\)-parameter by (B.SM1)–(B.SM2). The two augmentations and the length-one terms retain \(s,t\) and their homotopies. They have not been replaced by a pointwise naturality claim.

We identify this coend with the dual of the old \(H_f\) explicitly. Write \(R_I=P_{\mathcal A_f}(p^*\mathcal E_X(-,I))\), a homotopy-representable right module, and \(R_I^\vee(a)=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_{\mathrm{Mod}-\mathcal A_f} (R_I,\mathcal A_f(-,a))\). Put \(Z_{I,a}=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal A_f} (R_I,p^*\mathcal E_X(-,pa))\). There is a natural zigzag \[ \mathcal E_X(I,pa)\longrightarrow Z_{I,a} \longleftarrow R_I^\vee(a). \tag{B.KC13} \] The first arrow is restricted Yoneda followed by the bar augmentation; it is a quasi-isomorphism by the full mapping-complex equivalence of (B.SM1)–(B.SM2). The second is induced by the canonical \(\mathcal A_f(-,a)\to p^*\mathcal E_X(-,pa)\), and is a quasi-isomorphism since \(R_I\) is h-projective. This proves the assertion in every degree and in both parameters.

For \(N=q^*\mathcal E_Y(-,J)\), evaluation gives \[ \begin{aligned} N\otimes_{\mathcal A_f}R_I^\vee &\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal A_f}(R_I,N),\\ v\otimes\phi&\longmapsto\bigl(x\longmapsto v\,\phi(x)\bigr),\\ \operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal A_f}(R_I,N) &\cong \operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_{\mathcal E_Y} (H_f(-,I),\mathcal E_Y(-,J)). \end{aligned} \tag{B.KC14} \] The first map is balanced, right-linear and a chain map, with the right-module convention of B.1ad. It is a quasi-isomorphism: \(R_I\) is homotopy equivalent to a representable, for which it is exactly co-Yoneda. The last line is the literal induction–restriction adjunction, since \(H_f=q_!R_I\). Use whole replacements of (B.KC13) before any tensor that needs to preserve a quasi-isomorphism; no ordinary tensor of unresolved nonflat modules is being substituted for a derived one.

Changing \(\mathcal A_f^+\) to \(\mathcal A_f\) is also an actual bar map: apply \(\rho\) to every object and internal arrow in (B.RK6). All faces and length signs commute. It is a quasi-isomorphism by the induction–restriction equivalence for \(\rho\); after replacing the two source modules by h-projectives the comparison is a homotopy equivalence, and induction preserves it. Both resulting right bar kernels are whole h-projective: filter by bar length, then by the path weights of their internal Hom coefficients; the outer factors are exterior endpoint representables. Thus this comparison retains whole, not just columnwise, naturality.

Equations (B.KC10)–(B.KC14) identify \(W_f\), by actual quasi-isomorphism roofs, with the right-Yoneda dual of \(H_f\). Double Yoneda evaluation is a quasi-isomorphism on each column because that column is homotopy representable. After whole endpoint replacements these roofs give the comparison of \(D W_f\) with \(H_f\), where \(D\) is the left-to-right dual (B.RK1). This proves the needed roof connection with the original geometric graph, not just with another functor having the same \(H^0\).

Return to right-module base change and the resolved mate. Dualize (B.KC8); use the signed composition evaluations (B.RK2)–(B.RK4) and the preceding roof comparisons. For inverse images the map \(L_a\to C_a\) gives \(D C_a\to D L_a\), a natural columnwise homotopy equivalence, so the endpoints are the existing \(P_a\). Resolve the full right kernels before selecting inverses. We obtain the comparison roof \[ \begin{aligned} H_f\otimes_{\mathcal E_Y}P_g &\xrightarrow{\ \beta_f\ }P_u\otimes_{\mathcal E_{X'}}H_{f'},\\ T_{P_g}T_{H_f}&\longrightarrow T_{H_{f'}}T_{P_u}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.KC15} \] The first line uses balanced right tensor order: compact support and then base change on the left, base change and then compact support on the right. The arrow is represented on the common whole h-projective kernel models just constructed. Its inverse and both homotopies exist there, not on an unresolved target.

To identify the map, evaluate on a replacement string \(s:j_!e_XI\to B\), \(r:v^*B\to C\). The proper factor is \((h'_*r)\beta_{h,B}\) by (B.KC4), and the common open edge is \(r(v^*s)\theta^{-1}\) by (B.KC6)–(B.KC7). These are exactly (B.CB5)–(B.CB6). The length-one bar terms are the graph edge homotopies, with (B.KC11)'s signs. If a higher fold has first been replaced by its strict \(UQ\) roof, its higher coefficients are already the images of the free words; (B.KC10) does not discard them. In particular the second coefficient of (B.IA12) must remain when this cell is inserted into the composition square. The identical-word identities (B.GC12)–(B.GC13) specify those boundary comparisons; a joint global lift is an additional requirement.

Now put \(L_0=T_{H_f}\), \(L_1=T_{H_{f'}}\), \(S=T_{P_u}\), \(V=T_{P_g}\) in the common models, and let \(\vartheta:L_1S\to VL_0\) be the inverse of (B.KC15). For a resolved \(r_0:P_0\to U_0N\), set \(e_0=\varepsilon_0L_0r_0\). The exact resolved mate equations are \[ \begin{aligned} \zeta&=\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}(V e_0\,\vartheta_{P_0}),\\ r_1c-\zeta&=db,\\ e_1L_1c-Ve_0\,\vartheta_{P_0} &=d(\varepsilon_1L_1b). \end{aligned} \tag{B.KC16} \] Here \(r_1:P_1\to U_1VN\); \(c:SP_0\to P_1\) and its witness are lifted in the whole natural Hom complex as in (B.BM16). These are the actual unit/counit adjunction maps (B.RK10). Neither \(\vartheta_{U_0N}\) nor an inverse on an unresolved right adjoint is used. The unit witness and both pasting witnesses are precisely (B.BM16)–(B.BM18) with this supplied cell and its comparison roofs. The right mate is not thereby an isomorphism.

The one-square whole-bimodule map has the stated comparison with the compact-support roof. What remains is the simultaneous relative assembly over changing compactifications and composition/base-change arrays, with their specified (B.GC13) and (B.IA12) faces and both inverse homotopies. That requires checking the boundaries of the full free parameter presentation before (B.ND9) is applied; it is not implied by independent choices of the above lifts. Geometric nearby multiplicative descent, normalized coefficient-system transport and strict-heart effacement are not established by this construction. \(\square\)

The proper–open kernel and the common mixed cube

Proposition B.1af (one common target for the six vertices). Keep the Noetherian, separated finite-type, unbounded ordinary torsion scope and the locally semifree endpoint categories of B.1ae. The actual mixed cube (B.GC12) has a comparison in whole bimodules, with an explicit boundary for its two composite routes. Its proper–open edge is the derived exchange of (B.GC3), and its common target uses the actual sheaf maps, not an arbitrary identification of represented objects. The comparison can be lifted relative to the supplied graph and nested-resolution faces. The global changing-array assembly is not inferred merely from this elementary cube.

Use the two-map square (B.GC1). To avoid confusing a geometric functor with a kernel, retain \(L=i_!\), \(K=k_!\), \(H=h_*\), \(P=p_*\), and write \(\mathbb L_F\) for the whole left kernel of an elementary operation \(F\). Thus \(\mathbb L_G\otimes\mathbb L_F\) represents the opposite of \(GF\). Tensors below are balanced over their indicated intermediate endpoint categories, with the canonical associators.

The missing proper–open edge. For \(I\in\mathcal E_U\), \(J\in\mathcal E_D\), set \[ \begin{aligned} M_\epsilon(J,I)&=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(LH e_UI,e_DJ),\\ \chi_\epsilon(w\otimes z)&=w\,P(z)\,\epsilon_{e_UI},\\ z&:K e_UI\longrightarrow e_CA,\qquad w:P e_CA\longrightarrow e_DJ . \end{aligned} \tag{B.MX1} \] The input of the second line is \(B_P\otimes_{\mathcal E_C}B_K\). The raw open kernel is written using its adjunction, as in (B.KC2). The other word has the composition map \(B_L\otimes_{\mathcal E_Y}B_H\to M_\epsilon\). Both formulas are balanced chain maps: the middle action moves through \(P\), and the homogeneous Leibniz rule is the rule for ordered composition. There is no permutation of \(w,z\).

Augment the whole kernels and denote the resulting maps by \(\chi\) and \(\pi\). They give \[ \mathbb L_P\otimes\mathbb L_K \xrightarrow{\ \chi\ }M_\epsilon \xleftarrow{\ \pi\ }\mathbb L_L\otimes\mathbb L_H, \qquad \pi\lambda_\epsilon-\chi=d\omega_\epsilon . \tag{B.MX2} \] Here \(\lambda_\epsilon\) points from the left word to the right word; \(|\omega_\epsilon|=-1\). To prove both arrows are quasi-isomorphisms, fix \(I\). Since \(H e_UI\) is K-injective, reducing its homotopy-corepresentable column and applying co-Yoneda identifies the right word with the mapping complex for the exact \(L\)-image. For the left word choose \(s:K e_UI\to C_0\) with K-injective target. The same reduction identifies \(\chi\) with precomposition by \((P s)\epsilon_{e_UI}:LH e_UI\to P C_0\). This is precisely the quasi-isomorphism proved in (B.GC3), using B.1n on the original K-injective input. Hom into \(e_DJ\) preserves it. This argument does not apply \(P\) to an arbitrary quasi-isomorphism.

Both word kernels are whole h-projective by B.1ae. Thus (B.ND7) supplies \(\lambda_\epsilon,\omega_\epsilon\) in the whole bimodule Hom complex. As in (B.KC5), \(\lambda_\epsilon\) has a bimodule-linear homotopy inverse and both inverse witnesses. This is the actual derived proper–open exchange, with the variance reversed by the left kernel.

All six objects, with their maps to the same target. Pull the square back along \(D'\to D\), with notation as in (B.GC12). Put \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} v&F_v&\tau_v:A_DLH\longrightarrow F_v\\ \hline 0&A_DLH&1\\ 1&A_DPK&A_D\epsilon\\ 2&P'A_CK&(\beta_pK)(A_D\epsilon)\\ 3&P'K'A_U&(P'\theta_k)(\beta_pK)(A_D\epsilon)\\ 4&L'A_YH&\theta_iH\\ 5&L'H'A_U&(L'\beta_h)(\theta_iH). \end{array} \tag{B.MX3} \] The six directed edges on geometric operations are \(0\to1\to2\to3\) and \(0\to4\to5\to3\). Their labels are, respectively, \(A_D\epsilon,\beta_pK,P'\theta_k\) and \(\theta_iH,L'\beta_h,\epsilon'A_U\). Equation (B.GC12) says that the last route also has composite \(\tau_3\), as an actual natural map on complexes.

Let \(W_v\) be the ordered tensor of whole kernels for the letters of \(F_v\), and set \[ M_\square(J,I) =\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet} (A_DLH e_UI,e_{D'}J),\qquad a_v:W_v\longrightarrow M_\square . \tag{B.MX4} \] These maps have a concrete definition. For a word \(F_m\cdots F_1\), augment its kernel factors to maps \(z_b:F_b eI_{b-1}\to eI_b\). Compose them in the order \(z_mF_m(z_{m-1})\cdots(F_m\cdots F_2)(z_1)\), then precompose with \(\tau_v\). This is a balanced chain map natural in both endpoints. Intermediate images need not be K-injective for this raw composition to be defined. Their derived meaning is established separately below; raw direct image is not declared exact.

Every \(a_v\) is a quasi-isomorphism. The following reductions check all six cases, not only the two endpoints.

  • For \(v=0\), \(H\) is applied to the original K-injective input; \(L,A_D\) are exact. Successive corepresentable reductions compute precisely the source of (B.MX4).
  • For \(v=1\), choose \(s:K e_UI\to C_0\) with K-injective target. Its map from the source is \(A_D((Ps)\epsilon_{e_UI})\), a quasi-isomorphism by (B.GC3) and exactness of \(A_D\).
  • For \(v=2\), also choose \(t:A_CC_0\to D_0\). The map is the left side of (B.GC13). Its two proper comparisons have exactly the K-injective inputs required there.
  • For \(v=4\), use the open-base-change isomorphism \(\theta_iH\); the subsequent \(A_Y,L'\) operations are exact.
  • For \(v=5\), choose \(u:A_U e_UI\to B'\) with K-injective target. The comparison is \(L'((H'u)\beta_{h,e_UI})\theta_{i,H e_UI}\). Equation (B.BC3), followed by exact \(L'\), proves it is a quasi-isomorphism.
  • For \(v=3\), additionally choose \(v':K'B'\to D'\!_0\) with K-injective target. The comparison is \((P'v')\epsilon'_{B'}L'((H'u)\beta_{h,e_UI})\theta_{i,H e_UI}\), the standard lower route in the paragraph following (B.GC13). That proof establishes its quasi-isomorphism, retaining both replacements.

In each reduction, a kernel column is replaced through an actual homotopy equivalence to its corepresentable. Tensoring preserves that homotopy. The remaining map is precomposition into the K-injective final endpoint. Thus no flatness of unresolved sheaves or exactness of a proper image is assumed. The resulting objectwise quasi-isomorphisms are quasi-isomorphisms of the whole bimodules because the maps themselves are already natural.

The edge witnesses belong to this common comparison. For an edge \(u\to v\), choose \[ \lambda_{uv}:W_v\longrightarrow W_u,\qquad a_u\lambda_{uv}-a_v=d\omega_{uv}. \tag{B.MX5} \] Whole h-projectivity and (B.ND7) give both entries. Each \(\lambda_{uv}\) is a whole homotopy equivalence. They can represent the elementary maps of (B.KC5), (B.KC7), and (B.MX2), with the other factors retained. Indeed the augmented elementary formula is exactly precomposition with its labelled sheaf map in (B.MX3). Whiskering its original witness gives (B.MX5); the equality of raw composites supplies no extra term. For a witness in a right tensor factor the action is \((1\otimes\omega)(x\otimes y)=(-1)^{|x|}x\otimes\omega(y)\). This is the ordinary graded tensor rule, so the assertion concerns homogeneous natural maps, not just degree-zero elements. If a different whole lift was already chosen, apply the same Hom quasi-isomorphism to their difference; retain the resulting comparison homotopy rather than replacing the previous lift without a witness.

Here is the kernel diagram. Its arrows run opposite to those on the geometric operations: \[ \begin{array}{ccccc} W_0&\xleftarrow{\lambda_{01}}&W_1&\xleftarrow{\lambda_{12}}&W_2\\ {\scriptstyle\lambda_{04}}\uparrow&&&& \uparrow{\scriptstyle\lambda_{23}}\\ W_4&\xleftarrow{\lambda_{45}}&W_5&\xleftarrow{\lambda_{53}}&W_3 . \end{array} \qquad a_v:W_v\longrightarrow M_\square . \tag{B.MX6} \] The common target identifies which maps this diagram compares. Replacing \(a_3\) by an arbitrary isomorphism class would lose that information.

The whole two-route boundary, including its witness. Define \[ \begin{aligned} T&=\lambda_{01}\lambda_{12}\lambda_{23}, & B&=\lambda_{04}\lambda_{45}\lambda_{53},\\ \Omega_T&=\omega_{01}\lambda_{12}\lambda_{23} +\omega_{12}\lambda_{23}+\omega_{23},\\ \Omega_B&=\omega_{04}\lambda_{45}\lambda_{53} +\omega_{45}\lambda_{53}+\omega_{53},\\ d(\Omega_T-\Omega_B)&=a_0(T-B). \end{aligned} \tag{B.MX7} \] The two telescoping sums follow directly from (B.MX5). All \(\lambda\)'s are closed of degree zero; no Koszul sign is omitted in these sums.

The necessary filler is stronger than \(T=B\) on cohomology: \[ dH=T-B,\qquad a_0H-(\Omega_T-\Omega_B)=dK,\qquad |H|=-1,\quad |K|=-2 . \tag{B.MX8} \] To prove both equations simultaneously, use the actual resolution category of the common target. Its objects are pairs \((W,a:W\to M_\square)\), with \(W\) whole h-projective and \(a\) a quasi-isomorphism. A degree-\(n\) map is a triple \((b,f,h)\), with \(b:{M_\square}\to M_\square\), \(f:W\to W'\) of degree \(n\) and \(h:W\to M_\square\) of degree \(n-1\).
