Its differential and composition are \[ \begin{aligned} D(b,f,h)&=(db,df,a'f-ba-dh),\\ (c,g,k)(b,f,h)&=(cb,gf,kf+(-1)^{|c|}ch). \end{aligned} \tag{B.MX9} \] These are the graph formulas (B.DA7). The identities \(D^2=0\), associativity and the signed Leibniz rule follow by expansion, using \(da=da'=0\). Projection onto \(b\) is surjective in each graded degree. Its Hom kernel is the shifted cone of \(\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')\xrightarrow{a'\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}(W,M_\square)\); it is acyclic because \(W\) is whole h-projective.

The edges in (B.MX5) are the closed triples \((1,\lambda_{uv},\omega_{uv})\). Their composite difference is the kernel cycle \((0,T-B,\Omega_T-\Omega_B)\). Acyclicity supplies its primitive \((0,H,K)\), which is exactly (B.MX8). In particular the chosen six edge witnesses are retained, not replaced by unrelated pointwise choices. A map \(H\) satisfying only the first equation would not yet compare those witnesses.

The relative boundary is specified before it is lifted. Start with the free path category on the six reversed edges. Adjoin a degree-minus-one arrow \(c:3\to0\) with \[ dc=e_{01}e_{12}e_{23}-e_{04}e_{45}e_{53}, \qquad d^2c=0 . \tag{B.MX10} \] The target functor sends every vertex to \(M_\square\), every edge to \(1\), and \(c\) to \(0\); hence it respects this differential. The already chosen edge triples form its relative boundary lift. Equation (B.ND9), applied to (B.MX9), supplies the lift of \(c\); its two non-base components are \(H,K\). This is an application to a checked free presentation, not to a quotient with an unverified commutativity relation.

For comparison of different composites of these lifts, the next standard free boundary is \[ \begin{aligned} \Xi_{c,b,a} &=L(c)H_{b,a}-H_{cb,a}+H_{c,ba}-H_{c,b}L(a),\\ d\Xi_{c,b,a}&=0 . \end{aligned} \tag{B.MX11} \] Here \(dH_{b,a}=L(b)L(a)-L(ba)\), and the symbols denote closed degree-zero edges of the specified target diagram. Expanding the four differentials cancels each ordered triple product. When these are resolution-graph lifts of the same target composition, their full graph obstruction has zero base component and is a cycle in the same acyclic kernel. It therefore has a degree-minus-two primitive, including the next witness component. Longer boundaries are supplied by the already specified free dg index and its differential, not guessed from a list of pairwise homotopies. This explains exactly the relative hypothesis needed when inserting this cube into a larger array.

Retain the original graphs, bars and nested coefficient. Use the two replacement strings in (B.GC13), not a new claim that \(A_U e_UI\) is K-injective. Their folds compare the objects \(z=t(A_Cs)\theta_k^{-1}\) and \(z=v'(K'u)\). For each homogeneous selected-edge word, (B.GC13) proves equality after the specified outer proper comparisons. Its first coefficients retain the endpoint maps, and its higher endpoint maps vanish while the graph homotopies remain present.

Pass to the strict \(UQ\) roofs already constructed in (B.SF7). The two-sided bar of a strict functor applies that functor to every object and every arrow in each bar tensor. It preserves the internal differential, multiplication faces and identity insertions because those are precisely the strict dg-functor identities. It also preserves ordered composition of strict functors. The quasi-equivalence comparisons are the ones proved in (B.KC12)–(B.KC14), with whole replacements made before tensoring. These statements therefore give maps on the actual bar kernels, not merely an identification of their representing objects.

For the nested right-resolution face, this strict roof must still contain \[ K_2(S,T)=(0,0,\beta^*k_S h_T), \qquad \text{ordinary multiplicativity witness} =(-1)^{|S|+1}K_2(S,T). \tag{B.MX12} \] This is (B.IA12), in its suspended convention. The strictification evaluates its free words using both \(K_1\) and \(K_2\); it does not replace \(K\) by \(K_1\). The graph-to-bar transfer uses (B.KC10)'s length-one sign and (B.KC11)'s opposite-Hom sign. The endpoint functors kill the higher graph vertices, so the supplied higher comparison faces project to the prescribed endpoint diagram. Their differential identities are (B.RS8), (B.GC13), and (B.IA12), already checked on homogeneous words. They can consequently be retained as fixed faces in the relative lift (B.ND9). An arbitrary extra face, without those identities, is not covered by this assertion.

Right kernels and the resolved mate. Dualize through the canonical evaluation roofs (B.RK2)–(B.RK4), retaining the actual comparison with \(H_f\) from (B.KC12)–(B.KC15). If a family of inverses is needed on a parameter diagram, first resolve the entire diagram over its free index and endpoint product category, as in (B.ND5)–(B.ND8). A quasi-isomorphism between those whole h-projectives has a whole natural inverse and both witnesses. Objectwise inverse choices alone do not justify this step.

On these models, set \(L_0=T_{H_f}\), \(L_1=T_{H_{f'}}\), \(S=T_{P_u}\), \(V=T_{P_g}\). For the resulting resolved left inverse \(\vartheta\), the right mate is obtained from \[ \begin{aligned} r_0:P_0&\longrightarrow U_0N,\qquad e_0=\varepsilon^0_N L_0r_0,\\ \zeta_N&=\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}(Ve_0\,\vartheta_{P_0}),\\ r_1c_N-\zeta_N&=db_N,\qquad e_1L_1c_N-Ve_0\,\vartheta_{P_0} =d(\varepsilon^1_{VN}L_1b_N). \end{aligned} \tag{B.MX13} \] The full Hom-complex adjunction carries the retained cube homotopy and its boundary to the mate diagram. For vertical and horizontal pasting use the actual witnesses (B.BM17) and (B.BM18); horizontal pasting retains its intermediate replacements and the coefficient (B.MX12). All arguments of \(\vartheta\) are h-projective. No value at an unresolved \(U_0N\), and no invertibility of the right mate, is asserted.

This supplies the proper–open kernel edge, a common six-vertex model for the actual mixed cube, and its relative resolved-mate boundary. To finish the enhanced operation system one must still assemble the entire changing-compactification and finite composition arrays with their shared unit, counit and triangle faces and prove their common-refinement compatibility in these kernel models. Geometric nearby attaching maps and multiplicative descent, whole coefficient-system completion/rationalization and strict-heart higher effacement are not established by this construction. \(\square\)

Transport the nested adjunction across refinements

Proposition B.1ag (both nested replacements must travel). Consider a strict normalized diagram of the intermediate squares (B.IA1). Its refinement functors on \(\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C\) are quasi-equivalences; the horizontal functors \(\beta,F,G\) need not be. There is a transport-labelled nested resolution graph over the entire refinement category. Its projection is surjective on graded Hom groups and a quasi-isomorphism on each Hom complex. Its fold to the common-span right replacement retains the nonzero second coefficient of (B.IA12). The actual sequential right maps and counits have the comparison witnesses below. A unit comparison has a second witness, and that second witness supplies the left-triangle comparison rather than leaving an unexplained closed defect. All constructions use possibly unbounded modules over an arbitrary commutative coefficient ring.

Here is the precise input. For \(g:i\to j\), write \(a_g,b_g,c_g\) for the three refinement functors. The categories \(\mathcal D,\mathcal E\) stay fixed, and \[ \begin{gathered} b_g\alpha_i=\alpha_j a_g,\qquad c_g\beta_i=\beta_j a_g,\qquad p_jc_g=p_i,\\ F_jb_g=F_i,\qquad G_jc_g=G_i,\qquad T_i=G_i\beta_i=T_j a_g . \end{gathered} \tag{B.NR1} \] Identity and composite refinement functors agree literally. For the geometric squares, these are the normalized forms of the specified proper-image comparisons in (B.SN1)–(B.SN13); evaluation back to the original squares retains their named isomorphisms. This input is not an assertion that arbitrary independently chosen models already form such a strict diagram.

Use the actual canonical induction isomorphisms \[ \begin{aligned} A_g&:\alpha_{j!}a_{g!}\longrightarrow b_{g!}\alpha_{i!},& B_g&:\beta_{j!}a_{g!}\longrightarrow c_{g!}\beta_{i!},\\ C_g&:T_{j!}a_{g!}\longrightarrow T_{i!},& P_g&:p_{j!}c_{g!}\longrightarrow p_{i!}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.NR2} \] They are balanced-tensor maps, not chosen inverses of quasi-isomorphisms. Their associativity is the equality on tensor generators already checked in (B.CR6)–(B.CR9).

A labelled graph, not conjugation by a homotopy equivalence. An object over \(i,Y\) is the actual nested pair \[ r_i:R_i\longrightarrow G_i^*Y,\qquad t_i:Z_i\longrightarrow\beta_i^*R_i,\qquad q_i=\beta_i^*r_i\,t_i:Z_i\longrightarrow T_i^*Y, \tag{B.NR3} \] where \(R_i,Z_i\) are h-projective and \(r_i,t_i\) are quasi-isomorphisms. A degree-\(n\) morphism \(U\), labelled by \(g:i\to j\), has vertex maps \(f:Y\to Y'\), \(\rho:R_i\to c_g^*R_j\), \(z:Z_i\to a_g^*Z_j\), and witnesses \(k:R_i\to G_i^*Y'\), \(h:Z_i\to\beta_i^*c_g^*R_j\) of degree \(n-1\). The two edge components of its differential are \[ \begin{aligned} (DU)_k&=c_g^*r_j\,\rho-G_i^*f\,r_i-dk,\\ (DU)_h&=a_g^*t_j\,z-\beta_i^*\rho\,t_i-dh . \end{aligned} \tag{B.NR4} \] The vertex components use the ordinary Hom differential. For \(V\) of degree \(m\), labelled \(u:j\to l\), after \(U\), composition is labelled \(ug\) and is \[ \begin{aligned} f_{VU}&=f_Vf_U,\\ \rho_{VU}&=c_g^*\rho_V\,\rho_U,\\ z_{VU}&=a_g^*z_V\,z_U,\\ k_{VU}&=c_g^*k_V\,\rho_U+(-1)^mG_i^*f_V\,k_U,\\ h_{VU}&=a_g^*h_V\,z_U+(-1)^m\beta_i^*c_g^*\rho_V\,h_U . \end{aligned} \tag{B.NR5} \] Restriction is a strict dg functor and (B.NR1) identifies the middle modules, so these are well typed. Expanding \(D^2\) cancels the two copies of each edge defect. In the Leibniz identity the differential of a witness changes its degree by one, giving precisely the displayed \((-1)^m\). For a triple composite, both expansions have the three terms with coefficients \(1,(-1)^{|W|},(-1)^{|W|+|V|}\). This proves associativity. Identities have identity vertex maps, identity label and zero witnesses. Taking direct sums over labels gives a dg category.

Let \(\mathcal H\) have objects \((i,Y)\) and \(\mathcal H((i,Y),(j,Y'))=\bigoplus_{g:i\to j}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal E}(Y,Y')\), with composition using the composite label. Projection sends \(U\) to \((g,f)\). On one label, forget \(z,h\) first. Its kernel is the shifted cone of the first map below; the remaining projection has kernel the shifted cone of the second: \[ \begin{aligned} \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_i}(Z_i,a_g^*Z_j) &\xrightarrow{\ a_g^*t_j\circ-\ } \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A_i}(Z_i,\beta_i^*c_g^*R_j),\\ \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_i}(R_i,c_g^*R_j) &\xrightarrow{\ c_g^*r_j\circ-\ } \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C_i}(R_i,G_i^*Y'). \end{aligned} \tag{B.NR6} \] Both are quasi-isomorphisms: their sources of Hom are h-projective, and restrictions preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Both projections are surjective as graded maps, by choosing the forgotten components zero; this does not claim that this zero section is a chain map. Thus each kernel, and then the total kernel, is acyclic. Direct sums over labels preserve exactness. Replacements exist over every \((i,Y)\). This proves the asserted Hom property without claiming that \(a_g^*Z_j\) or \(\beta_i^*R_i\) is h-projective.

For a closed degree-zero \(U\) with \(f\) a quasi-isomorphism, (B.NR4) and two-out-of-three show successively that \(\rho\) and \(z\) are quasi-isomorphisms. Their induction adjoints \(\bar\rho=\varepsilon^{c_g}c_{g!}\rho\) and \(\bar z=\varepsilon^{a_g}a_{g!}z\) are homotopy equivalences between h-projectives: apply (B.SM2) to each actual restriction-side quasi-isomorphism. No step assumes that induction preserves an arbitrary quasi-isomorphism. The maps \(\rho,z,\bar\rho,\bar z\) are not treated as invertible chain maps for conjugation.

The second coefficient survives a change of fibre. The common graph has objects \(q_i\) and labelled maps \((f,z,H)\), with the analogue of (B.NR4). In the suspended convention of (B.RS7), the fold is \[ \begin{aligned} K_1(U)&=(f_U,z_U,H_U),\\ H_U&=\beta_i^*c_g^*r_j\,h_U+\beta_i^*k_U\,t_i,\\ K_2(V,U)&=(0,0,\beta_i^*c_g^*k_V\,h_U),\qquad K_s=0\quad(s>2). \end{aligned} \tag{B.NR7} \] Every expression is pulled to the source fibre \(i\). The selected-edge expansion in (B.RS8) applies there verbatim: the two available edges give the two terms of \(K_1\), selecting both gives \(K_2\), and there is no selection of three edges. Restriction preserves products and differentials, so every split/merge cancellation has the same composite label. This proves all arities, including the three-input identity. The ordinary multiplicativity homotopy is \((-1)^{|V|+1}K_2(V,U)\), not an unsigned replacement. Higher coefficients vanish on identity inputs.

The common graph has the same Hom projection property, now using \(a_g^*q_j\) and h-projective \(Z_i\). Hence \(K_1\) is a quasi-isomorphism on each labelled Hom complex. An object of the common graph is isomorphic in \(H^0\), over its identity label, to a folded nested replacement: lift the identity on \(Y\) in both directions and use injectivity on \(H^0\) to verify their composites. Applying (B.SF7) to this entire labelled graph gives a strict roof over \(\mathcal H\). This is one use of \(UQ\) on a specified higher functor; it is not an unsupported assertion that \(Q\) is functorial on arbitrary higher maps.

The actual sequential right comparison. Put \(W_i=\alpha_{i!}Z_i\) and \(s_i=d_{i,R_i}\alpha_{i!}t_i\), as in (B.IA3). Let \(U\) be closed of degree zero, with arbitrary closed degree-zero \(f:Y\to Y'\). Define \[ \begin{aligned} w_g&=\alpha_{j!}\bar z\,A_g^{-1}:b_{g!}W_i\longrightarrow W_j,\\ v_i&=\varepsilon^{\beta_i}_{R_i}\beta_{i!}t_i,\qquad R_g=p_{j!}\bar\rho\,P_g^{-1}:p_{i!}R_i\longrightarrow p_{j!}R_j . \end{aligned} \tag{B.NR8} \] Write \(\kappa_g:b_{g!}F_i^*\to F_j^*\) for the actual mate of \(F_jb_g=F_i\); it need not be invertible. Adjoint the witness \(h_U\) along \(a_g\), writing \(h_U^\sharp=\varepsilon^{a_g}_{\beta_j^*R_j}a_{g!}h_U\). Then \[ s_jw_g-F_j^*R_g\,\kappa_g\,b_{g!}s_i =d\!\left(d_{j,R_j}\alpha_{j!}h_U^\sharp\,A_g^{-1}\right). \tag{B.NR9} \] Here is a check of the less immediate term. The \(\beta_j\)-adjoint of \(\operatorname{Adj}_{a_g}(\beta_i^*\rho\,t_i)\) is \(\bar\rho\,c_{g!}v_i\,B_g\). Apply \(p_{j!}\), then the balanced isomorphism \(p_{j!}\beta_{j!}\cong F_{j!}\alpha_{j!}\). The result is the \(F_j\)-adjoint of \(F_j^*R_g\,\kappa_g\,b_{g!}s_i\,A_g\), because the four balanced maps commute on a tensor generator. This is exactly the second identity of (B.SM7) in the two fibres. Adjointing the second line of (B.NR4) and using that equality proves (B.NR9). Thus both actual intermediate maps, and not merely their derived isomorphism classes, are retained.

Counits with their defect. Define \(e_i=\varepsilon^{T_i}_Y T_{i!}q_i\), the same sequential/common counit as (B.IA8). Let \[ \Theta_U= \varepsilon^{T_j}_{Y'}T_{j!} \bigl(\varepsilon^{a_g}_{T_j^*Y'}a_{g!}H_U\bigr). \quad e_jT_{j!}\bar z-f e_i C_g=d\Theta_U . \tag{B.NR10} \] Its domain is \(T_{j!}a_{g!}Z_i\), its codomain is \(Y'\), and its degree is \(-1\). Indeed the folded closed-map equation is \(a_g^*q_j\,z-T_i^*f\,q_i=dH_U\). Take its \(a_g\)-adjoint, then its \(T_j\)-adjoint. The composed-counit identity identifies the second term with \(f e_i C_g\). This also proves \(\Theta_U C_{g,Z_i}^{-1}=\operatorname{Adj}_{T_i}(H_U)\). No quasi-isomorphism claim about a counit is needed.

One unit comparison, including its second witness. Let \(Q_i,Q_j\) be h-projective and let \(A:a_{g!}Q_i\to Q_j\) be a closed homotopy equivalence. Write \[ A^\flat=a_g^*A\,\eta^{a_g}_{Q_i},\qquad L_i=T_{i!}Q_i,\quad L_j=T_{j!}Q_j,\quad f=T_{j!}A\,C_{g,Q_i}^{-1}:L_i\longrightarrow L_j . \tag{B.NR11} \] Choose the nested replacements over \(L_i,L_j\) and the actual unit lifts \(u_i:Q_i\to Z_i(L_i)\), \(u_j:Q_j\to Z_j(L_j)\), with \(q_i u_i-\eta^{T_i}_{Q_i}=d\ell_i\) and \(q_j u_j-\eta^{T_j}_{Q_j}=d\ell_j\), as in (B.IA6)–(B.IA7). Lift the closed \((g,f)\) through the nested graph, retaining its \(z,H_U\). The unit defect and its image witness are \[ \begin{aligned} D_U&=a_g^*u_j\,A^\flat-z u_i,\\ I_U&=a_g^*\ell_j\,A^\flat-T_i^*f\,\ell_i-H_Uu_i,\\ dD_U&=0,\qquad dI_U=a_g^*q_j\,D_U . \end{aligned} \tag{B.NR12} \] The last equality follows by expansion. The remaining degree-zero terms cancel by the actual composed-unit identity \(a_g^*\eta^{T_j}_{Q_j}A^\flat=T_i^*f\,\eta^{T_i}_{Q_i}\). Thus the pair \((D_U,I_U)\) is a closed element of the shifted cone of \(\operatorname{Hom}(Q_i,a_g^*q_j)\), not just an unexplained closed map. That cone is acyclic. It supplies \(J_U\) of degree \(-1\) and \(K_U\) of degree \(-2\) with \[ dJ_U=D_U,\qquad a_g^*q_j\,J_U-I_U=dK_U . \tag{B.NR13} \] Both equations matter. Finding only \(J_U\) does not prove the second with \(K_U=0\). One can see the two-stage correction explicitly: first choose \(J_U\) by injectivity on \(H^0\); the difference \(a_g^*q_jJ_U-I_U\) is closed in degree \(-1\). Surjectivity on \(H^{-1}\) allows subtraction of a closed map from \(J_U\) so that this difference is a boundary, giving \(K_U\).

The left-triangle comparison now has a boundary. Use the actual left-triangle witness \(\lambda_i=\operatorname{Adj}_{T_i}(\ell_i)\), so \(d\lambda_i=e_iT_{i!}u_i-1_{L_i}\). This is the witness of (B.IA9): adjointing the two terms of (B.IA7) gives \(\varepsilon^G G_!(r\,\varepsilon^\beta\beta_!h+k)\) there. Put \(\bar J_U=\operatorname{Adj}_{a_g}(J_U)\). The comparison built from the unit and counit homotopies, and its second filler, are \[ \begin{aligned} \Xi_U&=e_jT_{j!}\bar J_U\,C_{g,Q_i}^{-1} +\Theta_U T_{j!}a_{g!}u_i\,C_{g,Q_i}^{-1},\\ \Gamma_U&=\operatorname{Adj}_{T_i}(K_U),\\ \Xi_U-\lambda_j f+f\lambda_i&=d\Gamma_U . \end{aligned} \tag{B.NR14} \] For a direct verification, adjunction identifies the first line with \(\operatorname{Adj}_{T_i}(a_g^*q_jJ_U+H_Uu_i)\). Naturality and (B.NR11) identify \(\lambda_j f-f\lambda_i\) with \(\operatorname{Adj}_{T_i}(a_g^*\ell_j A^\flat-T_i^*f\ell_i)\). Subtract and apply (B.NR13). Adjunction is an isomorphism of complexes, so its differential introduces no additional sign. The diagram below shows the two unit routes whose defect is \(d\bar J_U\): \[ \begin{array}{ccc} a_{g!}Q_i&\xrightarrow{\ a_{g!}u_i\ }&a_{g!}Z_i(L_i)\\ {\scriptstyle A}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle\bar z}\\ Q_j&\xrightarrow{\ u_j\ }&Z_j(L_j). \end{array} \qquad u_jA-\bar z\,a_{g!}u_i=d\bar J_U . \tag{B.NR15} \] The arrows \(u_i,u_j\) are units, not asserted equivalences. The degree-minus-two filler in (B.NR14) is what makes the displayed triangle witnesses compatible; the fact that their difference is closed alone would not suffice.

What is joined, and what still has to be joined. The labelled graph and fold are defined over the whole specified refinement category, not separately on each edge. A supplied parameter diagram is first resolved over its whole product/transport category as in (B.TD4) and (B.ND6); this supplies the h-projective Hom sources used above without claiming arbitrary restriction preserves them. A free dg presentation of that supplied diagram can then be lifted through the Hom-surjective acyclic-kernel projection, relative to already checked free faces, using (B.ND9). The finite equations above give the actual targets and boundaries of the unit, counit and left-triangle comparisons. That lifting statement does not supply an absent target presentation or authorize prescribing arbitrary old homotopies with incompatible boundaries.

The original bar comparisons, the nonzero nested \(K_2\), and the mixed-cube pair \((H,K)\) from (B.MX8) are part of the joint presentation. The shared right-triangle and geometric composition, refinement and mixed-cube faces require compatible maps in the complete graph-bar arrays. The fixed-model construction here does not establish that general assembly, geometric nearby-cycle multiplicative descent, whole coefficient-system transport or strict-heart effacement. \(\square\)

Join the two triangles over the whole refinement family

Proposition B.1ah (choose the two stages together). In the strict normalized refinement system (B.NR1), the nested replacements, their actual units and counits, and both triangle witnesses can be chosen as maps of the whole refinement/input diagram. The right triangle has a second witness, and that witness compares the two triangle homotopies after the actual counit. The paired target (B.JT5) then varies by genuine target-diagram maps, including when the input module varies. The comparison uses (B.TD4), (B.IA6)–(B.IA13) and (B.NR13). Gluing of the entire geometric mixed-cube/master-bar presentation is an additional assertion. All modules may be unbounded, over an arbitrary commutative coefficient ring.

Which category contains a natural homotopy? Let \(I\) be the ordinary refinement category, let \(\mathcal T_A,\mathcal T_C\) be its transport categories for \(a_g,c_g\), and let \(\mathcal T_E\) be the constant-\(\mathcal E\) transport category. The equalities in (B.NR1) give strict dg functors \[ \widehat\beta:\mathcal T_A\longrightarrow\mathcal T_C,\qquad \widehat G:\mathcal T_C\longrightarrow\mathcal T_E,\qquad \widehat T=\widehat G\widehat\beta . \tag{B.JF1} \] For example \(\widehat\beta(i,A)=(i,\beta_iA)\) and \(\widehat\beta(g,v)=(g,\beta_jv)\); its target is correct because \(c_g\beta_i=\beta_j a_g\). The other formulas are the same, using \(G_jc_g=G_i\). Here \(T_i=G_i\beta_i\). A module \(Y\) over \(\mathcal T_E\) is precisely a strict input family \(Y_i\), with closed maps \(n_g:Y_i\to Y_j\). These input maps need not be quasi-isomorphisms.

Restriction along each functor in (B.JF1) is fibrewise restriction. Its left adjoint is canonically fibrewise induction with the actual balanced-tensor comparison on each structure map. This last assertion needs a check when the fibre category varies. For any one of these functors \(\widehat F\), induction of a transport representable at \((i,X)\), evaluated at \(j\), is \[ \begin{aligned} \bigl(\widehat F_!\mathcal T_A(-,(i,X))\bigr)_j &=\bigoplus_{g:i\to j}\mathcal C_j(-,c_gF_iX),\\ F_{j!}\bigl(\mathcal T_A(-,(i,X))_j\bigr) &=\bigoplus_{g:i\to j}\mathcal C_j(-,F_j a_gX). \end{aligned} \tag{B.JF2} \] The displayed instance has \(F_i:\mathcal A_i\to\mathcal C_i\) with \(F_ja_g=c_gF_i\); for the other functors replace the letters accordingly. The two sums are identified term by term by that equality. The identification is natural in every homogeneous transport morphism, since both composites act by the same \(F_j(v)\) and labelled transport composition. An arbitrary module is the coequalizer of sums of shifts of representables tensored with its value complexes, using the module action and composition as the two maps. Both induction constructions preserve those sums, tensors and coequalizers. The displayed identification therefore descends to every module. Equivalently, on balanced tensors it moves the index arrow onto the source module, as in (B.ND8). In particular it identifies the units, counits and Hom-complex adjunctions, not just the isomorphism classes of the values.

Induction preserves whole-diagram h-projectivity: its Hom into an acyclic module is the Hom of the h-projective source into its restriction, which is still objectwise acyclic. Evaluation preserves h-projectivity here by (B.TD4). No converse from pointwise h-projectivity is used.

First build the right-input family, then its left image. Choose whole semifree replacements \[ R\xrightarrow{r}\widehat G^*Y,\qquad Z\xrightarrow{t}\widehat\beta^*R,\qquad q=\widehat\beta^*r\,t:Z\longrightarrow\widehat T^*Y . \tag{B.JF3} \] The first replacement is over \(\mathcal T_C\), the second over \(\mathcal T_A\). Both are quasi-isomorphisms, and \(q\) is one as well. Their structure maps give the nested refinement maps of (B.NR3) with zero edge defects along this specified strict diagram. This choice does not set the nonzero \(K_2\) of the full nested resolution graph to zero.

Put \(L=\widehat T_!Z\), and use (B.JF2) to write its components as \(L_i=T_{i!}Z_i\). If \(z_g:Z_i\to a_g^*Z_j\) is the structure map and \(\bar z_g\) its induction adjoint, then its structure maps and the actual counit are \[ \begin{aligned} \tau_g&=T_{j!}\bar z_g\,C_{g,Z_i}^{-1}:L_i\longrightarrow L_j,\\ e_i&=\epsilon^{T_i}_{Y_i}\,T_{i!}q_i:L_i\longrightarrow Y_i,\\ \tau_{hg}&=\tau_h\tau_g,\qquad e_j\tau_g=n_ge_i . \end{aligned} \tag{B.JF4} \] Here \(C_g:T_{j!}a_{g!}\to T_{i!}\) is exactly (B.NR2)'s tensor isomorphism. The composition equality follows by the structure-map law of \(Z\) and associativity on balanced tensors. The counit equality is the adjoint of \(a_g^*q_j\,z_g=T_i^*n_g\,q_i\), using the composed ordinary unit. Thus \(e:L\to Y\) is already a map of entire diagrams before the second resolution is chosen.

Now resolve \(\widehat G^*L\), and then its restriction: \[ R^L\xrightarrow{r^L}\widehat G^*L,\qquad Z^L\xrightarrow{t^L}\widehat\beta^*R^L,\qquad q^L=\widehat\beta^*r^L\,t^L:Z^L\longrightarrow\widehat T^*L . \tag{B.JF5} \] There is no circular choice: \(L\) and \(\tau\) were constructed from the first stage, and (B.JF5) resolves that already specified diagram. All four replacements in (B.JF3) and (B.JF5) are h-projective in their whole transport categories; their restricted targets need not be h-projective.

Use the same nested unit in both triangles. Set \(P=\widehat\beta_!Z\); then \(L=\widehat G_!P\) through the canonical composition isomorphism. Whole-diagram Hom lifting first gives closed \(v:P\to R^L\), and then closed \(u:Z\to Z^L\), with degree-minus-one witnesses \(k,h\): \[ \begin{aligned} r^Lv-\eta^{\widehat G}_P&=dk,\\ t^Lu-\widehat\beta^*v\,\eta^{\widehat\beta}_Z&=dh,\\ \ell&=\widehat\beta^*r^L\,h+ \widehat\beta^*k\,\eta^{\widehat\beta}_Z,\\ q^Lu-\eta^{\widehat T}_Z&=d\ell . \end{aligned} \tag{B.JF6} \] The first lift uses h-projectivity of \(P\), proved by induction, and the second uses h-projectivity of \(Z\). Expanding the differential of the third line and substituting the first two lines gives the fourth, by the composed-unit identity. These are the actual nested unit formulas of (B.IA6)–(B.IA7), now in the natural Hom complexes.

The counit at the second stage and its left-triangle witness are \[ e^L=\epsilon^{\widehat T}_L\,\widehat T_!q^L,\qquad \lambda=\operatorname{Adj}_{\widehat T}(\ell),\qquad d\lambda=e^L\widehat T_!u-1_L . \tag{B.JF7} \] The last equality uses the ordinary left triangle before passing to replacements. For an arbitrary whole h-projective left-input family \(Q\), the same construction with \(Q\) in place of \(Z\) and \(L_Q=\widehat T_!Q\) supplies its left unit and triangle. When \(Q=Z\), reuse exactly (B.JF5)–(B.JF7), not a separately chosen second copy. If a supplied \(Q\) is only pointwise h-projective, first replace the whole diagram and retain the resulting comparison; pointwise h-projectivity alone does not justify this lift.

Lift the counit through both nested replacements. Apply the same whole-diagram Hom argument to \(e:L\to Y\). It gives closed \(\rho:R^L\to R\), \(z:Z^L\to Z\), and witnesses \(k_e,h_e\), all natural, satisfying \[ \begin{aligned} r\rho-\widehat G^*e\,r^L&=dk_e,\\ tz-\widehat\beta^*\rho\,t^L&=dh_e,\\ H&=\widehat\beta^*r\,h_e+\widehat\beta^*k_e\,t^L,\\ qz-\widehat T^*e\,q^L&=dH . \end{aligned} \tag{B.JF8} \] The sources for these two lifts are respectively \(R^L\) and \(Z^L\); neither proof assumes that restriction preserves h-projectivity. The third line is precisely the first folding coefficient of (B.IA12), including both terms.

The full right-triangle boundary. In the natural Hom complexes put \[ D=zu-1_Z,\qquad I=Hu+\widehat T^*e\,\ell,\qquad dD=0,\qquad qD=dI . \tag{B.JF9} \] Indeed, insert (B.JF6) and (B.JF8) in \(qzu-q\); the remaining term is \(\widehat T^*e\,\eta^{\widehat T}_Z-q=0\), the ordinary adjunction identity for the actual adjoint \(e=\operatorname{Adj}_{\widehat T}(q)\). Postcomposition by \(q\) induces a quasi-isomorphism \(\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_A}(Z,Z)\to \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T_A}(Z,\widehat T^*Y)\). Its shifted cone has differential \((x,y)\mapsto(dx,qx-dy)\). It is acyclic because \(Z\) is h-projective over \(\mathcal T_A\), not merely at each fibre. A primitive of its closed element \((D,I)\) gives both witnesses \[ dJ=D,\qquad qJ-I=dK,\qquad |J|=-1,\quad |K|=-2 . \tag{B.JF10} \] One can see the second step directly. First choose \(J_0\) with \(dJ_0=D\), using injectivity on \(H^0\). The difference \(qJ_0-I\) is closed of degree minus one. Surjectivity on \(H^{-1}\) allows a closed correction to \(J_0\) whose image removes that cohomology class. The remaining difference is \(dK\). A choice of \(J_0\) alone would not justify setting \(K=0\).

This second witness joins the two triangle homotopies along their common counit. Set \(\theta=\operatorname{Adj}_{\widehat T}(H)\) and \(\Gamma=\operatorname{Adj}_{\widehat T}(K)\). Applying the Hom-complex adjunction gives \[ \begin{aligned} d\theta&=e\,\widehat T_!z-e\,e^L,\\ e\,\widehat T_!J-\theta\,\widehat T_!u-e\lambda&=d\Gamma . \end{aligned} \tag{B.JF11} \] For the second line, the adjoints of \(qJ,Hu,\widehat T^*e\,\ell\) are respectively \(e\widehat T_!J,\theta\widehat T_!u,e\lambda\); the adjunction is a chain isomorphism, so no extra differential sign is introduced. Differentiating the left side cancels its two copies of \(e\widehat T_!(zu)\), of \(e e^L\widehat T_!u\), and of \(e\). This checks its boundary, while (B.JF10) supplies the actual primitive. The two triangle routes, rather than just their equal homotopy classes, are thus compared.

The actual varying paired target. At \(i\) use the five vertices \(Z_i,T_i^*L_i,T_i^*Y_i,L_i,Y_i\), and the seven arrows of (B.JT5), with \(q_i,e_i\). Let \(\kappa_g:a_{g!}T_i^*\to T_j^*\) be the actual mate for \(T_ja_g=T_i\). Write \(A_g=\bar z_g\), \(B_g=T_j^*\tau_g\,\kappa_{g,L_i}\), and \(C'_g=T_j^*n_g\,\kappa_{g,Y_i}\). The five vertex comparisons are \(A_g,B_g,C'_g,\tau_g,n_g\). They respect all seven edges as follows: \[ \begin{aligned} B_g\,a_{g!}\eta^{T_i}_{Z_i}&=\eta^{T_j}_{Z_j}A_g,\\ C'_g\,a_{g!}(T_i^*e_i)&=T_j^*e_j\,B_g,\\ C'_g\,a_{g!}q_i&=q_jA_g,\\ \tau_g C_{g,Z_i}&=T_{j!}A_g,\\ \tau_g\epsilon^{T_i}_{L_i}C_{g,T_i^*L_i} &=\epsilon^{T_j}_{L_j}T_{j!}B_g,\\ n_g\epsilon^{T_i}_{Y_i}C_{g,T_i^*Y_i} &=\epsilon^{T_j}_{Y_j}T_{j!}C'_g,\\ n_ge_i&=e_j\tau_g . \end{aligned} \tag{B.JF12} \] The first line is naturality of the unit and its composition identity; the second uses naturality of \(\kappa_g\) and (B.JF4); the third is the adjoint of the structure equality for \(q\). The fourth is the definition of \(\tau_g\). In the fifth and sixth lines, the counit-composition identity reduces the left side to the receiving counit followed by \(T_{j!}(T_j^*\tau_g\,\kappa_g)\) or \(T_{j!}(T_j^*n_g\,\kappa_g)\), exactly the displayed right side. The final line was proved in (B.JF4). The four path relations of (B.JT6) hold in every fibre by the ordinary adjunction identities, and these edge equalities preserve them. Composition of the five comparisons follows from the structure laws for \(Z,Y,L\) and associativity of the actual mates. Thus this is a map of the whole target presentation, not an inference from a square that commutes only up to homotopy. When \(n_g\) is a quasi-isomorphism, the equivalence conclusions of (B.RT3) follow by restriction and the quasi-equivalence unit. No equivalence is claimed for a general \(n_g\), for the unit, or for a noninvertible right mate.

The two routes in (B.JF11) are displayed here: \[ \begin{array}{ccccccc} L&\xrightarrow{\widehat T_!u}&\widehat T_!Z^L& \xrightarrow{\widehat T_!z}&L&\xrightarrow{e}&Y\\ L&\xrightarrow{\widehat T_!u}&\widehat T_!Z^L& \xrightarrow{e^L}&L&\xrightarrow{e}&Y . \end{array} \tag{B.JF13} \] The upper composite is shortened to \(e\) by \(e\widehat T_!J\). The witness \(\theta\widehat T_!u\) compares the upper composite with the lower one, and \(e\lambda\) shortens the lower composite to \(e\). The difference between these two homotopy routes is \(d\Gamma\), exactly (B.JF11). The rows are not asserted to be literally equal chain maps. Every object and arrow belongs to the same resolved family.

For an additional dg parameter category, pull back to its free index \(Q\mathcal J\) and perform this entire two-stage construction over \((Q\mathcal J)^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes\mathcal T_A\), and similarly for the other two transport categories. The path-cell filtration of (B.ND6), followed by (B.TD4), proves h-projectivity after evaluation; (B.ND4) gives the graded naturality signs. The induction identification (B.JF2) remains valid with those tensor signs, so every displayed Hom lift takes place in the whole parameter-and-refinement category. An arbitrary nonflat index is not silently substituted for the free one.

Remaining geometric join. The construction retains the original strict folding roofs, the nonzero nested second coefficient, and the mixed-cube pair \((H,K)\) in (B.MX8). It does not identify independently chosen old pointwise replacements or homotopies with the new natural choices. Compatible old whole-diagram faces can be compared and retained through the resolution graphs and the relative free lifting theorem (B.ND9), after their actual target maps and boundaries are supplied. The horizontal geometric base-change functors need not be quasi-equivalences; their joins still require the resolved mates of (B.MX13) and the original common mapping target. The full mixed-cube/composition array, geometric multiplicative descent, coefficient-system transport and strict-heart effacement are not established by this construction. \(\square\)

Join the unit comparison to the resolved cube

Proposition B.1ai (the unit interface, with its higher witness). In the common resolved model of (B.MX13), the unit comparison of (B.BM16) extends over a specified whole mixed-cube cell, retaining the already chosen mate and unit lifts. Its extension includes a degree-minus-three witness comparing the second unit witnesses. This supplies the unit interface of that cube, not the entire changing-geometric-model presentation.

Work over an arbitrary commutative coefficient ring, with possibly unbounded modules. Use the whole parameter/refinement categories of (B.JF1)–(B.JF3), and the free dg parameter extension after (B.JF13) when needed. In particular, h-projectivity below is whole h-projectivity. Let \(L_i\dashv U_i\), \(S,V\), and the resolved left comparison have the meanings of (B.BM1), (B.BM16), and (B.MX13). The induction functors preserve h-projectives. They need not be equivalences.

One set of actual unit targets. Fix a whole h-projective \(Q\), and put \(N=L_0Q\), \(X=L_1SQ\), and \(Y=VN\). From the existing whole-family construction choose \[ \begin{aligned} r_0:P_0&\longrightarrow U_0N,& r_X:A&\longrightarrow U_1X,\\ r_Y:B&\longrightarrow U_1Y,\\ r_0u_0-\eta^0_Q&=d\ell_0,& r_Xu_1-\eta^1_{SQ}&=d\ell_1,\\ e_0&=\varepsilon^0_NL_0r_0,& \lambda_0&=\operatorname{Adj}_{L_0}^{-1}(\ell_0),\\ \lambda_1&=\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}^{-1}(\ell_1). \end{aligned} \tag{B.UC1} \] The three \(r\)'s are quasi-isomorphisms with whole h-projective sources. The unit maps \(u_0,u_1\) are closed; the two \(\ell\)'s have degree \(-1\). Hence \(d\lambda_0=e_0L_0u_0-1_N\) and \(d\lambda_1=e_XL_1u_1-1_X\), where \(e_X=\varepsilon^1_XL_1r_X\). Use the very same nested stages and witnesses as (B.JF6)–(B.JF7) on an overlap. No unresolved restriction module is declared h-projective.

Transpose every degree, not just a closed edge. Let \(\Theta\) be the complex of whole dg-natural transformations from \(L_1S\) to \(VL_0\) on the specified resolved inputs. For homogeneous \(\vartheta\in\Theta^n\) define \[ \begin{aligned} \Psi(\vartheta)&=\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}(Ve_0\,\vartheta_{P_0}),\\ F(\vartheta)&=\Psi(\vartheta)Su_0,& G(\vartheta)&=U_1(\vartheta_Q)\eta^1_{SQ},\\ \mathcal A(\vartheta)&=\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}(V\lambda_0\,\vartheta_Q),\\ d\mathcal A(\vartheta)+\mathcal A(d\vartheta) &=F(\vartheta)-G(\vartheta). \end{aligned} \tag{B.UC2} \] Here \(\operatorname{Adj}\) is the actual Hom-complex isomorphism in all degrees. The map \(\Psi\) is a chain map. For the last line, the signed Leibniz rule gives \(d(V\lambda_0\,\vartheta_Q)=V(d\lambda_0)\vartheta_Q- V\lambda_0(d\vartheta)_Q\). Naturality on the closed map \(u_0\) identifies \(Ve_0\,\vartheta_{P_0}L_1Su_0\) with \(Ve_0\,VL_0u_0\,\vartheta_Q\). The remaining term transposes to \(G(\vartheta)\). Only the h-projective inputs \(Q,P_0\) are used; \(\vartheta_{U_0N}\) is not.

Keep both lifts in one graded complex. A degree-\(n\) element \(e\) of a complex \(\mathcal E\) is a tuple \[ \begin{aligned} e&=(\vartheta,c,b,z,h),\\ c &:SP_0\longrightarrow B,&z &:A\longrightarrow B,\\ b &:SP_0\longrightarrow U_1Y,&h &:A\longrightarrow U_1Y,\\ |c|=|z|&=n,&|b|=|h|&=n-1,\\ \partial e&=\bigl(d\vartheta,dc,\, r_Yc-\Psi(\vartheta)-db,\, dz,\,r_Yz-U_1(\vartheta_Q)r_X-dh\bigr). \end{aligned} \tag{B.UC3} \] The two graph maps are chain maps, so \(\partial^2=0\). For a closed degree-zero element, \((c,b)\) is exactly the resolved mate lift in (B.BM16), and \((z,h)\) lifts the actual map \(\vartheta_Q:X\to Y\). They are not new unit targets.

The projection \(\mathcal E\to\Theta\) is surjective in each graded degree. Its kernel is the direct sum of the shifted cones of \(\operatorname{Hom}(SP_0,r_Y)\) and \(\operatorname{Hom}(A,r_Y)\). Both are acyclic by whole h-projectivity. Compatible existing lifts can therefore be retained while a specified free linear cell diagram in \(\Theta\) is lifted. At a new generator, choose any graded lift of its target value. Its differential error is a cycle in the kernel; subtract a primitive. This is the relative obstruction calculation of (B.ND9). It does not assign a composition law to \(\mathcal E\), or claim that \(\Psi\) alone preserves multiplication. Products are first formed using the actual pasting formulas (B.BM17)–(B.BM18).

A chain map to the full unit-defect cone. Let \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal C^n&=\operatorname{Hom}^n(SQ,B) \oplus\operatorname{Hom}^{n-1}(SQ,U_1Y),\\ \delta(D,I)&=(dD,r_YD-dI),\\ D_e&=cSu_0-zu_1,\\ I_e&=bSu_0-hu_1-(-1)^nU_1(\vartheta_Q)\ell_1 +\mathcal A(\vartheta),\\ \Phi(e)&=(D_e,I_e),&\delta\Phi(e)&=\Phi(\partial e). \end{aligned} \tag{B.UC4} \] The complex \(\mathcal C\) is acyclic: it is a shifted cone of the quasi-isomorphism \(\operatorname{Hom}(SQ,r_Y)\), with the displayed sign convention. Explicitly, the second component of \(\Phi(\partial e)\) is \[ \begin{aligned} &r_YD_e-F(\vartheta)+G(\vartheta)+U_1(\vartheta_Q)d\ell_1\\ &\quad{}-db\,Su_0+dh\,u_1 +(-1)^nU_1((d\vartheta)_Q)\ell_1+\mathcal A(d\vartheta) =r_YD_e-dI_e . \end{aligned} \tag{B.UC5} \] The expression follows from (B.UC1) and (B.UC3); the equality uses (B.UC2). The first component is \(dD_e=D_{\partial e}\), since the unit lifts are closed. The sign on the \(\ell_1\) term changes for a degree-minus-one cube cell. Keeping the degree-zero sign there would break the chain-map identity.

Resolve the unit comparison together with the cube. Form \[ \begin{aligned} \widetilde{\mathcal E}^{\,n}&=\mathcal E^n\oplus\mathcal C^{n-1},\\ \widetilde\partial(e,j)&=(\partial e,\Phi(e)-\delta j),\\ j&=(J,K),&|J|&=n-1,\quad |K|=n-2 . \end{aligned} \tag{B.UC6} \] Equation (B.UC4) proves \(\widetilde\partial^{\,2}=0\). Projection to \(\mathcal E\) is a degreewise surjection with acyclic kernel \(\mathcal C[-1]\), whose differential is \(-\delta\). The same relative generator argument retains any previously fixed compatible unit faces. For closed degree-zero \(e\), a closed lift gives \[ dJ=cSu_0-zu_1,\qquad r_YJ-I_e=dK. \tag{B.UC7} \] The second equation is necessary. A primitive of the first difference alone does not prescribe its image under \(r_Y\).

This also joins the actual counit and the two left-triangle witnesses. Put \(\beta=\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}^{-1}b\), \(\gamma=\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}^{-1}h\), \(e_Y=\varepsilon^1_YL_1r_Y\), and \(\Gamma=\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}^{-1}K\). Transposing the second equation of (B.UC7) gives \[ \begin{aligned} &e_YL_1J-\beta L_1Su_0+\gamma L_1u_1\\ &\qquad{}+\vartheta_Q\lambda_1-V\lambda_0\vartheta_Q=d\Gamma . \end{aligned} \tag{B.UC8} \] Every summand has source \(X=L_1SQ\) and target \(Y\). This uses the actual \(\lambda_0,\lambda_1\) shared with the whole-family triangle construction, not unrelated primitives.

The two routes of the original mixed cube. Apply this construction to the two pasted comparisons in the common model of (B.MX13). Their left cells come from the six labelled words and augmentations of (B.MX3)–(B.MX8), the original graph/bar comparison, and its strict roof. Take their right lifts using (B.BM17)–(B.BM18), and call the resulting closed elements of \(\mathcal E\) \(e_T,e_B\). The full retained left cube cell gives a degree-minus-one element \(\vartheta_H\) with \(d\vartheta_H=\vartheta_T-\vartheta_B\). Lift it relatively to \(e_H\in\mathcal E^{-1}\) with \(\partial e_H=e_T-e_B\), using the acyclic kernel of (B.UC3). Here \(\vartheta_H\) means the image of the full cell \((0,H,K)\) of (B.MX8) through the specified strict common roof. It does not authorize dropping \(K\), the nested \(K_2\) of (B.MX12), or the signed graph-to-bar transfer. If only objectwise inverse maps rather than that whole common roof are supplied, this application is not yet available.

Let \(j_T=(J_T,K_T)\), \(j_B=(J_B,K_B)\) be the retained unit comparisons from (B.UC7). Then \(\delta(j_T-j_B-\Phi(e_H))=0\). Acyclicity gives \(w_H=(J_H,K_H)\in\mathcal C^{-2}\) with \[ \begin{aligned} \delta w_H&=j_T-j_B-\Phi(e_H),\\ dJ_H&=J_T-J_B-D_{e_H},\\ r_YJ_H-dK_H&=K_T-K_B-I_{e_H},\\ |J_H|&=-2,& |K_H|&=-3 . \end{aligned} \tag{B.UC9} \] Thus the two unit-homotopy routes are compared as full cone elements, not just as cohomology classes of degree-zero endpoints. At any further specified free linear cell, the same calculation yields a cycle in the same acyclic kernel and supplies the next witness with its fixed boundary retained. It does not manufacture an unspecified geometric boundary.

The first layer has these actual endpoints: \[ \begin{gathered} \begin{array}{ccccc} SQ&\xrightarrow{Su_0}&SP_0&\xrightarrow{c}&B\\ SQ&\xrightarrow{u_1}&A&\xrightarrow{z}&B . \end{array}\\ dJ=\text{upper composite}-\text{lower composite},\\ r_YJ-I_e=dK . \end{gathered} \tag{B.UC10} \] Equation (B.UC9) compares this entire two-level diagram for the top and bottom cube routes. Under the actual Hom-complex adjunction it also compares their counit/left-triangle diagrams (B.UC8), since that adjunction commutes with differential in every degree.

Scope. These are whole Hom complexes; evaluation uses (B.ND6) and (B.TD4), not a converse from pointwise projectivity. Horizontal functors can be non-equivalences, and no invertibility of a right mate is inferred. The fixed common-model cube has this higher unit interface. The full changing-compactification and finite composition presentation still needs its shared right-triangle and nested horizontal faces joined on actual overlaps; (B.JF8)–(B.JF11) and (B.BM18) are their existing providers. Geometric multiplicative descent, coefficient transport and strict-heart effacement are not established by this construction. \(\square\)

Join the right triangle to resolved base change

Proposition B.1aj (the right triangle across an actual mate). The resolved mate of (B.BM16) admits a comparison between the two retained right-triangle homotopies of (B.JF10). The comparison uses the actual unit interface, counit naturality, and the homotopy obtained by transposing the mate lift. It retains a second, degree-minus-three witness. All choices and equalities below take place in the whole parameter/refinement Hom complexes; no assertion of invertibility of a right mate is needed.

Retain the original two stages. Use the whole categories of (B.JF1)–(B.JF3), with the free dg parameter extension following (B.JF13) when required. Let \(L_i\dashv U_i\), \(S,V\), and the closed natural comparison \(\vartheta:L_1S\to VL_0\) be the actual common-model data of (B.MX13). The induction functors preserve whole h-projectives. Fix a whole h-projective right input \(N\), and write \[ \begin{aligned} q_0:Q_0&\longrightarrow U_0N,& q_1:Q_1&\longrightarrow U_1VN,\\ M_i&=L_iQ_i,& e_0&=\varepsilon^0_N L_0q_0,\\ e_1&=\varepsilon^1_{VN} L_1q_1 . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RJ1} \] The \(q_i\) are quasi-isomorphisms with whole h-projective sources. For each \(i\), reuse the second replacement \(\rho_i:R_i\to U_iM_i\), the unit \(u_i:Q_i\to R_i\), and the counit lift \(z_i:R_i\to Q_i\) from (B.JF6)–(B.JF10): \[ \begin{aligned} \rho_i u_i-\eta^i_{Q_i}&=d\ell_i,& q_i z_i-U_i e_i\,\rho_i&=dH_i,\\ dJ_i&=z_i u_i-1_{Q_i},\\ q_iJ_i-H_i u_i-U_i e_i\,\ell_i&=dK_i . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RJ2} \] Here \(u_i,z_i\) are closed; \(\ell_i,H_i,J_i\) have degree \(-1\), and \(K_i\) has degree \(-2\). In particular \(H_i\) is the full two-term nested coefficient in (B.JF8), not its first summand. Put \(e_0^M=\varepsilon^0_{M_0}L_0\rho_0\). The Hom-complex adjunction, with \(\operatorname{Adj}_i\) mapping a left-side Hom to its right-side Hom, gives \[ \begin{aligned} \lambda_0&=\operatorname{Adj}_0^{-1}\ell_0,& \alpha_0&=\operatorname{Adj}_0^{-1}H_0,& \Gamma_0&=\operatorname{Adj}_0^{-1}K_0,\\ d\lambda_0&=e_0^M L_0u_0-1_{M_0},\\ d\alpha_0&=e_0L_0z_0-e_0e_0^M,\\ e_0L_0J_0&=\alpha_0L_0u_0+e_0\lambda_0+d\Gamma_0 . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RJ3} \] These are the already shared left/right triangle formulas (B.JF7), (B.JF11), not newly chosen homotopies.

The actual mate and its three comparison maps. Write \(X=L_1SQ_0\). Take whole h-projective replacements \(r_A:A\to U_1X\), \(r_C:C\to U_1VM_0\). Choose the left unit \(u_X:SQ_0\to A\) with \(r_Au_X-\eta^1_{SQ_0}=d\ell_X\). Reuse the mate lifts at \(N\) and \(M_0\): \[ \begin{aligned} c:SQ_0&\longrightarrow Q_1,& c_M:SR_0&\longrightarrow C,\\ q_1c-\operatorname{Adj}_1(Ve_0\,\vartheta_{Q_0})&=db,\\ r_Cc_M-\operatorname{Adj}_1(Ve_0^M\,\vartheta_{R_0})&=db_M . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RJ4} \] All occurrences of \(\vartheta\) are evaluated on whole h-projectives. The sources of \(b,b_M\) are respectively \(SQ_0,SR_0\), their targets are \(U_1VN,U_1VM_0\), and both have degree \(-1\). The closed lifts \(w,v,a\), with degree-minus-one witnesses, satisfy \[ \begin{aligned} w:C&\longrightarrow Q_1,& q_1w-U_1(Ve_0)r_C&=dh_w,\\ v:A&\longrightarrow C,& r_Cv-U_1(\vartheta_{Q_0})r_A&=dh_v,\\ a:A&\longrightarrow R_1,& \rho_1a-U_1(L_1c)r_A&=dh_a,\\ \beta&=\operatorname{Adj}_1^{-1}b,& d\beta&=e_1L_1c-Ve_0\vartheta_{Q_0}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.RJ5} \] They exist by the whole Hom lifting theorem applied to \(C\) or \(A\). The final identity is the transpose of (B.RJ4); \(\beta:X\to VN\) is the prescribed homotopy, not an arbitrary witness with the same endpoints. For later use define \[ \begin{aligned} \upsilon&=\operatorname{Adj}_1(V\lambda_0\,\vartheta_{Q_0}),\\ \chi&=\operatorname{Adj}_1(V\alpha_0\,\vartheta_{R_0}),\\ \xi&=\operatorname{Adj}_1(V\Gamma_0\,\vartheta_{Q_0}). \end{aligned} \tag{B.RJ6} \] Their degrees are \(-1,-1,-2\), and their sources are \(SQ_0,SR_0,SQ_0\); their targets are \(U_1VM_0,U_1VN,U_1VN\).

Four full cone comparisons. First retain the unit comparison \((J_U,K_U)\) of (B.UC7), applied to \(Q_0\), and choose the unit-naturality comparison \((J_F,K_F)\) for the actual \(c\): \[ \begin{aligned} dJ_U&=c_MSu_0-vu_X,&r_CJ_U-I_U&=dK_U,\\ I_U&=b_MSu_0-h_vu_X -U_1(\vartheta_{Q_0})\ell_X+\upsilon,\\ dJ_F&=u_1c-au_X,&\rho_1J_F-I_F&=dK_F,\\ I_F&=\ell_1c-U_1(L_1c)\ell_X-h_au_X . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RJ7} \] Both \(J\)'s have degree \(-1\) and both \(K\)'s degree \(-2\). The second pair exists because \(\rho_1(u_1c-au_X)=dI_F\): substitute (B.RJ2), (B.RJ5), and the ordinary unit naturality \(\eta^1_{Q_1}c=U_1(L_1c)\eta^1_{SQ_0}\). The whole h-projective source is \(SQ_0\); \(c\) need not be a quasi-isomorphism.

Next compare the mate with the actual counit at \(N\): \[ \begin{aligned} dJ_C&=cSz_0-wc_M,\\ q_1J_C-I_C&=dK_C,\\ I_C&=bSz_0-h_wc_M-U_1(Ve_0)b_M+\chi . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RJ8} \] Indeed, the difference of the unlifted transposes is \[ \operatorname{Adj}_1\bigl(V(e_0L_0z_0-e_0e_0^M) \vartheta_{R_0}\bigr)=d\chi. \] Naturality of \(\vartheta\) on \(z_0\) and (B.RJ4)–(B.RJ5) therefore give \(q_1(cSz_0-wc_M)=dI_C\). The full cone of \(\operatorname{Hom}(SR_0,q_1)\) gives \(J_C,K_C\), since \(SR_0\) is whole h-projective.

Finally lift the particular homotopy \(\beta\) through \(q_1\): \[ \begin{aligned} dt&=z_1a-wv,&q_1t-I_\beta&=dk,\\ I_\beta&=U_1\beta\,r_A+H_1a+U_1e_1\,h_a\\ &\qquad{}-h_wv-U_1(Ve_0)h_v . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RJ9} \] Here \(t:A\to Q_1\) has degree \(-1\) and \(k:A\to U_1VN\) degree \(-2\). To check the prescribed boundary, insert \(q_1z_1=U_1e_1\rho_1+dH_1\), the equations for \(a,w,v\), and \(U_1(d\beta)=U_1(e_1L_1c-Ve_0\vartheta_{Q_0})\). This gives \(q_1(z_1a-wv)=dI_\beta\). Whole h-projectivity of \(A\) then supplies the entire pair \(t,k\). Replacing this calculation by an unspecified lift of the endpoints would lose the \(U_1\beta r_A\) term.

For clarity, every existence argument just used has the same form. For a whole h-projective source \(P\) and a replacement \(r:B\to D\), use the acyclic complex \[ \mathcal C_r^n(P)=\operatorname{Hom}^n(P,B) \oplus\operatorname{Hom}^{n-1}(P,D),\qquad \delta(x,y)=(dx,rx-dy). \] A closed pair \((D,I)\) with \(rD=dI\) has a primitive \((J,K)\) satisfying \(dJ=D,\ rJ-I=dK\). This follows from the quasi-isomorphism \(\operatorname{Hom}(P,r)\); it is not a claim that each desired primitive can be chosen with \(K=0\). Previously supplied compatible pairs in (B.RJ7)–(B.RJ9) can be retained.

Compare the two right triangles without discarding a face. Define maps of degree \(-1\), from \(SQ_0\) to \(Q_1\), by \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal B&=J_CSu_0+wJ_U-tu_X-z_1J_F,\\ d\mathcal B&=cS(z_0u_0)-z_1u_1c,\\ \mathcal R&=cSJ_0-J_1c-\mathcal B,&d\mathcal R&=0. \end{aligned} \tag{B.RJ10} \] The second equation is obtained by substituting the four first-component boundaries; the intermediate \(wc_MSu_0\), \(wvu_X\), and \(z_1au_X\) cancel in order. The final equality then follows from the two equations for \(dJ_i\). A closed \(\mathcal R\) alone is not yet the required compatible comparison.

Its prescribed image under \(q_1\) is computed using all four second witnesses. Put \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal T={}&K_CSu_0+U_1(Ve_0)K_U+h_wJ_U\\ &{}-ku_X+U_1\beta\,\ell_X-U_1e_1K_F-H_1J_F,\\ \mathcal V={}&\xi+bSJ_0-K_1c-\mathcal T . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RJ11} \] Every term has degree \(-2\), source \(SQ_0\), and target \(U_1VN\). A direct expansion gives \[ \begin{aligned} q_1\mathcal B={}&bS(z_0u_0-1)+\chi Su_0+U_1(Ve_0)\upsilon\\ &{}-H_1u_1c-U_1e_1\ell_1c+d\mathcal T,\\ q_1cSJ_0={}&\chi Su_0+U_1(Ve_0)\upsilon +bS(z_0u_0-1)\\ &{}+d(\xi+bSJ_0),\\ q_1J_1c={}&H_1u_1c+U_1e_1\ell_1c+d(K_1c),\\ q_1\mathcal R={}&d\mathcal V . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RJ12} \] Here are the sign-sensitive steps in the first expansion. The product \(dh_w\,J_U\) is \(d(h_wJ_U)+h_wdJ_U\), and \(dH_1\,J_F=d(H_1J_F)+H_1dJ_F\). The remaining \(\beta,\ell_X\) terms combine as \[ -U_1\beta\,r_Au_X+U_1(d\beta)\ell_X =-b+d(U_1\beta\,\ell_X), \] using \(r_Au_X=\eta^1_{SQ_0}+d\ell_X\) and \(U_1\beta\,\eta^1_{SQ_0}=b\). These are precisely the three product terms in \(\mathcal T\), with their displayed signs. For the second line of (B.RJ12), naturality of the closed \(\vartheta\) on the degree-minus-one \(J_0\), followed by (B.RJ3), yields the terms \(\chi Su_0\), \(U_1(Ve_0)\upsilon\), and \(d\xi\). The remaining identity is \((db)SJ_0=d(bSJ_0)+bS(dJ_0)\). The third line is the retained second right-triangle equation (B.RJ2). Subtracting gives the fourth line, without assuming that any unresolved square strictly commutes.

Now \((\mathcal R,\mathcal V)\) is a closed element of \(\mathcal C_{q_1}^{-1}(SQ_0)\). Its acyclicity supplies \[ \begin{aligned} dP&=\mathcal R,&q_1P-\mathcal V&=dW,\\ P:SQ_0&\longrightarrow Q_1,&|P|&=-2,\\ W:SQ_0&\longrightarrow U_1VN,&|W|&=-3 . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RJ13} \] This is the promised full compatibility of the right triangles, including their images at the actual right input. The degree-minus-three term is not an assertion that \(\mathcal V=q_1P\) literally.

The four composite routes being compared are: \[ \begin{array}{ccccccc} SQ_0&\xrightarrow{Su_0}&SR_0&\xrightarrow{Sz_0}&SQ_0&\xrightarrow{c}&Q_1\\ SQ_0&\xrightarrow{u_X}&A&\xrightarrow{v}&C&\xrightarrow{w}&Q_1\\ SQ_0&\xrightarrow{u_X}&A&\xrightarrow{a}&R_1&\xrightarrow{z_1}&Q_1\\ SQ_0&\xrightarrow{c}&Q_1&\xrightarrow{u_1}&R_1&\xrightarrow{z_1}&Q_1 . \end{array} \tag{B.RJ14} \] The first minus the second row has witness \(J_CSu_0+wJ_U\); the third minus the second has witness \(tu_X\); the fourth minus the third has witness \(z_1J_F\). Their signed sum is \(\mathcal B\). Shortening the first and fourth rows by the retained right triangles gives respectively \(cSJ_0\) and \(J_1c\). Their discrepancy from \(\mathcal B\) is \(dP\), whose image discrepancy is \(dW\). Thus the diagram records actual objects, arrows and both levels of comparison, rather than equalities asserted only after passing to cohomology.

Geometric hypotheses. All Hom complexes and cone primitives here are in the whole supplied diagram category. The free-index and evaluation arguments of (B.ND6), (B.TD4), and (B.JF13) give their fibrewise interpretations; pointwise h-projectivity is not substituted for whole h-projectivity. The comparison uses the actual \(\vartheta\) from the common graph/bar roof and preserves the old \(J_i,K_i\). When a comparison with a composite in the original nested resolution graph is required, the retained \(K_2\) of (B.BM14), (B.MX12) must be inserted before identifying the folded composite. Ordinary composition of the already folded maps above does not assert that this \(K_2\) vanishes.

This supplies the shared right-triangle interface for a closed resolved mate, and for an actual whole family of such mates. Extending \(P,W\) over the higher mixed-cube cells and the nested horizontal composition faces in the full changing-compactification presentation requires an additional geometric construction; a linear cone argument does not manufacture those target boundaries. Geometric multiplicative descent, coefficient transport and strict-heart effacement are not established by this construction. \(\square\)

Join the right-triangle comparison to the cube

Proposition B.1ak (retain the unit cube and both right-triangle witnesses). The right-triangle comparison (B.RJ13) extends over the original mixed-cube cell in the fixed common resolved model (B.MX13), retaining the already chosen endpoint comparisons and the entire unit-cube face (B.UC9). Its final witness has degree \(-4\). The proof is a graded extension of the actual four-face calculation, not an inference from equality of degree-zero endpoints. Modules can be unbounded over an arbitrary commutative coefficient ring.

Keep the whole parameter/refinement categories, all replacements and the fixed maps of (B.RJ1)–(B.RJ6). In particular \(u_i,z_i,J_i,K_i,u_X,\ell_X,w,h_w\) are fixed. Let \(\Theta\) be the complex of homogeneous whole dg-natural comparisons \(L_1S\to VL_0\) on the resolved inputs. A homogeneous comparison has naturality sign \(\vartheta_B L_1S(f)=(-1)^{|\vartheta||f|}VL_0(f)\vartheta_A\). No value on an unresolved restriction module is introduced.

First retain all mate and map lifts in one complex. In degree \(n\), let \(e=(\vartheta,c,b,c_M,b_M,v,h_v,a,h_a)\). The maps \(c,c_M,v,a\) have degree \(n\), and \(b,b_M,h_v,h_a\) degree \(n-1\), with exactly the sources and targets of (B.RJ4)–(B.RJ5). Define \[ \begin{aligned} \Psi_N(\vartheta)&=\operatorname{Adj}_1(Ve_0\vartheta_{Q_0}),\\ \Psi_M(\vartheta)&=\operatorname{Adj}_1(Ve_0^M\vartheta_{R_0}),\\ \vartheta'&=d\vartheta,\qquad (c',c_M',v',a')=(dc,dc_M,dv,da),\\ b'&=q_1c-\Psi_N(\vartheta)-db,\\ b_M'&=r_Cc_M-\Psi_M(\vartheta)-db_M,\\ h_v'&=r_Cv-U_1(\vartheta_{Q_0})r_A-dh_v,\\ h_a'&=\rho_1a-U_1(L_1c)r_A-dh_a . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RC1} \] These primed components define \(\partial_{\mathscr E}e\). Every displayed graph map is a chain map, including the map from \(c\) into the \(a\)-lift target, so \(\partial_{\mathscr E}^2=0\). Write \(\beta(e)=\operatorname{Adj}_1^{-1}b\), and use \(\upsilon(\vartheta),\chi(\vartheta),\xi(\vartheta)\) from (B.RJ6), now in every degree. Their degrees are \(n-1,n-1,n-2\).

For a replacement \(r:B\to D\), write \(\mathcal C_r(P)\) for the full cone complex used after (B.RJ9), with \(\delta(x,y)=(dx,rx-dy)\). Use the five particular complexes \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal C_U&=\mathcal C_{r_C}(SQ_0),& \mathcal C_F&=\mathcal C_{\rho_1}(SQ_0),\\ \mathcal C_C&=\mathcal C_{q_1}(SR_0),& \mathcal C_\beta&=\mathcal C_{q_1}(A),\\ \mathcal C_N&=\mathcal C_{q_1}(SQ_0). \end{aligned} \tag{B.RC2} \] They are acyclic by the whole h-projectivity of \(SQ_0,SR_0,A\), not by pointwise projectivity.

The four faces are chain maps in every degree. Define \(\Phi_\nu(e)=(D_\nu(e),I_\nu(e))\in\mathcal C_\nu^n\) for \(\nu=U,F,C,\beta\), using \[ \begin{aligned} D_U&=c_MSu_0-vu_X,\\ I_U&=b_MSu_0-h_vu_X -(-1)^nU_1(\vartheta_{Q_0})\ell_X+\upsilon(\vartheta),\\ D_F&=u_1c-au_X,\\ I_F&=\ell_1c-(-1)^nU_1(L_1c)\ell_X-h_au_X . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RC3} \] The other two faces are \[ \begin{aligned} D_C&=cSz_0-wc_M,\\ I_C&=bSz_0-h_wc_M-U_1(Ve_0)b_M+\chi(\vartheta),\\ D_\beta&=z_1a-wv,\\ I_\beta&=U_1\beta(e)\,r_A+H_1a+U_1e_1h_a\\ &\qquad{}-h_wv-U_1(Ve_0)h_v . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RC4} \] Then \[ \begin{aligned} \delta\Phi_\nu(e)&=\Phi_\nu(\partial_{\mathscr E}e),\\ d\upsilon(\vartheta)+\upsilon(d\vartheta) &=\Psi_M(\vartheta)Su_0-U_1(\vartheta_{Q_0})\eta^1_{SQ_0},\\ d\chi(\vartheta)+\chi(d\vartheta) &=\Psi_N(\vartheta)Sz_0-U_1(Ve_0)\Psi_M(\vartheta),\\ d\xi(\vartheta)-\xi(d\vartheta) &=\operatorname{Adj}_1(V(d\Gamma_0)\vartheta_{Q_0}). \end{aligned} \tag{B.RC5} \] The last three identities are the graded Leibniz rule and the retained equations (B.RJ3). They justify the first identity for the \(U,C\) faces. For the \(F\) face, use \(d(\ell_1c)=d\ell_1c-\ell_1dc\), the unit naturality on the homogeneous \(c\), and the last equation of (B.RC1). After cancellation, \(\rho_1D_F-dI_F=\ell_1dc+(-1)^nU_1(L_1dc)\ell_X-h_a'u_X\), precisely \(I_F(\partial_{\mathscr E}e)\). For the final face, \(d\beta(e)=e_1L_1c-Ve_0\vartheta_{Q_0}-\beta(\partial_{\mathscr E}e)\). Substituting it gives \(q_1D_\beta-dI_\beta= U_1\beta(\partial_{\mathscr E}e)r_A+H_1da+U_1e_1h_a' -h_wdv-U_1(Ve_0)h_v'\), the required \(I_\beta\) at the primed tuple. The first components commute with differential because the fixed maps \(u_i,z_i,w,u_X\) are closed.

Include the entire four-face lift. Set \[ \begin{aligned} \mathscr F^n&=\mathscr E^n\oplus \bigoplus_{\nu=U,F,C,\beta}\mathcal C_\nu^{\,n-1},\\ f&=(e,j_U,j_F,j_C,j_\beta),\\ j_U&=(J_U,K_U),\quad j_F=(J_F,K_F),\\ j_C&=(J_C,K_C),\quad j_\beta=(t,k),\\ \partial_{\mathscr F}f &=\bigl(\partial_{\mathscr E}e,\, (\Phi_\nu(e)-\delta j_\nu)_\nu\bigr). \end{aligned} \tag{B.RC6} \] Equation (B.RC5) proves that this differential squares to zero. Its closed degree-zero elements are exactly the data and four full faces in (B.RJ4)–(B.RJ9).

Retaining only \(\vartheta,c_M,b_M,v,h_v\) and \(j_U\) gives the old unit extension \(\widetilde{\mathscr U}\) of (B.UC3)–(B.UC6), with \(Q=Q_0,\ P_0=R_0,\ B=C\). This projection is a degreewise surjective chain map with acyclic kernel. To see this without assuming that the coupled lifts are a direct sum, first filter the omitted \(c,b,a,h_a\) complex by its \(a,h_a\) subcomplex. The subcomplex and quotient are the shifted cones of \(\operatorname{Hom}(A,\rho_1)\) and \(\operatorname{Hom}(SQ_0,q_1)\). In the full kernel, the three omitted face cones shifted by \(-1\) form a subcomplex; the quotient is this omitted-lift complex. This finite filtration has acyclic subquotients, so its total kernel is acyclic. Consequently an already fixed whole unit-cube cell can be retained while the other three faces are supplied relatively.

The right-triangle discrepancy is an anticommuting map. For homogeneous \(f\in\mathscr F^n\) put \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal B(f)&=J_CSu_0+wJ_U-tu_X-z_1J_F,\\ \mathcal R(f)&=(-1)^n cSJ_0-J_1c-\mathcal B(f),\\ d\mathcal R(f)+\mathcal R(\partial_{\mathscr F}f)&=0 . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RC7} \] The sign in the first term of \(\mathcal R\) is essential: \(J_0\) is composed on the right, whereas \(J_1\) is composed on the left. To verify the last line, use \(d(cSJ_0)=dc\,SJ_0+(-1)^ncS(dJ_0)\) and \(d(J_1c)=dJ_1c-J_1dc\). The four first-component equations of (B.RC6) give \(\mathcal B(\partial_{\mathscr F}f) =cS(z_0u_0)-z_1u_1c-d\mathcal B(f)\). The two retained right-triangle equations complete the cancellation.

Define degree-\((n-2)\) maps from \(SQ_0\) to \(U_1VN\) by \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal T(f)={}&K_CSu_0+U_1(Ve_0)K_U+h_wJ_U-ku_X\\ &{}+(-1)^nU_1\beta(e)\ell_X-U_1e_1K_F-H_1J_F,\\ \mathcal V_0(e)={}&\xi(\vartheta)+(-1)^n bSJ_0-K_1c,\\ \mathcal V(f)={}&\mathcal V_0(e)-\mathcal T(f). \end{aligned} \tag{B.RC8} \] For \(n=0\) these are exactly (B.RJ11), without a new choice of primitive. Let \(\mathcal A(e)=bS(z_0u_0-1)+\chi(\vartheta)Su_0+ U_1(Ve_0)\upsilon(\vartheta)-H_1u_1c-U_1e_1\ell_1c\). The full graded expansion is \[ \begin{aligned} q_1\mathcal B(f) &=\mathcal A(e)+d\mathcal T(f)-\mathcal T(\partial_{\mathscr F}f),\\ q_1\bigl((-1)^ncSJ_0-J_1c\bigr) &=\mathcal A(e)+d\mathcal V_0(e) -\mathcal V_0(\partial_{\mathscr E}e),\\ q_1\mathcal R(f)-d\mathcal V(f) &=-\mathcal V(\partial_{\mathscr F}f). \end{aligned} \tag{B.RC9} \] Here the second components of (B.RC6) read, for example, \(q_1J_C=I_C+dK_C-K_C'\). The extra primed terms in all four faces assemble to \(-\mathcal T(\partial_{\mathscr F}f)\); omitting them would only prove the closed-edge calculation. In the sign-sensitive part, the \(\beta,\ell_X\) terms combine to \[ -b+d\bigl((-1)^nU_1\beta(e)\ell_X\bigr) +(-1)^nU_1\beta(\partial_{\mathscr E}e)\ell_X. \] The terms from \(dh_wJ_U\) and \(dH_1J_F\) give the primed corrections \(-h_wJ_U'\) and \(+H_1J_F'\), respectively. For the second line of (B.RC9), naturality on the degree-minus-one \(J_0\) supplies the additional \((-1)^n\). It cancels the displayed sign before \(cSJ_0\). Equation (B.RJ3), followed by the last identity of (B.RC5), gives the \(\xi\) contribution; and \((-1)^n(db)SJ_0=d((-1)^nbSJ_0)+bS(dJ_0)\). These computations prove (B.RC9) in every degree.

Thus \(\Omega(f)=(\mathcal R(f),\mathcal V(f))\) has degree \(-1\) as a map into \(\mathcal C_N\), and \[ \begin{aligned} \delta\Omega+\Omega\partial_{\mathscr F}&=0,\\ \mathscr G^n&=\mathscr F^n\oplus\mathcal C_N^{\,n-2},\\ \partial_{\mathscr G}(f,p) &=\bigl(\partial_{\mathscr F}f,\,\delta p-\Omega(f)\bigr),\\ \partial_{\mathscr G}^{\,2}&=0 . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RC10} \] The plus differential on the \(\mathcal C_N[-2]\) summand is deliberate. Replacing it by the sign for a once-shifted cone would not square to zero. The kernel of \(\mathscr G\to\mathscr F\) is the acyclic complex \(\mathcal C_N[-2]\), and the projection is surjective in every degree. At degree zero, a closed lift has \(p=(P,W)\) and \(\delta p=\Omega(f)\), exactly (B.RJ13).

Retain the original mixed-cube face. Let \(\vartheta_T,\vartheta_B,\vartheta_H\) be the two pasted left comparisons and their full degree-minus-one cube cell from (B.MX13), so \(d\vartheta_H=\vartheta_T-\vartheta_B\). This is the image of the full \((0,H,K)\) cell through the original common graph/bar roof; the retained nested \(K_2\) and transfer signs are not discarded. Let \(f_T,f_B\) be the closed endpoint data from B.1aj, using the unit faces retained by B.1ai.

The old unit-cube record consists of \(e_H^U\), with differential \(e_T^U-e_B^U\), and \(w_U\) satisfying \(\delta w_U=j_{U,T}-j_{U,B}-\Phi_U(e_H^U)\), as in (B.UC9). With the differential convention of (B.RC6), its retained degree-minus-one element is \[ \begin{aligned} u_H&=(e_H^U,-w_U)\in\widetilde{\mathscr U}^{-1},\\ \partial u_H&=u_T-u_B,\\ \pi(f_H)&=u_H,\qquad \partial_{\mathscr F}f_H=f_T-f_B . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RC11} \] The last lift exists by the acyclic kernel of \(\pi:\mathscr F\to\widetilde{\mathscr U}\). Explicitly, choose a graded lift of \(u_H\). Its differential minus the prescribed endpoint difference is a cycle in that kernel; subtract a primitive there. This retains the full old unit-cube witness with its required minus sign, as well as both endpoint four-face records. It does not replace them with independently selected pointwise homotopies.

Now retain any endpoint comparisons \(p_T=(P_T,W_T)\), \(p_B=(P_B,W_B)\) satisfying (B.RJ13). Equation (B.RC10) shows that \(p_T-p_B+\Omega(f_H)\) is closed in \(\mathcal C_N^{-2}\). Acyclicity supplies \(p_H=(P_H,W_H)\) with \[ \begin{aligned} \delta p_H&=p_T-p_B+\Omega(f_H),\\ dP_H&=P_T-P_B+\mathcal R(f_H),\\ q_1P_H-dW_H&=W_T-W_B+\mathcal V(f_H),\\ |P_H|&=-3,\qquad |W_H|=-4 . \end{aligned} \tag{B.RC12} \] Equivalently \(\partial_{\mathscr G}(f_H,p_H)=(f_T,p_T)-(f_B,p_B)\). This compares the full right-triangle witnesses over the actual cube. A primitive of the first equation alone, or a new arbitrary choice of endpoint \(P,W\), would not supply this relative extension.

The comparison complexes and the retained-data map are: \[ \begin{array}{ccccc} \mathscr G&\xrightarrow{\mathrm{forget}\ (P,W)}& \mathscr F&\xrightarrow{\mathrm{retain}\ U}& \widetilde{\mathscr U}\\ (f,p)&\longmapsto&f&\longmapsto&(e_U,j_U). \end{array} \tag{B.RC13} \] Both arrows are degreewise surjective chain maps with acyclic kernels. The right-hand endpoint and cube records are the existing unit comparison; the middle layer adds the other three faces; the left layer retains the right triangles and the degree-minus-four cube witness. A further specified free linear cell can be extended by the same kernel argument, after its target differential and all retained faces are actually supplied.

Scope. The fixed-common-model mixed cube carries unit and right-triangle interfaces with their prescribed higher witnesses. These linear complexes do not provide a multiplicative presentation. A complete changing-compactification and finite composition diagram requires the nested horizontal faces, their prescribed \(K_2\), and compatible higher overlap boundaries. This construction does not imply arbitrary proper-image quasi-isomorphisms, the existence of unresolved inverses, or invertibility of the right mate. It also does not establish geometric multiplicative descent, coefficient-system transport or strict-heart effacement. \(\square\)

Retain every stage in horizontal mate pasting

Proposition B.1al (the target of an arbitrary horizontal string). The resolved two-stage construction (B.BM18) has one ordered formula for every finite string of adjunctions. It retains every intermediate replacement and every lift witness. Cutting the string anywhere, or evaluating any binary parenthesization of these cuts, gives the same mate lift and the same counit homotopy, under the canonical balanced associators. This supplies actual horizontal target maps for the remaining assembly; it does not assert that all of their unit and triangle faces have already been joined across changing geometric models.

Fix \(m\geq1\). For \(0\leq i<m\), let \(L_i\dashv U_i\) and \(L_i'\dashv U_i'\) be the induction/restriction adjunctions at the two ends of the horizontal array, with vertical induction functors \(S_i\) and specified closed comparisons \[ \theta_i:L_i'S_i\longrightarrow S_{i+1}L_i. \tag{B.HS1} \] As in (B.BM16), these comparisons need only be natural on the whole h-projective inputs used below. They are never evaluated at an unresolved restriction module. The induction functors preserve whole h-projectivity; the restrictions preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Keep the actual kernel models and strict common roofs of B.1ad--B.1af when applying this calculation geometrically.

Keep the nested replacement at every vertex. Set \(Q_m=N\), \(Q_m'=S_mN\). Choose the two chains \[ \begin{aligned} q_i:Q_i&\longrightarrow U_iQ_{i+1},& q_i':Q_i'&\longrightarrow U_i'Q_{i+1}',\\ e_i&=\varepsilon^i_{Q_{i+1}}L_iq_i,& e_i'&=\varepsilon^{i'}_{Q_{i+1}'}L_i'q_i',\\ a_i&=S_{i+1}e_i\,\theta_{i,Q_i},& c_m&=1_{S_mN}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.HS2} \] The \(q_i,q_i'\) are quasi-isomorphisms with whole h-projective sources. The final module \(N\) need not itself be h-projective. Choose closed \(c_i:S_iQ_i\to Q_i'\), descending from \(i=m-1\) to \(0\), together with degree-minus-one \(b_i\), by \[ \begin{aligned} q_i'c_i-\operatorname{Adj}_{L_i'}(c_{i+1}a_i)&=db_i,\\ D_i=\operatorname{Adj}_{L_i'}^{-1}(b_i),\qquad dD_i&=e_i'L_i'c_i-c_{i+1}a_i . \end{aligned} \tag{B.HS3} \] Existence is the Hom quasi-isomorphism out of \(S_iQ_i\), whose whole h-projectivity has just been specified. These are the actual successive resolved transposes, not a product of unresolved right mates. In particular every \(D_i\) is the full Hom-complex transpose of the retained \(b_i\).

For \(a\leq b\), write \[ \begin{aligned} P_{b:a}&=L_{b-1}\cdots L_a,& P_{b:a}'&=L_{b-1}'\cdots L_a',& U_{a:b}'&=U_a'\cdots U_{b-1}',\\ E_{a:a}&=1,&E_{b:a}&=e_{b-1}L_{b-1}E_{b-1:a},\\ E_{a:a}'&=1,&E_{b:a}'&=e_{b-1}'L_{b-1}'E_{b-1:a}',\\ A_{a:a}&=1,&A_{b:a}&=a_{b-1}L_{b-1}'A_{b-1:a},\\ \Xi_{a:a}&=1,& \Xi_{b:a}&=(\theta_{b-1}P_{b-1:a})(L_{b-1}'\Xi_{b-1:a}),\\ A_{b:a}&=S_bE_{b:a}\,\Xi_{b:a,Q_a}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.HS4} \] Empty strings mean the identity functor or map on the indicated object. The last identity follows by induction: move \(\theta_{b-1}\) past \(E_{b-1:a}:P_{b-1:a}Q_a\to Q_{b-1}\). Both ends are h-projective whenever this move is needed. The final step uses \(\theta_{m-1}\) only at such inputs, not at \(N\). Thus the ordered composite uses exactly the resolved naturality allowed in (B.BM18).

One full counit witness for the string. Define \[ \begin{aligned} D_{b:a} &=\sum_{i=a}^{b-1} E_{b:i+1}'\,P_{b:i+1}' \bigl(D_i\,L_i'A_{i:a}\bigr),\\ dD_{b:a} &=E_{b:a}'P_{b:a}'c_a-c_bA_{b:a}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.HS5} \] All summands have source \(P_{b:a}'S_aQ_a\), target \(Q_b'\), and degree \(-1\). The sum is finite because the string is finite, not because any module is bounded. To verify its differential, substitute (B.HS3). The negative term for index \(i\) is \(-E_{b:i+1}'P_{b:i+1}'(c_{i+1}a_iL_i'A_{i:a})\). It cancels the positive term for index \(i+1\), by the recursions for \(A\) and \(E'\). The only surviving terms are the two displayed endpoints. All outer factors are closed of degree zero, so no factor interchange or additional sign is implicit.

Let \[ \begin{aligned} q_{a:b}'&=(U_{a:b-1}'q_{b-1}')\cdots (U_a'q_{a+1}')q_a',\\ B_{b:a}&=\operatorname{Adj}_{P_{b:a}'}(D_{b:a}),\\ \zeta_{b:a}&=\operatorname{Adj}_{P_{b:a}'} (c_bS_bE_{b:a}\,\Xi_{b:a,Q_a}),\\ q_{a:b}'c_a-\zeta_{b:a}&=dB_{b:a}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.HS6} \] For \(a=b\), set \(q_{a:a}'=1\), \(D_{a:a}=B_{a:a}=0\). The composite adjunction is \(P_{b:a}'\dashv U_{a:b}'\). Its counit is the iterated counit, so the transpose of \(q_{a:b}'\) is exactly \(E_{b:a}'\), as can also be checked by applying each Hom adjunction in order. This proves the last line from (B.HS5). Exactness of restriction makes \(q_{a:b}'\) a quasi-isomorphism; its source remains \(Q_a'\), not an unresolved intermediate module. At the full interval \(c_b=c_m=1\), so \(c_0,B_{m:0}\) are the desired lift and complete witness for the pasted left cell \(\Xi_{m:0}\).

Cuts preserve the witness, not only its class. For \(a<k<b\), \[ \begin{aligned} D_{b:a} &=E_{b:k}'P_{b:k}'D_{k:a} +D_{b:k}P_{b:k}'A_{k:a},\\ B_{b:a} &=U_{a:k}'(q_{k:b}')\,B_{k:a} +\operatorname{Adj}_{P_{k:a}'} (B_{b:k}A_{k:a}). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HS7} \] The first equality partitions the sum (B.HS5) at \(k\): for \(i<k\), factor the final \(E'\); for \(i\geq k\), factor the initial \(A\). The second follows by the full Hom-complex adjunction, naturality of its unit and counit, and the equality between the transpose of \(q_{k:b}'\) and \(E_{b:k}'\). This argument also proves the signs of the degree-minus-one term; it is not a transpose limited to closed degree-zero maps.

For \(a=0,k=1,b=2\), the second line is exactly \[ B_{2:0}=U_0'q_1'\,b_0+ \operatorname{Adj}_{L_0'}(b_1S_1e_0\,\theta_{0,Q_0}), \tag{B.HS8} \] with \(Q_1=R,Q_0=Z,Q_1'=R',Q_0'=Z'\), \(b_1=b_\nu\), \(b_0=b_\psi\). It is (B.BM18), including both terms. Repeatedly partitioning the same finite sum proves equality for every binary parenthesization. No new primitive is chosen at an internal node, and no cancellation of a merely closed unexplained defect is claimed.

The cut and its homotopies have the following native diagram: \[ \begin{array}{ccccc} P_{b:a}'S_aQ_a& \xrightarrow{\ P_{b:k}'A_{k:a}\ }& P_{b:k}'S_kQ_k& \xrightarrow{\ A_{b:k}\ }&S_bQ_b\\ {\scriptstyle P_{b:a}'c_a}\downarrow&& {\scriptstyle P_{b:k}'c_k}\downarrow&& \downarrow{\scriptstyle c_b}\\ P_{b:a}'Q_a'& \xrightarrow{\ P_{b:k}'E_{k:a}'\ }& P_{b:k}'Q_k'& \xrightarrow{\ E_{b:k}'\ }&Q_b'. \end{array} \tag{B.HS9} \] The left and right squares commute up to \(P_{b:k}'D_{k:a}\) and \(D_{b:k}\), respectively. Equation (B.HS7) is the precise outer homotopy. This is a homotopy-commutative diagram, not a claim of strict commutativity.

Bind the parameter folds to the original nested graph. For this identification keep the adjunctions identical, with \(S_i=1,\theta_i=1\), and allow an arbitrary terminal vertex map instead of the identity in (B.HS2). The closed degree-zero equation (B.HS3) is then the nested replacement-graph equation. For general homogeneous vertex and witness coordinates use the same graded sum (B.HS5), whether or not the graph differential vanishes; its chain and higher identities are (B.RS8), not an assumption that these coordinates are closed lifts. Transport all edges and witnesses to the innermost category by \(U_{0:i}=U_0\cdots U_{i-1}\). The one-input witness in (B.HS6) then becomes the selected-edge coefficient \(W_1\) of (B.RS4). Indeed the transpose identity \(\operatorname{Adj}_{L_i}(h\,\varepsilon^i L_iq_i)=U_i(h)q_i\) moves each witness to its original position in the ordered product. It holds in every homogeneous degree. This verifies the link to (B.NR7); it does not supply a different fold whose higher coefficients vanish.

For example, in a three-stage string, write \(\widetilde q_i,\widetilde h_i\) for these transported maps, with edge indices \(0,1,2\). For parameter arrows \(t:x^0\to x^1\), \(s:x^1\to x^2\), \(u:x^2\to x^3\), the retained coefficients are \[ \begin{aligned} W_2(s,t) &=\widetilde q_2^{\,2}\widetilde h_1(s)\widetilde h_0(t) +\widetilde h_2(s)\widetilde q_1^{\,1}\widetilde h_0(t)\\ &\quad+\widetilde h_2(s)\widetilde h_1(t)\widetilde q_0^{\,0},\\ W_3(u,s,t) &=\widetilde h_2(u)\widetilde h_1(s)\widetilde h_0(t). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HS10} \] They have degrees \(|s|+|t|-2\) and \(|u|+|s|+|t|-3\); their graph triples have one greater degree. The full all-length coefficients, bar differential and cut convolution are (B.RS4), (B.RS8), and (B.RS9), respectively. Their proof is algebraic and does not require the intermediate restricted modules to be h-projective. For the right-replacement graphs the Hom quasi-isomorphism instead follows by forgetting the inner replacement one at a time and using whole h-projectivity of each \(Q_i\), exactly as in (B.NR6). This distinguishes the algebraic fold identity from the reason that its graph projections are quasi-equivalences. The ordinary multiplicativity correction still has sign \((-1)^{|s|+1}K_2(s,t)\); at three stages \(K_3\) need not vanish.

The strict roof (B.SF7) evaluates every word using these coefficients. Its cut equality follows from (B.RS10); it does not follow by pretending that \(K_1\) is a strict functor. The graph-to-bar signs and opposite-Hom convention remain those of (B.KC10)--(B.KC11).

Geometric hypotheses. Equations (B.HS5)--(B.HS8) specify the full horizontal mate targets, counit witnesses and all cut comparisons for each supplied finite resolved string. They can be used as the actual input to the unit and right-triangle complexes of B.1ai--B.1ak after passing to the stated common strict roof. They do not yet identify the retained triangles of a composite adjunction with the sequential triangles on every overlap of changing compactifications. That common target presentation and its shared unit, triangle and mixed-cube faces still have to be assembled; the degree-minus-four witness of (B.RC12) and the higher coefficients above must be retained there. Geometric multiplicative descent, coefficient-system transport and strict-heart effacement are not established by this construction. \(\square\)

Compare the sequential and composite triangles

Proposition B.1am (the second folding coefficient enters the second triangle witness). For any finite nested chain in the whole normalized refinement categories of B.1ah, the sequential unit and counit lifts admit a nested right-triangle primitive. Folding that primitive gives the composite right triangle only after adding the original second folding coefficient to its second witness. The resulting two-level triangle and its comparison with the left triangle are independent of the binary parenthesization of the fixed master string. Previously chosen whole-diagram triangle records can remain unchanged, with the explicit degree-minus-two and degree-minus-three transition below. This is an actual comparison over the supplied refinement family, not completion of the full geometric base-change array.

Work with a finite string \(L_i\dashv U_i\), \(0\leq i<m\), in the whole transport module categories. Concretely these are the inductions and restrictions of strict functors between the transport categories, as in (B.JF1)--(B.JF2), now with finitely many intermediate categories. Induction preserves whole h-projectivity and restriction preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Evaluation has the properties proved in (B.TD4); an extra dg parameter is replaced by its free index before using (B.ND6). Thus the following Hom arguments are about entire diagrams, not independent fibrewise choices. No boundedness or field assumption is made.

Keep the original right-input chain \[ q_i:Q_i\longrightarrow U_iQ_{i+1},\qquad Q_m=N, \qquad q=q_{0:m}:Q_0\longrightarrow U_{0:m}N. \tag{B.NT1} \] The \(q_i\) are quasi-isomorphisms with whole h-projective sources for \(i<m\), and \(q\) is their ordered restriction composite (B.HS6). Put \(P_{b:a}=L_{b-1}\cdots L_a\), \(P=P_{m:0}\), \(U=U_{0:m}\), and \[ \begin{aligned} A_i&=P_{i:0}Q_0,\qquad M=A_m=PQ_0,\\ e_i&=\varepsilon^i L_iq_i,\qquad v_i=E_{i:0}:A_i\longrightarrow Q_i,\\ v_0&=1,\qquad v_m=e=\operatorname{Adj}_{P}^{-1}(q),\\ q_iv_i&=U_i(v_{i+1})\eta^i_{A_i}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.NT2} \] The last identity is the ordinary adjunction identity for \(v_{i+1}=e_iL_iv_i\). Each \(A_i\) is whole h-projective, although \(N\) need not be. The maps \(\eta^i_{A_i}:A_i\to U_iA_{i+1}\) are unit maps, not assumed quasi-isomorphisms.

Resolve the left image and lift the entire nested unit. Choose \(r_i:R_i\to U_iR_{i+1}\), \(R_m=M\), with whole h-projective replacement sources and quasi-isomorphisms \(r_i\). Write \(r=r_{0:m}:R_0\to UM\). Descending from \(u_m=1_M\), choose closed \(u_i:A_i\to R_i\) and degree-minus-one \(\ell_i\) with \[ r_i u_i-U_i(u_{i+1})\eta^i_{A_i}=d\ell_i . \tag{B.NT3} \] Every lift uses \(\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,r_i)\); it does not use a quasi-isomorphism claim about the unit. Let \(\ell=W_1(u)\) be the first folding coefficient for this unit ladder. The algebraic formula (B.RS4) applies even though the source unit edges are not quasi-isomorphisms, and gives \(ru_0-\eta^P_{Q_0}=d\ell\).
