Likewise descend from \(z_m=e:M\to N\), choosing closed \(z_i:R_i\to Q_i\) and degree-minus-one \(h_i\) with \[ q_i z_i-U_i(z_{i+1})r_i=dh_i . \tag{B.NT4} \] Here the Hom source is \(R_i\). Set \(H=W_1(z)\); then \(qz_0-U(e)r=dH\). These are the same two folded unit/counit equations as (B.JF6) and (B.JF8), with every intermediate stage retained.

Solve the right triangle inside the nested graph. Define \[ \begin{aligned} D_i&=z_iu_i-v_i,\\ I_i&=h_i u_i+U_i(z_{i+1})\ell_i,\\ dD_i&=0,\qquad q_iD_i-U_i(D_{i+1})\eta^i_{A_i}=dI_i,\qquad D_m=0. \end{aligned} \tag{B.NT5} \] Expand \(q_i z_i u_i\), first using (B.NT4), then (B.NT3), and subtract (B.NT2). The two retained degree-zero maps are closed, so the result is exactly the displayed \(dI_i\).

There are degree-minus-one \(J_i:A_i\to Q_i\) and degree-minus-two \(K_i:A_i\to U_iQ_{i+1}\), with \(J_m=0\), satisfying \[ \begin{aligned} dJ_i&=D_i,\\ q_iJ_i-U_i(J_{i+1})\eta^i_{A_i}-I_i&=dK_i . \end{aligned} \tag{B.NT6} \] Here is the complete descending construction. Suppose \(J_{i+1}\) has been chosen. The pair \((D_i,I_i+U_i(J_{i+1})\eta^i_{A_i})\) is closed in the cone with differential \(\delta(x,y)=(dx,q_ix-dy)\), by (B.NT5) and \(dJ_{i+1}=D_{i+1}\). That cone is acyclic because \(\operatorname{Hom}(A_i,q_i)\) is a quasi-isomorphism. Choose its full primitive \((J_i,K_i)\). Starting with \(J_m=0\) proves every equation. This also proves acyclicity of the nested Hom kernel of projection to its terminal vertex: forgetting one inner stage has precisely such a shifted cone as kernel. Crucially, this uses the receiving replacement \(q_i\) and h-projectivity of \(A_i\), not the false premise that a source unit is a quasi-isomorphism.

Let \(\mathcal J\) denote the degree-minus-one nested graph map with vertex coordinates \(J_i\) and edge coordinates \(K_i\). Let \(v\) denote the canonical ladder (B.NT2), with zero edge witnesses. Equations (B.NT6) say \(D\mathcal J=zu-v\) as a full graph equality, not just an equality on its first vertex.

The fold is not multiplicative in its first coefficient. Use the original higher fold, denoted \(\mathcal F\) here, in exactly the suspension convention (B.RS7)--(B.RS8). Transport every edge to the innermost category by \(U_{0:i}\) before evaluating its path sums. Define \[ \begin{aligned} K_{\mathrm{seq}}&=W_1(\mathcal J),& C&=W_2(z,u),\\ I&=Hu_0+U(e)\ell,& J&=J_0,\qquad K=K_{\mathrm{seq}}+C . \end{aligned} \tag{B.NT7} \] Both \(K_{\mathrm{seq}}\) and \(C\) have degree \(-2\). For the closed degree-zero inputs \(z,u\), the ordinary multiplicativity homotopy is \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal H(z,u)&=-\mathcal F_2(z,u),\\ \mathcal F_1(zu)-\mathcal F_1(z)\mathcal F_1(u) &=D\mathcal H(z,u),\\ W_1(zu)&=I+dC,\\ dJ&=z_0u_0-1,\qquad qJ-I=dK . \end{aligned} \tag{B.NT8} \] The minus in the first line is \((-1)^{|z|+1}\), not an optional convention. Since the graph differential on a pure third component is minus its ordinary differential, the third component of \(D(-\mathcal F_2)\) is \(+dC\). Next apply the chain map \(\mathcal F_1\) to \(D\mathcal J=zu-v\). Its terminal vertex is zero, its initial vertex is \(J_0\), and \(W_1(v)=0\); hence \(qJ_0-dK_{\mathrm{seq}}=W_1(zu)=I+dC\). Rearranging proves the final line. This is why using \(K_{\mathrm{seq}}\) alone can give a false second triangle equation.

The two homotopy routes are summarized by the following diagram of boundaries: \[ \begin{array}{ccc} \mathcal F_1(zu)-\mathcal F_1(v)&=&D\mathcal F_1(\mathcal J)\\ {\scriptstyle -\,D\mathcal H(z,u)}\downarrow&& \downarrow{\scriptstyle -\,D\mathcal H(z,u)}\\ \mathcal F_1(z)\mathcal F_1(u)-\mathcal F_1(v)&=& D\bigl(\mathcal F_1(\mathcal J)-\mathcal H(z,u)\bigr). \end{array} \tag{B.NT9} \] The arrows mean subtraction of the indicated boundary, not new degree-zero module maps. In the lower right, the third component of \(\mathcal F_1(\mathcal J)-\mathcal H\) is precisely \(K_{\mathrm{seq}}+C\).

For two stages the correction is the actual nested coefficient \(C=U_0(h_1)\ell_0\). For an arbitrary finite string it is the entire selected-pair sum (B.RS4), not just this one product. The cut convolution (B.RS9) and equality (B.RS10) identify both \(\mathcal F_1(\mathcal J)\) and \(\mathcal F_2(z,u)\) for every binary tree on the same master string. Thus \(J,K\) are identical under every such parenthesization, with the balanced associators retained. The higher coefficients, including the nonzero cubic coefficient (B.HS10), remain in the strict roof on parameter words. This conclusion is not obtained by suppressing those coefficients.

Compare with the left triangle and preserve an older right triangle. Let \[ \begin{aligned} e^M&=\operatorname{Adj}_P^{-1}(r),& \lambda&=\operatorname{Adj}_P^{-1}(\ell),& \alpha&=\operatorname{Adj}_P^{-1}(H),& \Gamma&=\operatorname{Adj}_P^{-1}(K). \end{aligned} \] Then the full Hom adjunction, applied to (B.NT3), (B.NT4) and (B.NT8), gives \[ \begin{aligned} d\lambda&=e^M P u_0-1_M,\\ d\alpha&=ePz_0-e\,e^M,\\ ePJ-\alpha Pu_0-e\lambda&=d\Gamma . \end{aligned} \tag{B.NT10} \] These are exactly the left/right comparison identities (B.JF7), (B.JF11), now with the second coefficient included by construction.

If an older whole-diagram pair \(J_{\mathrm{old}},K_{\mathrm{old}}\) for these same retained \(u_0,z_0,\ell,H,q\) is already fixed, leave it unchanged. The difference is closed in the same acyclic full cone, so there exist \(P_2,W_3\) with \[ \begin{aligned} J-J_{\mathrm{old}}&=dP_2,& |P_2|&=-2,\\ qP_2-(K-K_{\mathrm{old}})&=dW_3,& |W_3|&=-3 . \end{aligned} \tag{B.NT11} \] This compares the actual second witnesses as well as the first homotopies; it does not silently replace an old record by a newly chosen one. The equality-of-inputs hypothesis matters. If unit or counit lifts differ, first retain and compare their complete cone data as in B.1aj--B.1ak; (B.NT11) does not identify incompatible endpoint records.

All lifts above occur in the whole normalized refinement categories. The actual transport induction comparisons (B.JF2) therefore make them natural under their specified refinement and input maps. For additional specified free cells one uses the same acyclic-kernel calculation, relative to the already checked boundary. It remains necessary to give the actual noninvertible base-change and horizontal-composition overlap maps before making that relative application. In particular (B.HS6) supplies the horizontal mate target, and (B.RC11)--(B.RC12) supplies the retained mixed-cube triangle; their joint changing-model target presentation requires an additional comparison of geometric diagrams. Geometric multiplicative descent, coefficient-system transport and strict-heart effacement are not established by this construction. \(\square\)

Join horizontal mates and retained triangle cubes

Proposition B.1an (keep the horizontal witness while joining the triangles). In a supplied common geometric refinement/base-change model, the actual finite-string horizontal mate of (B.HS6) and the retained unit-cube record of (B.RC11) can be kept simultaneously while the other three faces are supplied. The corrected sequential triangle of (B.NT7) then transports the complete right-triangle comparison and its degree-minus-four cube witness by an explicit chain isomorphism. This retains compatible old records; it does not identify incompatible choices without a comparison. The result concerns the whole parameter/refinement Hom complexes, over an arbitrary commutative ring and with unbounded modules.

Put the actual horizontal input in the common target. For one finite horizontal string, use (B.HS2)--(B.HS6) and, in the notation of B.1ak, set \[ \begin{aligned} (L_0,U_0)&=(P_{m:0},U_{0:m}),& (L_1,U_1)&=(P'_{m:0},U'_{0:m}),\\ S&=S_0,\qquad V=S_m,& \vartheta&=\Xi_{m:0},\\ q_0&=q_{0:m},\qquad q_1=q'_{0:m},& c&=c_0,\qquad b=B_{m:0},\\ q_1c-\Psi_N(\vartheta)&=db,& \Psi_N(\vartheta)&=\operatorname{Adj}_1(Ve_0\vartheta_{Q_0}). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HC1} \] Here \(Q_1\) in the two-column notation means the primed initial replacement \(Q'_0\) of the string; \(e_0=E_{m:0}\). The subscripts \(0,1\) on \(L_i,U_i\) now distinguish the two composite adjunctions, not two consecutive stages. The identity is exactly (B.HS6), since its terminal \(c_m\) is the identity. The left comparison is the actual pasted resolved cell, and \(b\) is its full retained witness, not a product of unresolved right mates. Balanced-tensor associators are those already used in (B.HS4). No invertibility of \(\vartheta\) or its mate is assumed.

Use the fixed other replacements and maps of (B.RJ1)--(B.RJ6) in the same whole category. Let \(\Theta\) be the homogeneous comparison complex of B.1ak. Define the mate complex \[ \begin{aligned} \mathscr M^n&=\{(\vartheta,c,b): |\vartheta|=|c|=n,\ |b|=n-1\},\\ \partial_{\mathscr M}(\vartheta,c,b) &=\bigl(d\vartheta,dc,q_1c-\Psi_N(\vartheta)-db\bigr),\\ \mathscr B&=\widetilde{\mathscr U}\times_{\Theta}\mathscr M . \end{aligned} \tag{B.HC2} \] The sources of \(c,b\) are \(SQ_0\), and their targets are \(Q_1,U_1VN\), respectively. Since \(\Psi_N\) is a chain map, \(\partial_{\mathscr M}^2=0\). The fibre product requires equality of the actual \(\vartheta\) coordinates. It does not merely match their cohomology classes.

The map from (B.RC6) is \[ \begin{aligned} \pi_{\mathscr B}:\mathscr F&\longrightarrow\mathscr B,\\ (e,j_U,j_F,j_C,j_\beta) &\longmapsto \bigl((\vartheta,c_M,b_M,v,h_v,j_U),(\vartheta,c,b)\bigr). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HC3} \] It is a degreewise surjective chain map: the differential of these retained coordinates does not involve \(a,h_a,j_F,j_C,j_\beta\). Its kernel has the three omitted face cones \(\mathcal C_F[-1]\oplus\mathcal C_C[-1]\oplus\mathcal C_\beta[-1]\) as a subcomplex. The quotient is the full cone of \(\operatorname{Hom}(A,\rho_1)\), in coordinates \(a,h_a\); its differential is \((da,\rho_1a-dh_a)\) because \(c=0\) in the kernel. These four cones are acyclic by the whole h-projectivity hypotheses of (B.RC2) and of \(A\). This finite filtration proves that \(\ker\pi_{\mathscr B}\) is acyclic. In particular one need not discard \(c,b\) in order to retain the old unit cube.

Supply the common cube boundary before lifting it. Retain the actual left cube \(d\vartheta_H=\vartheta_T-\vartheta_B\) from (B.MX13), the complete unit cell \(u_H\) of (B.RC11), and closed horizontal endpoint triples \(m_T,m_B\) from (B.HC1). Their \(\vartheta\) coordinates must be those of the retained unit endpoints. The pair \[ \bigl(c_T-c_B,\ b_T-b_B+\Psi_N(\vartheta_H)\bigr) \in\mathcal C_{q_1}(SQ_0)^0 \tag{B.HC4} \] is closed: differentiation of its second entry is \(q_1(c_T-c_B)\), by the two mate equations and the displayed differential of \(\vartheta_H\). Acyclicity gives a full primitive \((c_H,b_H)\), of degrees \(-1,-2\). Thus \[ \begin{aligned} dc_H&=c_T-c_B,\\ q_1c_H-\Psi_N(\vartheta_H)-db_H&=b_T-b_B,\\ \pi_{\mathscr B}(f_H)&=(u_H,(\vartheta_H,c_H,b_H)),\\ \partial_{\mathscr F}f_H&=f_T-f_B . \end{aligned} \tag{B.HC5} \] For the last two lines retain any already fixed endpoint lifts \(f_T,f_B\). Take a graded lift of the third line. Its differential minus \(f_T-f_B\) is a cycle in \(\ker\pi_{\mathscr B}\); subtract a primitive in that kernel. This proves the relative assertion and preserves both the full unit-cube face and the horizontal mate cube. If \(c_H,b_H\) were already fixed with the required equations, use them unchanged.

If an older horizontal mate lift for the same \(\vartheta\) differs from (B.HC1), add a bridge with \(\vartheta_H=0\) and the two actual lifts as endpoints. Their full difference is closed in the same cone, so (B.HC4)--(B.HC5) apply. The old records are not overwritten. Likewise, changing unit or counit inputs first requires their full comparison from B.1aj--B.1ak; the following change of triangles assumes those inputs fixed.

Transport the corrected sequential triangle, including its second witness. At each of the two columns keep \(q_i,u_i,z_i,\ell_i,H_i\). Let \((J_i,K_i)\) be an old triangle and let \((J_i^+,K_i^+)\) be the corrected folded triangle of (B.NT7)--(B.NT8), or another fixed whole triangle for exactly these inputs. By (B.NT11), choose and retain \[ \begin{aligned} J_i^+-J_i&=dP_i,& |P_i|&=-2,\\ K_i^+-K_i&=q_iP_i-dW_i,& |W_i|&=-3 . \end{aligned} \tag{B.HC6} \] Write \(\Omega,\Omega^+\) for (B.RC7)--(B.RC10) using the old and new triangles. The complex \(\mathscr F\) does not change: none of its differential or four-face maps uses \(J_i,K_i\).

Set \[ \begin{aligned} Z_0&=\operatorname{Adj}_0^{-1}(W_0),\\ \sigma(\vartheta)&=\operatorname{Adj}_1(VZ_0\vartheta_{Q_0}),\\ d\sigma(\vartheta)+\sigma(d\vartheta) &=\operatorname{Adj}_1(V(dZ_0)\vartheta_{Q_0}). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HC7} \] Here \(|Z_0|=-3\) and, if \(|\vartheta|=n\), \(|\sigma(\vartheta)|=n-3\). The plus sign in the last line follows from the odd degree of \(Z_0\). The formula uses the full Hom-complex adjunction, not its degree-zero restriction.

For \(f\in\mathscr F^n\), with coordinates \(c,b,\vartheta\), define a degree-minus-two map into \(\mathcal C_N\) by \[ \begin{aligned} \Lambda(f)&=(X(f),Y(f)),\\ X(f)&=cSP_0-P_1c,\\ Y(f)&=bSP_0+\sigma(\vartheta)-W_1c . \end{aligned} \tag{B.HC8} \] The degrees of \(X,Y\) are \(n-2,n-3\). This uses both witnesses \(P_i,W_i\); omitting the transposed \(W_0\) term is not justified.

We claim \[ \Omega^+-\Omega =\delta\Lambda-\Lambda\partial_{\mathscr F}. \tag{B.HC9} \] For the first coordinate, (B.RC7) gives \(\Delta\mathcal R=(-1)^ncS(dP_0)-(dP_1)c\). This equals \(dX-X(\partial f)\) by the Leibniz rule, since \(P_i\) has even degree. For the second coordinate, the only changed terms of (B.RC8) are \(\xi,(-1)^nbSJ_0,-K_1c\). Transposing (B.HC6) gives \(\Gamma_0^+-\Gamma_0=e_0L_0P_0-dZ_0\). Naturality of \(\vartheta\) on the degree-minus-two \(P_0\) has no extra sign. Hence \[ \begin{aligned} \Delta\xi(\vartheta) &=\Psi_N(\vartheta)SP_0-d\sigma(\vartheta)-\sigma(d\vartheta),\\ \Delta\mathcal V(f) &=\Delta\xi(\vartheta)+(-1)^nbS(dP_0) -q_1P_1c+(dW_1)c,\\ q_1X(f)-dY(f)-Y(\partial f)&=\Delta\mathcal V(f). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HC10} \] For the last equality insert \(b'=q_1c-\Psi_N(\vartheta)-db\). The terms \(dc\,SP_0,P_1dc\) cancel in the first coordinate. In the second use \(d(bSP_0)=db\,SP_0-(-1)^nbS(dP_0)\) and \(d(W_1c)=dW_1c-W_1dc\); the \(W_1dc\) terms cancel against \(Y(\partial f)\). The remaining terms are exactly the middle line. This proves (B.HC9) in every homogeneous degree, including the nonclosed cube input.

Let \(\mathscr G,\mathscr G^+\) be the twice-shifted extensions of (B.RC10) for \(\Omega,\Omega^+\). Then \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal T:\mathscr G&\longrightarrow\mathscr G^+,& \mathcal T(f,p)&=(f,p+\Lambda(f)),\\ \mathcal T^{-1}(f,p)&=(f,p-\Lambda(f)),& \partial_{\mathscr G^+}\mathcal T &=\mathcal T\partial_{\mathscr G}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.HC11} \] Indeed the second coordinate on the left is \(\delta p+\delta\Lambda(f)-\Omega^+(f) =\delta p-\Omega(f)+\Lambda(\partial f)\), by (B.HC9). Thus this is an actual triangular chain isomorphism over the unchanged \(\mathscr F\), not only an agreement of classes. For successive specified transitions on the same fixed inputs, take \(P_i^{02}=P_i^{01}+P_i^{12}\) and \(W_i^{02}=W_i^{01}+W_i^{12}\). Formula (B.HC8) is linear in these transition records, so \(\mathcal T_{02}=\mathcal T_{12}\mathcal T_{01}\) exactly. This assertion uses the stated additive records; it does not identify separately chosen transition primitives without another comparison.

In particular, for a retained cube \(\partial_{\mathscr G}(f_H,p_H)=(f_T,p_T)-(f_B,p_B)\), put \[ \begin{aligned} p_T^+&=p_T+\Lambda(f_T),& p_B^+&=p_B+\Lambda(f_B),\\ p_H^+&=p_H+\Lambda(f_H),\\ \delta p_H^+ &=p_T^+-p_B^++\Omega^+(f_H). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HC12} \] The two entries of \(\Lambda(f_H)\) have degrees \(-3,-4\), so this transports the original last cube witness as well as its first homotopy. The unit-cube element, the two horizontal mate witnesses and all four-face records \(f_T,f_B,f_H\) remain unchanged. Keep the old comparison and this explicit transition in the record; do not silently relabel its old \(p\) as the new one.

The retained data and the change of triangles fit into \[ \begin{array}{ccc} \mathscr G&\xrightarrow{\ \mathcal T\ }&\mathscr G^+\\ {\scriptstyle\mathrm{retain}\ (u,m)}\downarrow&& \downarrow{\scriptstyle\mathrm{retain}\ (u,m)}\\ \mathscr B&\xrightarrow{\ 1\ }&\mathscr B . \end{array} \tag{B.HC13} \] This diagram displays an actual chain isomorphism over the common target retaining both the unit and mate records. The vertical maps forget the other faces and triangle comparisons, not the specified unit or mate data.

For a fixed master string, (B.HS7) gives identical \(c,b\) under every cut and (B.NT7)--(B.NT8), with (B.RS9)--(B.RS10), gives identical corrected \(J_i^+,K_i^+\). Retain one whole choice of \(P_i,W_i\) for these endpoint records rather than rechoose it at each cut. Equations (B.HC7)--(B.HC12) are then identical under every parenthesization. In particular the original \(W_2\) contained in \(K_i^+\) remains present. The higher folding coefficients on longer parameter words have not been set to zero.

This supplies the shared linear target and the actual horizontal/unit/triangle overlap maps for every supplied common model and cube with these boundaries. It does not make \(\mathscr B,\mathscr F,\mathscr G\) into a multiplicative presentation or assert that all geometric higher faces have already been supplied. Their composition maps and higher overlap boundaries must still be constructed and checked using the original graph/bar roof. Geometric multiplicative descent, whole coefficient-system transport and strict-heart effacement are not established by this construction. \(\square\)

Encode all four faces in one arrow graph

Proposition B.1ao (typed four-face paths and their full graph witnesses). The complete comparison of B.1ak--B.1an has an explicit representation in one dg category of arrows. It retains the two intermediate replacements \(A,C\), all four cone faces, the actual horizontal-mate witness, and the last degree-minus-four cube coordinate. No right mate is evaluated on an unresolved restriction module. The distinction between the unit and counit versions of an endpoint is essential: their comparison is the already prescribed transpose \(\beta\), not an identity imposed on the target. We also give the actual composition law for graph-valued triangle comparisons. These constructions supply a typed common-model boundary presentation; the final changing-geometric-model assembly remains a separate obligation.

The arrow category does not require its objects to be quasi-isomorphisms. For any unital dg category \(\mathscr D\), let \(\operatorname{Ar}(\mathscr D)\) have objects \(a:X\to N\) closed of degree zero. A degree-\(n\) map from \(a_0\) to \(a_1\) is \((c,v,b)\), with \(c:X_0\to X_1\), \(v:N_0\to N_1\) of degree \(n\), and \(b:X_0\to N_1\) of degree \(n-1\). Put \[ \begin{aligned} d_{\rm ar}(c,v,b)&=(dc,dv,a_1c-va_0-db),\\ (c_s,v_s,b_s)(c_t,v_t,b_t) &=\bigl(c_sc_t,v_sv_t,b_sc_t+(-1)^{|s|}v_sb_t\bigr). \end{aligned} \tag{B.FG1} \] These are the graph formulas (B.RG2)--(B.RG3). Expanding the third component proves \(d_{\rm ar}^2=0\), the graded Leibniz rule and strict associativity; the unit is \((1,1,0)\). The two product terms yield the same ordered terms under either bracketing, with the sign \((-1)^{|r|+|s|}\) on the last one. Only \(da_i=0\) is used. The earlier quasi-isomorphism hypotheses belong to the projection assertions, not to these dg axioms. Thus the following unit arrows are legitimate objects even when they are not quasi-isomorphisms.

Use the whole diagram category on the \(U_1\) side of (B.RJ1)--(B.RJ5). Write \(X=L_1SQ_0\), and retain the following seven graph objects: \[ \begin{aligned} \mathsf Q_0^u&=(SQ_0\xrightarrow{\eta^1}U_1L_1SQ_0),& \mathsf R_0^u&=(SR_0\xrightarrow{\eta^1}U_1L_1SR_0),\\ \mathsf A&=(A\xrightarrow{r_A}U_1X),& \mathsf C&=(C\xrightarrow{r_C}U_1VM_0),\\ \mathsf Q_1^u&=(Q_1\xrightarrow{\eta^1}U_1M_1),& \mathsf R_1&=(R_1\xrightarrow{\rho_1}U_1M_1),\\ \mathsf Q_1^q&=(Q_1\xrightarrow{q_1}U_1VN). \end{aligned} \tag{B.FG2} \] The two objects with underlying \(Q_1\) are not identified. Every unit is evaluated on the displayed resolved input. All the maps below belong to the same whole Hom complexes; the graph argument does not replace whole h-projectivity by pointwise h-projectivity.

The fixed graph arrows, written as their three components, are \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf s_u&=(Su_0,U_1L_1Su_0,0),& \mathbf s_z&=(Sz_0,U_1L_1Sz_0,0),\\ \mathbf u_X&=(u_X,1,\ell_X),& \mathbf u_1&=(u_1,1,\ell_1),\\ \mathbf z_1&=(z_1,U_1e_1,H_1),& \mathbf e_1&=(1,U_1e_1,0),\\ \mathbf w&=(w,U_1(Ve_0),h_w). \end{aligned} \tag{B.FG3} \] Their types are, in order, \(\mathsf Q_0^u\to\mathsf R_0^u\), the reverse, \(\mathsf Q_0^u\to\mathsf A\), \(\mathsf Q_1^u\to\mathsf R_1\), \(\mathsf R_1\to\mathsf Q_1^q\), \(\mathsf Q_1^u\to\mathsf Q_1^q\), and \(\mathsf C\to\mathsf Q_1^q\). They are closed by unit naturality, (B.RJ2), (B.RJ5), and \(q_1=U_1(e_1)\eta^1_{Q_1}\). The two retained triangle arrows are \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf J_0&=(SJ_0,U_1L_1SJ_0,0),& d_{\rm ar}\mathbf J_0&=\mathbf s_z\mathbf s_u-1,\\ \mathbf J_1&=(J_1,0,K_1),& d_{\rm ar}\mathbf J_1&=\mathbf z_1\mathbf u_1-\mathbf e_1. \end{aligned} \tag{B.FG4} \] Both have degree \(-1\). In particular \(K_1\) is present in the actual arrow, and the second equation has \(\mathbf e_1\), not an identity between distinct graph objects.

Encode a homogeneous RC record before taking its boundary. For \(e\in\mathscr E^n\) from (B.RC1), put \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf c_L(e)&=(c,U_1L_1c,0),\\ \mathbf c_R(e)&=(c,U_1(Ve_0\vartheta_{Q_0}),b),\\ \mathbf c_M(e)&=(c_M,U_1(Ve_0^M\vartheta_{R_0}),b_M),\\ \mathbf v(e)&=(v,U_1\vartheta_{Q_0},h_v),\\ \mathbf a(e)&=(a,U_1L_1c,h_a). \end{aligned} \tag{B.FG5} \] Their types are respectively \(\mathsf Q_0^u\to\mathsf Q_1^u\), \(\mathsf Q_0^u\to\mathsf Q_1^q\), \(\mathsf R_0^u\to\mathsf C\), \(\mathsf A\to\mathsf C\), and \(\mathsf A\to\mathsf R_1\). Each assignment commutes with differential. For example its third coordinate for \(\mathbf c_R\) is precisely \(q_1c-\operatorname{Adj}_1(Ve_0\vartheta_{Q_0})-db\), since the second coordinate is composed with the source unit. The comparison \(\vartheta\) is evaluated at \(Q_0\), never at \(U_0N\).

Let \(\beta(e)=\operatorname{Adj}_1^{-1}b\). The graph arrow \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf b(e)&=(0,U_1\beta(e),0): \mathsf Q_0^u\longrightarrow\mathsf Q_1^q,\\ |\mathbf b(e)|&=n-1,\\ d_{\rm ar}\mathbf b(e)+\mathbf b(\partial_{\mathscr E}e) &=\mathbf e_1\mathbf c_L(e)-\mathbf c_R(e) \end{aligned} \tag{B.FG6} \] is the required bridge. Indeed \(d\beta=e_1L_1c-Ve_0\vartheta-\beta(\partial e)\); its unit transpose is \(U_1\beta\,\eta^1_{SQ_0}=b\). Thus the last coordinate on both sides of (B.FG6) is \(-b\). Declaring \(\mathbf e_1\mathbf c_L=\mathbf c_R\) would discard this prescribed homotopy.

For \(f=(e,j_U,j_F,j_C,j_\beta)\in\mathscr F^n\), write the component pairs as in (B.RC6), and define degree-\(n-1\) graph arrows \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf j_U(f)&=(J_U,U_1(V\lambda_0\vartheta_{Q_0}),K_U),\\ \mathbf j_F(f)&=(J_F,0,K_F),\\ \mathbf j_C(f)&=(J_C,U_1(V\alpha_0\vartheta_{R_0}),K_C),\\ \mathbf j_\beta(f)&=(t,U_1\beta(e),k). \end{aligned} \tag{B.FG7} \] Their sources and targets are respectively \((\mathsf Q_0^u,\mathsf C)\), \((\mathsf Q_0^u,\mathsf R_1)\), \((\mathsf R_0^u,\mathsf Q_1^q)\), and \((\mathsf A,\mathsf Q_1^q)\). All four identities hold in every degree: \[ \begin{aligned} d_{\rm ar}\mathbf j_U(f)+\mathbf j_U(\partial f) &=\mathbf c_M(e)\mathbf s_u-\mathbf v(e)\mathbf u_X,\\ d_{\rm ar}\mathbf j_F(f)+\mathbf j_F(\partial f) &=\mathbf u_1\mathbf c_L(e)-\mathbf a(e)\mathbf u_X,\\ d_{\rm ar}\mathbf j_C(f)+\mathbf j_C(\partial f) &=\mathbf c_R(e)\mathbf s_z-\mathbf w\mathbf c_M(e),\\ d_{\rm ar}\mathbf j_\beta(f)+\mathbf j_\beta(\partial f) &=\mathbf z_1\mathbf a(e)-\mathbf w\mathbf v(e). \end{aligned} \tag{B.FG8} \] Here \(\partial=\partial_{\mathscr F}\). To check the first identity, its first coordinate is \(D_U\). Its second is \(U_1(V(d\lambda_0)\vartheta)\), because the degree of \(\lambda_0\) is \(-1\), so the differentiated-\(\vartheta\) terms cancel. The last coordinate is \(I_U-\upsilon\), namely \(b_MSu_0-h_vu_X-(-1)^nU_1(\vartheta_{Q_0})\ell_X\), exactly the difference of the graph products. The third identity is the same computation with \(\alpha_0,\chi\), giving \(I_C-\chi\). The second uses the zero middle coordinate and gives exactly \(I_F\). For the fourth, the second coordinate follows from the displayed differential of \(\beta\); the last is \(I_\beta-U_1\beta r_A\), which is the difference of the last coordinates of \(\mathbf z_1\mathbf a\) and \(\mathbf w\mathbf v\). These are componentwise proofs of (B.FG8), not just equalities after applying a projection.

Paste the actual four faces. In the single arrow category, set \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf B(f)&=\mathbf j_C(f)\mathbf s_u+\mathbf w\mathbf j_U(f) -\mathbf j_\beta(f)\mathbf u_X-\mathbf z_1\mathbf j_F(f),\\ d_{\rm ar}\mathbf B(f)+\mathbf B(\partial f) &=\mathbf c_R(e)\mathbf s_z\mathbf s_u -\mathbf z_1\mathbf u_1\mathbf c_L(e). \end{aligned} \tag{B.FG9} \] The interior paths through \(\mathsf A,\mathsf C,\mathsf R_1\) cancel in order by (B.FG8). The first coordinate is exactly \(\mathcal B\) of (B.RC7). The last is exactly \(\mathcal T\) of (B.RC8): in particular the third component of \(-\mathbf j_\beta\mathbf u_X\) is \(-ku_X+(-1)^nU_1\beta\,\ell_X\). Thus its sign and both product terms \(h_wJ_U,H_1J_F\) have not been discarded.

Correct the resulting triangle discrepancy by the bridge (B.FG6): \[ \begin{aligned} \widehat{\mathbf R}(f) &=(-1)^n\mathbf c_R(e)\mathbf J_0-\mathbf J_1\mathbf c_L(e) -\mathbf B(f)-\mathbf b(e),\\ d_{\rm ar}\widehat{\mathbf R}(f) +\widehat{\mathbf R}(\partial f)&=0 . \end{aligned} \tag{B.FG10} \] For the second line use the graded Leibniz rule, (B.FG4), (B.FG9), and (B.FG6). The four uncancelled terms before subtracting \(\mathbf b\) are exactly \(\mathbf e_1\mathbf c_L-\mathbf c_R\). This also explains why that subtraction cannot be omitted, even when the first-coordinate path diagram already commutes up to homotopy.

Let \(\gamma(f)=U_1(V\Gamma_0\vartheta_{Q_0})\), of degree \(n-2\), where \(\Gamma_0=\operatorname{Adj}_0^{-1}K_0\) is the retained second triangle witness. Its unit transpose is \(\xi(e)\). A componentwise expansion gives \[ \begin{aligned} \widehat{\mathbf R}(f) &=\bigl(\mathcal R(f),\, d\gamma(f)-\gamma(\partial f),\, \mathcal V(f)-\xi(e)\bigr). \end{aligned} \tag{B.FG11} \] The first and last coordinates follow from (B.RC7)--(B.RC8). For the middle coordinate, move \(\vartheta\) past \(J_0\); its sign \((-1)^n\) cancels the displayed sign in (B.FG10). The \(\beta\) terms from \(\mathbf B\) and \(\mathbf b\) cancel. What remains is \(U_1(V(e_0L_0J_0-\alpha_0L_0u_0-e_0\lambda_0)\vartheta)=U_1(V(d\Gamma_0)\vartheta)\), by (B.RJ3). Since \(|\Gamma_0|=-2\), this is \(d\gamma(f)-\gamma(\partial f)\). This calculation uses the complete \(K_0\), including the \(W_2\) correction of (B.NT7).

For \(g=(f,p)\in\mathscr G^n\), with \(p=(P,W)\) from (B.RC10), define \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf P(g)&=(P,\gamma(f),W): \mathsf Q_0^u\longrightarrow\mathsf Q_1^q, &|\mathbf P(g)|&=n-2,\\ d_{\rm ar}\mathbf P(g)-\mathbf P(\partial_{\mathscr G}g) &=\widehat{\mathbf R}(f),\\ d_{\rm ar}\mathbf P(g_H) &=\mathbf P(g_T)-\mathbf P(g_B)+\widehat{\mathbf R}(f_H) &&\text{if }\partial_{\mathscr G}g_H=g_T-g_B . \end{aligned} \tag{B.FG12} \] The last coordinate of the second line is \((q_1P-\xi-dW)-(q_1P-dW-\mathcal V)=\mathcal V-\xi\); the other two are (B.FG11). In the cube line \(\mathbf P(g_H)\) has graph degree \(-3\), hence its last coordinate \(W_H\) has degree \(-4\). Nothing in this encoding removes it.

The endpoints and the four routes now have the following typed form: \[ \begin{array}{ccccc} \mathsf Q_0^u&\xrightarrow{\mathbf s_u}&\mathsf R_0^u &\xrightarrow{\mathbf s_z}&\mathsf Q_0^u\xrightarrow{\mathbf c_R}\mathsf Q_1^q\\ \mathsf Q_0^u&\xrightarrow{\mathbf s_u}&\mathsf R_0^u &\xrightarrow{\mathbf c_M}&\mathsf C\xrightarrow{\mathbf w}\mathsf Q_1^q\\ \mathsf Q_0^u&\xrightarrow{\mathbf u_X}&\mathsf A &\xrightarrow{\mathbf v}&\mathsf C\xrightarrow{\mathbf w}\mathsf Q_1^q\\ \mathsf Q_0^u&\xrightarrow{\mathbf u_X}&\mathsf A &\xrightarrow{\mathbf a}&\mathsf R_1\xrightarrow{\mathbf z_1}\mathsf Q_1^q\\ \mathsf Q_0^u&\xrightarrow{\mathbf c_L}&\mathsf Q_1^u &\xrightarrow{\mathbf u_1}&\mathsf R_1\xrightarrow{\mathbf z_1}\mathsf Q_1^q . \end{array} \tag{B.FG13} \] The adjacent differences have the witnesses in (B.FG9); closing the shortened endpoints additionally uses \(\mathbf b\). This is a diagram of homogeneous paths and their specified boundaries, not a claim that every displayed arrow is closed for a nonclosed input \(f\).

Retain \(\vartheta\) itself with these records. Then every old coordinate is recoverable without inverses: \(c,b\) from \(\mathbf c_R\), \(c_M,b_M\) from \(\mathbf c_M\), \(v,h_v,a,h_a\) from \(\mathbf v,\mathbf a\), all four first/second face pairs from \(\mathbf j_\nu\), and \(P,W\) from \(\mathbf P\). Hence the original unit cube and actual horizontal mate remain recorded; the construction is not a replacement by a smaller comparison with the same endpoints.

Composition really needs a cross term. The following algebraic construction may be used in the arrow category just defined. For any dg category \(\mathscr D\), take triangle objects \((X,Y,u,z,J)\) with \(du=dz=0\) and \(dJ=zu-1_X\). A degree-\(n\) comparison is \((c,r,h,k,p)\), with types \(X_0\to X_1,Y_0\to Y_1,X_0\to Y_1,Y_0\to X_1,X_0\to X_1\) and degrees \(n,n,n-1,n-1,n-2\). Define \[ \begin{aligned} R(f)&=(-1)^ncJ_0-J_1c-ku_0-z_1h,\\ Df&=(dc,dr,ru_0-u_1c-dh,\, cz_0-z_1r-dk,\,dp-R(f)). \end{aligned} \tag{B.FG14} \] Expansion gives \(dR(f)+R(Df)=0\), so \(D^2=0\). For homogeneous \(s,t\), with \(|s|=m\), the actual composition is \[ \begin{aligned} (st)_c&=c_sc_t,&(st)_r&=r_sr_t,\\ (st)_h&=h_sc_t+(-1)^m r_sh_t,& (st)_k&=k_sr_t+(-1)^m c_sk_t,\\ (st)_p&=c_sp_t+p_sc_t+(-1)^m k_sh_t. \end{aligned} \tag{B.FG15} \] Here all products are those of \(\mathscr D\). To verify the last Leibniz coordinate, put \(\Delta_u(t)=r_tu_0-u_1c_t\), \(\Delta_z(s)=c_sz_1-z_2r_s\). Then \(R(st)-R(s)c_t-(-1)^mc_sR(t)=(-1)^m\Delta_z(s)h_t-k_s\Delta_u(t)\). The derivative of the last term in (B.FG15) is \((-1)^m(dk_s)h_t-k_s(dh_t)\). Substituting \(dk_s=\Delta_z(s)-k_{Ds}\), \(dh_t=\Delta_u(t)-h_{Dt}\) gives exactly the required two remaining Leibniz terms. The other coordinates are the graph calculation (B.FG1).

Strict associativity follows by expanding both bracketings. If \(|r|=l\), their last coordinates are the same six terms: \(c_rc_sp_t+c_rp_sc_t+p_rc_sc_t +(-1)^mc_rk_sh_t+(-1)^lk_rh_sc_t+(-1)^{l+m}k_rr_sh_t\). The unit \((1,1,0,0,0)\) is closed and two-sided. Thus this is a dg category in all degrees.

For a small integral check of necessity, take a free complex with basis in degrees \(-1,0,1\), with \(d(e_{-1})=e_0\) and other differentials zero; put \(u=z=1,J=0\). Let \(h_s:e_0\mapsto e_{-1}\), \(h_t:e_1\mapsto e_0\), all other images zero. Set \(c_s=c_t=r_t=1\), \(r_s=\operatorname{diag}(2,2,1)\), \(k_s=-h_s,k_t=-h_t,p_s=p_t=0\). These are closed degree-zero comparisons: \(dh_s=r_s-1\), \(dh_t=0\), and their discrepancies vanish. Their composite has \(h=h_s+2h_t,k=-h_s-h_t,R=-h_t\). Its required \(p=-h_sh_t\) satisfies \(dp=-h_t\). Omitting this term leaves the nonzero last differential coordinate \(h_t\).

The higher product boundaries are also specified, not replaced by existence claims. For retained degree-minus-one \(f_H,g_H\) with boundaries \(f_T-f_B,g_T-g_B\), define \[ \begin{aligned} L&=g_Hf_T+g_Bf_H,&U&=g_Tf_H+g_Hf_B,\\ DL&=DU=g_Tf_T-g_Bf_B,&D(g_Hf_H)&=U-L,\\ D(h_r\cdots h_1) &=\sum_{i=1}^r(-1)^{r-i}h_r\cdots D(h_i)\cdots h_1 &&(|h_i|=-1). \end{aligned} \tag{B.FG16} \] These follow from the proved Leibniz rule; strict associativity identifies their bracketings. They describe these actual products, not every as-yet-unspecified geometric higher cell.

To see why this construction retains both triangle witnesses, for each original endpoint take arrow objects \((Q_i,U_iN_i,q_i)\) and \((R_i,U_iN_i,U_i(e_i)\rho_i)\). In their arrow category the unit, counit and triangle are \((u_i,1,U_i(e_i)\ell_i)\), \((z_i,1,H_i)\), and \((J_i,0,K_i)\). Equation (B.RJ2) says exactly that the third is a triangle between the product of the first two and the identity. Its \(K_i\) is not erased; nor is \(U_i(e_i)\rho_i\) asserted to be a quasi-isomorphism. A degree-minus-one comparison in this triangle category again has a degree-minus-four last graph coordinate.

For fixed \(u,z\), a specified change \(J_i^+=J_i+d\Pi_i\), \(|\Pi_i|=-2\), gives a strict dg isomorphism \[ \begin{aligned} T(f)&=(c,r,h,k,p+c\Pi_0-\Pi_1c),\\ T(st)&=T(s)T(t),& D^+T&=TD . \end{aligned} \tag{B.FG17} \] The chain identity is the Leibniz rule; multiplicativity is the literal cancellation of \(c_s\Pi_1c_t\). The cross term is unchanged. In the arrow category choose \(\Pi_i=(P_i,0,W_i)\), so its differential is \((dP_i,0,q_iP_i-dW_i)\), retaining both entries of (B.HC6). The inverse subtracts the displayed correction. Successive specified additive transition records compose exactly. A change in unit or counit inputs is not covered by this assertion.

Fixed-model and varying-model comparisons. Equations (B.FG2)--(B.FG13) give the typed graph representation of the entire fixed-common-model four-face and cube record, including \(\beta,\Gamma_0\) and all original higher witnesses. Equations (B.FG14)--(B.FG17) supply an actual multiplicative triangle target and its product boundaries. The four-face record has distinct intermediate objects and a nontrivial endpoint bridge; it has not silently been identified with one direct middle map \(r\) in (B.FG14). Pasting between changing adjunction/compactification models must still be represented by actual maps between these diagrams, with the full original bar folding coefficients and their geometric overlap boundaries. Strict associativity of formal graph paths does not alone prove that assembly. Nearby-cycle multiplicative descent, whole coefficient transport and strict-heart effacement are not established by this construction. \(\square\)

Transport the whole four-face diagram through a proper refinement

Proposition B.1ap (actual right-refinement transport, with its target labels). Use the complete data of B.1ak--B.1ao over the original commutative coefficient ring. Let \(G:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C'_1\) be an actual proper-refinement dg quasi-equivalence of B.1m, and write \(R=G_!\). Keep the left adjunction, the target module category, \(V\), and \(N\) fixed. Write \(L'_1\dashv U'_1\) for the new right-side adjunction. The maps (B.CR7)--(B.CR9), now denoted \[ \begin{aligned} c_P:L'_1RP&\xrightarrow{\sim}L_1P,& \kappa_Z:RU_1Z&\longrightarrow U'_1Z,\\ \kappa_{L_1P}R\eta^1_P&=U'_1(c_P)\eta'^1_{RP},& \epsilon'^1_ZL'_1\kappa_Z&=\epsilon^1_Zc_{U_1Z}, \end{aligned} \tag{B.FT1} \] give an explicit transport of all seven objects and their entire four-face and mixed-cube record. Its new horizontal input is \(S'=RS\), and its comparison is \(\vartheta'_P=\vartheta_Pc_{SP}\). No intermediate object, endpoint bridge, or higher homotopy is discarded. Successive such refinements agree by a specified dg natural isomorphism satisfying the unit and pentagon identities. This is a construction for these actual induced replacement diagrams, not a claim that arbitrary separately chosen models or horizontal geometric pastings have already been compared.

Keep the maps before restriction. Define \(\mathcal A_U\) to have objects \((P,Z,q:P\to UZ)\), with \(q\) closed of degree zero. Retain \(Z\) itself, not just \(UZ\). A degree-\(n\) arrow is \((a,w,h)\), where \(a:P\to P'\), \(w:Z\to Z'\) have degree \(n\), and \(h:P\to UZ'\) has degree \(n-1\). Put \[ \begin{aligned} D(a,w,h)&=(da,dw,q'a-U(w)q-dh),\\ (a_s,w_s,h_s)(a_t,w_t,h_t) &=(a_sa_t,w_sw_t,h_sa_t+(-1)^{|s|}U(w_s)h_t). \end{aligned} \tag{B.FT2} \] The differential squares to zero by the dg functor identity for \(U\) and \(dq=dq'=0\). Expanding a product gives the Leibniz rule; expanding a triple product gives the same three terms in its last coordinate, with signs \(1,(-1)^{|r|},(-1)^{|r|+|s|}\). Units are \((1,1,0)\). Thus this is a dg category. Forgetting to \((a,U(w),h)\) is a dg functor to (B.FG1), but need not be faithful. Consequently an equality after applying \(U\) is not used as a proof of an equality of the retained \(w\)'s.

The seven decorated objects have the sources of (B.FG2), and actual target labels \[ \begin{array}{c|ccccccc} \text{object}&\mathsf Q_0^u&\mathsf R_0^u&\mathsf A&\mathsf C&\mathsf Q_1^u&\mathsf R_1&\mathsf Q_1^q\\ Z&L_1SQ_0&L_1SR_0&X&VM_0&M_1&M_1&VN \end{array} \tag{B.FT3} \] where \(X=L_1SQ_0\), \(M_i=L_iQ_i\). Every displayed \(U_1(w)\) in (B.FG3)--(B.FG7) is lifted to its displayed \(w\). In particular the targets of \(\mathbf c_L,\mathbf a\) use \(L_1c\), that of \(\mathbf c_R\) uses \(Ve_0\vartheta\), and the bridge uses \(\beta=\operatorname{Adj}_1^{-1}b\). For \(\mathbf J_1\) and \(\mathbf j_F\) the target component is zero. The lift of \(\mathbf P\) uses \(\bar\gamma=V\Gamma_0\vartheta_{Q_0}\), not merely its restriction.

Here is the check that these really satisfy the identities upstairs. The target components of the four face equations (B.FG8), for a degree-\(n\) record \(f\), are respectively \[ \begin{aligned} d(V\lambda_0\vartheta_{Q_0})+ V\lambda_0\vartheta_{Q_0}(\partial f) &=Ve_0^M\vartheta_{R_0}L_1Su_0-\vartheta_{Q_0},\\ 0&=L_1c-L_1c,\\ d(V\alpha_0\vartheta_{R_0})+ V\alpha_0\vartheta_{R_0}(\partial f) &=Ve_0\vartheta_{Q_0}L_1Sz_0-Ve_0Ve_0^M\vartheta_{R_0},\\ d\beta(f)+\beta(\partial f)&=e_1L_1c-Ve_0\vartheta_{Q_0}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.FT4} \] In the first and third lines the notation with \(\partial f\) means evaluation of the corresponding linear assignment on that record. Their differentiated-\(\vartheta\) terms cancel because \(\lambda_0,\alpha_0\) have degree minus one. The remaining equations are (B.RJ3) and homogeneous naturality of \(\vartheta\); the last is the actual adjunction transpose of the defining differential of \(b\). The fixed unit arrows are checked by naturality before restriction. The target component of the corrected discrepancy is \[ \begin{aligned} \widehat{\mathbf R}(f)_Z &=V(e_0L_0J_0-\alpha_0L_0u_0-e_0\lambda_0)\vartheta_{Q_0}\\ &=d\bar\gamma(f)-\bar\gamma(\partial f), &\bar\gamma(f)&=V\Gamma_0\vartheta_{Q_0}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.FT5} \] Indeed the \(\beta\) terms from \(-\mathbf B\) and \(-\mathbf b\) cancel; moving the degree-\(n\) comparison through \(J_0\) cancels the factor \((-1)^n\). Now use (B.RJ3). Since \(\Gamma_0\) has degree minus two, the last sign is a minus. The first and last coordinates are exactly the already proved RC equations. This proves the decorated lifts of (B.FG8)--(B.FG12) without assuming faithfulness of restriction. It retains the complete \(K_0\), including the correction in (B.NT7).

The actual transport functor. Before changing any target labels, set \[ \begin{aligned} T_G(P,Z,q)&=(RP,Z,\kappa_ZRq),\\ T_G(a,w,h)&=(Ra,w,\kappa_{Z'}Rh). \end{aligned} \tag{B.FT6} \] This is a strict unital dg functor \(\mathcal A_{U_1}\to\mathcal A_{U'_1}\). For the differential, closedness of \(\kappa\) and naturality for every homogeneous \(w\) give \(U'_1(w)\kappa_Z=\kappa_{Z'}R(U_1w)\). Substitution into (B.FT2) gives precisely \(\kappa_{Z'}R(q'a-U_1(w)q-dh)\). For a product the two third-coordinate terms are \(\kappa Rh_sRa_t\) and \((-1)^{|s|}U'_1(w_s)\kappa Rh_t\); the same naturality makes them \(\kappa R(h_sa_t+(-1)^{|s|}U_1(w_s)h_t)\). Target components remain the actual \(w\)'s. No tensor factors are interchanged, so there is no additional sign.

Induction preserves whole h-projective modules by (B.DA4). If \(q:P\to U_1Z\) is a replacement with \(P\) whole h-projective, then \(\kappa_ZRq\) is a quasi-isomorphism. To see this, restriction along \(G\) and the induction unit give \[ G^*(\kappa_ZRq)\eta^G_P=\chi_Zq, \qquad \chi_Z:U_1Z\xrightarrow{\sim}G^*U'_1Z. \tag{B.FT7} \] Here \(\chi\) is the actual map (B.CR6); the identity follows from (B.CR8) and naturality of the unit. The unit on \(P\) is a quasi-isomorphism by the whole-module semifree argument (B.SM1), and \(\chi_Zq\) is one. Thus the restricted map is one; detection in B.1s proves the assertion. This does not assume that ordinary induction preserves arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms, or that restriction preserves h-projectivity. Unit arrows themselves need not be quasi-isomorphisms. When whole diagram modules are used, this argument is made in that whole module category, with its actual quasi-equivalence; fibrewise projectivity alone is insufficient.

Restore canonical unit labels, explicitly. Put \(c_0=c_{SQ_0}\), \(c_R=c_{SR_0}\), \(c_1=c_{Q_1}\). The letter \(c_R\) here denotes this degree-zero induction isomorphism, not the bold comparison \(\mathbf c_R\). For the seven objects choose new targets \(Z'_i\) and isomorphisms \(\delta_i:Z'_i\to Z_i\): \[ \begin{array}{c|ccccccc} i&\mathsf Q_0^u&\mathsf R_0^u&\mathsf A&\mathsf C&\mathsf Q_1^u&\mathsf R_1&\mathsf Q_1^q\\ Z'_i&L'_1RSQ_0&L'_1RSR_0&L'_1RSQ_0&VM_0&L'_1RQ_1&L'_1RQ_1&VN\\ \delta_i&c_0&c_R&c_0&1&c_1&c_1&1 \end{array} \tag{B.FT8} \] Replace each transported object by \(q'_i=U'_1(\delta_i^{-1})\kappa_{Z_i}Rq_i\). The closed graph isomorphism from this object to (B.FT6) is \((1,\delta_i,0)\), with inverse \((1,\delta_i^{-1},0)\). For the unit objects (B.FT1) says exactly \(q'_i=\eta'^1_{RP_i}\). Every arrow from object \(i\) to object \(j\), of any degree, becomes \[ \overline T_G(a,w,h)= \bigl(Ra,\delta_j^{-1}w\delta_i, U'_1(\delta_j^{-1})\kappa_{Z_j}Rh\bigr). \tag{B.FT9} \] This follows by composing the two graph isomorphisms, whose third coordinates vanish and whose degree is zero. It is a dg functor on this entire labelled diagram. Naturality of \(c\) gives \(c_1^{-1}L_1(c)c_0=L'_1R(c)\), as required for the new \(\mathbf c_L\) and \(\mathbf a\); it is not a guessed identification of their target maps.

For clarity, its replacement maps and endpoint counit are \[ \begin{aligned} q'_1&=\kappa_{VN}Rq_1,&e'_1&=e_1c_1,\\ r'_A&=U'_1(c_0^{-1})\kappa_XRr_A,& \rho'_1&=U'_1(c_1^{-1})\kappa_{M_1}R\rho_1,\\ r'_C&=\kappa_{VM_0}Rr_C,& \vartheta'_{Q_0}&=\vartheta_{Q_0}c_0. \end{aligned} \tag{B.FT10} \] The formula for \(e'_1\) follows from the counit identity in (B.FT1) and naturality of \(c\), so it really is \(\epsilon'^1_{VN}L'_1(q'_1)\). All seven source objects are induced by \(R\); the two copies of \(RQ_1\) remain distinct unit/counit graph objects. All first-coordinate arrows and homotopies are induced by \(R\). Each third coordinate is transformed by its receiving target in (B.FT9). Thus \(\ell_X\) receives the factor \(U'_1c_0^{-1}\); \(\ell_1,h_a,K_F\) receive \(U'_1c_1^{-1}\); \(b_M,h_v,K_U\) receive \(\kappa_{VM_0}R\); and \(b,H_1,K_1,h_w,K_C,k,W\) receive \(\kappa_{VN}R\). The left-side data are unchanged. This accounts for every original third coordinate, rather than just the closed arrows.

The two especially important target labels transform as \[ \beta'=\beta c_0 =\operatorname{Adj}'_1{}^{-1}(\kappa_{VN}Rb), \qquad \bar\gamma'=\bar\gamma c_0. \tag{B.FT11} \] To prove the transpose equality, compose \(U'_1(\beta c_0)\) with \(\eta'^1_{RSQ_0}\), use (B.FT1), then naturality of \(\kappa\), and finally \(U_1\beta\eta^1=b\). This gives \(\kappa_{VN}Rb\) in every homogeneous degree. The endpoint bridge therefore remains prescribed, not replaceable by zero. In particular the transported extension arrow is \((RP,\bar\gamma c_0,\kappa_{VN}RW)\). Applying the dg functor to the full cube gives \[ D\overline T_G\mathbf P(g_H)= \overline T_G\mathbf P(g_T)-\overline T_G\mathbf P(g_B) +\overline T_G\widehat{\mathbf R}(f_H). \tag{B.FT12} \] Its last coordinate still has degree minus four and is exactly \(\kappa_{VN}RW_H\). The actual horizontal-mate record of B.1an is transported together with its four face pairs; no new choice replaces it.

Composition of refinements, not only composition of formal paths. For composable proper refinements \(g,h\), let \(m:R_hR_g\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{hg}\) be their actual induction comparison. Flattening the tensors in their original order in (B.CR7)--(B.CR9), with the geometric comparison (B.CR4), gives \[ \begin{aligned} \kappa_hR_h(\kappa_g)&=\kappa_{hg}m_{U_1(-)},\\ c_{g,P}c_{h,R_gP}&=c_{hg,P}L''_1(m_P),\\ \mathfrak m_{(P,Z,q)}&=(m_P,1_Z,0):T_hT_g(P,Z,q)\to T_{hg}(P,Z,q). \end{aligned} \tag{B.FT13} \] The first line and naturality of \(m\) make the last triple closed. For an arbitrary homogeneous \((a,w,h_0)\), its first coordinate is naturality of \(m\), its second is the same \(w\), and its third is \(\kappa_{hg}R_{hg}(h_0)m_P=\kappa_hR_h(\kappa_gR_g(h_0))\). Hence \(\mathfrak m\) is an actual dg natural isomorphism on the whole decorated category. The inverse uses \(m_P^{-1}\) and has zero third coordinate. The tensor associators and geometric comparison satisfy the pentagon and units by B.1m; all three coordinates therefore do so here. After (B.FT8), the target component on the five changed-target objects is \(L''_1(m_P)\) for their corresponding source parameter, and on \(\mathsf C,\mathsf Q_1^q\) it is the identity. The second line of (B.FT13) checks this canonical-label comparison. It must not be replaced by an identity on unequal canonical unit targets.

Retain all supplied bar coefficients. A strict degree-zero dg functor induces a map on the suspended bar tensors by applying it to every arrow. With \(b_1(st)=-sDt\) and \(b_2(su\otimes st)=(-1)^{|u|}s(ut)\), (B.FT6) commutes with each elementary bar operation: it commutes with \(D\), preserves the ordered product, and does not change degrees. Thus it commutes with their sum in every length. Apply this to the decorated lifts of the supplied folding/overlap data, retaining the actual target-side labels as above. A higher coefficient with coordinates \((0,0,W_r)\) is sent to \((0,0,\kappa R W_r)\) before the target changes, and then by (B.FT9). It is not set to zero for \(r>1\). More generally a nonzero target coordinate is transported by (B.FT9), not inferred from its restriction. The zero-third-coordinate isomorphisms (B.FT8) telescope between adjacent factors exactly as in (B.SN11); no extra bar signs or omitted endpoint factors occur. The same identities retain each already supplied geometric overlap boundary and commute with (B.FT13). This assertion transports supplied decorated coefficients; it does not assert that an arbitrary unlabelled arrow-graph record has a lift through a nonfaithful restriction functor.

The following typed diagram displays the two stages for each of the seven rows of (B.FT3). The vertical arrows are the actual decorated morphisms; their target components remain visible. The right-hand isomorphisms are from canonical new targets to transported old targets: \[ \begin{array}{ccccc} (P_i,Z_i,q_i)&\xrightarrow{\ T_G\ }&(RP_i,Z_i,\kappa Rq_i) &\xleftarrow{\ (1,\delta_i,0)\ }&(RP_i,Z'_i,q'_i)\\ {\scriptstyle(a,w,h)}\downarrow&&{\scriptstyle(Ra,w,\kappa Rh)}\downarrow &&\downarrow{\scriptstyle\overline T_G(a,w,h)}\\ (P_j,Z_j,q_j)&\xrightarrow{\ T_G\ }&(RP_j,Z_j,\kappa Rq_j) &\xleftarrow{\ (1,\delta_j,0)\ }&(RP_j,Z'_j,q'_j). \end{array} \tag{B.FT14} \] The right square commutes by (B.FT9). This schematic applies to the seven distinct objects, their four faces, the bridge and the full cube; it does not identify objects sharing a source. Its reproducible source is the displayed array itself. The \(A,C\) replacements are retained wherever they occur in the original paths; no path is made to pass through an additional object.

This gives the right-side proper-refinement map on the full diagram, with comparison for successive refinements and all supplied higher coordinates. Simultaneous change of the left adjunction, comparison with independently chosen replacement diagrams, and the geometric horizontal-composition/base-change assembly remain to be constructed and checked. Geometric nearby-cycle multiplicative descent, whole coefficient transport and strict-heart effacement are not established by this construction. The fixed-model proposition does not establish the corresponding general geometric assertion. \(\square\)

Join both refinements with the horizontal comparison

Proposition B.1aq (the induced two-sided diagram). Use the whole four-face data of B.1ak--B.1ao and the actual normalized induction presentations of (B.NR1)--(B.NR2). Both adjunction models may now change. The induced seven-object diagram, all its four faces and the full mixed-cube witness admit the simultaneous transport below. The horizontal induction comparison changes two source objects, and the left refinement also changes the target at \(C\). Neither change may be omitted. The statement applies over the original commutative coefficient ring to possibly unbounded whole h-projective sources. It does not identify independently chosen replacement diagrams, nor assert an unconstructed geometric overlap.

Specify the actual square first. Write \(E_i=G_{i!}\) for the two proper-refinement inductions, \(L_i'\dashv U_i'\) for the new adjunctions, and retain their balanced-tensor comparisons and actual mates: \[ \begin{aligned} a_{i,P}:L_i'E_iP&\xrightarrow{\sim}L_iP,& \kappa_{i,Z}:E_iU_iZ&\longrightarrow U_i'Z,\\ \kappa_{i,L_iP}E_i\eta^i_P&=U_i'(a_{i,P})\eta'^i_{E_iP},& \varepsilon'^i_ZL_i'\kappa_{i,Z}&=\varepsilon^i_Za_{i,U_iZ}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.BT1} \] Here \(i=0,1\), and the two final target categories, \(V\), and \(N\) are unchanged. These are (B.CR7)--(B.CR9), not inverses selected in a derived category. The horizontal comparison is a specified closed natural isomorphism \[ \begin{aligned} d_P:E_1SP&\xrightarrow{\sim}S'E_0P,\\ V(a_{0,P})\,\vartheta'_{E_0P}\,L_1'd_P &=\vartheta_P\,a_{1,SP}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.BT2} \] The second line is an equality of actual target-side maps, for every required homogeneous parameter coefficient. It cannot be deduced by applying a restriction functor and assuming that functor is faithful.

In the strict normalized horizontal square, (B.NR2)'s balanced induction isomorphism, in the required orientation, is \(d\): both sides induce along the same composite dg functor. Associativity sends a balanced tensor to the same flattened tensor, so it proves naturality, invertibility and compatibility with composition. If \(\vartheta\) is supplied as a map of the whole normalized transport diagram, (B.JF2)'s identification of whole induction with fibrewise induction gives exactly the second line of (B.BT2). Equivalently, at the induced objects it defines the transported coefficient by \(\vartheta'_{E_0P}=V(a_{0,P})^{-1}\vartheta_Pa_{1,SP}(L_1'd_P)^{-1}\). This formula does not extend a comparison to unrelated objects by fiat. The original geometric comparison is identified with it only through that supplied whole-diagram map. A horizontal geometric functor need not be a quasi-equivalence; \(d\) is an induction-composition isomorphism, not a claim that the geometric base-change map \(\vartheta\) or its right mate is invertible.

Transport the left triangle before using it. Put \(Q_0'=E_0Q_0\), \(R_0'=E_0R_0\), \(M_0'=L_0'Q_0'\), and abbreviate \(a=a_{0,Q_0}:M_0'\to M_0\), \(a_R=a_{0,R_0}\). The old right replacement, second replacement, and their witnesses give \[ \begin{aligned} q_0'&=\kappa_{0,N}E_0q_0,& e_0'&=e_0a,\\ \rho_0'&=U_0'(a^{-1})\kappa_{0,M_0}E_0\rho_0,& e_0^{M\prime}&=a^{-1}e_0^M a_R,\\ u_0'&=E_0u_0,& z_0'&=E_0z_0,\\ \ell_0'&=U_0'(a^{-1})\kappa_{0,M_0}E_0\ell_0,& H_0'&=\kappa_{0,N}E_0H_0,\\ J_0'&=E_0J_0,&K_0'&=\kappa_{0,N}E_0K_0. \end{aligned} \tag{B.BT3} \] The ordinary counit equations in (B.BT1) prove the two formulas for \(e_0'\) and \(e_0^{M\prime}\); the unit equation proves the formula involving \(\ell_0'\). Naturality of \(\kappa_0\) for the actual map \(e_0\) proves the equation involving \(H_0'\). Applying these operations to both equations of (B.RJ2) retains the old \(J_0,K_0\), rather than choosing fresh triangle witnesses. Adjointing the three witnesses gives \[ \begin{aligned} \lambda_0'&=a^{-1}\lambda_0a,& \alpha_0'&=\alpha_0a_R,&\Gamma_0'&=\Gamma_0a,\\ d\lambda_0'&=e_0^{M\prime}L_0'u_0'-1_{M_0'},\\ d\alpha_0'&=e_0'L_0'z_0'-e_0'e_0^{M\prime},\\ e_0'L_0'J_0'&=\alpha_0'L_0'u_0'+e_0'\lambda_0'+d\Gamma_0'. \end{aligned} \tag{B.BT4} \] For example naturality gives \(a_RL_0'E_0u_0=L_0u_0a\); substituting this identity verifies the first and last differential equations directly. The analogous identity for \(z_0\) verifies the middle equation. Adjunction is an isomorphism of Hom complexes in every degree, so these calculations also apply to the homogeneous parameter coefficients used in the cube.

Two source comparisons and six target comparisons. For the right-side diagram set \[ \begin{aligned} X'&=L_1'S'E_0Q_0,&x&=a_{1,SQ_0}(L_1'd_{Q_0})^{-1}:X'\xrightarrow{\sim}X,\\ Y'&=L_1'S'E_0R_0,&y&=a_{1,SR_0}(L_1'd_{R_0})^{-1}:Y'\xrightarrow{\sim}L_1SR_0,\\ M_1'&=L_1'E_1Q_1,&b&=a_{1,Q_1}:M_1'\xrightarrow{\sim}M_1. \end{aligned} \tag{B.BT5} \] Use the following seven labelled objects. An entry \(\lambda_i\) is a map \(P_i'\to E_1P_i\), whereas \(\delta_i\) is a map \(Z_i'\to Z_i\). These have different roles and must not be interchanged. \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c} i&P_i'&Z_i'&\lambda_i&\delta_i\\\hline Q_0^u&S'E_0Q_0&X'&d_{Q_0}^{-1}&x\\ R_0^u&S'E_0R_0&Y'&d_{R_0}^{-1}&y\\ A&E_1A&X'&1&x\\ C&E_1C&VM_0'&1&Va\\ Q_1^u&E_1Q_1&M_1'&1&b\\ R_1&E_1R_1&M_1'&1&b\\ Q_1^q&E_1Q_1&VN&1&1 \end{array} \tag{B.BT6} \] With \(q_i:P_i\to U_1Z_i\) denoting the original object map, define \[ q_i'=U_1'(\delta_i^{-1})\kappa_{1,Z_i}E_1q_i\,\lambda_i. \tag{B.BT7} \] For \(Q_0^u,R_0^u,Q_1^u\) these are exactly the new ordinary units: substitute (B.BT1), then use naturality of \(\eta'^1\) for \(d^{-1}\). In particular, a unit has not been replaced by a quasi-isomorphism. For \(A,C,R_1,Q_1^q\), these are the transported old replacements. They are quasi-isomorphisms by the precise induction-unit/detection argument of (B.FT7), followed by the displayed isomorphisms. Induction preserves whole h-projectivity by the Hom adjunction. The first two new source objects are isomorphic to the corresponding induced old sources. Thus every required whole h-projective source remains such, without assuming that restriction preserves h-projectivity or that induction preserves arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms.

One dg formula transports every face. Keep the decorated arrow category \(\mathcal A_{U_1}\) of (B.FT2)--(B.FT4), whose second coordinate is the actual target map \(w:Z_i\to Z_j\), not only its restriction. On a homogeneous triple define \[ \mathscr B(a_*,w,h)= \left( \lambda_j^{-1}E_1a_*\lambda_i, \delta_j^{-1}w\delta_i, U_1'(\delta_j^{-1})\kappa_{1,Z_j}E_1h\lambda_i \right). \tag{B.BT8} \] The letter \(a_*\) here denotes an arrow component, not the comparison \(a\) of (B.BT3). This is a strict dg functor on the full labelled subcategory. To check the third coordinate of its differential, substitute (B.BT7) into \(q_j'a_*'-U_1'w'q_i'-dh'\). The first term becomes the transported \(q_ja_*\). Naturality of \(\kappa_1\) for the homogeneous \(w\), and \(\delta_j\delta_j^{-1}=1\), convert the second term to the transported \(U_1wq_i\). All comparisons have degree zero and are closed, so the third term is the transported \(dh\), with no new sign. In a product, the adjacent \(\lambda\)'s and \(\delta\)'s cancel. The two witness terms retain exactly the coefficients \(1\) and \((-1)^{|s|}\) of (B.FT4). Identities have zero witness and remain identities. This proves differential, composition and unit compatibility in all degrees, not just for closed edges.

The canonical new object maps to the raw right-induced object by the closed graph isomorphism \((\lambda_i,\delta_i,0)\); its inverse is \((\lambda_i^{-1},\delta_i^{-1},0)\). Only these genuine isomorphisms are inverted. A chosen replacement homotopy equivalence is never used as a chain-level inverse in (B.BT8).

Here are enough explicit entries to identify this with the actual four-face calculation rather than an unlabelled isomorphic diagram: \[ \begin{aligned} c'&=E_1c\,d_{Q_0}^{-1},&c_M'&=E_1c_M\,d_{R_0}^{-1},\\ u_X'&=E_1u_X\,d_{Q_0}^{-1},&v'&=E_1v,\\ a_*'&=E_1a_*,&w'&=E_1w,\\ \vartheta'_{E_0Q_0}&=(Va)^{-1}\vartheta_{Q_0}x,& \vartheta'_{E_0R_0}&=(Va_R)^{-1}\vartheta_{R_0}y,\\ b'_{\rm mate}&=\kappa_{1,VN}E_1b_{\rm mate}\,d_{Q_0}^{-1},& \beta'&=\beta x,\\ b_M'&=U_1'((Va)^{-1})\kappa_{1,VM_0}E_1b_M\,d_{R_0}^{-1},& h_v'&=U_1'((Va)^{-1})\kappa_{1,VM_0}E_1h_v. \end{aligned} \tag{B.BT9} \] In this display \(b_{\rm mate}\) is (B.RC1)'s old degree-minus-one mate witness, distinguished from the isomorphism \(b\) of (B.BT5). The old map called \(a\) in the four-face diagram is denoted \(a_*\) here. The target component of that arrow is \(b^{-1}(L_1c)x=L_1'c'\), by naturality of \(a_1\). The target component of \(c_M'\) is \((Va)^{-1}(Ve_0^M)\vartheta_{R_0}y=(Ve_0^{M\prime})\vartheta'_{E_0R_0}\). The target component of \(w'\) is \((Ve_0)(Va)=Ve_0'\), and that of the right counit is \(e_1b=e_1'\). These are equalities before restriction.

Likewise the three transposed left witnesses have the required targets: \[ \begin{aligned} (V\lambda_0')\vartheta'_{E_0Q_0} &=(Va)^{-1}(V\lambda_0)\vartheta_{Q_0}x,\\ (V\alpha_0')\vartheta'_{E_0R_0} &=(V\alpha_0)\vartheta_{R_0}y,\\ (V\Gamma_0')\vartheta'_{E_0Q_0} &=(V\Gamma_0)\vartheta_{Q_0}x. \end{aligned} \tag{B.BT10} \] Equations (B.BT3)--(B.BT4) and (B.BT9)--(B.BT10), together with (B.BT8), specify the transformed \(J_U,K_U,J_F,K_F,J_C,K_C,t,k\) with their original incidences. For instance \(J_U'=E_1J_Ud_{Q_0}^{-1}\), while \(K_U'=U_1'((Va)^{-1})\kappa_{1,VM_0}E_1K_Ud_{Q_0}^{-1}\). The additional factor \((Va)^{-1}\) at \(C\) is essential; the earlier right-only rule would give the wrong comparison when the left adjunction changes.

The original discrepancy, endpoint bridge, lift and cube therefore transport together. Writing \(\mathbf P=(P,\bar\gamma,W)\) as in (B.FG11), their last lift is \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf P'&=(E_1P\,d_{Q_0}^{-1},\ \bar\gamma x,\ \kappa_{1,VN}E_1W\,d_{Q_0}^{-1}),\\ D\mathbf P'-\mathbf P'\partial&=\mathscr B(\widehat R),\\ D\mathbf P'(g_H)&=\mathbf P'(g_T)-\mathbf P'(g_B) +\mathscr B(\widehat R(f_H)). \end{aligned} \tag{B.BT11} \] The second and third lines follow by applying the strict dg functor to (B.FG11)--(B.FG13). They retain the whole degree-minus-four coordinate of the cube, not only its first component. The \(\beta x\) bridge in (B.BT9) and the \(\bar\gamma x\) target component in (B.BT11) are retained independently of that final witness.

Successive two-sided refinements. For refinements \(g\), then \(h\), use the actual induction compositors \(\mu_i:E_i^hE_i^g\to E_i^{hg}\). The horizontal and output comparisons satisfy \[ \begin{aligned} d^{hg}_P\mu_{1,SP} &=S''\mu_{0,P}\,d^h_{E_0^gP}\,E_1^hd^g_P,\\ a^g_{i,P}a^h_{i,E_i^gP} &=a^{hg}_{i,P}L_i''\mu_{i,P}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.BT12} \] For the normalized induction diagrams these identities follow on each balanced tensor by flattening the same ordered factors; no permutation or sign is introduced. They include all nonidentity proper-image comparisons upon evaluating the normalization back to the original models, as in (B.SN6). The mate identity is the adjoint identity (B.FT13). Consequently the canonical iterated transport is compared with direct transport by closed graph isomorphisms whose witness coordinate is zero and whose first two components are \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} i&\text{source component}&\text{target component}\\\hline Q_0^u&S''\mu_{0,Q_0}&L_1''S''\mu_{0,Q_0}\\ R_0^u&S''\mu_{0,R_0}&L_1''S''\mu_{0,R_0}\\ A&\mu_{1,A}&L_1''S''\mu_{0,Q_0}\\ C&\mu_{1,C}&VL_0''\mu_{0,Q_0}\\ Q_1^u&\mu_{1,Q_1}&L_1''\mu_{1,Q_1}\\ R_1&\mu_{1,R_1}&L_1''\mu_{1,Q_1}\\ Q_1^q&\mu_{1,Q_1}&1_{VN} \end{array} \tag{B.BT13} \] To verify the table, first compare the raw right-induced objects by \((\mu_{1,P_i},1_{Z_i},0)\), using the actual mate composition. Conjugate by the two systems \((\lambda_i,\delta_i,0)\). The first identity of (B.BT12) gives the first two source entries; the second gives their target entries and the entries at \(A,C,Q_1^u,R_1\). The other source entries are the original \(\mu_1\). This also proves naturality on every homogeneous triple in (B.BT8). The unit and pentagon equations reduce to the induction unit and pentagon equations on these same components, so they hold before passing to homotopy classes. In particular the canonical comparison is not declared to have identity target components at \(A\) or \(C\).

Keep the supplied bars. Since (B.BT8) preserves differential and ordered multiplication, it commutes with both the internal bar differential and the signed multiplication faces. Apply it to every supplied decorated coefficient. A higher coefficient with only witness \(W_r\) becomes \(U_1'(\delta_j^{-1})\kappa_{1,Z_j}E_1W_r\lambda_i\). The zero-witness graph isomorphisms telescope exactly as in (B.SN11). Thus the nonzero nested \(K_2\) of (B.MX12), its suspension sign, and all supplied higher coefficients survive. An arbitrary ordinary arrow-graph coefficient without an actual target-side lift is not silently promoted to a decorated one.

The diagram records the two distinct comparisons used at each vertex: \[ \begin{array}{ccc} P_i'&\xrightarrow{\lambda_i}&E_1P_i\\ {\scriptstyle q_i'}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle\kappa_{1,Z_i}E_1q_i}\\ U_1'Z_i'&\xrightarrow{U_1'\delta_i}&U_1'Z_i. \end{array} \qquad \begin{gathered} \lambda_{Q_0^u}=d_{Q_0}^{-1},\quad\lambda_{R_0^u}=d_{R_0}^{-1},\\ \delta_A=x,\qquad\delta_C=Va. \end{gathered} \tag{B.BT14} \] The square commutes by (B.BT7). Its horizontal maps are actual isomorphisms; its vertical maps need not be. The table (B.BT6) preserves the seven original vertices and the paths on which each occurs.

Geometric hypotheses. The simultaneous induced refinement of the four-face diagram has actual source/target comparisons and successive-refinement coherence. It uses (B.BT2)'s supplied whole-diagram comparison; merely having a map with the same name, a derived isomorphism class, or separately chosen pointwise replacements does not establish that input. Comparing independently chosen replacement diagrams still requires their actual target maps and checked shared boundaries, especially at the three unit objects, whose structure maps need not be invertible. The full geometric horizontal-composition/base-change and higher overlap assembly is therefore still open. Geometric nearby-cycle multiplicative descent, coefficient-system completion and rationalization with derived limits and strict-heart effacement are not established by this construction. \(\square\)

Whole replacement comparison without inverting units

Proposition B.1ar (one whole envelope, including the unit vertices). Fix the actual decorated seven-object diagram of (B.FT2)--(B.FT5), or its induced bilateral transport in B.1aq. There is an explicit path envelope of this entire diagram and a whole semifree replacement of that envelope. It compares back to the original objects, faces and full cube without assuming that a unit map is a quasi-isomorphism. Independent whole replacements of this same envelope admit natural graph comparisons with all relative free choice-coherences. Their comparisons back to the original diagram include an explicit second witness. This does not identify geometric diagrams with different, as yet uncompared, target maps.

An envelope for every arrow, not only replacements. Work in the actual decorated category \(\mathcal A_U\) of (B.FT2). Write \(q:P\to Y=UZ\), with \(q\) closed of degree zero; no quasi-isomorphism condition on \(q\) is imposed. Set \[ \begin{aligned} W(q)^n&=P^n\oplus Y^n\oplus Y^{n-1},\\ d_W(p,y,z)&=(dp,dy,-dz+qp-y),\\ r(p,y,z)&=p,& t(p,y,z)&=y,\\ H(p,y,z)&=z,\\ j(p)&=(p,qp,0),& s(p,y,z)&=(0,-z,0). \end{aligned} \tag{B.PE1} \] Here \(r,t,j\) have degree zero and \(H,s\) degree minus one. Use the ordinary right module action on the three summands; the shifted differential has the displayed minus sign. The module Leibniz rule follows directly, and the last coordinate of \(d_W^2\) is \(-d(qp-y)+qdp-dy=0\). With \(d\) on maps denoting the Hom differential, substitution gives \[ \begin{aligned} dr=dt=dj&=0,& dH&=qr-t,\\ rj&=1,& tj&=q,& Hj&=0,\\ ds&=1-jr,& ts&=-H,& rs=Hs&=0. \end{aligned} \tag{B.PE2} \] For example \((d_Ws+sd_W)(p,y,z)=(0,y-qp,z)\). Thus \(r\) and \(j\) are chain homotopy inverses for any \(q\). If \(P\) is h-projective, so is \(W(q)\): precomposition with these maps identifies its Hom complex up to homotopy with \(\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)\). No projectivity of \(UZ\) is needed. Since \(t\) is homotopic to \(qr\), it is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when \(q\) is. In particular the envelope has not turned a non-quasi-isomorphic unit into a replacement of its target.

For a homogeneous decorated arrow \(f=(a,w,h):q\to q'\) of degree \(n\), define \[ \begin{aligned} W(f)(p,y,z)&=(ap,U(w)y,hp+(-1)^nU(w)z),\\ F(q)&=(W(q),Z,t),& F(f)&=(W(f),w,0). \end{aligned} \tag{B.PE3} \] Both are strict unital dg functors. For the differential, the third coordinate of \(d_W'W(f)-(-1)^nW(f)d_W\) on \(p\) is \(q'a-U(w)q-dh\), the third coordinate in (B.FT2). Its remaining diagonal blocks are \(da,U(dw),(-1)^{n+1}U(dw)\), with the other block zero. For a product of degrees \(m,n\), the third-source block is \(h_sa_t+(-1)^mU(w_s)h_t\) and the last diagonal block is \((-1)^{m+n}U(w_sw_t)\). These are exactly \(W(sf)\)'s blocks. The identity is immediate. Moreover \(t'W(f)=U(w)t\), proving the assertion for \(F\). The actual target map is still \(w\), not an equality inferred from its restriction.

The projection \(H\) is not a graded natural transformation to \(UZ\). Its precise defect is essential: \[ \begin{aligned} r'W(f)&=ar,& t'W(f)&=U(w)t,\\ H'W(f)-(-1)^nU(w)H&=hr,\\ C_q&=(r,1_Z,H):F(q)\longrightarrow q,\\ fC_q&=C_{q'}F(f),& DC_q&=0. \end{aligned} \tag{B.PE4} \] The first two naturality coordinates follow from the projections. The third is \(hr+(-1)^nU(w)H=H'W(f)\), exactly the defect just displayed. Consequently \(C\), unlike \(H\) alone, is a strict dg natural comparison. It is an objectwise homotopy equivalence in \(\mathcal A_U\): \[ J_q=(j,1_Z,0),\qquad C_qJ_q=1_q,\qquad 1_{F(q)}-J_qC_q=D(s,0,0). \tag{B.PE5} \] The last third coordinate is \(ts=-H\), not zero. The maps \(J_q\) are used only as objectwise inverses; no naturality of the family \(J\) is asserted.

Keep the actual canonical unit and counit interface. For the actual dg adjunction \(L\dashv U\), write \(\operatorname{Adj}(q):LP\to Z\) for the transpose of \(q\). This notation fixes its direction. Put \(e_q=\operatorname{Adj}(q)\), \(e_t=\operatorname{Adj}(t)\), and \(\beta=\operatorname{Adj}(H)\). Let \(J_L(P)=(P,LP,\eta_P)\) and \(J_L(a)=(a,La,0)\). Naturality of the unit makes \(J_L\) a dg functor. The canonical closed arrows \(E_q=(1_P,e_q,0)\) and \(E_t=(1_W,e_t,0)\) satisfy \[ \begin{aligned} d\beta&=e_qLr-e_t,\\ E_qJ_L(r)-C_qE_t&=D(0,\beta,0),\\ (0,\beta,0)&:J_L(W(q))\longrightarrow q \quad\text{has degree }-1. \end{aligned} \tag{B.PE6} \] The actual target-side equality is the transpose of \(dH=qr-t\). The third coordinate of the right side is \(-U(\beta)\eta_W=-H\), equal to the left side. This proves the square before any assumption that \(U\) is faithful. For degree-\(n\) \(f\), this witness itself has the explicitly controlled defect \[ (0,\beta',0)J_L(W(f)) -(-1)^nf(0,\beta,0) =(0,\operatorname{Adj}(hr),0). \tag{B.PE7} \] Indeed its target component is the transpose of the second line of (B.PE4), and its other components vanish. Thus (B.PE6) is not silently promoted to a strictly natural square of homotopies.

At an old unit object \(q=\eta_P\), one has \(e_q=1_{LP}\). Hence \(e_t\) is homotopic to \(Lr\), and is a homotopy equivalence, because a dg functor preserves an explicit chain homotopy equivalence. Neither \(\eta_P\) nor \(t\) need be quasi-isomorphisms. For a concrete example over a field, take \(L=T\otimes-\), \(U=\operatorname{Hom}(T,-)\), with \(T=k^2\), and \(P=k\) in degree zero. The unit sends \(1\) to the identity endomorphism in \(\operatorname{Hom}(T,T)\), a one-dimensional subspace of a four-dimensional space. It is not a quasi-isomorphism; nevertheless (B.PE1)--(B.PE7) apply. Keep \(e_t\) and its witnesses as maps. Do not insert a homotopy inverse in an expression requiring a genuine chain isomorphism, such as the target conjugation in (B.BT8).

Resolve the seven objects as one diagram. Take \(\mathcal I\) to be the small labelled full dg subcategory of \(\mathcal A_U\) on the seven objects in (B.FT3), with their actual target maps. Distinct labels remain distinct even when underlying objects coincide. The supplied four faces, the \(\beta\) bridge, \(\bar\gamma\), and the full cube are actual homogeneous arrows with the boundaries checked in (B.FT4)--(B.FT5). For an original higher bar presentation, first use its supplied strict decorated roof; a mere restricted map is not an invented decorated lift. Pull the inclusion back to \(\mathcal J=Q\mathcal I\) of B.1t, and denote the resulting strict diagram by \(D\). Apply (B.ND5)--(B.ND6) to the whole diagram \(WD\), as a module over \(\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}\otimes\mathcal C\): \[ \begin{aligned} \rho:V&\xrightarrow{\ \simeq\ }WD, &q_i^\rho&=t_i\rho_i,\\ D^\rho_i&=(V_i,Z_i,q_i^\rho), &D^\rho(f)&=(V(f),w_f,0),\\ C_i^\rho&=(r_i\rho_i,1_{Z_i},H_i\rho_i):D_i^\rho\longrightarrow D_i. \end{aligned} \tag{B.PE8} \] Here \(V\) is whole semifree, and every \(V_i\) is h-projective by the free-index path filtration, not by an assertion that pointwise projectivity implies diagram projectivity. The maps \(q^\rho\) are strictly natural, and (B.PE4) proves strict naturality and closedness of \(C^\rho\). If \(q_i\) is a genuine replacement, so is \(q_i^\rho\); at the unit vertices no such assertion is made. Applying the strict functor \(F\) and the natural comparison to the full decorated diagram retains every original boundary. A formerly nonzero third coordinate, including the degree-minus-four cube term, is now the third-source block of \(W(f)\); it has not disappeared merely because \(F(f)\)'s external third coordinate is zero.

For completeness \(C_i^\rho\) is also an objectwise graph homotopy equivalence. Since \(W_i\) is homotopy equivalent to the original h-projective \(P_i\), the quasi-isomorphism \(\rho_i:V_i\to W_i\) is a homotopy equivalence. Choose \(\sigma,A,B\) with \(dA=\rho\sigma-1\), \(dB=\sigma\rho-1\). The cycle \(\rho B-A\rho\) can be made a boundary by changing \(B\) by a closed map: postcomposition by \(\rho\) on \(\operatorname{Hom}(V_i,-)\) is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus choose \(K\) so that \(\rho B-A\rho=dK\). Suppressing \(i\), in the graph category put \[ \begin{aligned} R&=(\rho,1,0),& S&=(\sigma,1,tA),\\ RS-1&=D(A,0,0),& SR-1&=D(B,0,tK). \end{aligned} \tag{B.PE9} \] The last coordinate in the second identity is \(t\rho B-d(tK)=tA\rho\); closedness of \(S\) follows from \(dA=\rho\sigma-1\). Compose \(R\) with (B.PE5). The use of \(A,B,K\) here is objectwise; it is not a substitute for the whole natural choice comparison below. The canonical-unit interface for \(V_i\) is (B.PE6) with \(r\rho\), \(t\rho\), \(H\rho\); transpose these actual maps before restriction.

Compare independent whole choices over this envelope. Let \(\rho:V\to WD\) and \(\rho':V'\to WD\) be two whole h-projective replacements. By (B.ND7), postcomposition by \(\rho'\) on the whole natural Hom complex with source \(V\) is a quasi-isomorphism. It supplies a closed degree-zero \(a\) and a degree-minus-one graded natural \(h\) such that \[ \begin{aligned} \rho'a-\rho&=dh,\\ A_{\rho',\rho}&=(a,1_Z,th):D^\rho\longrightarrow D^{\rho'},\\ DA_{\rho',\rho}&=0. \end{aligned} \tag{B.PE10} \] All seven components are chosen simultaneously. The sign in (B.ND4), together with naturality of \(t\), gives the third-coordinate naturality of \(A\). The source map \(a\) is a quasi-isomorphism and hence a whole homotopy equivalence. The comparison to the original diagram requires a second witness, not just \(rh\): \[ \begin{aligned} C^{\rho'}A_{\rho',\rho}-C^\rho&=DB_{\rho',\rho},\\ B_{\rho',\rho}&=(rh,0,Hh), &|rh|&=-1,& |Hh|&=-2. \end{aligned} \tag{B.PE11} \] The third coordinate of \(DB\) is \(qrh-d(Hh)=(dH+t)h-dHh+Hdh=th+Hdh\), exactly that of the left side. For a degree-\(n\) index arrow, \(h_jV(f)=(-1)^nW(f)h_i\). Insert (B.PE4)'s defect to obtain \(B_jD^\rho(f)=(-1)^nD(f)B_i\): the extra term is \((-1)^nh_fr_ih_i\), precisely the graph product's term. This proves whole graded naturality of \(B\), despite the nonnaturality of \(H\) alone. Omitting \(Hh\) would change the boundary.

All higher choice cells use a genuine acyclic projection. Form a dg category whose objects are these whole maps \(\rho\). A degree-\(n\) arrow is \(x=(\lambda,a,h)\), with \(a:V\to V'\) of degree \(n\), \(h:V\to WD\) of degree \(n-1\), and \(\lambda\in k^n\), where \(k\) is concentrated in degree zero. Keep \(\lambda\) as a formal scalar coordinate even if its action on \(WD\) is zero. For composable arrows \(x_s,x_t\), define \[ \begin{aligned} D(\lambda,a,h)&=(0,da,\rho'a-\lambda\rho-dh),\\ x_sx_t&=(\lambda_s\lambda_t,a_sa_t, h_sa_t+(-1)^{|s|}\lambda_sh_t),\\ \pi(\lambda,a,h)&=\lambda,\\ \Phi(\lambda,a,h)&=(a,\lambda1_Z,th). \end{aligned} \tag{B.PE12} \] These are the graph differential and multiplication of (B.FT2), with a retained scalar coordinate, and so obey \(D^2=0\), Leibniz and associativity. The unit is \((1,1,0)\). Projection \(\pi\) to the one-object dg category \(k\) is degreewise surjective. Its Hom kernel is the shifted cone of \(\operatorname{Hom}(V,\rho')\), acyclic by (B.ND7). This argument uses \(\rho'\), never the unit map. The map \(\Phi\) is a strict dg functor to the category of whole decorated diagrams and graded natural transformations, since \(t\) is closed and strictly natural. Reverse lifts of scalar \(1\) exist; each composite minus its identity is a closed kernel element and hence a boundary. Applying \(\Phi\) proves that (B.PE10)'s graph comparison is a whole homotopy equivalence.

For every homogeneous choice arrow, put \(B(x)=(rh,0,Hh)\), of degree \(|x|-1\). A computation using \(dH=qr-t\) strengthens (B.PE11): \[ \begin{aligned} DB(x)+B(Dx)&=C^{\rho'}\Phi(x)-\lambda C^\rho,\\ B(st)&=B(s)\Phi(t)+(-1)^{|s|}\lambda_sB(t). \end{aligned} \tag{B.PE13} \] For the first equality, the first coordinate is \(rdh+r(\rho'a-\lambda\rho-dh)\), and the third is \(th+Hdh+H(\rho'a-\lambda\rho-dh)\); these simplify to the claimed coordinates. Target coordinates are zero. For the product equality, both nonzero coordinates are the corresponding projections of \(h_sa_t+(-1)^{|s|}\lambda_sh_t\); the target coordinate of \(B(s)\) is zero, so no term is missing from its graph product. These identities also verify the compatibility of the comparison-back witnesses with higher choice differentials and compositions.

Now (B.ND9) lifts any specified relative free choice-comparison diagram over \(k\), preserving its already supplied boundary lifts, through \(\pi\). Applying \(\Phi\) and (B.PE13) gives natural higher comparisons and the compatible comparisons back to the original diagram. No claim is made for a nonfree quotient with unchecked relations. The basic shape, on each of the seven labels and with all index maps retained, is \[ \begin{array}{ccc} D^\rho&\xrightarrow{\ A_{\rho',\rho}\ }&D^{\rho'}\\ {C^\rho}\downarrow&&\downarrow{C^{\rho'}}\\ D&\xrightarrow{\ 1\ }&D \end{array} \qquad C^{\rho'}A-C^\rho=DB. \tag{B.PE14} \] This is a homotopy-commutative square, not a strictly commutative one; \(B\) includes its degree-minus-two component. Equations (B.PE12)--(B.PE13) explain how the square varies over the chosen free comparison index.

Geometric hypotheses. The whole roof preserves the unit and is independent of its whole-diagram resolution choices for the seven-object decorated diagram, including the induced bilateral model. This construction uses no acyclic-cone assertion at \(\eta\); it includes the four faces, their target maps and the full cube. It does not assert that two separately constructed geometric diagrams already have this same target or matching shared boundaries. That identification, the full horizontal-composition/base-change overlap assembly, geometric nearby-cycle multiplicative descent, coefficient-system completion and rationalization with derived limits and strict-heart effacement remain required. \(\square\)

Compare envelope choices across geometric refinements

Proposition B.1as (the actual refinement map between envelopes). In the full scope of B.1m, the unit-safe whole envelope in B.1ar is compatible with the actual compactification-refinement dg functor, its induction and its mate. This supplies a common target for an induced old replacement and an independently chosen replacement on the refined model, over the same supplied whole parameter index. It includes the seven source/target labels of the bilateral diagram and the successive-refinement comparisons. An unresolved base-change mate is not inferred from this proper-refinement construction.

Bind the geometric maps before choosing replacements. For a proper refinement \(h:\overline X_0\to\overline X_1\) fixing the protected open and its final target, take \(G=G_h\) exactly as in (B.CR2), including the image of its graph homotopy. Let \(R=G_!\), \(L=F_{0!}\), \(L'=F_{1!}\), \(U=F_0^*\), and \(U'=F_1^*\). The clopen adjunction map (B.CR1) and proper-image composition (B.CR5) give the actual maps \[ \begin{aligned} c_P:L'RP&\xrightarrow{\sim}LP,\\ \kappa_Z:RUZ&\longrightarrow U'Z,\\ \varepsilon'_ZL'\kappa_Z&=\varepsilon_Zc_{UZ},\\ \kappa_{LP}R\eta_P&=U'(c_P)\eta'_{RP}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.ER1} \] These are (B.CR7)--(B.CR9), not chosen isomorphism classes. In particular \(\kappa\) exists on all restriction modules here, by its balanced-tensor formula. Write \(Tq=(RP,Z,q^g)\), \(q^g=\kappa_ZRq\), and \(T(a,w,h)=(Ra,w,\kappa Rh)\), as in (B.FT6). The functor \(T\) is strict dg. Neither its definition nor the following envelope calculation requires the structure map \(q\) to be a quasi-isomorphism.

Use \(r,t,H,j,s\) for the maps of \(W(q)\), and superscript \(g\) for those of \(W'(Tq)\), formed with \(U'\). There is a closed map \[ \begin{aligned} \Theta_q:RW(q)&\longrightarrow W'(Tq),\\ \Theta_q&=(Rr,\kappa_ZRt,\kappa_ZRH),\\ r^g\Theta_q&=Rr,&t^g\Theta_q&=\kappa_ZRt,\\ H^g\Theta_q&=\kappa_ZRH,&\Theta_qRj&=j^g. \end{aligned} \tag{B.ER2} \] The three entries on the second line are the three projections into the envelope, not a decorated graph arrow: their unshifted degrees are \(0,0,-1\). This intrinsic formula uses the actual dg induction on maps; it therefore includes its shift identifications rather than assuming that a choice of bases makes induction commute with shifts literally. Closedness follows from \(d(\kappa RH)=\kappa R(qr-t)=q^gRr-\kappa Rt\). The first two components are closed. The final identity follows from \(rj=1,tj=q,Hj=0\).

For every homogeneous decorated \(f=(a,w,h)\), the comparison is strictly natural: \[ W'(Tf)\Theta_q=\Theta_{q'}RW(f). \tag{B.ER3} \] The first and second projections use naturality of \(r,t,\kappa\). For the third, (B.PE4) gives \(\kappa R(H'W(f))=\kappa R(hr)+(-1)^{|f|}\kappa R(U(w)H)\). Naturality of \(\kappa\) turns its last term into \((-1)^{|f|}U'(w)\kappa RH\), the last coordinate of the other composite. This retains \(h\) and its sign in every degree.

Let \(F,F'\) be the two envelope functors.
