Then \[ \begin{aligned} \tau_q&=(\Theta_q,1_Z,0):TF(q)\longrightarrow F'T(q),\\ D\tau_q&=0,& C^g_q\tau_q&=T(C_q). \end{aligned} \tag{B.ER4} \] The first assertion is \(t^g\Theta=\kappa Rt\); the second uses all three projection identities in (B.ER2). Thus it is an equality of decorated maps, retaining their actual target components. No faithfulness of \(U'\) is invoked. Although \(\Theta\) need not be a chain isomorphism, \(\tau\) is an objectwise graph homotopy equivalence with explicit inverse and witnesses. Put \[ \begin{aligned} \upsilon_q&=(Rj\,r^g,1_Z,H^g),\\ \tau_q\upsilon_q-1&=D(-s^g,0,0),\\ \upsilon_q\tau_q-1&=D(-Rs,0,0). \end{aligned} \tag{B.ER5} \] Closedness of \(\upsilon\) is \(q^gr^g-t^g=dH^g\). The first composite has source component \(j^gr^g\) and witness \(H^g\); the second has \(R(jr)\) and \(\kappa RH\). Equation (B.PE2), including \(ts=-H\), gives the displayed differentials. As with (B.PE5), these inverses are objectwise witnesses, not an asserted natural inverse family. In particular no inverse to \(\kappa\), to a unit, or to a homotopy equivalence as a literal chain isomorphism has been used.

Transport a whole replacement to this actual new target. Let \(D:\mathcal J\to\mathcal A_U\) be the supplied seven-object decorated diagram over its free index, with h-projective source modules at every object. Take \(\rho:V\to WD\) as in (B.PE8). Use the whole induction along \(1_{\mathcal J^{\mathrm{op}}}\otimes G\), identified with pointwise \(R\) by (B.ND8). Define \[ \begin{aligned} \rho^g&=\Theta_D R\rho:RV\longrightarrow W'TD,\\ t^g\rho^g&=\kappa R(t\rho),\\ C^{\rho^g}&=T(C^\rho). \end{aligned} \tag{B.ER6} \] This is a closed natural whole quasi-isomorphism. Here is the necessary check: induction preserves whole h-projectivity by its Hom adjunction, so \(RV\) is whole h-projective. At each index value \(V_i\) and \(W(D_i)\) are h-projective, the former by (B.ND6) and the latter by (B.PE2). Hence \(\rho_i\) is a homotopy equivalence. The dg functor \(R\) preserves that explicit equivalence, and \(\Theta_i\) is one by (B.ER5). Their composite is a quasi-isomorphism at every index value. This is not an application of ordinary induction to an arbitrary quasi-isomorphism, nor a claim that \(WD\) is automatically whole h-projective. Formula (B.ER4) proves the last equality, component by component. The actual source, target and full cube maps of the old diagram therefore compare to the new ones simultaneously.

If \(\rho':V'\to W'TD\) is an independently chosen whole h-projective replacement on that refined model, (B.ND7) now applies to an identified common target. Choose \(a,h\) in the whole Hom complexes with \[ \begin{aligned} \rho'a-\rho^g&=dh,& da&=0,\\ A&=(a,1_Z,t^gh),\\ C^{\rho'}A-T(C^\rho)&=D(r^gh,0,H^gh). \end{aligned} \tag{B.ER7} \] This is precisely (B.PE10)--(B.PE11), now between the independent new model and the transported old one. The graph map \(A\) is a whole homotopy equivalence. The final coordinate has degree minus two and is required. All relative free choice-comparisons and their compatibility with comparison back follow from (B.PE12)--(B.PE13), over this same identified whole target. Values at a different, unconnected parameter index are not silently substituted.

Successive geometric refinements. For \(g\), then \(h\), use the actual induction compositor \(\mu:R_hR_g\to R_{hg}\) from (B.CR4), together with its mate identity. Let \(m_q=(\mu_P,1_Z,0):T_hT_gq\to T_{hg}q\). It is a closed graph isomorphism by that mate identity. On envelopes, \[ \begin{aligned} W''(m_q)\Theta^h_{T_gq}R_h\Theta^g_q &=\Theta^{hg}_q\mu_{W(q)},\\ W''(m_D)\,\rho^{h,g} &=\rho^{hg}\mu_V. \end{aligned} \tag{B.ER8} \] For the first equality the source projection is the naturality equation for \(\mu\) and \(r\). Each of the other two projections is the mate identity \(\kappa^{hg}_Z\mu_{UZ}=\kappa^h_ZR_h\kappa^g_Z\), composed respectively with \(R_hR_gt\) and \(R_hR_gH\). These three projections determine the map into the direct-sum envelope. The second equality follows by naturality of \(\mu\) on \(\rho\). Induction's unit and pentagon identities now give the same equations for every finite refinement string: project to these three components, flatten the ordered balanced tensors, and use (B.CR4)'s actual composition identities. No independently chosen inverse of \(\Theta\) is used to assert coherence. Independent replacement choices at those vertices are subsequently compared in the fixed receiving envelope as in (B.ER7); specified relative free higher boundaries are retained by (B.PE12)--(B.PE13).

Restore all seven bilateral labels. In (B.BT6)--(B.BT8), take \(R=E_1\), and retain the specified closed isomorphisms \(\lambda_i:P_i'\to RP_i\), \(\delta_i:Z_i'\to Z_i\). The normalized object \(\bar q_i=U'(\delta_i^{-1})q_i^g\lambda_i\) has the actual graph isomorphism \[ \begin{aligned} I_i&=(\lambda_i,\delta_i,0):\bar q_i\longrightarrow Tq_i,\\ W'(I_i)&=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_i,U'\delta_i,U'\delta_i),\\ \bar\Theta_i&=W'(I_i^{-1})\Theta_i. \end{aligned} \tag{B.ER9} \] The diagonal formula uses the envelope direct-sum coordinates; it includes the shifted third block with the same degree-zero map. The functor on the normalized diagram is conjugation by the \(I_i\)'s, so (B.ER3) proves naturality of \(\bar\Theta\) for every homogeneous arrow. Its receiving target is now the normalized geometric envelope, with the actual target at \(C\) changed by \(\delta_C=Va\), as well as the changes at \(A\) and the unit vertices. The two horizontal source comparisons \(\lambda_{Q_0^u}=d_{Q_0}^{-1}\), \(\lambda_{R_0^u}=d_{R_0}^{-1}\) are not dropped.

The transported whole source remains \(RV_i\); its target label becomes \(Z_i'\). Its actual replacement and comparison-back components are \[ \begin{aligned} \bar\rho_i&=\bar\Theta_iR\rho_i,\\ \bar q_i^{\bar\rho}&=U'(\delta_i^{-1})\kappa_{Z_i}R(t_i\rho_i),\\ \bar C_i&=(\lambda_i^{-1}R(r_i\rho_i),1_{Z_i'}, U'(\delta_i^{-1})\kappa_{Z_i}R(H_i\rho_i)). \end{aligned} \tag{B.ER10} \] The \(\bar\rho\)'s are whole quasi-isomorphisms because (B.ER9) is an actual isomorphism after (B.ER6). Compare them with independent whole replacements of \(W'\bar D\) by (B.ER7). The \(\lambda_i\)'s act on the old comparison-back source, not by an invented isomorphism on the newly chosen \(RV_i\). Equations (B.BT12)--(B.BT13) and functoriality of \(W'\) supply the normalized versions of (B.ER8), with their nonidentity target components. Every original decorated face, the \(\beta\) and \(\bar\gamma\) components, and the nested second and cube coefficients are retained: (B.ER3) applies to their actual homogeneous arrows, and (B.ER9) only conjugates by the displayed graph isomorphisms. Ordered bar differentials are preserved by these dg functors; no absent decorated lift is created.

Check the actual adjunction targets as well. Denote by \(e_t,\beta\) the transposes of \(t,H\) from (B.PE6). Let \(e_{t^g},\beta^g\) be their new-envelope counterparts. Transposing the second and third projections in (B.ER2), using the counit identity in (B.ER1), gives actual maps before restriction: \[ \begin{aligned} e_{q^g}&=e_qc_P,\\ e_{t^g}L'\Theta_q&=e_tc_{W(q)},\\ \beta^g L'\Theta_q&=\beta c_{W(q)},\\ e_{\bar t_i}L'\bar\Theta_i&=\delta_i^{-1}e_{t_i}c_{W(q_i)},\\ \bar\beta_iL'\bar\Theta_i&=\delta_i^{-1}\beta_i c_{W(q_i)}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.ER11} \] For example \(\operatorname{Adj}'(\kappa RH)=\varepsilon'L'(\kappa RH)=\varepsilon c_{UZ}L'RH=\varepsilon LHc_W=\beta c_W\), by naturality of \(c\) for the degree-minus-one \(H\). The other lines are the same computation, and target conjugation gives the last two. Their differentials are the transported (B.PE6) unit/counit square; its nonzero graded naturality defect (B.PE7) is retained through (B.ER3). At a canonical old unit, \(e_q=1\) and \(e_{q^g}=c_P\); restoration by the prescribed target isomorphism gives the new canonical unit using (B.ER1). A general whole-envelope replacement of that object is still compared by (B.PE6), not declared literally canonical or quasi-isomorphic to the unit's target.

The resulting comparison diagram is \[ \begin{array}{ccc} TFD&\xrightarrow{\ \tau_D\ }&F'TD\\ {T(C_D)}\downarrow&&\downarrow{C^g_D}\\ TD&\xrightarrow{\ 1\ }&TD. \end{array} \tag{B.ER12} \] This square commutes strictly by (B.ER4). Replacing its top row by independently chosen whole resolutions gives the witnessed square (B.ER7), whose second witness must not be erased. Equations (B.ER8)--(B.ER11) specify its refinement composition, bilateral labels and actual adjunction interfaces.

Proper refinement and geometric inverse image. The common target required for independent choices across the actual proper-refinement maps, including their normalized bilateral labels, is defined over the specified whole index. This uses the globally defined mate \(\kappa\) of (B.CR8). For geometric base change, the left inverse comparison in (B.BM15) is defined on resolved h-projective inputs. Equations (B.BM16)--(B.BM18) intentionally use \(\operatorname{Adj}(Ve^0_N\theta_{P_0})\), not \(\theta_{U_0N}\). Therefore (B.ER2) cannot be reused there by postulating a mate on unresolved \(U_0N\). The remaining changing-index assembly must retain those resolved-only transposes, the actual mixed cell (B.GC12)--(B.GC13), both inverse witnesses and the nested second coefficient (B.MX12). Geometric nearby-cycle multiplicative descent, whole coefficient completion and rationalization with derived limits and strict-heart effacement are not established by this construction. \(\square\)

Resolved base-change transport and its comparison witnesses

Proposition B.1at (transport without an unresolved mate). The resolved left comparison supplied by (B.KC15) transports the decorated objects, homogeneous arrows and whole path envelopes used above. Its homotopies have an explicit signed naturality witness, to which the existing bar comparison applies. This identifies the receiving envelope for independently chosen replacements of the transported diagram. It does not make the right mate invertible, identify unrelated replacement targets, or supply the higher changing-index assembly without its boundary checks.

Keep the domain of the comparison explicit. Work with actual dg adjunctions \(L_i\dashv U_i\), for \(i=0,1\), between the chosen module models. Let \(S\) act on their source categories and \(V\) on their target categories. Assume that \(S\) preserves h-projectives and that a closed degree-zero dg-natural map \[ \theta_P:L_1SP\longrightarrow VL_0P \tag{B.ZT1} \] is supplied on the full dg subcategory of admitted h-projective source models. In applications it is a map of the whole kernel models, not independently chosen values at each object. Naturality includes nonclosed homogeneous maps. No value on an unresolved \(U_0Z\) is assumed. Write \(\operatorname{Adj}_i\) for the chain isomorphism from maps out of \(L_i\) to maps into \(U_i\). For \(q:P\to U_0Z\), set \(e_q=\varepsilon^0_ZL_0q\). For a degree-\(n\) decorated arrow \(f=(a,w,h):q\to q'\), set \(\beta_f=\varepsilon^0_{Z'}L_0h\), of degree \(n-1\). Define \[ \begin{aligned} \zeta_q&=\operatorname{Adj}_1(Ve_q\,\theta_P),\\ T_\theta(q)&=(SP,VZ,\zeta_q),\\ T_\theta(f)&=(Sa,Vw,\operatorname{Adj}_1(V\beta_f\,\theta_P)). \end{aligned} \tag{B.ZT2} \] This is a strict dg functor on the admitted decorated category. Indeed, the transpose of the third component of \(Df\) is \(e_{q'}L_0a-we_q-d\beta_f\). Naturality of the closed \(\theta\) identifies its transported first term with \(Ve_{q'}\theta_{P'}L_1Sa\); the chain adjunction then gives exactly (B.FT3). For a degree-\(m\) arrow \(g=(b,v,k)\), the transpose of the composite witness is \(\beta_gL_0a+(-1)^m v\beta_f\). The same naturality identity proves preservation of composition. The unit has zero witness. This argument uses \(\theta\) only on h-projective sources, and does not require \(q\) or \(\theta\) to be invertible.

The receiving envelope. Use \(r,t,H,j,s\) for the path envelope \(W(q)\) of (B.PE1)--(B.PE2). Its source is h-projective because \(W(q)\) is homotopy equivalent to \(P\), even when \(U_0Z\) is not h-projective. Put \(e_t=\varepsilon^0_ZL_0t\) and \(\beta=\varepsilon^0_ZL_0H\). Use superscript \(*\) for the envelope \(W'(T_\theta q)\) formed with \(U_1\). Define a map by its three envelope projections: \[ \begin{aligned} \Theta_q:SW(q)&\longrightarrow W'(T_\theta q),\\ r^*\Theta_q&=Sr,\\ t^*\Theta_q&=\operatorname{Adj}_1(Ve_t\,\theta_{W(q)}),\\ H^*\Theta_q&=\operatorname{Adj}_1(V\beta\,\theta_{W(q)}). \end{aligned} \tag{B.ZT3} \] These are envelope projections of unshifted degrees \(0,0,-1\), not the entries of a decorated graph arrow. Since \(d\beta=e_qL_0r-e_t\), their differentials satisfy \(d(H^*\Theta)=\zeta_qSr-t^*\Theta\). The first two projections are closed, so \(\Theta\) is a closed map into the direct-sum envelope. Naturality of \(\theta\) on \(j\) and \(s\), with (B.PE2), also gives \[ \begin{aligned} \Theta_qSj&=j^*,\\ (t^*\Theta_q)Ss&=-H^*\Theta_q,\\ (H^*\Theta_q)Ss&=0. \end{aligned} \tag{B.ZT4} \] For every homogeneous decorated \(f:q\to q'\), \[ W'(T_\theta f)\Theta_q=\Theta_{q'}SW(f). \tag{B.ZT5} \] The first projection is naturality of \(r\). For the second use \(t'W(f)=U_0(w)t\), transpose and apply naturality of \(\theta\) on \(W(f)\). For the third use the complete equation \(H'W(f)=hr+(-1)^nU_0(w)H\). Its transpose has both terms; naturality on \(r\) turns the first into the transported witness composed with \(Sr\), and the second remains \((-1)^nU_1(Vw)H^*\Theta\). This is the third projection of the left side. In particular the graph homotopy is not discarded to obtain naturality.

Let \(F,F'\) be the envelope functors and \(C,C^*\) their comparison-back maps. There are explicit graph maps and inverse witnesses \[ \begin{aligned} \tau_q&=(\Theta_q,1_{VZ},0):T_\theta Fq\longrightarrow F'T_\theta q,\\ \upsilon_q&=(Sj\,r^*,1_{VZ},H^*),\\ C^*_q\tau_q&=T_\theta C_q,\\ \tau_q\upsilon_q-1&=D(-s^*,0,0),\\ \upsilon_q\tau_q-1&=D(-Ss,0,0). \end{aligned} \tag{B.ZT6} \] The transpose defining the structure map of \(T_\theta Fq\) is the second projection in (B.ZT3); hence \(\tau\) is closed. Closedness of \(\upsilon\) follows from \(t^*\Theta Sj=\zeta_q\) and \(dH^*=\zeta_qr^*-t^*\). The two composite sources are \(j^*r^*\) and \(S(jr)\), with witnesses \(H^*\) and \(H^*\Theta\). Now (B.PE2) and (B.ZT4) give the two displayed boundaries. Thus \(\Theta\) is a homotopy equivalence without inverting \(\theta\). The inverse \(\upsilon\) is an objectwise witness, not an asserted strictly natural inverse family.

The actual target-side transposes are retained as well: \[ \begin{aligned} e_{\zeta_q}&=Ve_q\,\theta_P,\\ e_{t^*}L_1\Theta_q&=Ve_t\,\theta_{W(q)},\\ \beta^*L_1\Theta_q&=V\beta\,\theta_{W(q)}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.ZT7} \] Each equality is the chain adjunction applied to its defining projection; these are actual maps before restriction, not conclusions from faithfulness of \(U_1\). At an old canonical unit \(e_q=1\), the first map is \(\theta_P\), not an invented identity. In general the unit is not a quasi-isomorphism, and its envelope still uses (B.PE6)--(B.PE7).

Whole choices over the transported diagram. Let \(D\) be the supplied decorated diagram over its free parameter index, and \(\rho:R\to WD\) a whole h-projective replacement. Require the whole extension of \(S\) to agree with pointwise transport and preserve whole h-projectivity. Induction along a strict source functor has this property by (B.ND8). For the actual kernel functor \(S=T_{P_u}\), it follows instead from (B.RK1): each kernel column is h-projective, and tensor transport takes a whole representable cell at \((j,X)\) to \(\mathcal J(j,-)\otimes P_u(-,X)\). Hom from this diagram into an acyclic diagram is Hom from the h-projective column into its acyclic value at \(j\). Thus the image cell is whole h-projective. Tensoring the graded-split semifree filtration and using the recursive primitive argument of B.1l proves the assertion for a semifree source; a general h-projective source is homotopy equivalent to such a source. This identifies the whole functor without equating kernel transport with strict-functor induction. Require \(\theta\) to be natural over that same whole index. Then \[ \begin{aligned} \rho^\theta&=\Theta_D S\rho:SR\longrightarrow W'T_\theta D,\\ C^{\rho^\theta}&=T_\theta C^\rho. \end{aligned} \tag{B.ZT8} \] This is a whole quasi-isomorphism: evaluation of \(R\) is h-projective by (B.ND6), and \(WD\) is objectwise h-projective by (B.PE2). Therefore each \(\rho_i\) is a homotopy equivalence. A dg functor preserves those witnesses, and \(\Theta_i\) is a homotopy equivalence by (B.ZT6). This does not claim that induction preserves an arbitrary quasi-isomorphism. It also does not assert that \(WD\) was whole h-projective. An independent whole replacement \(\rho':R'\to W'T_\theta D\) now has this same identified whole target. Apply (B.PE10)--(B.PE13): if \(\rho'a-\rho^\theta=dh\), its comparison-back boundary has all three entries \((r^*h,0,H^*h)\), including the degree-minus-two entry. Bilateral normalization, when supplied, uses the actual graph isomorphisms of (B.ER9), with their seven target labels. It does not create isomorphisms between independently chosen replacement sources.

A homotopy of left comparisons is generally not strict naturality. Suppose \(\theta'-\theta=dK\), where \(K\) is a degree-minus-one graded-natural map on the same admitted whole sources. Put \[ \begin{aligned} k_q&=\operatorname{Adj}_1(Ve_q\,K_P),\\ B_q&=(1_{SP},1_{VZ},k_q):T_\theta q\longrightarrow T_{\theta'}q,\\ b_K(f)&=(0,0,(-1)^{n+1}\operatorname{Adj}_1(V\beta_f\,K_P)). \end{aligned} \tag{B.ZT9} \] The graph map \(B_q\) is closed, with inverse obtained from \(-K\). The arrow \(b_K(f)\) has graph degree \(n-1\); its third coordinate has degree \(n-2\). These arrows satisfy \[ \begin{aligned} Db_K(f)+b_K(Df) &=B_{q'}T_\theta(f)-T_{\theta'}(f)B_q,\\ b_K(gf) &=b_K(g)T_\theta(f)+(-1)^{|g|}T_{\theta'}(g)b_K(f),\\ b_K(1)&=0. \end{aligned} \tag{B.ZT10} \] For the first identity, graded naturality reads \(K_{P'}L_1Sa=(-1)^nVL_0a\,K_P\). The transpose of the difference's third component is consequently \[ (-1)^n V(d\beta_f+\beta_{Df})K_P-V\beta_f\,dK_P. \tag{B.ZT11} \] Taking the differential of the last entry in (B.ZT9), remembering that \(D(0,0,x)=(0,0,-dx)\), and then adding \(b_K(Df)\), gives exactly (B.ZT11). For composition substitute \(\beta_{gf}=\beta_gL_0a+(-1)^{|g|}v\beta_f\). Moving \(K\) past the degree-\(n\) map \(L_1Sa\) supplies \((-1)^n\); the two remaining terms are precisely the two products in (B.ZT10). The unit has \(\beta_1=0\). Thus the sign and degree of this witness are essential, not optional corrections to an otherwise strictly natural family.

These are exactly (B.KC9)'s equations. For a fixed graph object \(Q\), apply the covariant dg functor \(\operatorname{Hom}(Q,-)\) to obtain its left-module comparison, and then use the signed length-one bar map (B.KC10). Its quasi-isomorphism conclusion retains that proposition's h-projective right-module hypothesis. If a contravariant Hom realization is used instead, the opposite-category signs of (B.KC11) must be inserted. This passage supplies a witnessed bar comparison, not permission to erase \(b_K\). For successive \(K\) and \(K'\), from \(\theta\) to \(\theta'\) and then to \(\theta''\), direct graph multiplication gives \[ \begin{aligned} B^{K+K'}_q&=B^{K'}_qB^K_q,\\ b_{K+K'}(f)&=b_{K'}(f)B^K_q+B^{K'}_{q'}b_K(f). \end{aligned} \tag{B.ZT12} \] The first equation adds the two third coordinates; in the second, each zero source and target component leaves only its displayed third coordinate. Higher homotopies between these choices still require their own relative boundary equations.

Vertical pasting uses the same receiving envelope. For a second comparison \(\theta_2:L_2S_2\to V_2L_1\), define \(\theta_{21}=V_2\theta_1\,\theta_{2,S_1}\). With the canonical ordered induction associators, \[ \begin{aligned} T_{\theta_2}T_{\theta_1}&=T_{\theta_{21}},\\ \Theta^{21}_q&=\Theta^2_{T_{\theta_1}q}\,S_2\Theta^1_q. \end{aligned} \tag{B.ZT13} \] The first equality follows by transposing twice in (B.ZT2): the intermediate transpose is exactly \(V_1e_q\theta_{1,P}\), or \(V_1\beta_f\theta_{1,P}\) for the witness. For the second project first to the source, giving \(S_2S_1r\). Transpose the second projection. Naturality of \(\theta_2\) on the closed map \(\Theta^1_q\), followed by (B.ZT7), gives \(V_2V_1e_t\,V_2\theta_{1,W}\theta_{2,S_1W}\). The third projection is the same calculation with \(\beta\), so all three agree. This proof never evaluates a comparison on an unresolved target. The unit comparison gives the identity, and ordered tensor associativity proves the corresponding equality for every finite vertical string. This is vertical pasting; the nested horizontal coefficient in (B.BM18) remains separate.

The envelope comparison and its actual target square are \[ \begin{array}{ccc} T_\theta FD&\xrightarrow{\ \tau_D\ }&F'T_\theta D\\ {T_\theta C_D}\downarrow&&\downarrow{C^*_D}\\ T_\theta D&\xrightarrow{\ 1\ }&T_\theta D. \end{array} \tag{B.ZT14} \] It commutes strictly. Replacing its top sources by independent whole choices introduces precisely the second comparison witness in (B.ZT8), not a new assertion that their chosen chain models coincide.

Exact geometric application and the remaining boundary. In (B.KC15)--(B.KC16), use the actual whole right kernels and the specified inverse: \(L_0=T_{H_f}\), \(L_1=T_{H_{f'}}\), \(S=T_{P_u}\), and \(V=T_{P_g}\). Admit the whole h-projective kernel sources and their induction models already constructed there. The inverse is chosen in the whole kernel Hom complex with both inverse homotopies, so the required source naturality is retained. Its resolved transpose is exactly (B.BM16), and (B.ZT7) is exactly the last equation of (B.KC16). The actual proper--open replacement edges remain the ones in (B.KC4), (B.KC6)--(B.KC7), and (B.GC13); they have not been replaced by abstract isomorphism classes.

In particular, if \(r_1c-\zeta_q=db\), the right-mate comparison is the closed decorated arrow \((c,1,b):T_\theta q\to r_1\). Apply the envelope functor to this arrow, retaining \(b\). Unless \(c\) is separately proved a homotopy equivalence, its envelopes are not thereby interchangeable as replacement targets. Equation (B.ZT6) does not imply that the right mate is invertible. The vertical witness in (B.BM17) is retained after transporting the first counit homotopy; the nested horizontal witness is still the two-term expression in (B.BM18), with the second coefficient (B.MX12). Its shared boundaries with (B.GC12)--(B.GC13) and the four-face diagram must be checked over the actual changing index before invoking (B.ND9). The formulas above give transport and comparisons on resolved inputs; they do not establish that full assembly. Geometric nearby multiplicative descent, whole coefficient transport and rationalization with derived limits and strict-heart effacement are not established by this construction. \(\square\)

Lift changing diagrams without inverting comparison arrows

Proposition B.1au (resolve the receiving envelope, not the comparison arrow). Over a specified common free parameter index and receiving adjunction model, independently chosen whole path-envelope replacements admit a dg projection onto the category of actual decorated diagrams. This projection is surjective and a quasi-isomorphism on Hom complexes even when the base comparison arrow is not invertible. It lifts any supplied relative free diagram, retaining its actual target maps and a second comparison-back witness. Applied to the typed four-face and cube provider, it preserves every supplied boundary. It does not construct a missing geometric base face or turn a homotopy-natural family into a strict natural map by forgetting its witnesses.

Objects and their receiving targets. Fix the receiving dg functor \(U\) and a free index \(\mathcal J\) as in B.1ar. Let \(\mathcal B\) be the small labelled dg category of the admitted diagrams \(D:\mathcal J\to\mathcal A_U\), whose source modules are h-projective at each value; its arrows are the full graded natural transformations. In particular target-side maps are retained before restriction. For every chosen object use a whole h-projective replacement \[ \rho_i:R_i\xrightarrow{\simeq}WD_i, \qquad q_i^\rho=t_i\rho_i, \qquad C_i^\rho=(r_i\rho_i,1,H_i\rho_i). \tag{B.CE1} \] These are the whole diagrams of (B.PE8), not just unrelated objectwise resolutions. The whole source \(R_i\) exists by (B.ND5). Every value is h-projective by (B.ND6). The comparison \(C_i^\rho\) is strictly natural over \(\mathcal J\) and an objectwise graph homotopy equivalence by (B.PE9). It is not asserted to have a whole strictly natural homotopy inverse. No quasi-isomorphism assumption is made on the original structure maps of \(D_i\), including its unit vertices.

Make a dg category \(\mathcal R_W\) of these pairs \((D_i,\rho_i)\). A degree-\(n\) arrow is \(x=(f,a,h)\), where \(f:D_0\to D_1\) is a degree-\(n\) graded natural decorated arrow, \(a:R_0\to R_1\) has degree \(n\), and \(h:R_0\to WD_1\) has degree \(n-1\). The last two are whole graded natural maps. Define \[ \begin{aligned} Dx&=(Df,da,\rho_1a-W(f)\rho_0-dh),\\ \pi(x)&=f. \end{aligned} \tag{B.CE2} \] For \(x=(f,a,h)\) of degree \(n\) and \(y=(g,b,k)\) of degree \(m\), put \[ yx=(gf,ba,ka+(-1)^mW(g)h), \qquad 1_{(D,\rho)}=(1_D,1_R,0). \tag{B.CE3} \] These are the arrow-graph formulas applied to the strict dg functor \(W\). Its source map is retained as the full \(f\), not recovered from \(W(f)\). Expanding the third differential uses \(dW(f)=W(Df)\), \(d\rho_i=0\), and the ordinary Hom Leibniz rule; its cross terms cancel, giving \(D^2=0\) and the graded product rule. The three terms of a triple product have coefficients \(1,(-1)^{|z|},(-1)^{|z|+|y|}\), proving associativity. Units follow directly. Thus \(\pi\) is a strict dg functor, whether or not \(W\) or \(U\) is faithful.

Projection is degreewise surjective: \((f,0,0)\) is a graded lift of any \(f\). Its Hom kernel is \[ \begin{aligned} \ker\pi^n&=\operatorname{Hom}^n(R_0,R_1) \oplus\operatorname{Hom}^{n-1}(R_0,WD_1),\\ d(a,h)&=(da,\rho_1a-dh). \end{aligned} \tag{B.CE4} \] All Hom complexes here are whole natural Hom complexes over the index-product category. Postcomposition by \(\rho_1\) is a quasi-isomorphism on them by (B.ND7), since \(R_0\) is whole h-projective and \(\rho_1\) is objectwise a quasi-isomorphism. Its shifted cone (B.CE4) is therefore acyclic. The map used in this argument is \(\rho_1\), not \(q_1\), \(t_1\rho_1\), a unit, or the base comparison \(f\). This is the reason a noninvertible right mate presents no obstruction to lifting its arrow.

The lifted decorated diagram and its full comparison back. Write \(f=(a_f,w_f,h_f)\) at each parameter value. There is a strict dg functor into the category of whole decorated diagrams, \[ \Phi(D_i,\rho_i)=D_i^\rho, \qquad \Phi(f,a,h)=(a,w_f,t_1h). \tag{B.CE5} \] For the differential, use \(t_1W(f)=U(w_f)t_0\); applying \(t_1\) to the third coordinate in (B.CE2) gives exactly the graph differential of (B.CE5). The same identity proves preservation of (B.CE3). Whole graded naturality also holds: for an index arrow of degree \(l\), \(h\) moves past it with \((-1)^{(n-1)l}\), exactly the product of the graph's third-coordinate sign \((-1)^l\) and the degree-\(n\) naturality sign \((-1)^{nl}\). This retains \(w_f\) itself, not only its image under \(U\).

For every homogeneous \(x\), define the degree-\(n-1\) decorated map \[ B(x)=(r_1h,0,H_1h):D_0^\rho\longrightarrow D_1. \tag{B.CE6} \] Its third coordinate has degree \(n-2\). This is a whole graded natural map even though \(H_1\) alone is not natural. Indeed substitute \(H_{1,j}W(D_1(u))=h_{D_1(u)}r_{1,i}+(-1)^{|u|}U(w_{D_1(u)})H_{1,i}\) from (B.PE4), and then the graded naturality of \(h\). The two terms are precisely those in the graph product with \(B(x)\). Direct computation gives \[ \begin{aligned} DB(x)+B(Dx)&=C_1^\rho\Phi(x)-fC_0^\rho,\\ B(yx)&=B(y)\Phi(x)+(-1)^m gB(x),\\ B(1)&=0. \end{aligned} \tag{B.CE7} \] For the first equation the source component reduces to \(r_1\rho_1a-r_1W(f)\rho_0\). The third component is \(t_1h+H_1(\rho_1a-W(f)\rho_0)\), using \(dH_1=q_1r_1-t_1\). Equation (B.PE4) identifies it with the third component on the right, including \(h_fr_0\rho_0\) and its signed target term. The target components cancel before restriction. For the product equation, its third component follows from \(H_2W(g)h=h_gr_1h+(-1)^mU(w_g)H_1h\). The term involving \(h_g\) must be retained; deleting the base graph homotopy would change the product law. These are also the algebraic comparison equations of (B.KC9). Any use of its bar comparison still retains (B.KC10)'s source-projectivity and (B.KC11)'s variance hypotheses.

A single arrow, then its composites. For a closed degree-zero \(f:D_0\to D_1\), (B.ND7) lifts the actual whole map \(W(f)\rho_0\). Choose \[ \begin{aligned} da&=0,&\rho_1a-W(f)\rho_0&=dh,\\ \widetilde f&=(a,w_f,t_1h),\\ C_1^\rho\widetilde f-fC_0^\rho&=D(r_1h,0,H_1h). \end{aligned} \tag{B.CE8} \] The target is still \(WD_1\), not an identification of \(WD_0\) with \(WD_1\). The source map \(a\) need not be a quasi-isomorphism. In particular the inverse witnesses for the envelope itself in (B.ZT6) do not supply an inverse to \(\widetilde f\).

If \(x,y\) are closed lifts of \(f,g\), and \(z\) is an independently chosen closed lift of the same actual composite \(gf\), then \(yx-z\) is a closed kernel element. Acyclicity gives a degree-minus-one \(K\) with \[ \begin{aligned} DK&=yx-z,&\pi K&=0,\\ D\Phi(K)&=\Phi(y)\Phi(x)-\Phi(z),\\ DB(K)&=C_2^\rho\Phi(K)-B(yx)+B(z). \end{aligned} \tag{B.CE9} \] The last equation is (B.CE7) applied to \(K\). Here \(B(K)\) has degree minus two, with a degree-minus-three third coordinate. It is the compatibility witness between the two comparison-back homotopies. Comparing different geometric base composites instead requires their actual supplied base comparison; a zero-base kernel filler cannot establish that missing fact.

Every specified relative free boundary is lifted, not guessed. Let \(\mathcal K\) be obtained from \(\mathcal K_0\) by freely adjoining homogeneous generators in well-founded order, with their differentials in earlier stages. Let \(E:\mathcal K\to\mathcal B\) be the supplied strict base diagram and suppose its already fixed boundary has a compatible lift into \(\mathcal R_W\). At a degree-\(n\) generator \(v\), take any graded lift \(x_0\) of \(E(v)\). If \(L\) is the earlier lift, set \[ \delta=Dx_0-L(dv),\qquad \pi\delta=0,\quad D\delta=0,\qquad DK=\delta,\quad L(v)=x_0-K. \tag{B.CE10} \] The cycle condition uses the checked differential of the free presentation and the earlier dg lift: \(D L(dv)=L(d^2v)=0\). The kernel primitive \(K\) has degree \(n\) and exists by (B.CE4). Extend multiplicatively; identities stay the identities of (B.CE3). At a limit stage retain all earlier assignments. This is the concrete relative construction of (B.ND9), now over actual changing diagrams instead of the scalar-only projection of (B.PE12). Applying \(\Phi\) and (B.CE7) retains every higher comparison and its compatible comparison back. It is not a claim that a nonfree quotient or an unverified boundary admits such a lift.

For the existing seven labelled objects, take the actual targets of (B.FT3), the four decorated faces and the endpoint bridge checked in (B.FT4), and the full cube checked in (B.FT5). In its supplied free presentation, (B.CE10) can keep already chosen lower faces fixed. The retained base coordinate of the lifted cube is exactly the original \(\mathbf P(f_H)\), including its degree-minus-four third coordinate. The new source maps and witnesses are chosen to satisfy that full boundary, not just its image after restriction. The target component of every \(\Phi(x)\) remains \(w_f\), so neither \(\beta\) nor \(\bar\gamma\) is erased. The finite diagnostic accompanying this construction uses independent resolution models at all seven objects, lifts the supplied lower and upper faces before the change faces, and finally lifts the full cube with its given differential. It checks these algebraic identities, not the separate geometric identification of a new overlap diagram.

Change the parameter index without assuming projectivity survives restriction. For a dg functor \(\psi:\mathcal J'\to\mathcal J\), where \(\mathcal J'\) is again an admitted free index, restriction is pointwise. It commutes with \(W\) and preserves objectwise quasi-isomorphisms, but need not preserve whole h-projectivity. Instead choose a new whole h-projective replacement \(\lambda:R^\psi\to\psi^*R\) by (B.ND5), and set \[ \begin{aligned} \rho^\psi&=(\psi^*\rho)\lambda: R^\psi\longrightarrow W(\psi^*D),\\ I_\lambda&=(\lambda,1,0): (\psi^*D)^{\rho^\psi}\longrightarrow\psi^*(D^\rho),\\ (\psi^*C^\rho)I_\lambda&=C^{\rho^\psi}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.CE11} \] The first map is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism and its source is whole h-projective over the new index. Each value of \(\psi^*R\) is h-projective because it is a value of \(R\); hence each \(\lambda\) is a homotopy equivalence. The proof of (B.PE9) applied valuewise makes \(I_\lambda\) an objectwise graph homotopy equivalence. Its source, target and third coordinates give the last equality directly. No inverse of a unit and no assertion about \(\psi\otimes1\) being a quasi-equivalence is used.

For two restrictions, compose the two actual maps to the restricted old source: \((\chi^*\lambda_\psi)\lambda_\chi\). The resulting envelope map and an independently chosen replacement for \((\psi\chi)^*D\) have the same literal receiving envelope. Equations (B.PE10)--(B.PE13), or the identity-base case of (B.CE2)--(B.CE10), compare them with all specified relative free choice boundaries. Do not replace this re-resolution by a claim that the initially restricted source is already whole h-projective.

Bind the noninvertible geometric arrows. For the actual (B.KC16) or (B.BM16) data, the closed arrow to be lifted is \[ f_{\mathrm{bc}}=(c,1,b):T_\theta q_0\longrightarrow r_1, \qquad r_1c-\zeta_{q_0}=db. \tag{B.CE12} \] Both objects are in the same receiving \(\mathcal A_{U_1}\) after the resolved transport of B.1at. Use its supplied whole parameter scope; for a single instance the index has one object. Equation (B.CE8) applies to this actual arrow even if \(c\) is not a quasi-isomorphism. The two independently chosen envelopes are distinct receiving objects connected by \(W(f_{\mathrm{bc}})\), not silently equated. This is also valid at non-quasi-isomorphic unit structure maps, because the acyclic projection still uses the whole envelope replacement \(\rho_1\).

For two geometric base changes, work in the final receiving category. The three objects are \(T_{\theta_{21}}q_0\), \(T_{\theta_2}q_1\), and \(q_2\). The actual composite of \(T_{\theta_2}f_1\) with \(f_2\) is \[ \begin{aligned} c_{21}&=c_2S_2c_1,\\ b_{21}&=b_2S_2c_1+ \operatorname{Adj}_2(V_2D_1\,\theta_{2,S_1P_0}),\\ D_1&=\varepsilon^1 L_1b_1. \end{aligned} \tag{B.CE13} \] This is exactly (B.BM17), using (B.ZT2) on the first arrow's third coordinate and (B.ZT13) on its source object. Thus the replacement-level composition comparison (B.CE9) has a specified geometric base composite. A different independently chosen geometric arrow must first be related to that base composite by its actual Hom witness; it is not automatically the same arrow. Horizontal composition still retains (B.BM18)'s nested two-term witness and the second folding coefficient (B.MX12).

For any one closed lifted comparison the full square is \[ \begin{array}{ccc} D_0^\rho&\xrightarrow{\ \Phi(x)\ }&D_1^\rho\\ {C_0^\rho}\downarrow&&\downarrow{C_1^\rho}\\ D_0&\xrightarrow{\ f\ }&D_1, \end{array} \qquad C_1^\rho\Phi(x)-fC_0^\rho=DB(x). \tag{B.CE14} \] The bottom arrow may be noninvertible. The square is witnessed, not strictly commutative, and (B.CE9)--(B.CE10) keep its higher comparisons compatible.

Changing geometric presentations. The common receiving models for actual noninvertible comparison arrows, independently selected whole resolutions, and index re-restrictions are given by the preceding construction. To use this across changing geometric presentations, first put their maps in the actual common receiving category via the checked B.1as--B.1at transports and their specified index maps. The family \(B_q\) from (B.ZT9) is generally not strictly natural; retain (B.ZT10)'s witness and its actual strict bar/free roof before treating it as a map of whole diagrams. The geometric (B.GC13) edge, the nested (B.MX12) coefficient and their higher shared boundaries must be verified in that base presentation. Surjectivity of \(\pi\) cannot create a missing geometric face or certify an unchecked relation. Full changing-model horizontal/composition assembly, nearby-cycle multiplicative descent, normalized coefficient completion and rationalization with derived limits and strict-heart higher effacement are not established by this construction. \(\square\)

Strictify the recorded comparison homotopy on a free cylinder

Proposition B.1av (a strict common index retains the naturality defect). The actual comparison of B.1at, including its arrow witness (B.ZT10), has an explicit common strict dg parameter cylinder whenever its parameter category is presented semifreely. Both endpoint sections of this cylinder are quasi-equivalences. Its realization in the receiving decorated category retains the actual target maps and the full comparison homotopy. The construction works over any commutative coefficient ring and for unbounded Hom complexes. It requires neither a tensor-flatness hypothesis nor a strict naturality assertion about the original comparison. It supplies the strict roof for the comparison described at the end of B.1au; separately prescribed geometric higher boundaries still have to satisfy their compatibility equations.

The comparison data and normalization. Let \(\mathcal A\) be a small semifree dg category: its underlying graded category is free on homogeneous generators in a well-founded order, and each generator's differential is a finite linear combination of earlier paths, possibly including identities. Let \(N_0,N_1:\mathcal A\to\mathcal E\) be strict dg functors, with closed degree-zero objectwise isomorphisms \(B_a:N_0a\to N_1a\). Suppose the supplied linear arrow assignment \(b_f:N_0a\to N_1b\), of degree \(|f|-1\) for \(f:a\to b\), satisfies \[ \begin{aligned} D b_f+b_{df}&=B_bN_0(f)-N_1(f)B_a,\\ b_{gf}&=b_gN_0(f)+(-1)^{|g|}N_1(g)b_f, \qquad b_1=0. \end{aligned} \tag{B.CY1} \] These are the exact identities (B.KC9) and (B.ZT10), not just an equality on closed arrows in the homotopy category. For B.1at use \(N_0=T_\theta D\), \(N_1=T_{\theta'}D\), \(B_a=B_{D(a)}\), and \(b_f=b_K(D(f))\) for the actual parameter diagram \(D\). The inverse of each \(B_a\) is its explicit graph arrow with \(-k_{D(a)}\). Thus the isomorphism hypothesis is satisfied here; an arbitrary objectwise homotopy equivalence is not silently given a strict inverse.

Conjugate the second diagram onto the first diagram's objects, putting \[ \begin{aligned} \overline N_1(a)&=N_0(a),& \overline N_1(f)&=B_b^{-1}N_1(f)B_a,\\ h_f&=B_b^{-1}b_f. \end{aligned} \tag{B.CY2} \] Closedness and the inverse identities for \(B\) show directly that \(\overline N_1\) is a strict dg functor. Multiplying (B.CY1) by \(B_b^{-1}\) gives \[ \begin{aligned} D h_f+h_{df}&=N_0(f)-\overline N_1(f),\\ h_{gf}&=h_gN_0(f)+(-1)^{|g|}\overline N_1(g)h_f, \qquad h_1=0. \end{aligned} \tag{B.CY3} \] The family \(B\) is strictly natural from \(\overline N_1\) to \(N_1\) by definition. It is not strictly natural from \(N_0\) to \(N_1\) in general. Normalization has not asserted that \(h\) or \(b\) vanishes.

Adjoin contractible pairs, not new relations. Form \(C\mathcal A\) with the same objects, the copy \(i_0\mathcal A\), and two free arrows for each original generator \(t:a\to b\) of degree \(n\): \[ \begin{aligned} z_t,v_t &:a\longrightarrow b,& |z_t|&=n-1,& |v_t|&=n,\\ dz_t&=-v_t,&dv_t&=0. \end{aligned} \tag{B.CY4} \] There are no quotient relations beyond linearity, units and the free category laws. Extend the differential by the graded Leibniz rule. It squares to zero because it does on the old generators and on each new pair. This is again semifree: retain the order of the old generators and put each \(v_t\) before \(z_t\); the new pair differentials involve no old or later generators.

Define a second section \(i_1\) and a degree-minus-one linear assignment \(H\) recursively by \[ \begin{aligned} H(t)&=z_t,&H(1)&=0,\\ H(gf)&=H(g)i_0(f)+(-1)^{|g|}i_1(g)H(f),\\ i_1(t)&=i_0(t)+v_t-H(dt). \end{aligned} \tag{B.CY5} \] The value \(H(dt)\) uses only earlier generators, so the definition is well founded, even if \(dt\) contains a scalar identity. Extend \(i_1\) multiplicatively and preserve units. The product rule for \(H\) is unambiguous on free paths: expanding a triple product in either order has the three signs \(1,(-1)^{|g|},(-1)^{|g|+|f|}\) in left-to-right notation. By induction on the original generators, \[ di_1(f)=i_1(df),\qquad dH(f)+H(df)=i_0(f)-i_1(f). \tag{B.CY6} \] Indeed assume both identities on earlier generators and their paths. Then \(di_1(t)=i_0(dt)-dH(dt)=i_1(dt)\), since \(d^2t=0\). The homotopy identity on \(t\) is \(-v_t+H(dt)=i_0(t)-i_1(t)\), precisely (B.CY5). For a product, expand its differential and (B.CY5); the terms involving \(H\) of a differential cancel with opposite Leibniz signs, leaving the product difference. Thus both identities extend to every path and finite linear combination. Limit stages take the union of earlier assignments. The nonlinear correction \(-H(dt)\) is necessary; merely using \(i_0(t)+v_t\) generally fails to give a chain map.

The strict collapse is \[ p:C\mathcal A\longrightarrow\mathcal A, \qquad pi_0=pi_1=1,\qquad p(z_t)=p(v_t)=0. \tag{B.CY7} \] Its compatibility with the differential follows from (B.CY4); its second section identity follows inductively from (B.CY5), because every term of \(H\) contains a new letter.

A contraction on actual Hom complexes. Write a nonempty free word with new letters uniquely as old path segments separated by single new letters. Differential preserves the number of new letters. On words containing a new letter define a degree-minus-one operator \(S\) by acting on the first new letter, reading the written product from left to right. If that letter is \(v_t\), replace it by \(-z_t\) and multiply by \((-1)^{|u|}\), where \(u\) is the entire old prefix; if it is \(z_t\), set the value to zero. Set \(S=0\) on old words and extend linearly. Then \[ dS+Sd=1-i_0p, \qquad S^2=0,\quad pS=0,\quad Si_0=0. \tag{B.CY8} \] For the identity, the two-letter complex has contraction \(v_t\mapsto-z_t\), \(z_t\mapsto0\), since \(d(-z_t)=v_t\). A differential in the old prefix changes its degree by one, so its two contributions to \(dS+Sd\) cancel. A differential after the first new letter cancels because \(S\) lowers the degree of that letter by one. The remaining contribution is exactly the original word, whether the first new letter is \(v_t\) or \(z_t\). Old-only words contribute zero on both sides. This calculation also allows a prefix differential to produce an identity: total degree and the unique empty old segment are retained. The three side identities follow from the definition. Every word and every differential expression is finite; no infinite summation or completion is used. In particular this is an actual contraction over the coefficient ring, not a tensor-exactness or spectral-convergence argument.

It follows that \(p\) is a quasi-isomorphism on each Hom complex. It is the identity on objects, hence a dg quasi-equivalence. Both \(i_0\) and \(i_1\) are quasi-equivalences, since their composites with \(p\) are the identity. They are not claimed to be identical or strict inverses to \(p\).

Realize the given homotopy, including all free paths. There is a strict dg functor \(F:C\mathcal A\to\mathcal E\) defined by \[ F i_0=N_0,\qquad F(z_t)=h_t,\qquad F(v_t)=-D h_t. \tag{B.CY9} \] The differential relations hold: \(F(dz_t)=-F(v_t)=D h_t\) and \(D F(v_t)=0\). Induction in (B.CY5), using (B.CY3), gives \(F H(f)=h_f\) and \(F i_1=\overline N_1\) for every arrow, not only for the original generators. Indeed the endpoint formula on \(t\) becomes \(N_0(t)-D h_t-h_{dt}=\overline N_1(t)\), and the two product rules agree. The strict common-index diagram is therefore \[ \begin{array}{ccccc} \mathcal A&\xrightarrow{\ i_0\ }&C\mathcal A &\xleftarrow{\ i_1\ }&\mathcal A\\ &&\downarrow F&&\\ &&\mathcal E&& \end{array} \quad Fi_0=N_0,\qquad Fi_1=\overline N_1 \xrightarrow[\cong]{\ B\ }N_1. \tag{B.CY10} \] The arrow labelled \(B\) is an isomorphism of diagrams on the right endpoint index, not an additional strict equality of the left and right restrictions. The collapse \(p\) of (B.CY7) is a strict quasi-equivalence back to either endpoint index. Thus the actual diagrams may be compared through one strict common parameter category. Their non-strict comparison remains present as \(F(z_t)=h_t\); erasing the new generators would erase the datum the cylinder was built to retain. Induction of modules uses these strict dg functors, subject to the replacement requirements of B.1m and B.1s, not the original non-strict family as if it were a strict functor.

If the given index is not semifree, first precompose both diagrams and all the comparison data with the same strict \(q:Q\mathcal A\to\mathcal A\) of (B.SF1). Its staged construction is semifree and a quasi-equivalence even when the original units do not split. Apply the present construction to \(Q\mathcal A\). This gives a common free roof, not a claimed extension over relations of the original category. If lower geometric boundaries were already fixed, their exact pullbacks must be retained; this construction does not assert an unproved relative extension of independently prescribed data.

Actual whole inverse choices and geometric scope. For the same whole comparison \(\beta:A\to B\) of (B.KC15), let its supplied whole inverse choices \(\theta_i:B\to A\) have witnesses \(dA_i=\beta\theta_i-1_B\) and \(dB_i=\theta_i\beta-1_A\). Their explicit comparison is \[ K_{ij}=\theta_i A_j-B_i\theta_j, \qquad dK_{ij}=\theta_j-\theta_i. \tag{B.CY11} \] The differential of the first term is \(\theta_i\beta\theta_j-\theta_i\), and that of the second is \(\theta_i\beta\theta_j-\theta_j\), proving the equation. These are whole homogeneous maps before evaluation, so they give the required graded natural \(K\) on the admitted h-projective inputs. No comparison is evaluated on an unresolved \(U(Z)\). If a particular \(K_{ij}\) has already been prescribed by a geometric face, use that datum instead; a different formula with the same differential is not automatically equal or homotopic to it. In particular this construction does not supply a prescribed higher boundary among three or more inverse choices merely from pairwise existence.

For the actual (B.ZT9)--(B.ZT10) family, \(B\) has identity source and target components and \(b_f\) has only its third component. Hence \(h_f=B^{-1}b_f\) still has zero source and target components. Its differential also does. If \(J:\mathcal A_{U_1}\to\mathcal T_1\) denotes the functor retaining the actual target coordinate, then \[ JF=(JN_0)p,\qquad J F(z_t)=J F(v_t)=0. \tag{B.CY12} \] These equalities hold before applying \(U_1\), with no faithfulness assumption. All object values of \(F\) are the admitted \(N_0(a)\), so their source modules remain h-projective. Whole projectivity over the enlarged parameter category is a separate matter: choose the whole replacement over \(C\mathcal A\) using (B.ND5), and after either endpoint restriction use (B.CE11)'s whole re-resolution. Do not infer preservation of whole projectivity from the fact that the section is a quasi-equivalence. Once a strict relative base diagram and its boundaries are actually supplied, (B.CE10) lifts it to independently selected whole envelope models.

The common receiving presentation requires the actual (B.GC13) horizontal edge, the nested (B.MX12) coefficient and their prescribed shared higher boundaries. The bounded strictification above does not establish the full changing-model geometric multiplication, nearby-cycle descent, completed coefficient transport or strict-heart higher effacement. \(\square\)

Place the horizontal mate in the actual nested graph

Proposition B.1aw (the resolved horizontal mate is one nested arrow). The horizontal comparison (B.BM18), with its actual left comparisons and independently selected receiving replacements, is a closed arrow in a single decorated nested graph. Its image under the original two-stage fold is exactly the displayed horizontal mate, including both witness terms. The same presentation retains (B.MX12) on composable homogeneous arrows and admits a strict receiving functor from its free bar resolution. The receiving functor is not asserted to be a quasi-equivalence: the transported source structure maps need not be quasi-isomorphisms. This joins the actual mate to the supplied fold, beyond the identical-adjunction specialization used to identify the coefficients after (B.HS9).

Use a decorated graph, not only a graph of replacements. Fix dg adjunctions \(L\dashv U\) and \(M\dashv W\), in the strict common models already used above. Write \(\mathcal N_{U,W}\) for the small labelled category of admitted objects \[ X=(Z,R,N;t,r),\qquad Z\xrightarrow{\ t\ }UR\xrightarrow{\ U r\ }UWN, \qquad r:R\longrightarrow WN. \tag{B.HN1} \] Here \(Z,R\) are the specified h-projective source modules and \(t,r\) are closed degree-zero maps; neither structure map is required to be a quasi-isomorphism. Work in the whole parameter module categories when parameters are present. Labels and the actual terminal object \(N\) are retained, not identified whenever their restrictions happen to agree. A homogeneous arrow of degree \(n\) is \[ \begin{aligned} x&=(a,b,w;h,k):X\longrightarrow X',\\ a &:Z\to Z',\quad b:R\to R',\quad w:N\to N',\\ h &:Z\to UR'\ [n-1],\qquad k:R\to WN'\ [n-1]. \end{aligned} \tag{B.HN2} \] The three vertex maps have degree \(n\). The brackets in the last line specify the degree of the maps, not a change of endpoint object. Keep \(w\) before applying \(W\) or \(UW\); no faithfulness assumption is made.

Use exactly the graph differential and product of (B.IA10), now in the order (source, intermediate, actual target). For \(y:X'\to X''\) of degree \(m\), \[ \begin{aligned} Dx&=(da,db,dw;\ t'a-U(b)t-dh,\ r'b-W(w)r-dk),\\ yx&=(a_y a,b_y b,w_y w;\ h_y a+(-1)^mU(b_y)h,\\ &\hspace{12em} k_y b+(-1)^mW(w_y)k). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HN3} \] Identities have identity vertex maps and zero witnesses. Each edge is an ordinary decorated arrow graph (B.FT2), so its differential square, signed Leibniz rule and associativity hold componentwise. The two edges share the same intermediate vertex map, whose ordinary differential and product agree on both sides. This proves the dg laws on the fibre product, without any acyclicity inference from \(t\) or \(r\).

The existing fold on this larger receiving category. Define the object value \(F_0X=(Z,N,U(r)t)\) in \(\mathcal A_{UW}\). The coefficients, with the suspended convention (B.RS7), are \[ \begin{aligned} F_1(x)&=(a,w,\ U(r')h+U(k)t),\\ F_2(y,x)&=(0,0,U(k_y)h),\qquad F_j=0\quad(j>2). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HN4} \] This is (B.IA12)/(B.MX12), with the vertex order stated explicitly. To apply its selected-edge proof, send (B.HN1) to the two-edge string \(Z\to UR\to UWN\); send vertices to \(a,U(b),UW(w)\) and witnesses to \(h,U(k)\). This assignment respects (B.HN3). The proof of (B.RS8) is algebraic and does not use quasi-isomorphisms or projectivity of \(UR\). Its terminal differential and product are the images of the retained actual \(w\), and both higher terminal coordinates are zero already in the terminal category. Thus it proves the equations in the decorated target, not just after forgetting its terminal coordinate.

In particular \(DF_1=F_1D\). The two-input equation, useful for checking the sign of a composition witness, is \[ \begin{aligned} DF_2(y,x) &=F_2(Dy,x)+(-1)^{m-1}F_2(y,Dx)\\ &\quad+(-1)^m\bigl(F_1(y)F_1(x)-F_1(yx)\bigr). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HN5} \] For closed inputs the witness for \(F_1(yx)-F_1(y)F_1(x)\) is therefore \((-1)^{m+1}F_2(y,x)\), not its unsigned negative in every degree. At three inputs the identity is the cancellation \(F_2(zy,x)-F_1(z)F_2(y,x)=(-1)^{m-1}(F_2(z,y)F_1(x)-F_2(z,yx))\). For example, expanding either side leaves \(U(k_z)U(b_y)h_x\). At four inputs the only possible nonzero product is a product of two pure third-coordinate maps, hence zero. Above four inputs all terms vanish. This also checks the higher identities directly in the two-stage case. Higher coefficients vanish on a unit because its edge witnesses vanish.

Locate the actual source of (B.BM18). Restore subscripts \(0,1\) on both adjunctions. Keep its actual induction functors and closed comparisons \(\theta:L_1S\to TL_0\), \(\phi:M_1T\to VM_0\), and \(\Xi=(\phi L_0)(M_1\theta)\) in this order. Starting with \(t:Z\to U_0R\), \(r:R\to W_0N\), use their specified counit transposes \(e_L:L_0Z\to R\), \(e_M:M_0R\to N\). Put \[ \begin{aligned} A&=T(e_L)\theta_Z:L_1SZ\longrightarrow TR,\\ B&=V(e_M)\phi_R:M_1TR\longrightarrow VN,\\ \chi&=\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}(A):SZ\longrightarrow U_1TR,\\ \zeta_\nu&=\operatorname{Adj}_{M_1}(B):TR\longrightarrow W_1VN,\\ X&=(SZ,TR,VN;\chi,\zeta_\nu)\ \in\mathcal N_{U_1,W_1}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.HN6} \] The required h-projectivity of \(SZ\) and \(TR\) is the admitted induction/whole-module hypothesis, as in B.1at, not a claim about unresolved right-adjoint values. Its structure maps need not be quasi-isomorphisms. Its terminal object is \(VN\), not an object inferred from \(U_1W_1VN\).

The source of the folded arrow is the actual composite transpose. Indeed the successive Hom adjunctions give \[ \begin{aligned} U_1(\zeta_\nu)\chi &=\operatorname{Adj}_{M_1L_1}\bigl(B\,M_1(A)\bigr)\\ &=\operatorname{Adj}_{M_1L_1} \bigl(V(e_M M_0e_L)\,\Xi_Z\bigr) =\zeta_\Xi. \end{aligned} \tag{B.HN7} \] For the first equality transpose under \(L_1\): naturality of that adjunction identifies the transpose with \(\zeta_\nu A\); transposing under \(M_1\) gives \(B M_1(A)\). For the second use \(\phi_R M_1T(e_L)=VM_0(e_L)\phi_{L_0Z}\). Both inputs of \(\phi\) are admitted h-projectives. Thus the equality uses the actual counits, units and the given naturality, not a formal resemblance between two ladders.

Let \(Y=(Z',R',VN;t',r')\) be the receiving nested replacements from (B.BM18). Its chosen closed maps and degree-minus-one witnesses satisfy \[ \begin{aligned} r'c_\nu-\zeta_\nu&=db_\nu,\\ t'c_\psi-U_1(c_\nu)\chi&=db_\psi,\\ x&=(c_\psi,c_\nu,1_{VN};b_\psi,b_\nu):X\longrightarrow Y, \qquad Dx=0. \end{aligned} \tag{B.HN8} \] The middle expression is the original \(\kappa\), since postcomposition under the Hom adjunction gives \(\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}(c_\nu A)=U_1(c_\nu)\chi\). Substitution in (B.HN3) proves closedness of both edge coordinates. No unspecified inverse of a right mate is involved.

The folded arrow and its witness are therefore \[ \begin{aligned} F_1(x)&=(c_\psi,1_{VN},H): (SZ,VN,\zeta_\Xi)\longrightarrow(Z',VN,U_1(r')t'),\\ H&=U_1(r')b_\psi+U_1(b_\nu)\chi\\ &=U_1(r')b_\psi+ \operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}(b_\nu A),\\ dH&=(U_1(r')t')c_\psi-\zeta_\Xi. \end{aligned} \tag{B.HN9} \] The second equality is the Hom-complex adjunction on the homogeneous degree-minus-one map \(b_\nu\), so no extra sign is inserted. Directly, the two terms of \(dH\) are \(U_1(r')(t'c_\psi-U_1(c_\nu)\chi)\) and \(U_1(r'c_\nu-\zeta_\nu)\chi\); the middle terms cancel. This recovers (B.BM18) with its exact endpoints and both terms, not merely an equality of cohomology classes. In the following diagram the top two squares carry \(b_\psi\) and \(U_1b_\nu\); the outside rectangle carries \(H\): \[ \begin{array}{ccccc} SZ&\xrightarrow{\ \chi\ }&U_1TR&\xrightarrow{\ U_1\zeta_\nu\ }&U_1W_1VN\\ \downarrow c_\psi&&\downarrow U_1c_\nu&&\Vert\\ Z'&\xrightarrow{\ t'\ }&U_1R'&\xrightarrow{\ U_1r'\ }&U_1W_1VN. \end{array} \tag{B.HN10} \] This is a homotopy-commutative diagram with the displayed witnesses, not a claim that its squares commute strictly. Its rightmost identity comes from the actual identity of \(VN\).

A strict receiving map retaining the second coefficient. For \(\mathcal N=\mathcal N_{U_1,W_1}\), apply the free presentation \(q:Q\mathcal N\to\mathcal N\) and bar construction (B.SF1)--(B.SF6). Then \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal N&\xleftarrow[\simeq]{\ e=q\varepsilon\ }UQ\mathcal N \xrightarrow{\ \widetilde F\ }\mathcal A_{U_1W_1},\\ \widetilde F[x_j|\cdots|x_1]&=F_j(qx_j,\ldots,qx_1). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HN11} \] The differential (B.SF3) and the identities just checked prove that \(\widetilde F\) is a strict dg functor. The left arrow is a quasi-equivalence by (B.SF6). The right arrow is deliberately not labelled a quasi-equivalence. That conclusion in (B.SF7) used the additional Hom and essential-surjectivity hypotheses for replacement graphs; those hypotheses have not been proved for this enlarged decorated category. Its strictness proof, which is all that is used here, requires neither. A lift \(\widehat x\) of the closed arrow (B.HN8) can be chosen closed through the Hom-surjective quasi-isomorphism \(q\): correct a graded lift by a primitive of its differential error in the acyclic kernel. Its one-letter image is (B.HN9). Two-letter images retain (B.HN4), not zero. No multiplicative section of \(q\) is asserted.

Let \(J\) retain the actual terminal object and terminal map, and let \(I\) retain the initial source. As in (B.SF8), \[ J\widetilde F=J_{\mathcal N}e,\qquad I\widetilde F=I_{\mathcal N}e,\qquad JF_2=IF_2=0. \tag{B.HN12} \] These are equalities before applying either right-adjoint functor. Whole re-resolution over the common index, and after a restriction of that index, remains necessary as in (B.CE11); this roof does not justify a pointwise-to-whole projectivity inference.

Join to the existing geometric provider without substituting for it. The left comparisons in (B.HN6) are the resolved geometric comparisons (B.BM15), obtained from the original (B.GC12)--(B.GC13) cell and its retained whole inverse homotopies. The cell supplies its actual edge \(z=t(A_Cs)\theta_k^{-1}\) and all selected-edge coefficients, rather than an unresolved inverse. Its wordwise equality is already proved immediately after (B.GC13). Consequently any strict outer transfer of this receiving presentation must carry both terms of (B.HN9) and \(U_1(k_y)h_x\). When the specified outer maps satisfy that all-coefficient equality, (B.SF9) makes their induced square on \(UQ\mathcal N\) strictly commute. This gives the exact interface at which the existing geometric cell is inserted; it does not assert that separately chosen geometric boundaries already meet that hypothesis.

In particular, the seven actual targets of (B.FT3), the distinction between the unit and counit endpoint, and the degree-minus-four cube coordinate (B.FG13) must still be retained when this horizontal arrow is attached to the full changing-model diagram. The common-cylinder construction B.1av treats a supplied comparison homotopy; it does not erase that attachment obligation. The identification above compares the resolved mate with the nested fold. Simultaneous geometric higher-boundary assembly, nearby multiplicative descent, whole coefficient transport and strict-heart effacement are not established by this construction. The fixed-model identities do not establish the general geometric system. \(\square\)

Attach the horizontal counit bridge with its second boundary

Proposition B.1ax (the actual endpoint bridge, before restriction). The horizontal arrow of (B.HN9) supplies exactly the counit homotopy required by the decorated four-face target (B.FT3). Its composition boundary contains the second coefficient of (B.HN4). This coefficient cannot be omitted even when only the first endpoint comparison is wanted. The endpoint construction extends to every arrow of the strict receiving roof (B.HN11). This identifies the endpoint part of the attachment; it does not assert that independently prescribed intermediate faces or geometric cubes already fit together.

Transpose the whole decorated arrow. Fix a dg adjunction \(L\dashv U\) between the admitted whole module categories, with its actual Hom-complex adjunction, unit \(\eta\) and counit. For \(Q=(P,N,q:P\to UN)\) in (B.FT2), write \(e_Q=\operatorname{Adj}^{-1}(q):LP\to N\). There is a strict dg functor to the ordinary arrow category of the target category: \[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal C_L(Q)&=(LP\xrightarrow{e_Q}N),\\ \mathcal C_L(a,w,h)&=(La,w,\operatorname{Adj}^{-1}h). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HB1} \] In particular it retains \(w\), not just \(U(w)\). The Hom adjunction commutes with differential and satisfies, for every homogeneous map, \(\operatorname{Adj}^{-1}(h a)=\operatorname{Adj}^{-1}(h)L(a)\) and \(\operatorname{Adj}^{-1}(U(w)h)=w\operatorname{Adj}^{-1}(h)\). No factors change order. Applying these identities to (B.FT2) gives the arrow differential and product (B.FG1), including its sign \((-1)^{|y|}\). It also preserves the unit. This proves (B.HB1) without requiring \(q\) to be a quasi-isomorphism or \(U\) to be faithful.

Identify the given horizontal counit, rather than choosing another one. Use exactly \(X,Y,A,B,\chi,\zeta_\nu,x\) of (B.HN6)--(B.HN9). Put \[ \begin{aligned} D_\psi&=\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}^{-1}(b_\psi),& D_\nu&=\operatorname{Adj}_{M_1}^{-1}(b_\nu),\\ e'_L&=\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}^{-1}(t'),& e'_M&=\operatorname{Adj}_{M_1}^{-1}(r'),\\ e_X&=B\,M_1(A),&e_Y&=e'_M M_1(e'_L). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HB2} \] These maps use the original resolved inputs. In particular no comparison is evaluated on an unresolved right-adjoint value. Transposing the two terms of \(H\), first under \(L_1\) and then under \(M_1\), gives \[ \begin{aligned} \beta_x&=\operatorname{Adj}_{M_1L_1}^{-1}(H)\\ &=e'_M M_1(D_\psi)+D_\nu M_1(A),\\ d\beta_x&=e_Y M_1L_1(c_\psi)-e_X. \end{aligned} \tag{B.HB3} \] For the first term the first transpose is \(r'D_\psi\); its second is \(e'_M M_1(D_\psi)\). For the second term the first transpose is \(b_\nu A\); its second is \(D_\nu M_1(A)\). These are Hom-complex identities, so they apply to the degree-minus-one witnesses. For the differential, transpose the two equations of (B.HN8): \(dD_\psi=e'_L L_1c_\psi-c_\nu A\) and \(dD_\nu=e'_M M_1c_\nu-B\). Differentiate the middle line of (B.HB3). The two terms with \(e'_M M_1(c_\nu A)\) cancel. All other factors are closed of degree zero. The result is its last line. This also identifies (B.HB3) with the two-stage case of (B.HS5), with the same counits and not only the same differential.

A universal endpoint bridge in the decorated category. For any \(Q=(P,N,q)\), retain its separate unit object \(Q^u=(P,LP,\eta_P)\). For \(f=(a,w,h):Q_0\to Q_1\) of degree \(n\), set \[ \begin{aligned} E_Q&=(1_P,e_Q,0):Q^u\longrightarrow Q,\\ A(f)&=(a,La,0):Q_0^u\longrightarrow Q_1^u,\\ \mathcal B(f)&=(0,\beta_f,0):Q_0^u\longrightarrow Q_1,\\ \beta_f&=\operatorname{Adj}^{-1}(h),\\ |E_Q|&=0,\qquad |A(f)|=n,\qquad |\mathcal B(f)|=n-1. \end{aligned} \tag{B.HB4} \] The unit transpose \(U(e_Q)\eta_P=q\) makes \(E_Q\) closed. Unit naturality makes \(A\) a strict dg functor. All these maps are in \(\mathcal A_U\), before its possibly nonfaithful forgetful functor. Direct calculation gives \[ D\mathcal B(f)+\mathcal B(Df)=E_{Q_1}A(f)-fE_{Q_0}. \tag{B.HB5} \] The first coordinate is zero. In the target coordinate this reads \(d\beta_f+\operatorname{Adj}^{-1}(q_1a-U(w)q_0-dh)=e_{Q_1}La-we_{Q_0}\). The last coordinate on either side is \(-h\), because \(U(\beta_f)\eta_{P_0}=h\). Thus the equation is proved in all degrees, not just for closed comparisons.

For composable \(f,g\), with \(|g|=m\), the same calculation also gives \[ \mathcal B(gf)=\mathcal B(g)A(f)+(-1)^m g\mathcal B(f), \qquad \mathcal B(1)=0. \tag{B.HB6} \] Its target component is \(\operatorname{Adj}^{-1}(h_g)L(a_f)+(-1)^m w_g\operatorname{Adj}^{-1}(h_f)\), the transpose of the product witness in (B.FT2). Its first and third components vanish. This is the precise product rule for this degree-minus-one bridge; treating it as an ordinary degree-zero natural transformation would give the wrong sign.

Apply this construction to \(L=M_1L_1\), \(U=U_1W_1\), and \(f=F_1(x)\). In (B.FG5)--(B.FG6), the exact endpoint records are \(\mathbf c_L=A(f)\), \(\mathbf c_R=fE_X\), \(\mathbf e_1=E_Y\), and \(\mathbf b=\mathcal B(f)\). The actual target component of \(\mathbf c_R\) is \(e_X\), since \(f\) has terminal map \(1_{VN}\); (B.HN7) identifies it with \(V(e_M M_0e_L)\Xi_Z\). The target component of \(\mathbf b\) is precisely (B.HB3). The following homotopy rectangle displays the distinction between the two endpoint paths: \[ \begin{array}{ccc} X^u&\xrightarrow{\ A(f)\ }&Y^u\\ \downarrow E_X&&\downarrow E_Y\\ F_0X&\xrightarrow{\ f\ }&F_0Y \end{array} \qquad E_YA(f)-fE_X=D\mathcal B(f)\quad(Df=0). \tag{B.HB7} \] Here \(X^u,Y^u\) denote the unit objects associated to the folded objects \(F_0X,F_0Y\). The rectangle is homotopy-commutative, not strictly commutative. Its reproducible diagram source is this displayed array, and its witness is the actual two-term counit in (B.HB3). It does not identify the intermediate \(\mathsf A,\mathsf C\) of (B.FT3) with an endpoint.

The second coefficient is part of the bridge boundary. For general composable homogeneous nested arrows \(x,y\), let \(|x|=n\), \(|y|=m\), use the coefficients (B.HN4), and set \(B_1(x)=\mathcal B(F_1x)\), \(B_2(y,x)=\mathcal B(F_2(y,x))\), \(A_x=A(F_1x)\). The degree of \(B_2\) is \(m+n-2\). Then \[ \begin{aligned} &B_1(yx)-B_1(y)A_x-(-1)^mF_1(y)B_1(x)\\ &\quad=(-1)^m\bigl(DB_2(y,x)+B_2(Dy,x)\\ &\hspace{5em}+(-1)^{m-1}B_2(y,Dx)+F_2(y,x)E_X\bigr). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HB8} \] To prove this, solve (B.HN5) for \(F_1(yx)-F_1(y)F_1(x)\), then apply \(\mathcal B\) and (B.HB6). Since the initial coordinate of \(F_2\) is zero, \(A(F_2)=0\). Equation (B.HB5) therefore says \(\mathcal B(DF_2)=-F_2E_X-D\mathcal B(F_2)\). Substitution gives every term and sign in (B.HB8).

Writing \(H_2=U_1(k_y)h_x\), its target and last coordinates can be seen explicitly: \[ \begin{aligned} \beta_2&=\operatorname{Adj}_{M_1L_1}^{-1}(H_2)\\ &=\operatorname{Adj}_{M_1}^{-1}(k_y)\, M_1\bigl(\operatorname{Adj}_{L_1}^{-1}(h_x)\bigr),\\ B_2&=(0,\beta_2,0),\\ (DB_2)_h&=-H_2,\qquad (F_2E_X)_h=H_2. \end{aligned} \tag{B.HB9} \] Naturality of the two Hom adjunctions proves the first line in the displayed order. The final two terms cancel in (B.HB8); dropping \(F_2E_X\) would leave \(-H_2\). Thus even a pure third-coordinate folding term supplies a necessary target-side composition homotopy. Neither a zero terminal coordinate for \(F_2\) nor equality on \(H^0\) permits discarding it.

All arrows of the strict roof, including its higher generators. Let \(\mathscr R=UQ\mathcal N\) and \(T=\widetilde F\) be (B.HN11). Apply the just-proved universal construction to its strict images: \[ \begin{aligned} \widetilde A&=A T,&\widetilde B(s)&=\mathcal B(Ts),\\ D\widetilde B(s)+\widetilde B(Ds) &=E_{\mathrm{target}(s)}\widetilde A(s)-T(s)E_{\mathrm{source}(s)},\\ \widetilde B(ts)&=\widetilde B(t)\widetilde A(s) +(-1)^{|t|}T(t)\widetilde B(s). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HB10} \] These hold on every homogeneous arrow because \(T\) is strict and (B.HB5)--(B.HB6) hold on every arrow of its receiving category. On a one-letter generator \(\widetilde B\) is \(B_1\); on a two-letter generator it is \(B_2\), with the generator normalization of (B.HN11). On longer single generators it is zero for this two-edge fold, but on their products it is determined by the displayed product rule, not set to zero. The free differential includes its split-word terms: its two-letter instance is exactly (B.HB8). This supplies the higher endpoint identities without assuming that \(F_1\) itself is multiplicative or inventing a multiplicative section of the roof projection.

Retain the existing geometric and cube boundaries. The actual mixed-cell transfer remains (B.GC13), including \(z=t(A_Cs)\theta_k^{-1}\) and every selected-edge coefficient. For its admitted strict outer maps, that equation compares the same homogeneous word before transposition; (B.HB1) and Hom naturality compare its counit transpose. No inverse is introduced on an unresolved object. Under the actual proper-refinement functor (B.FT9), the endpoint target witnesses become \[ \beta_x'=\beta_x c_{P_0},\qquad \beta_2'=\beta_2 c_{P_0},\qquad \bar\gamma'=\bar\gamma c_{P_0}, \tag{B.HB11} \] with the original canonical source comparison \(c_{P_0}:L'RP_0\to LP_0\). The transpose proof of (B.FT11) works in every degree, hence also for \(\beta_2\). Formula (B.FT9) acts on the entire decorated arrows, including their receiving-target factors. In particular, for a supplied full four-face cube the retained equation is still \[ D\mathbf P(g_H)=\mathbf P(g_T)-\mathbf P(g_B) +\widehat{\mathbf R}(f_H), \qquad \mathbf P(g_H)=(P_H,\bar\gamma(f_H),W_H). \tag{B.HB12} \] Here \(\mathbf P(g_H)\) has degree minus three and \(W_H\) has degree minus four. The discrepancy includes \(-\mathbf b\) as in (B.FG10); its target proof is (B.FT5). A transported cube retains \(\kappa RW_H\), not zero. This is a preservation statement for the actual supplied cube, not its existence for independently chosen geometric faces.

The endpoint attachment and its second boundary are specified before restriction and on a strict common roof. The simultaneous changing geometric diagram still needs the intermediate \(\mathsf A,\mathsf C\) face maps with their actual (B.FT4) targets and their common higher overlap boundary. Only after those identities are checked may the relative lift (B.CE10) keep them fixed. Neither the endpoint calculation nor acyclicity of a lifting kernel creates a missing face. Whole-index re-resolution remains required. Geometric nearby multiplicative descent, normalized coefficient transport with derived inverse limits and strict-heart higher effacement are not established by this construction. The endpoint identities alone do not establish those geometric comparisons. \(\square\)

Transport the seven-object diagram with canonical new units

Proposition B.1ay (a directed unit comparison, not a unit isomorphism). The fixed-common-model intermediate faces already constructed in B.1aj and B.1an admit a simultaneous transport through any resolved outer comparison of B.1at. The three unit vertices can be replaced by the canonical new unit vertices, without assuming the comparison invertible. The other four vertices remain their actual transported objects. This gives a receiving diagram with all four faces and the full cube. It does not identify that diagram with independently chosen standard replacements in a new geometric model.

The comparison at a unit vertex. Write the old and new adjunctions as \(L\dashv U\) and \(\widehat L\dashv\widehat U\). Let \(\Sigma,\Omega\) be the whole source and target dg functors, and let \(\sigma_P:\widehat L\Sigma P\to\Omega LP\) be the closed dg-natural comparison on the admitted whole h-projective sources. These are the data of (B.ZT1), with new letters to distinguish them from the inner \(S,V,\vartheta\) of the seven-object diagram. As there, \(\Sigma\) preserves the required whole h-projective sources. Write \(e_q=\operatorname{Adj}_L^{-1}q\), \(\beta_f=\operatorname{Adj}_L^{-1}h\). The existing strict dg transport is \[ \begin{aligned} Tq&=(\Sigma P,\Omega N,\widehat{\operatorname{Adj}}(\Omega e_q\,\sigma_P)),\\ T(a,w,h)&=(\Sigma a,\Omega w, \widehat{\operatorname{Adj}}(\Omega\beta_f\,\sigma_P)). \end{aligned} \tag{B.UT1} \] In particular \(T(P,LP,\eta_P)\) has target \(\Omega LP\), not \(\widehat L\Sigma P\). Put \[ \begin{aligned} u'_P&=(\Sigma P,\widehat L\Sigma P,\widehat\eta_{\Sigma P}),\\ K_P&=(1_{\Sigma P},\sigma_P,0):u'_P\longrightarrow T(P,LP,\eta_P). \end{aligned} \tag{B.UT2} \] This arrow is closed: the third coordinate of its differential is \(\widehat{\operatorname{Adj}}(\sigma_P)-\widehat U(\sigma_P)\widehat\eta_{\Sigma P}=0\). There is no inverse in this construction. Naturality of the degree-zero \(\sigma\), in every homogeneous degree, and the Hom adjunction give \[ \begin{aligned} T(A(a))K_P&=K_{P'}\widehat A(\Sigma a),\\ T(E_q)K_P&=E_{Tq},\\ T(\mathcal B(f))K_P&=\widehat{\mathcal B}(Tf). \end{aligned} \tag{B.UT3} \] Here \(A(a)=(a,La,0)\), and \(E,\mathcal B\) are (B.HB4). The first equality has identical first coordinates; its target equality is \(\Omega(La)\sigma_P=\sigma_{P'}\widehat L(\Sigma a)\); both witnesses are zero. The second target is \(\Omega e_q\sigma_P\), the counit transpose of \(Tq\). The third target is \(\Omega\beta_f\sigma_P\), the transpose of its transported witness. This proves all three identities before restriction and without evaluating \(\sigma\) on an unresolved right-adjoint value.

Exactly which vertices change. Set \(P_0=SQ_0\), \(P_R=SR_0\). In the old diagram \(L=L_1\), \(X=LP_0\), \(M_1=LQ_1\). Denote its new diagram by \(\overline D\). Its source object at each row is the \(\Sigma\)-image of the original source. Its target objects are \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{label}&\text{target of }\overline D\\ \hline \mathsf Q_0^u&\widehat L\Sigma P_0\\ \mathsf R_0^u&\widehat L\Sigma P_R\\ \mathsf A&\Omega X\\ \mathsf C&\Omega(VM_0)\\ \mathsf Q_1^u&\widehat L\Sigma Q_1\\ \mathsf R_1&\Omega M_1\\ \mathsf Q_1^q&\Omega(VN) \end{array} \tag{B.UT4} \] At the three unit rows use \(u'_P\). At the other four rows use \(Tq\) literally, with its structure map from (B.UT1). Those structure maps are not asserted to be quasi-isomorphisms. Thus, for example, the target of \(\mathsf A\) has not been relabelled as \(\widehat L\Sigma P_0\), and the targets of \(\mathsf Q_1^u,\mathsf R_1\) need not coincide.

The actual directed presentation suffices. Use the generators and their relations in (B.FG3)--(B.FG12), with the actual decorated targets of (B.FT3)--(B.FT5). Every generator whose target is a unit vertex has a unit source: these are \(\mathbf s_u,\mathbf s_z,\mathbf c_L,\mathbf J_0\), their differential records and identities. Each is an \(A(a)\). There is no generator from a nonunit vertex into a unit vertex. Keep this presentation; do not adjoin arbitrary arrows into unit vertices. Define \(K_i=K_{P_i}\) at a unit row and \(K_i=1\) at the other rows. For a generator \(g:i\to j\), put \[ \overline D(g)= \begin{cases} \widehat A(\Sigma a),&j\text{ is a unit row},\quad g=A(a),\\ T(g)K_i,&j\text{ is a nonunit row}. \end{cases} \tag{B.UT5} \] All labels refer to vertices, not accidental equalities of underlying modules. The comparison is the following strictly commutative square of decorated arrows: \[ \begin{array}{ccc} \overline D(i)&\xrightarrow{\ \overline D(g)\ }&\overline D(j)\\ \downarrow K_i&&\downarrow K_j\\ TD(i)&\xrightarrow{\ T(g)\ }&TD(j). \end{array} \tag{B.UT6} \] For a unit target this is the first identity of (B.UT3); for a nonunit target it is the definition. Naturality therefore holds on every word. To check that all differential and linear relations are preserved, separate their targets. A relation with nonunit target transports to that same relation under the strict functor \(T\), precomposed with \(K_i\); here \(K_j=1\), so no cancellation of a noninvertible map is used. A relation with unit target consists entirely of \(A\)-arrows. Its first-coordinate relation transports by \(\Sigma\) and then the strict dg functor \(\widehat A\). The comparisons \(K_i\) are closed, so these arguments also prove compatibility with differential, including the nonclosed generator \(\mathbf J_0\). Products and identities follow by the same word calculation. This proves the construction on the stated presentation, not on an arbitrary full subcategory.

Retain the intermediate target maps. Write \(\sigma_0=\sigma_{P_0}\), \(\sigma_R=\sigma_{P_R}\), \(\sigma_1=\sigma_{Q_1}\), and \(\vartheta_0=\vartheta_{Q_0}\), \(\vartheta_R=\vartheta_{R_0}\) in the original notation. The target components of representative arrows are \[ \begin{aligned} (\overline{\mathbf u}_X)_Z&=\sigma_0,& (\overline{\mathbf u}_1)_Z&=\sigma_1,\\ (\overline{\mathbf c}_L)_Z&=\widehat L\Sigma c,& (\overline{\mathbf a})_Z&=\Omega(Lc),\\ (\overline{\mathbf v})_Z&=\Omega\vartheta_0,& (\overline{\mathbf w})_Z&=\Omega(Ve_0),\\ (\overline{\mathbf c}_M)_Z&=\Omega(Ve_0^M\vartheta_R)\sigma_R,\\ (\overline{\mathbf c}_R)_Z&=\Omega(Ve_0\vartheta_0)\sigma_0,\\ (\overline{\mathbf e}_1)_Z&=\Omega e_1\sigma_1. \end{aligned} \tag{B.UT7} \] Every third coordinate at a nonunit target is exactly the transpose in (B.UT1). Precomposition with \(K_i\) leaves the transported arrow's first and third coordinates unchanged, because the comparison has identity first coordinate and zero third coordinate. The transported witness itself need not be zero and is not reconstructed from a restricted target map. The four face targets and the separate endpoint bridge are \[ \begin{aligned} (\overline{\mathbf j}_U)_Z&=\Omega(V\lambda_0\vartheta_0)\sigma_0,\\ (\overline{\mathbf j}_F)_Z&=0,\\ (\overline{\mathbf j}_C)_Z&=\Omega(V\alpha_0\vartheta_R)\sigma_R,\\ (\overline{\mathbf j}_\beta)_Z&=\Omega\beta,\\ (\overline{\mathbf b})_Z&=\Omega\beta\,\sigma_0. \end{aligned} \tag{B.UT8} \] The last two maps have different sources: \(\mathsf A\) has target \(\Omega X\), whereas \(\mathsf Q_0^u\) has target \(\widehat L\Sigma P_0\). The \(\sigma_0\) appears in the face path only upon composition with \(\overline{\mathbf u}_X\). Thus its target becomes \(\Omega\beta\sigma_0\), exactly the bridge target. Dropping \(\sigma_0\), or inserting it prematurely into the \(\mathsf A\)-origin face, is not an alternative normalization.

The full four face identities, with the original degree conventions and the record differential \(\partial\), are \[ \begin{aligned} D\overline{\mathbf j}_U(f)+\overline{\mathbf j}_U(\partial f) &=\overline{\mathbf c}_M\overline{\mathbf s}_u -\overline{\mathbf v}\overline{\mathbf u}_X,\\ D\overline{\mathbf j}_F(f)+\overline{\mathbf j}_F(\partial f) &=\overline{\mathbf u}_1\overline{\mathbf c}_L -\overline{\mathbf a}\overline{\mathbf u}_X,\\ D\overline{\mathbf j}_C(f)+\overline{\mathbf j}_C(\partial f) &=\overline{\mathbf c}_R\overline{\mathbf s}_z -\overline{\mathbf w}\overline{\mathbf c}_M,\\ D\overline{\mathbf j}_\beta(f)+\overline{\mathbf j}_\beta(\partial f) &=\overline{\mathbf z}_1\overline{\mathbf a} -\overline{\mathbf w}\overline{\mathbf v}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.UT9} \] These are images of (B.FG8), by the proof of (B.UT5). They can also be checked upstairs directly: the first and third target equations of (B.FT4) are acted on by \(\Omega\) and precomposed with \(\sigma_0,\sigma_R\), respectively; naturality of \(\sigma\) moves the unit-only arrows past these comparisons. The second uses \(\Omega(Lc)\sigma_0=\sigma_1\widehat L\Sigma c\). The fourth is simply \(\Omega\) of its old target equation, because its source is \(\mathsf A\), not a unit row. This verifies the target distinction needed for all four equations, rather than only their images under \(\widehat U\).

The full cube and ordered successive transports. Form the new bridge sum and corrected discrepancy by the same signed words as (B.FG9)--(B.FG10), including the separate term \(-\overline{\mathbf b}\).
