For \(\mathbf P(g_H)=(P_H,\bar\gamma(f_H),W_H)\), the actual transported lift and its boundary are \[ \begin{aligned} \overline{\mathbf P}(g_H) &=\bigl(\Sigma P_H,\Omega\bar\gamma(f_H)\sigma_0,\widehat W_H\bigr),\\ \widehat W_H &=\widehat{\operatorname{Adj}}\bigl( \Omega(\operatorname{Adj}_L^{-1}W_H)\sigma_0\bigr),\\ D\overline{\mathbf P}(g_H) &=\overline{\mathbf P}(g_T)-\overline{\mathbf P}(g_B) +\overline{\widehat{\mathbf R}}(f_H). \end{aligned} \tag{B.UT10} \] The first equality is (B.UT5), and the last is the image of the already supplied (B.FG12). Here the lift has degree minus three and its retained third coordinate \(\widehat W_H\) has degree minus four. The construction transports the specified \(W_H\); it does not set it to zero or infer it from the endpoint bridge. Likewise the degree-minus-two extension equation holds for every homogeneous record, not just for closed endpoints.

For two composable outer transports, use the strict composition conventions of (B.ZT13). The combined comparison and unit arrow are \[ \begin{aligned} \sigma^{21}_P&=\Omega_2(\sigma^1_P)\sigma^2_{\Sigma_1P},\\ K^{21}_P&=T_2(K^1_P)K^2_{\Sigma_1P}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.UT11} \] Their source and target components are identities and the displayed composite; their third components vanish. At a nonunit target, successive applications of (B.UT5) give \(T_2T_1(g)T_2(K^1_i)K^2_i\), which is precisely the combined rule. At unit targets both give the same \(\widehat A\)-arrow. Thus successive normalizations agree under these conventions, with all intermediate labels retained. With nonstrict functor models one must retain the specified associators of the original transport rather than claiming literal equality of differently parenthesized targets.

The geometric parameter inputs. The label-preserving inverse-image parameter category is constructed in B.1ac; its correctly oriented right-module kernels and composition roofs are given in B.1ad. For the mixed compact-support square, B.MX3–B.MX11 specifies the six operation words, their common mapping target and the two-route boundary. These are the inputs to be joined to the proper-refinement and folding family of B.SN12–B.SN13. The compositors in (B.IP11) become homotopy equivalences on h-projective inputs; the right-module comparisons in (B.RK2) remain roofs, not chosen strictly natural inverses. The joint comparison must retain their actual maps and shared higher boundaries.

Replacement choices and geometric comparisons. Independent whole replacements of the same seven-object envelope are compared in B.1ar; B.1as identifies the common envelope across actual proper refinements, including the normalized bilateral source and target comparisons. These constructions retain both comparison-back witnesses without assuming that unit arrows are quasi-isomorphisms. For horizontal geometric composition, B.1aw identifies the resolved mate with the original nested fold, and B.1ax supplies its counit endpoint bridge with the second folding coefficient. The endpoint bridge does not identify the intermediate A and C diagrams or supply their common higher boundary. The remaining comparison therefore concerns independently prescribed geometric diagrams and their actual shared boundaries, not the existence of whole replacement-choice comparisons over an already identified proper-refinement target.

Successive base change and the actual comparison roofs. For two successive base changes, the targets in B.1aj give the following route: the A-target comparison is the second left base-change map evaluated at the first transported initial resolution, and the C-target is the ordered double inverse image. B.1ad compares each ordered inverse-image transport with its direct-composite model by two actual maps into a common dual kernel. Applying the receiving left functor to the source-kernel roof gives a zigzag for the A-targets; the target-kernel roof gives cospans for the C-targets and counit endpoints. The endpoint maps exist on general modules, but their equivalence properties require the admitted resolved inputs. These are directed roofs, not chosen strictly natural inverses. The resolved vertical-pasting formula in B.1ab retains both endpoint-witness terms. For the second-resolution targets, B.1ay retains the span through the transported canonical unit rather than inverting the mate or its source lift. These individual routes do not identify independently prescribed geometric comparison cells on the whole parameter diagram: their common four faces and higher boundary must still be matched.

Scope of the remaining comparison. This construction supplies the induced receiving diagram and its actual map to the transported old diagram. It assumes the fixed-model faces. The whole-envelope method (B.CE10) resolves the resulting diagram without inverting any \(K_P\); after an index restriction, (B.CE11) still requires whole re-resolution. Comparing it with an independently prescribed new geometric diagram requires the actual maps of their intermediate targets and common boundaries. Changes in \(\sigma\) require the retained homotopies (B.ZT9)--(B.ZT10) and their common-cylinder realization, not a claim that objectwise comparisons are strictly natural. The original geometric transfer (B.GC13) retains every word coefficient. Those changing-parameter identifications, geometric nearby-cycle multiplicative descent, coefficient completion with derived inverse limits, strict-heart higher effacement are not established by the unit normalization. \(\square\)

Compare successive base-change kernels and their resolved mates

Proposition B.1az (two successive base changes on a common whole model). Fix two successive cartesian changes of base of one open/proper compactification. The ordered and direct left-kernel compact-support comparisons admit a comparison homotopy retaining their original lift witnesses. The actual right-kernel roofs transport this comparison to a whole right-kernel homotopy and its comparison-back witness. The chosen inverses have an explicit three-term comparison, and the resolved right mates have a full decorated-graph comparison whose endpoint bridge retains a degree-minus-two target.

The scope is the Noetherian separated finite-type compactification setting, with ordinary unbounded torsion coefficients and the common annihilator required by the proper-base-change theorem, as in B.1ae. The algebra uses the original commutative coefficient ring. Whole replacements are made on the specified common free parameter category times both endpoint categories. A change of index requires the re-resolution of (B.CE11). The assertion does not identify unspecified higher geometric cells or assert global compatibility of all composition/refinement arrays.

The actual left-kernel words

Use three cartesian rows \(X_i\xrightarrow{j_i}U_i\xrightarrow{h_i}Y_i\), for \(i=0,1,2\), with \(j_i\) open and \(h_i\) proper. The successive vertical scheme maps are \(u_i,v_i,g_i\). Their direct composites are \(u_{21}=u_1u_2\), \(v_{21}=v_1v_2\), \(g_{21}=g_1g_2\). In this paragraph capital letters denote kernels:

\[ \begin{gathered} \mathsf H_i=L_{h_i},\quad \mathsf J_i=L_{j_i},\\ \mathsf U_i=L_{u_i},\\ \mathsf V_i=L_{v_i},\\ \mathsf G_i=L_{g_i},\\ \mathsf W_i=\mathsf H_i\mathsf J_i . \end{gathered} \tag{B.OD1} \]

Juxtaposition denotes balanced tensor in left-kernel order; canonical tensor associators are retained. The proper and open maps of (B.KC5)–(B.KC8) are

\[ \begin{aligned} P_i:\mathsf H_i\mathsf V_i&\longrightarrow \mathsf G_i\mathsf H_{i-1},\\ O_i:\mathsf J_i\mathsf U_i&\longrightarrow \mathsf V_i\mathsf J_{i-1}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD2} \]

Each has its original whole witness \(\pi_i\lambda_i-\chi_i=d\omega_i\).

Start with the actual inverse-image compositor, \(C_bC_a\to C_{ba}\). Lift the composite from \(L_bL_a\) through \(L_{ba}\to C_{ba}\) by (B.ND7). With its lift witness retained, this gives

\[ \begin{gathered} c_a:L_bL_a\longrightarrow L_{ba},\\ \begin{aligned} &\epsilon_{ba}c_a\\ &\quad-\mu(\epsilon_b\otimes\epsilon_a)=d\eta_a . \end{aligned} \end{gathered} \tag{B.OD3} \]

Here \(\epsilon\) includes the evaluation in (B.IP4), and \(\mu\) is actual direct-image composition. The whole exterior-cell filtration of (B.KC2) and the quasi-isomorphism proof in (B.IP11) show that \(c_a\) is a quasi-isomorphism between whole h-projectives. It has a whole inverse with both inverse homotopies. This does not make independently chosen lifts strictly associative. Use \(c_u,c_v,c_g\) in one common model; the proper and open comparisons use the same \(c_v\).

For the proper rectangle the common raw complex is

\[ \begin{aligned} &M_{12}(Q,I)\\ &\quad=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}\bigl(h_{0,*}eI,\\ &\hspace{5em}g_{1,*}g_{2,*}eQ\bigr). \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD4} \]

Take homogeneous \(z_1:eI\to v_{1,*}eK_1\), \(z_2:eK_1\to v_{2,*}eK_2\) and \(w:h_{2,*}eK_2\to eQ\). The successive map (B.KC3) is

\[ g_{1,*}\!\left[g_{2,*}(w)\kappa_{2,K_2} h_{1,*}(z_2)\right] \kappa_{1,K_1}h_{0,*}(z_1). \]

Naturality of \(\kappa_1\) rewrites it as

\[ \begin{aligned} &g_{1,*}g_{2,*}(w) (g_{1,*}\kappa_{2,K_2})\\ &\,\cdot\kappa_{1,v_{2,*}K_2}h_{0,*} \!\left[v_{1,*}(z_2)z_1\right]. \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD5} \]

This is the direct map: its comparison is \(\kappa_{21}=(g_{1,*}\kappa_2)(\kappa_1v_{2,*})\), and (B.IP5) composes \(z_2,z_1\) as \(v_{1,*}(z_2)z_1\). No homogeneous factors were permuted. Equations (B.BC9)–(B.BC10) identify the same equality under the inverse-image adjunction in every resolution-string coefficient.

For clarity, the witness of the ordered proper map can be written before any inverse is chosen. Put

\[ \begin{aligned} M_1&=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet} (h_{0,*}eI,g_{1,*}eQ_1),\\ M_2&=\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet} (h_{1,*}eK_1,g_{2,*}eQ). \end{aligned} \]

There are balanced degree-zero composition maps

\[ \begin{aligned} F_g(y\otimes t)&=g_{1,*}(\epsilon y)t,\\ F_v(t\otimes z)&=g_{1,*}(t)\kappa_{1,K_1} h_{0,*}(\epsilon z) \end{aligned} \]

from \(\mathsf G_2\otimes M_1\) and \(M_2\otimes\mathsf V_1\), respectively, into \(M_{12}\). The ordered witness is

\[ \begin{aligned} \omega_o={}&F_g(1\otimes\omega_1)\\ &\quad\cdot(P_2\otimes1)\\ &+F_v(\omega_2\otimes1). \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD6} \]

The tensor \(1\otimes\omega_1\) acts on \(y\otimes t\) with sign \((-1)^{|y|}\). Differentiation and naturality of \(\kappa_1\) give \(\pi_o\lambda_o-\chi_o=d\omega_o\), where \(\lambda_o=(\mathsf G_2P_1)(P_2\mathsf V_1)\). Thus the original witnesses, rather than only their cohomology classes, occur in the comparison.

For the open rectangle use the actual right-adjoint mates \(\theta_i^R:u_{i,*}j_i^*\to j_{i-1}^*v_{i,*}\). Evaluating on the same inverse image of an open subset gives

\[ \theta_{21}^R= (\theta_1^Rv_{2,*})(u_{1,*}\theta_2^R). \tag{B.OD7} \]

For homogeneous \(z_1,z_2,w\) of the corresponding open kernels, the ordered expression is \(\theta_1^Ru_{1,*}[\theta_2^Ru_{2,*}(w)z_2]z_1\); by (B.OD7) it is \(\theta_{21}^Ru_{1,*}u_{2,*}(w)u_{1,*}(z_2)z_1\), the direct expression. Its common complex is \(\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}(eI,j_0^*v_{1,*}v_{2,*}eQ)\). The composition maps replacing \(F_g,F_v\) are \(F_V(y\otimes t)=j_0^*v_{1,*}(y)t\) and \(F_U(t\otimes z)=\theta_1^Ru_{1,*}(t)z\). They give precisely (B.OD6) with \(O\) in place of \(P\), including its tensor sign.

Preserve the full comparison pair

For either rectangle write \(A_o,A_d\) for its ordered and direct source words and \(B_o,B_d\) for its target words. Let \(a:A_o\to A_d\), \(b:B_o\to B_d\) be the compositor maps. In the proper case \(a=\mathsf H_2c_v\), \(b=c_g\mathsf H_0\); in the open case \(a=\mathsf J_2c_u\), \(b=c_v\mathsf J_0\). The compositor witnesses give

\[ \pi_db-\pi_o=d\tau_g,\qquad \chi_da-\chi_o=d\tau_v. \]

Together with the original ordered and direct witnesses, set

\[ \begin{aligned} \Delta&=b\lambda_o-\lambda_da,\\ K&=\tau_g\lambda_o+\omega_o\\ &\quad-\omega_da-\tau_v. \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD8} \]

The exact identity is \(dK=\pi_d\Delta\). The raw map \(\pi_d\) is a quasi-isomorphism by (B.KC3)–(B.KC7), using their K-injective argument, not preservation of arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms by proper image. Since \(A_o\) is whole h-projective, (B.ND7) gives

\[ \begin{gathered} dH=\Delta,\\ \pi_dH-K=dT,\\ |H|=-1,\quad |T|=-2. \end{gathered} \tag{B.OD9} \]

Indeed first choose a primitive \(H_0\) of \(\Delta\) by injectivity on cohomology. The closed difference \(\pi_dH_0-K\) is, in cohomology, the image of a closed degree-minus-one map \(Z\). Replace \(H_0\) by \(H_0-Z\); its remaining image difference is a boundary \(dT\). All maps are in the whole natural Hom complex. Denote the proper and open pairs by \((H_P,T_P)\), \((H_O,T_O)\).

Let \(O_o=(\mathsf V_2O_1)(O_2\mathsf U_1)\) and \(P_o=(\mathsf G_2P_1)(P_2\mathsf V_1)\). Define

\[ K_i=(P_i\mathsf J_{i-1})(\mathsf H_iO_i). \]

Closed degree-zero tensor interchange gives \(K_o=(\mathsf G_2K_1)(K_2\mathsf U_1) =(P_o\mathsf J_0)(\mathsf H_2O_o)\). The direct map is \(K_d=(P_{21}\mathsf J_0)(\mathsf H_2O_{21})\). The compact-support comparison is the explicit two-term homotopy

\[ \begin{aligned} &H_K\\ &\quad=(H_P\mathsf J_0)(\mathsf H_2O_o)\\ &\qquad+(P_{21}\mathsf J_0)(\mathsf H_2H_O),\\ &dH_K\\ &\quad=(c_g\mathsf W_0)K_o\\ &\qquad-K_d(\mathsf W_2c_u). \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD10} \]

The middle terms cancel because the same \(c_v\) occurs on both sides. Retain \(T_P,T_O\) and all compositor witnesses.

The actual right roofs, not only their endpoints

Use the complete right-module construction and compact-support comparison. Its route retains the refined graph with both \(s,t\) edges, the strict \(\rho:\mathcal A_f^+\to\mathcal A_f\), both signed bar comparisons, and the augmentations \(W_f\to L_h\otimes B_j\), \(L_h\to B_h\). Continue through the coend, the cospan (B.KC13), evaluation and induction–restriction in (B.KC14), and double Yoneda. These are the actual roofs from \(DW_f\) to \(H_f\).

The full dual is \(D(f)(\phi)=(-1)^{|f||\phi|}\phi f\); it satisfies \(dD(f)=D(df)\) and \(D(gf)=(-1)^{|f||g|}D(f)D(g)\). The inverse-image roof remains

\[ \begin{aligned} P_gP_h&\longrightarrow D(C_hC_g),\\ P_{hg}&\longrightarrow D(C_hC_g). \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD11} \]

Its right leg points from the direct kernel. Whole replacements precede inverses; both inverse homotopies are retained. Write \(q_i:R_i\to D_i\) for the resulting whole comparisons, including the original zigzags back to the right words:

\[ \begin{aligned} R_0&:\ H_{f_0}P_{g_{21}},\\ D_0&:\ D(\mathsf G_{21}\mathsf W_0),\\ R_1&:\ H_{f_0}P_{g_1}P_{g_2},\\ D_1&:\ D(\mathsf G_2\mathsf G_1\mathsf W_0),\\ R_2&:\ P_{u_{21}}H_{f_2},\\ D_2&:\ D(\mathsf W_2\mathsf U_{21}),\\ R_3&:\ P_{u_1}P_{u_2}H_{f_2},\\ D_3&:\ D(\mathsf W_2\mathsf U_2\mathsf U_1). \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD12} \]

These symbols denote whole representatives, not equality of unresolved tensor products. On the dual side set \(x=D(c_g\mathsf W_0)\), \(y=D(\mathsf W_2c_u)\), \(f_o=D(K_o)\), \(f_d=D(K_d)\), \(h=D(H_K)\). Their types are \(x:D_0\to D_1\), \(y:D_2\to D_3\), \(f_o:D_1\to D_3\), \(f_d:D_0\to D_2\); and \(dh=f_ox-yf_d\).

A closed right arrow \(B:R_i\to R_j\) is retained with its actual roof witness

\[ q_jB-fq_i=dA. \tag{B.OD13} \]

For example \(B=p_jfq_i\) and \(q_jp_j-1=ds_j\) give \(A=s_jfq_i\). For a path of closed arrows, the witness is the sum \(\sum_i f_n\cdots f_{i+1}A_iB_{i-1}\cdots B_1\). This follows by telescoping; it keeps the internal inverse-cancellation witnesses instead of replacing the original path by a new collapsed map. For homogeneous maps the composition rule is \(A_{gf}=A_gB_f+(-1)^{|g|}f_gA_f\), the resolution-graph rule.

The tensor, induction and bar operations used in this construction act on full Hom complexes. On a bar of length \(n\), a homogeneous map \(\phi\) acts with \((-1)^{n|\phi|}\), as in (B.RK7); (B.KC10) and (B.KC11) retain their length-one and opposite signs. RK3 evaluation is a closed natural map with its displayed sign. After passage to the existing strict \(UQ\) roof, a bracket word is an actual homogeneous arrow. Vanishing of the external KC10 terms in bar lengths at least two does not delete the image of that arrow or the internal coefficient \(K_2\) of (B.MX12).

Take the actual ordered and direct KC paths \(B_o:R_1\to R_3\), \(B_d:R_0\to R_2\), and the RK comparison maps \(X:R_0\to R_1\), \(Y:R_2\to R_3\), with witnesses \(A_o,A_d,A_x,A_y\) from (B.OD13). Set

\[ \begin{aligned} \Delta_R&=B_oX\\ &\quad-YB_d,\\ K_R={}&hq_0+A_oX\\ &+f_oA_x\\ &-A_yB_d\\ &-yA_d . \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD14} \]

Expansion gives \(dK_R=q_3\Delta_R\). The same whole-Hom argument as (B.OD9) supplies

\[ \begin{gathered} dH_R=\Delta_R,\\ q_3H_R-K_R=dT_R,\\ |T_R|=-2. \end{gathered} \tag{B.OD15} \]

An arbitrary primitive of \(\Delta_R\) would not establish the second equation. This constructs the comparison on the specified common realization; another stored representative requires its actual comparison roof, not merely an identification of represented objects.

Chosen inverses and the resolved right mate

Let \(\vartheta_o,\vartheta_d\) be the chosen whole inverses of \(B_o,B_d\), with all four homotopies

\[ \begin{aligned} \vartheta_oB_o-1&=dl_o,&B_o\vartheta_o-1&=dr_o,\\ \vartheta_dB_d-1&=dl_d,&B_d\vartheta_d-1&=dr_d. \end{aligned} \]

Their comparison is

\[ \begin{aligned} J={}&-\vartheta_oH_R\vartheta_d\\ &+l_oX\vartheta_d\\ &-\vartheta_oYr_d,\\ dJ={}&\vartheta_oY-X\vartheta_d . \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD16} \]

Direct differentiation cancels the terms with \(\vartheta_oB_o\) and \(B_d\vartheta_d\). Neither of the last two terms may be omitted.

For the mate use the actual factor maps \(s:S_d\to S_o\), \(v:V_d\to V_o\) represented by the RK roofs. Tensoring the same legs with \(H_{f_0}\) or \(H_{f_2}\), and using RK3–4, gives their comparison graphs with \(X=vL_0\), \(Y=L_2s\). If separate whole word replacements intervene, apply (B.OD14)–(B.OD15) to those supplied graphs first, retaining their degree-minus-two witness. A replacement is not declared to commute strictly with tensor. The inverse comparison on these actual factorized maps, evaluated at an admitted resolved \(P_0\), reads

\[ dJ_{P_0}= \vartheta_oL_2(s_{P_0}) -v_{L_0P_0}\vartheta_d . \]

For \(r_0:P_0\to U_0N\), put \(e_0=\varepsilon_0L_0r_0\) and, under \(L_2\dashv U_2\), define

\[ \begin{aligned} \zeta_o&=\operatorname{Adj}(V_oe_0\,\vartheta_o),\\ \zeta_d&=\operatorname{Adj}(V_de_0\,\vartheta_d),\\ \xi&=\operatorname{Adj}(V_oe_0\,J_{P_0}). \end{aligned} \]

The full Hom adjunction and naturality of \(v\) give

\[ \begin{aligned} d\xi={}&\zeta_os_{P_0}\\ &-U_2(v_N)\zeta_d . \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD17} \]

There is no evaluation at the unresolved \(U_0N\), and no equivalence claim for an arbitrary unresolved \(N\). The distinct targets \(V_dN,V_oN\) and their actual map \(v_N\) remain explicit.

Choose whole receiving replacements \(r_d:Q_d\to U_2V_dN\), \(r_o:Q_o\to U_2V_oN\), with the mate lifts \(r_dc_d-\zeta_d=db_d\), \(r_oc_o-\zeta_o=db_o\). Lift the actual target comparison as \(t:Q_d\to Q_o\), \(r_ot-U_2(v_N)r_d=dw\). This uses \(\operatorname{Hom}(Q_d,r_o)\), not an inverse of \(v_N\) or of the right mate. Set

\[ \begin{aligned} \delta&=c_os_{P_0}-tc_d,\\ K_M&=\xi+b_os_{P_0}\\ &\quad-U_2(v_N)b_d\\ &\quad-wc_d . \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD18} \]

Then \(dK_M=r_o\delta\), and (B.ND7) gives

\[ \begin{gathered} dj=\delta,\\ r_oj-K_M=dk,\\ |j|=-1,\quad |k|=-2. \end{gathered} \tag{B.OD19} \]

In the decorated graph the two closed arrows from \((S_dP_0,V_dN,\zeta_d)\) to \((Q_o,V_oN,r_o)\) are \((c_os_{P_0},v_N,b_os_{P_0}+\xi)\) and \((tc_d,v_N,wc_d+U_2(v_N)b_d)\). Thus \(D(j,0,k)=(\delta,0,K_M)\). The target map was retained before taking the difference; no nonfaithful forgetful functor erased it.

The all-degree endpoint bridge now gives

\[ \begin{aligned} \Gamma_{o,d}&=\operatorname{Adj}^{-1}(k),\\ d\Gamma_{o,d} &=e_oL_2j\\ &\quad-\operatorname{Adj}^{-1}(K_M). \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD20} \]

The zero middle coordinate of \((j,0,k)\) does not make this target zero. It is determined by the third coordinate. Equations (B.HB5), (B.HB6) and (B.HB8) retain the remaining graph coordinate and the second product coefficient. This proves the stated fixed-diagram comparison. \(\square\)

The boundary required to attach a prescribed four-face cube

The following gives an exact attachment criterion, not an assertion that all independently prescribed target data satisfy it. Use the four-face notation of B.1ao. For two DG realizations \(F,G\) on the same free diagram, let \(\alpha\) be the closed degree-zero vertex comparisons and \(\mathscr H\) a degree-minus-one comparison on its arrows. Its equations are

\[ \begin{aligned} &d\mathscr H(c)+\mathscr H(dc)\\ &\quad=\alpha_tF(c)-G(c)\alpha_s,\\ &\mathscr H(gf)\\ &\quad=\mathscr H(g)F(f)\\ &\, +(-1)^{|g|}G(g)\mathscr H(f). \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD21} \]

The graded Leibniz rule verifies consistency of these two equations on products. For \(\mathbf B=\mathbf j_C\mathbf{su} +\mathbf w\mathbf j_U-\mathbf j_\beta\mathbf u_X -\mathbf z\mathbf j_F\), the product rule determines

\[ \begin{aligned} &\mathscr H(\mathbf B)\\ &\quad=\mathscr H(\mathbf j_C)F(\mathbf{su})\\ &\qquad-G(\mathbf j_C)\mathscr H(\mathbf{su})\\ &\qquad+\mathscr H(\mathbf w)F(\mathbf j_U)\\ &\qquad+G(\mathbf w)\mathscr H(\mathbf j_U)\\ &\qquad-\mathscr H(\mathbf j_\beta)F(\mathbf u_X)\\ &\qquad+G(\mathbf j_\beta)\mathscr H(\mathbf u_X)\\ &\qquad-\mathscr H(\mathbf z)F(\mathbf j_F)\\ &\qquad-G(\mathbf z)\mathscr H(\mathbf j_F). \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD22} \]

All four face comparisons and all four product terms are required. For the corrected discrepancy \(\widehat R=\mathbf c_RJ_0-J_1\mathbf c_L-\mathbf B-\mathbf b\),

\[ \begin{aligned} &\mathscr H(\widehat R)\\ &\quad=\mathscr H(\mathbf c_R)F(J_0)\\ &\qquad+G(\mathbf c_R)\mathscr H(J_0)\\ &\qquad-\mathscr H(J_1)F(\mathbf c_L)\\ &\qquad+G(J_1)\mathscr H(\mathbf c_L)\\ &\qquad-\mathscr H(\mathbf B)\\ &\qquad-\mathscr H(\mathbf b). \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD23} \]

If \(D\mathbf P=\widehat R\), its next comparison must satisfy

\[ \begin{aligned} D\mathscr H(\mathbf P) &={}\alpha_tF(\mathbf P)\\ &-G(\mathbf P)\alpha_s\\ &-\mathscr H(\widehat R). \end{aligned} \tag{B.OD24} \]

Here \(\mathscr H(\mathbf P)\) has graph degree \(-3\); its third coordinate has degree \(-4\). The right side is closed by (B.OD21), but closedness alone does not identify its actual target. That target includes the original \(\Gamma\)-terms and the endpoint bridges. To use the relative whole-cone lift, one must first supply its target primitive, or prove the target is zero, before restriction. Acyclicity of the source resolution cone is not a replacement for this target comparison.

Consequently (B.OD20) supplies data needed by this attachment, not permission to discard \(\Gamma_{o,d}\), replace earlier triangle choices, omit \(K_2\), or infer a complete changing-parameter cube. Global mixed-array compatibility, geometric nearby-cycle multiplicative descent, coefficient completion, strict-heart higher effacement and recursive provider closure retain their stated scopes.

Paste successive base-change faces with their triangle witnesses

For two successive base changes on the common whole model of B.1az, the four faces of the ordered composite admit a comparison with the pasted first and second faces. The comparison retains the original unit, counit, endpoint and triangle witnesses, including a degree-minus-four coordinate. Receiving objects and the complete comparison pairs

Compare the prescribed ordered and direct triangle data

Proposition B.1bb (the fixed seven-object higher comparison). The actual ordered/direct kernel and inverse comparisons of B.1az extend to the seven-object and triangle data of B.1ao on the specified common whole model. \[ \begin{aligned} &H(\mathbf e_1)=(0,-\beta_t,0),\\ &H(\mathbf c_R)\\ &\quad=(-j,-V_oe_0J,-k),\\ &H(\mathbf b)=(0,\Gamma_{o,d},0). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HT5} \]

The first two follow from B.HT2–3 and unit transposition. To check the third, \(D\mathbf b=\mathbf e_1\mathbf c_L-\mathbf c_R\) gives

\[ H(D\mathbf b) =(0,-\beta_tLc_d-e_oLj+V_oe_0J,k). \]

Subtract this from \(a_tF(\mathbf b)-G(\mathbf b)a_s\). B.HT3 leaves \((0,d\Gamma_{o,d},-k)=D(0,\Gamma_{o,d},0)\), since \(U(\Gamma_{o,d})\eta=k\). This retains the original mate pair (j,k).

For the remaining generators, the target identities can be checked before any graph lift. For instance, \(d\lambda_0=e_0^ML_0u_0-1\) gives

\[ \begin{aligned} &H(D\mathbf j_U)_Z=-V_o(d\lambda_0)J,\\ &d(V_o\lambda_0J)+H(D\mathbf j_U)_Z\\ &\quad=-V_o\lambda_0dJ. \end{aligned} \]

Likewise \(d\alpha_0=e_0L_0z_0-e_0e_0^M\) verifies jC. Both b and jβ have target boundary comparison \(-\beta_tLc_d-e_oLj+V_oe_0J\), so B.HT3 verifies their two entries with the same \(\Gamma_{o,d}\). For J1 the two terms \(-\beta_t\) cancel; for jF the two terms \(-Lj\) cancel. Closed naturality verifies uX, w and u1.

Here is the full lift, not an inference from target equations alone. In a well-founded order, suppose H has already been defined on Dg. Its residual

\[ Z_g=a_tF(g)-G(g)a_s-H(Dg) \]

is closed by B.HT4 on earlier generators and \(D^2g=0\). If the displayed target component is T, the verified identity is \((Z_g)_Z=dT\). Subtract \(D(0,T,0)\) from \(Z_g\). The result is a closed, zero-target element of the full graph Hom complex. Except for the unit-headed arrows handled explicitly above, every receiving vertex is one of A, C, R or Qq with a whole quasi-isomorphic replacement. The kernel is therefore the shifted cone of \(\operatorname{Hom}(P_d,q_o)\), acyclic by (B.ND7). Choose a full zero-target primitive and add it to \((0,T,0)\). This produces H(g) with exactly the prescribed target and the required third coordinate. Earlier comparisons and all original F/G arrows and faces remain fixed. The free presentation and B.HT4 extend this to every path; no relations of an unexamined nonfree quotient are being imposed.

The actual target of the higher discrepancy

Retain all eight terms of B.OD22, even those whose target vanishes. For \(\mathbf B=\mathbf j_C\mathbf s_u+\mathbf w\mathbf j_U -\mathbf j_\beta\mathbf u_X-\mathbf z_1\mathbf j_F\), the table gives

\[ \begin{aligned} &H(\mathbf B)_Z\\ &\quad=V_o\alpha_0J_{R_0}LS_du_0\\ &\qquad+V_oe_0V_o\lambda_0J-\Gamma_{o,d}\\ &\quad=V_o\bigl(\alpha_0L_0u_0\\ &\qquad+e_0\lambda_0\bigr)J-\Gamma_{o,d}. \end{aligned} \tag{B.HT6} \]

The simplification uses naturality of J at the closed u0. The Hz1 term vanishes only because the prescribed target of F(jF) is zero; Hz1 itself is generally nonzero.

For the corrected discrepancy \(\widehat{\mathbf R}=\mathbf c_R\mathbf J_0 -\mathbf J_1\mathbf c_L-\mathbf B-\mathbf b\), the odd-degree naturality sign is essential:

\[ \begin{aligned} &J_{Q_0}LS_dJ_0\\ &\quad=-V_o(L_0J_0)J_{Q_0}. \end{aligned}\tag{B.HT7} \]

Thus the cR J0 term contributes \(+V_o(e_0L_0J_0)J\). The J1 cL target is zero. The two occurrences of \(\Gamma_{o,d}\), one from B.HT6 and the other from H(b), cancel. They are not separately set to zero. Consequently

\[ \begin{aligned} &H(\widehat{\mathbf R})_Z\\ &\quad=V_o\bigl(e_0L_0J_0\\ &\qquad-\alpha_0L_0u_0-e_0\lambda_0\bigr)J\\ &\quad=V_o(d\Gamma_0)J. \end{aligned}\tag{B.HT8} \]

Here \(\Gamma_0=\operatorname{Adj}_0^{-1}K_0\) retains the entire original K0, including the nested correction required by B.NT7.

Let the original full triangle fillers be \(P_d,P_o\), with \(DP_\sigma=\widehat R_\sigma\) and actual targets \(\gamma_\sigma=V_\sigma\Gamma_0\vartheta_\sigma\). For B.OD24 the closed graph residual is

\[ Z_P=a_{Qq}P_d-P_oa_{Q0u}-H(\widehat R). \]

Closed naturality of v at the degree-minus-two Γ0 gives

\[ \begin{aligned} &(Z_P)_Z=-V_o\Gamma_0dJ\\ &\qquad-V_o(d\Gamma_0)J\\ &\quad=d\bigl(-V_o\Gamma_0J\bigr). \end{aligned} \tag{B.HT9} \]

This is the required actual target primitive, not just closedness after applying U. Set \(T_P=-V_o\Gamma_0J\), of degree −3. The residual \(Z_P-D(0,T_P,0)\) is closed with target zero. Apply B.ND7 to the whole Hom from \(S_dQ_0\) through \(q_o\), obtaining a zero-target primitive \((h_P,0,w_P)\). Then

\[ \begin{gathered} H(P)=(h_P,T_P,w_P),\\ DH(P)=Z_P,\\ |h_P|=|T_P|=-3,\\ |w_P|=-4. \end{gathered}\tag{B.HT10} \]

The third coordinate is retained. Neither Pσ nor its original third coordinate is replaced: both occur literally in ZP.

Compare the ordered paste with the prescribed direct triangle

The ordered construction of B.1ba has

\[ \begin{aligned} &P_{\rm assembled}=m_QP_{1T}+P_2l_1\\ &\qquad-G l_1-K_{\rm paste},\\ &D\Omega=P_{\rm assembled}-P_{21}. \end{aligned} \]

Its actual target equals \(\gamma_o\); the Γ1 bridge cancels the additional \(\gamma_2h_0\) rather than being discarded. The full Ω has zero target, degree −3 and a degree-minus-four third coordinate. Take \(P_o=P_{21}\) in B.HT10. Since the initial vertex comparison a is closed, the comparison with the assembled filler is exactly

\[ \begin{aligned} &H(P)_{\rm assembled}\\ &\quad=H(P)_{21}-\Omega a_{Q0u}. \end{aligned}\tag{B.HT11} \]

Differentiation subtracts \((P_{\rm assembled}-P_{21})a_{Q0u}\), exactly the change in ZP. The target primitive remains TP because Ω has target zero. This preserves the original P1T, P2, P21, all six prior face-residual fillers, Γ0/Γ1/Γ21, and Ω's degree-minus-four witness in one explicit fixed ordered/direct comparison. It is not a replacement of them by an unspecified convenient primitive.

Scope of the comparison

The construction compares the specified closed two-step diagram on the admitted common whole parameter model. It does not automatically extend to every nonzero-degree record, an already prescribed horizontal gH cube, changing-index restrictions, or mixed horizontal/vertical UQ words. In particular H(P(gH)) has another degree and needs its own target calculation; B.HT10 must not be used as a certificate for that next dimension. Re-resolve after changed restriction; preserve KC signed bars and the GC/MX K2 terms. Global geometric assembly, nearby-cycle descent, coefficient completion, strict-heart higher effacement, recursive provider closure are not consequences of this fixed-diagram comparison.

\(\square\)

Compare homogeneous records with their full boundary

Proposition B.1bc (conditional homogeneous-record comparison). The target calculation of B.1bb extends to the full record differential, provided the actual graded comparison and its lower boundary are supplied on one whole parameter model. The construction retains the mate pair and the higher third coordinate; it does not assert that the geometric higher comparison has already been constructed.

Earlier constructions: B.RC; B.CE.

The full arrow graph B.FG retains the third coordinates.

Exact inputs and the remaining geometric distinction

Work on one admitted whole parameter model with the receiving adjunction \(L\dashv U\). Preserve the initial resolved triangle, including \(Q_0,R_0,u_0,z_0,J_0,\lambda_0,\alpha_0,\Gamma_0\), and the direct and ordered realizations of B.HT. For this calculation \(S_d,S_o,V_d,V_o\) and the closed comparisons \(s:S_d\to S_o\), \(v:V_d\to V_o\) are fixed. Do not identify different functors or parameter indices without their actual transport maps. The result is an interface on a common model, not permission to pretend that a changing-model diagram is fixed.

Let \(f\) be a homogeneous record of degree \(n\), with differential \(\partial f\) of degree \(n+1\). Its two cells \(\theta_\sigma(f)\) are chain-linear in the record: \(d\theta_\sigma(f)=\theta_\sigma(\partial f)\). The necessary additional datum is a graded natural, linear comparison \(J(f):LS_d\to V_oL_0\) of degree \(n-1\), satisfying

\[ \begin{aligned} &dJ(f)+J(\partial f)\\ &\quad=\theta_o(f)Ls\\ &\qquad-vL_0\theta_d(f). \end{aligned}\tag{B.RCmp1} \]

This is an input equation in the actual target category, before applying \(U\). The closed degree-zero comparison of B.HT1 alone does not specify \(J(f_H)\), nor its value on the boundary of a horizontal record.

For a supplied free cellular record presentation, lower values are kept fixed. A claim over an arbitrary complex with relations would need its own extension argument; no projectivity of that arbitrary complex is assumed. Changing the underlying parameter index requires B.CE11 re-resolution.

The existing geometric providers supply different, indispensable data:

Provider Actual supplied datum What it does not identify on its own
B.MX8–10 The six-edge whole-kernel cell \((H,K)\), with \(dH=T-B\) and the common-target witness equation \(J(f_H)\) after the chosen inverse, duality and seven-object transports
B.KC10–16 and B.MX12 Signed bar/dual roofs, the resolved mate and retained nested \(K_2\) Equality of independently prescribed higher faces
B.CE10–11 Relative lifts of a checked base diagram and re-resolution on restriction A missing base boundary
B.CY1–12 A strict free cylinder realizing an already supplied comparison homotopy A new homotopy not contained in its input

Thus the elementary mixed cube is not absent. The specific attachment still to verify is B.RCmp1, with its chosen geometric higher comparison and boundary, on the common whole model.

The full mate pair, with its record differential

Write \(e_\sigma=\epsilon Lq_\sigma\). Keep the receiving comparison \((t,v_N,w)\), with \(q_ot-U(v_N)q_d=dw\), and put \(\beta_t=\operatorname{Adj}^{-1}w\). The RC records retain

\[ \begin{aligned} dc_\sigma(f)&=c_\sigma(\partial f),\\ db_\sigma(f)&+b_\sigma(\partial f)\\ &=q_\sigma c_\sigma(f)\\ &\quad-\operatorname{Adj}(V_\sigma e_0\theta_\sigma(f)). \end{aligned} \]

Define the actual degree-\(n-1\) map

\[ \begin{aligned} K_M(f)&=\operatorname{Adj}(V_oe_0J(f))\\ &\quad+b_o(f)s\\ &\quad-U(v_N)b_d(f)-wc_d(f). \end{aligned} \]

Keep the full pair \(j(f),k(f)\), of degrees \(n-1,n-2\), satisfying

\[ \begin{aligned} &dj(f)+j(\partial f)\\ &=c_o(f)s-tc_d(f),\\ &q_oj(f)-K_M(f)\\ &=dk(f)-k(\partial f). \end{aligned}\tag{B.RCmp2} \]

The minus sign in the second equation is not optional. Indeed, differentiating \(K_M\), including \(d(-wc_d)=-(dw)c_d+w c_d(\partial f)\), gives

\[ dK_M(f)+K_M(\partial f)=q_o(c_o(f)s-tc_d(f)). \]

Consequently \((c_os-tc_d,K_M)\) is a chain map to the shifted Hom cone with differential \(\delta(x,y)=(dx,q_ox-dy)\). On a free cell whose lower boundary pair has already been selected, subtract that lower pair. The remaining cone element is closed. B.ND7 supplies its primitive through the actual whole quasi-isomorphism \(q_o\), giving B.RCmp2 without altering the lower choices. This is not an assertion that an objectwise cone is whole-acyclic.

Let \(\beta_\sigma(f)=\operatorname{Adj}^{-1}b_\sigma(f)\) and \(\Gamma(f)=\operatorname{Adj}^{-1}k(f)\). Full Hom adjunction gives

\[ \begin{aligned} &d\beta_t\\ &\quad=e_oLt-v_Ne_d,\\ &d\Gamma(f)\\ &\quad-\Gamma(\partial f)\\ &\quad=e_oLj(f)\\ &\qquad-V_oe_0J(f)\\ &\qquad-\beta_o(f)Ls\\ &\qquad+v_N\beta_d(f)\\ &\qquad+\beta_tLc_d(f). \end{aligned}\tag{B.RCmp3} \]

These are actual target maps; \(k\) has not been projected away.

The comparison on the four faces and the endpoint bridge

Use the full decorated graph differential of B.FT2 and the degree-minus-one comparison convention

\[ \begin{aligned} &DH(g)\\ &+H(Dg)\\ &\quad=a_tF(g)\\ &\qquad-G(g)a_s,\\ &H(gh)\\ &=H(g)F(h)\\ &+(-1)^{|g|}\\ &\quad G(g)H(h). \end{aligned}\tag{B.RCmp4} \]

Here \(F=d,G=o\); \(a\) is the seven-vertex comparison of B.HT. The fixed generators and vertex maps remain as in B.HT4–5. For the record-dependent arrows the target entries are

\[ \begin{array}{c|c} g(f)&H(g(f))_Z\\ \hline \mathbf c_R&-V_oe_0J\\ \mathbf c_M&-V_oe_0^MJ_{R_0}\\ \mathbf v&-J\\ \mathbf c_L,\mathbf a&-Lj\\ \mathbf j_U&V_o\lambda_0J\\ \mathbf j_C&V_o\alpha_0J_{R_0}\\ \mathbf j_F&0\\ \mathbf b,\mathbf j_\beta&\Gamma \end{array} \tag{B.RCmp5} \]

The full formulas, not just their target coordinates, include

\[ \begin{gathered} H(\mathbf c_L(f))\\ =-A(j(f)),\\ H(\mathbf c_R(f))\\ =(-j(f),\\ -V_oe_0J(f),\\ -k(f)),\\ H(\mathbf b(f))\\ =(0,\Gamma(f),0). \end{gathered}\tag{B.RCmp6} \]

The record differential is essential. B.FG6 says \(D\mathbf b(f)=\mathbf e_1\mathbf c_L(f)-\mathbf c_R(f) -\mathbf b(\partial f)\). Hence

\[ \begin{aligned} &H(D\mathbf b(f))\\ &\quad=(0,-\beta_tLc_d\\ &\qquad-e_oLj+V_oe_0J\\ &\qquad-\Gamma(\partial f),k(f)). \end{aligned} \]

Adding \(DH(\mathbf b(f))=(0,d\Gamma(f),-k(f))\) and using B.RCmp3 proves the full equation B.RCmp4. The last coordinates cancel because they were retained, not because they were assumed zero. For \(\mathbf c_R\), the last coordinate of \(DH(\mathbf c_R(f))+H(\mathbf c_R(\partial f))\) is

\[ \begin{aligned} &-q_oj+\operatorname{Adj}(V_oe_0J)\\ &\quad+dk-k(\partial f)\\ &\qquad=wc_d+U(v_N)b_d-b_os. \end{aligned} \]

This is exactly the last coordinate of its comparison boundary.

For the unit face, the lower-boundary contribution is

\[ H(D\mathbf j_U(f))_Z =-V_o(d\lambda_0)J(f)-V_o\lambda_0J(\partial f). \]

Adding \(d(V_o\lambda_0J(f))\) leaves \(-V_o\lambda_0(dJ(f)+J(\partial f))\), the required boundary. The counit face is identical with \(\alpha_0\) and its actual differential. The \(\mathbf j_\beta\) face uses B.RCmp3; the \(\mathbf j_F\) terms cancel. Thus the table is compatible with the nonclosed record, not only with its degree-zero endpoints.

At each remaining free generator subtract its already fixed lower comparison and the differential of the prescribed target triple \((0,T,0)\). The residual is closed with target zero. For the non-unit receiving vertices the whole Hom cone through the recorded replacement is acyclic. Lift this residual there, keeping the third coordinate. The unit-headed arrows use the explicit \(A(j)\) and naturality formulas above, not acyclicity of a unit. This is the same relative construction as B.HT, now with the record differential retained.

Target of the triangle comparison in every record degree

B.FG10 uses the degree-dependent discrepancy

\[ \begin{aligned} \widehat{\mathbf R}(f)&=(-1)^n\mathbf c_R(f)\mathbf J_0\\ &\quad-\mathbf J_1\mathbf c_L(f)\\ &\quad-\mathbf B(f)-\mathbf b(f). \end{aligned} \]

Since \(J(f)\) has degree \(n-1\), its actual graded naturality is

\[ \begin{gathered} J_{Q_0}(f)LS_dJ_0\\ =(-1)^{n-1}\\ V_o(L_0J_0)\\ \qquad J_{Q_0}(f). \end{gathered}\tag{B.RCmp7} \]

Multiplying this by the coefficient \((-1)^n\) in the discrepancy and by the minus sign in \(H(\mathbf c_R)\) gives a positive \(V_o(e_0L_0J_0)J(f)\), for every \(n\). The \(\mathbf J_1\mathbf c_L\) target vanishes, while

\[ H(\mathbf B(f))_Z =V_o(\alpha_0L_0u_0+e_0\lambda_0)J(f)-\Gamma(f). \]

The two \(\Gamma(f)\) occurrences cancel. Consequently

\[ \begin{gathered} H(\widehat{\mathbf R}(f))_Z\\ =V_o(d\Gamma_0)J(f). \end{gathered}\tag{B.RCmp8} \]

For \(g=(f,p)\) in the full RC record complex, B.FG12 says \(D\mathbf P_\sigma(g)=\mathbf P_\sigma(\partial g) +\widehat{\mathbf R}_\sigma(f)\). Its actual target is \(V_\sigma\Gamma_0\theta_\sigma(f)\). Put

\[ \begin{aligned} Z(g)&=a_{Qq}\mathbf P_d(g)-\mathbf P_o(g)a_{Q0u} -H(\widehat{\mathbf R}(f)),\\ T(g)&=-V_o\Gamma_0J(f). \end{aligned} \]

Closed naturality of \(v\), B.RCmp1 and B.RCmp8 give the exact identity

\[ \begin{gathered} Z(g)_Z\\ =dT(g)+T(\partial g). \end{gathered}\tag{B.RCmp9} \]

In detail the right side is \(-V_o(d\Gamma_0)J(f)-V_o\Gamma_0[dJ(f)+J(\partial f)]\). There is no acyclicity assumption on the actual target category. If the lower comparisons are already given, subtract \(H(\mathbf P(\partial g))\) from \(Z(g)\), then subtract \(D(0,T(g),0)\). The full residual is a closed zero-target graph element. The whole Hom cone supplies its primitive. This gives

\[ \begin{gathered} DH(\mathbf P(g))\\ +H(\mathbf P(\partial g))\\ =Z(g),\\ H(\mathbf P(g))_Z\\ =T(g), \end{gathered}\tag{B.RCmp10} \]

without replacing either original \(\mathbf P_\sigma\) or its witnesses. The degrees are

\[ \begin{gathered} |\mathbf P(g)|=n-2,\\ |H(\mathbf P(g))|=|T(g)|=n-3,\\ |\text{third coordinate of }H(\mathbf P(g))|\\ =n-4. \end{gathered} \]

The horizontal boundary and the scope of the result

For the recorded \(g_H\) with \(|g_H|=-1\) and \(\partial g_H=g_T-g_B\), B.RCmp10 becomes

\[ \begin{aligned} &DH(\mathbf P(g_H))\\ &=a\mathbf P_d(g_H)\\ &-\mathbf P_o(g_H)a\\ &-H(\widehat{\mathbf R}(f_H))\\ &-H(\mathbf P(g_T))\\ &+H(\mathbf P(g_B)). \end{aligned}\tag{B.RCmp11} \]

Its target primitive is \(-V_o\Gamma_0J(f_H)\), of degree minus four; its new third coordinate has degree minus five. The old \(\mathbf P(g_H)\) remains degree minus three with its original degree-minus-four third coordinate. The two must not be conflated. The endpoint target terms \(-T(g_T)+T(g_B)\) are required. Applying the closed-record B.HT9 equation without them leaves a nonzero boundary term.

This establishes the target and full-lift interface given B.RCmp1–3 on the actual common model. It does not construct the geometric \(J(f_H)\). That map, its endpoints and the corresponding mate pair require compatible representatives through the KC/GC/MX and HN roofs, preserving the relative unit face, both inverse witnesses, signed bar coefficients, \(K_2\), and the specified ordered \(\Omega\). Applying the fixed-degree \(\Omega\) formula to a nonclosed family additionally requires its family differential.

This conditional comparison does not establish all-array coherence, nearby-cycle descent, coefficient completion or the existence of its geometric inputs.

Keep the inverse witnesses and their higher obstruction

Proposition B.1bd (inverse witnesses and the obstruction to extending endpoints). The fixed comparison of B.1az does not imply that arbitrary endpoint homotopies extend over a higher cell. The obstruction is an explicit whole-Hom class. There is also an explicit alternative inverse package with two triangle coherences; its closed displacement from the original package must be retained.

Earlier constructions: B.CY; B.RCmp.

1. The exact higher obstruction

On the actual common model required by B.RCmp1, write the two mixed cells as \(\theta_{d,H},\theta_{o,H}\), with \(d\theta_{\sigma,H}=\theta_{\sigma,T}-\theta_{\sigma,B}\). Let the already chosen endpoint inverse comparisons satisfy

\[ dJ_E=\theta_{o,E}Ls-vL_0\theta_{d,E},\qquad E=T,B. \]

The required comparison on the higher record must satisfy

\[ \begin{aligned} \mathcal O&=\theta_{o,H}Ls\\ &\quad-vL_0\theta_{d,H}\\ &\quad-J_T+J_B,\\ dJ_H&=\mathcal O,\\ |\mathcal O|&=-1,\quad |J_H|=-2. \end{aligned}\tag{B.IW1} \]

Differentiation cancels the four endpoint terms, so \(d\mathcal O=0\). Existence with the stated fixed endpoints is therefore exactly vanishing of its class in the whole natural Hom complex

\[ [\mathcal O]\in H^{-1}\operatorname{Hom}(LS_d,V_oL_0). \]

This is not the acyclic zero-target kernel of a resolution graph. It cannot be filled merely because a receiving replacement is a quasi-isomorphism or because the two endpoints have the same represented object. If the actual geometry supplies a primitive, that precise primitive or its full comparison is needed.

2. Why pairwise inverse equations are insufficient

This example tests the inference, not the actual geometric kernels. Let \(E^0=E^1=\mathbb Z\), all other degrees vanish, and let the differential of \(E\) be zero. The map \(a:E^1\to E^0\) given by the identity is a nonzero degree-minus-one endomorphism; every Hom differential is zero and \(\operatorname{End}^{-2}(E)=0\).

Take every kernel comparison, inverse, roof and endpoint comparison map to be \(1_E\). Take the right-kernel mixed comparisons and their witnesses to be zero. All the ordinary inverse equations

\[ d\ell=\theta\beta-1,\qquad dr=\beta\theta-1 \]

then hold for any degree-minus-one \(\ell,r\). At the top endpoint choose \(\ell_{o,T}=a,r_{d,T}=0\). At the bottom choose \(\ell_{o,B}=r_{d,B}=0\); take all other inverse witnesses to be zero.

The literal B.OD16 formula

\[ J=-\theta_oH_R\theta_d+\ell_oX\theta_d-\theta_oYr_d \]

gives \(J_T=a,J_B=0\). Both satisfy their required closed endpoint equations. The two higher inverse cells may both be zero because their endpoint inverse maps are equal. Nevertheless B.IW1 gives \(\mathcal O=-a\), which has no degree-minus-two primitive.

Thus valid inverse maps, both valid inverse homotopies, and a supplied mixed kernel cube do not by themselves establish compatibility of arbitrarily selected endpoint comparison homotopies. This does not invalidate B.OD16 or the conditional RCmp calculation. It prevents promoting them to an unconditional higher geometric attachment.

3. A concrete triangle-coherent inverse package

Let \(\beta:A\to B,\theta:B\to A\) be closed degree-zero maps on the whole models, with the retained old witnesses

\[ d\ell=\theta\beta-1_A,\qquad dr=\beta\theta-1_B. \]

Define the closed inverse-coherence defect and an additional left witness

\[ \begin{gathered} \delta=\beta\ell-r\beta,\\ d\delta=0,\\ \ell^{c}=\ell-\theta\delta. \end{gathered}\tag{B.IW2} \]

The original \(\ell,r\) are not deleted or renamed. The new witness \(\ell^c\) has the same differential as \(\ell\), but their difference \(-\theta\delta\) is only known to be closed, not a boundary.

Set

\[ \tau=-r\delta. \]

Then, by direct differentiation,

\[ \begin{gathered} d\ell^c=\theta\beta-1_A,\\ d\tau=\beta\ell^c-r\beta. \end{gathered}\tag{B.IW3} \]

Indeed the right side of the second equation is \(\delta-\beta\theta\delta=-(dr)\delta=d(-r\delta)\). This adds an explicit degree-minus-two coherence without imposing acyclicity on \(\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)\).

The opposite triangle has an explicit witness too. Put

\[ \begin{aligned} \delta_R&=\theta r-\ell^c\theta,\\ Q&=r^2-\tau\theta,\\ \sigma&=\theta Q-\ell^c\delta_R . \end{aligned} \tag{B.IW4} \]

Here \(|\delta_R|=-1\), \(|Q|=|\sigma|=-2\), and the maps are respectively \(B\to A,B\to B,B\to A\). Their differentials give

\[ \begin{gathered} d\delta_R=0,\\ dQ=\beta\delta_R,\\ d\sigma=\delta_R. \end{gathered}\tag{B.IW5} \]

For the middle identity,

\[ \begin{aligned} &d(r^2-\tau\theta)\\ &\quad=(\beta\theta-1)r-r(\beta\theta-1)\\ &\qquad-(\beta\ell^c-r\beta)\theta\\ &\quad=\beta(\theta r-\ell^c\theta). \end{aligned} \]

The last follows by subtracting \(d(\ell^c\delta_R)=(\theta\beta-1)\delta_R\) from \(d(\theta Q)=\theta\beta\delta_R\). All products, signs, source/target types and degrees are literal.

These polynomial formulas are whole natural maps when their inputs are. They do not require evaluating an inverse on an unresolved right adjoint. They supply the two displayed triangle coherences, not an unspecified infinite coherent inverse system.

4. The old B.OD16 comparison is retained with its exact displacement

For the original square

\[ H_R:A_d\to B_o[-1],\qquad dH_R=\beta_oX-Y\beta_d, \]

retain its full roof witness as well as both pairs of inverse homotopies. Changing only the left witness used on the ordered side yields the additional comparison

\[ J^c=-\theta_oH_R\theta_d+\ell_o^cX\theta_d-\theta_oYr_d. \]

The old and new comparisons have the same differential, and their literal difference is

\[ \begin{gathered} J^c=J-C,\\ C=\theta_o\delta_oX\theta_d,\\ dC=0. \end{gathered}\tag{B.IW6} \]

There is no claim that \(C\) is exact. In the example above it is the nonzero map \(a\).

For the fixed higher input of B.IW1 this changes the obstruction by

\[ \mathcal O^c=\mathcal O+C_T-C_B, \tag{B.IW7} \]

provided the actual \(\theta_{\sigma,H}\) are kept unchanged. The example then has zero obstruction, but the formula is not a proof of vanishing for the geometric programme.

This distinction is operationally important: do not silently replace the old endpoint \(J_E\) and then claim that a primitive has been found for its original boundary. Keep \(J_E,J_E^c,C_E\) as distinct maps. Changing the canonical comparison route must propagate these literal closed displacements through its mate, four faces and target primitive. The original fixed comparison is still valid as a separate route.

5. Geometric application and its additional hypotheses

The geometric inputs are the MX cube, KC signed bar roofs and HN nested folding. B.CY11 and the obstruction above show that an inverse comparison alone does not supply arbitrary prescribed higher boundaries.

Application of B.RCmp1 requires the actual common geometric models and their precise endpoint choices, together with either of the following:

  1. a full primitive of B.IW1 retaining the endpoint \(J_T,J_B\); or
  2. a coherent whole-index inverse package, its endpoint-comparison displacements, and a proof of the corresponding higher boundary.

B.IW2–5 give part of the second construction. Normalization of individual inverse packages does not imply \(\mathcal O^c=0\) or construct the geometric \(J_H\). Both alternatives retain the signed bars, nested \(K_2\), original unit/counit/triangle witnesses and ordered \(\Omega\). A changed parameter index requires a new resolution of the whole restricted diagram.

The counterexample concerns the inference from pairwise choices; it does not compute the actual geometric obstruction or contradict a source theorem. The displayed coherences do not establish all-array coherence.

Place the mixed cube on one whole inverse model

Proposition B.1be (the whole-index mixed roof). The six-vertex cube of B.MX6–10 determines a strict signed bar roof on its free parameter category. The higher witness is an actual component of that roof. An inverse and both homotopies can be selected on the whole index before taking endpoint values. Their identification with independently chosen endpoint comparisons is a separate question.

Earlier constructions: B.KC; B.ND.

The actual free index and its two diagrams

Let \(\mathcal D\) be the B.MX10 free dg category on vertices \(0,1,2,3,4,5\), the six reversed closed edges

\[ \begin{gathered} e_{01}:1\to0,\ e_{12}:2\to1,\ e_{23}:3\to2,\\ e_{04}:4\to0,\ e_{45}:5\to4,\ e_{53}:3\to5, \end{gathered} \]

and the degree-minus-one generator \(c:3\to0\) with

\[ dc=e_{01}e_{12}e_{23}-e_{04}e_{45}e_{53}. \]

Use the exact whole bimodules \(W_i\), maps \(a_i:W_i\to M_\square\), edges \(\lambda_{ij}\), witnesses \(\omega_{ij}\), and full mixed pair \((H,K)\) of B.MX5–8. They define two strict dg diagrams:

\[ \begin{array}{c|ccc} &i&e_{ij}&c\\ \hline \mathcal W&W_i&\lambda_{ij}&H\\ \mathcal M&M_\square&1&0 . \end{array} \tag{B.MP1} \]

The first is a dg diagram because \(dH=T-B\); the second because the two edge words both map to the identity. Their parameter category is literally the stated free category, not a quotient asserting \(T=B\).

The comparison has object values \(\alpha_i=a_i\), arrow homotopies \(k_{e_{ij}}=\omega_{ij}\), and the indispensable higher value

\[ k_c=K. \tag{B.MP2} \]

For homogeneous paths extend by

\[ k_{gf}=k_g\mathcal W(f)+(-1)^{|g|}\mathcal M(g)k_f,\qquad k_1=0. \]

These are exactly the third coordinates of the resolution-graph composition B.MX9. On an edge, the B.KC9 differential equation is B.MX5. On \(c\), it is the second equation of B.MX8:

\[ \begin{aligned} &dk_c+k_{dc}\\ &=dK+\Omega_T-\Omega_B\\ &=a_0H\\ &=\alpha_0\mathcal W(c)\\ &\quad-\mathcal M(c)\alpha_3. \end{aligned}\tag{B.MP3} \]

The path differential and product rule extend this to all homogeneous words. Dropping \(K\) would lose B.MP3 even though the first equation \(dH=T-B\) remained true.

The signed bar map is a strict map of the whole diagrams

For each vertex \(i\), apply B.KC10 with the right representable \(\mathcal D(-,i)\). The source is

\[ \mathcal P\mathcal W(i) =B(\mathcal D(-,i),\mathcal D,\mathcal W). \]

It has the ordinary augmentation to \(\mathcal W(i)\). After co-Yoneda on the target, the comparison is the literal map

\[ \begin{gathered} \Psi_i(m\otimes x)\\ =\mathcal M(m)\alpha_a x,\\ \Psi_i(m\otimes t\otimes x)\\ =(-1)^{|m|+1}\mathcal M(m)k_t x,\\ \Psi_i\big|_{[n]}=0\quad(n\geq2). \end{gathered}\tag{B.MP4} \]

Its chain identity is B.KC9–10 with the input B.MP2–3, including the original total-degree convention (internal degree minus bar length). For a homogeneous parameter arrow \(u:i\to j\), the representable map postcomposes \(m\) by \(u\), with the B.RK7 factor \((-1)^{n|u|}\) on bar length \(n\). At length one the coefficient in \(\Psi_j\mathcal P\mathcal W(u)\) is \((-1)^{|u|+|u|+|m|+1}=(-1)^{|m|+1}\), exactly the coefficient in \(\mathcal M(u)\Psi_i\). Thus this is graded naturality, including nonzero-degree parameter arrows, not just naturality of closed edges. The original endpoint variables use the same Koszul interchange, because all \(a,\lambda,\omega,H,K\) are whole bimodule maps. It is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism by B.KC10: the right representable is h-projective and each \(\alpha_i\) is the actual B.MX4 quasi-isomorphism. No unresolved proper image is assumed exact.

In particular, at the distinguished length-one tensor with \(m=1_0\),

\[ \Psi_0(1_0\otimes c\otimes x)=-Kx. \tag{B.MP5} \]

The degree of \(c\) is minus one and this tensor has one bar position, so both sides have degree \(|x|-2\). The higher witness has become an actual component of the strict map; it was not discarded. The vanishing at external bar length at least two does not erase a nonzero image of an internal UQ word. On a larger supplied index use the strict UQ word images with the original \(K_2\), as B.MX12 requires.

Select the inverse on this index, not vertex by vertex

Take a whole h-projective replacement \(\rho:R\to\mathcal P\mathcal W\) over \(\mathcal D\) times the endpoint product category, and a whole replacement \(q:Q\to\mathcal M\). B.ND5 provides these without assuming that restriction preserves whole projectivity. Apply B.ND7 to the actual closed map \(\Psi\rho\). Obtain

\[ \begin{gathered} \beta:R\to Q,\\ b:R\to\mathcal M[-1],\\ q\beta-\Psi\rho=db. \end{gathered}\tag{B.MP6} \]

Here \(\beta,b\) are whole-index maps. The two maps to \(\mathcal M\) are quasi-isomorphisms, so \(\beta\) is a quasi-isomorphism between whole h-projectives. Select its whole inverse \(\theta:Q\to R\) and both whole inverse witnesses \(\ell,r\). The exact formulas B.IW2–5 then provide the additional \(\ell^c,\tau,\sigma\), also whole-index maps.

Thus this particular six-vertex geometry has an explicit strict roof

\[ \begin{gathered} \mathcal W\ \longleftarrow\ \mathcal P\mathcal W\\ \ \longleftarrow R\ \xrightarrow{\beta} Q\\ \ \xrightarrow{q}\mathcal M, \end{gathered}\tag{B.MP7} \]

with the recorded \(\Psi\rho\), its full witness \(b\), and the whole inverse package. The arrow to \(\mathcal W\) is the bar augmentation, not the non-strict family \(\alpha_i\). All original data remain accessible through B.MP1–5. The choices are not asserted to be unique or canonical.

Scope of the whole-index construction

B.MP1–7 instantiate the whole inverse-selection step on the actual MX parameter category with its actual higher comparison. The higher bar component is therefore determined by the given mixed cube. The inverse and witnesses must first be chosen on this whole index. For a new index, restrict the displayed diagram and then re-resolve as B.CE11 prescribes.

Application of the RCmp target and mate formulas requires transport of this roof through the original right-kernel dual/evaluation and factorized \(S,V\) comparisons of B.OD11–19. Its comparison with the fixed endpoint routes must retain the closed displacements \(C_T,C_B\); their exactness is an additional condition. The required datum is a geometric \(J_H\), or a primitive of the literal B.IW1 obstruction, on the same receiving seven-object diagram.

B.MP7 alone does not imply extension of the independently prescribed \(J_T,J_B\), compatibility over all changing arrays, or existence of the degree-minus-five witness.

Dualize the mixed model with all graph witnesses

Proposition B.1bf (signed dual graph and inverse span). The whole mixed model of B.1be has a signed right-dual graph and a safe comparison span. All statements retain the original coefficient, proper-base-change, whole-resolution and resolved-input hypotheses. The raw dual of the unresolved mapping target is not asserted to be an equivalence.

Earlier constructions: B.RK; B.IW.

1. The full graded dual, including graph witnesses

For a left kernel \(A\), use the literal B.RK1 full Hom dual \(DA(J,I)=\operatorname{Hom}(A(-,I),\mathcal E(J,-))\). For homogeneous \(f:A\to B\) of degree \(p\), its action is

\[ \begin{gathered} (Df)(\phi)=(-1)^{p|\phi|}\phi f,\\ d(Df)=D(df),\\ D(gf)\\ =(-1)^{|g||f|}(Df)(Dg). \end{gathered}\tag{B.RD1} \]

These formulas follow by the Hom differential and graded precomposition. They are the dg-opposite convention, not unsigned reversal.

Write an ordinary graph object as \(a:P\to Q\), and a degree-\(n\) arrow as \((c,v,h)\), with differential

\[ D_{\rm ar}(c,v,h)=(dc,dv,a'c-va-dh). \]

The dual graph object is \(Da:DQ\to DP\). The full dual graph map is

\[ \begin{gathered} \mathfrak D(c,v,h)\\ =(Dv,Dc,-Dh). \end{gathered}\tag{B.RD2} \]

It is a strict dg functor from the opposite graph category:

\[ \begin{gathered} D_{\rm ar}\mathfrak D(x)\\ =\mathfrak D(D_{\rm ar}x),\\ \mathfrak D(yx)\\ =(-1)^{|x||y|}\mathfrak D(x)\mathfrak D(y). \end{gathered}\tag{B.RD3} \]

For the third differential, both sides are \(Da\,Dv-Dc\,Da'+D(dh)\). For the product, dualizing \(h_yc_x+(-1)^{|y|}v_yh_x\) gives precisely the third coordinate of the right side, including the \((-1)^{|x|}\) in the reversed graph product. Thus a third-coordinate witness changes sign; it does not disappear.

2. Apply it to the actual MX cube

For B.MX5–9 use the ordinary graph convention \((c,v,h)=(\lambda,1,\omega)\). The mixed cell is \((H,0,K)\). After dualization the recorded data are

\[ \begin{array}{c|c} \begin{gathered}\text{left graph}\\ \text{datum}\end{gathered}& \begin{gathered}\text{right graph}\\ \text{datum}\end{gathered}\\ \hline \begin{gathered}a_i:W_i\\ \to M_\square\end{gathered}& \begin{gathered}Da_i:DM_\square\\ \to DW_i\end{gathered}\\ \begin{gathered}(\lambda_{ij},1,\\ \omega_{ij})\end{gathered}& \begin{gathered}(1,D\lambda_{ij},\\ -D\omega_{ij})\end{gathered}\\ \begin{gathered}(H,0,\\ K)\end{gathered}& \begin{gathered}(0,DH,\\ -DK).\end{gathered} \end{array}\tag{B.RD4} \]

The parameter category is \(\mathcal D^{\rm op}\); its mixed generator runs from \(0\) to \(3\). Both edge words reverse order. For the top word it is \(D\lambda_{23}D\lambda_{12}D\lambda_{01}\). The bottom word has the corresponding reversed order. Since the edges have degree zero, no extra sign occurs in these words. The full mixed differential is

\[ \begin{gathered} D_{\rm ar}(0,DH,-DK)\\ =(0,D(T-B),\\ -D\Omega_T+D\Omega_B). \end{gathered}\tag{B.RD5} \]

Indeed \(d(DK)=DH\,Da_0-D\Omega_T+D\Omega_B\). Its \(DH\,Da_0\) term cancels the target/source term in the graph differential. This retains both original mixed equations, not only the equation for \(H\).

The raw maps \(Da_i\) are not thereby quasi-isomorphisms, and \(DM_\square\) has not been proved whole h-projective. B.RD4 is an actual dg diagram; it is not an acyclic lifting category. In particular, do not try to fill B.IW1 by inverting \(Da_i\).

3. The safe dual roof and the inverse coherences

Let \(p=\epsilon\rho:R\to\mathcal W\) be the B.MP7 bar augmentation, and retain \(\beta:R\to Q\), \(\theta:Q\to R\) and its whole inverse package. The dual comparison span at every vertex is

\[ \begin{gathered} DW_i\xrightarrow{Dp_i}DR_i\\ \xleftarrow{D\beta_i}DQ_i. \end{gathered}\tag{B.RD6} \]

The first arrow is an objectwise homotopy equivalence: \(p_i\) is a quasi-isomorphism between h-projective endpoint modules. B.ND6 supplies h-projectivity of \(R_i\), and B.MX supplies it for \(W_i\). The Hom dual preserves this actual homotopy equivalence. The second arrow is a whole homotopy equivalence, since \(\beta\) has its inverse and both homotopies on the whole parameter diagram. Neither statement uses the unproved exactness of dualizing a quasi-isomorphism with an unresolved source.

Use the coherent alternative \(\ell^c,r,\tau,\sigma\) of B.IW2–5. For the dual map and inverse put

\[ \begin{gathered} \gamma=D\beta,\quad\eta=D\theta,\\ \ell^\vee=Dr,\quad r^\vee=D\ell^c,\\ \tau^\vee=-D\tau,\quad\sigma^\vee=-D\sigma. \end{gathered} \]

Their literal differentials are

\[ \begin{gathered} d\ell^\vee=\eta\gamma-1,\\ dr^\vee=\gamma\eta-1,\\ d\tau^\vee=\gamma\ell^\vee-r^\vee\gamma,\\ d\sigma^\vee=\eta r^\vee-\ell^\vee\eta. \end{gathered}\tag{B.RD7} \]

The two inverse homotopies are exchanged by duality. The degree-minus-two coherences also acquire a minus sign. The old \(\ell\), its dual, and the B.IW6 displacement remain separate retained data.

The B.MP6 comparison with the geometric target also has an exact dual:

\[ \begin{gathered} q\beta-\Psi\rho=db\\ \quad\Longrightarrow\quad\\ (D\beta)(Dq)-D(\Psi\rho)\\ =d(Db). \end{gathered}\tag{B.RD8} \]

This equation retains the actual signed bar component \(-K\) inside \(\Psi\), and its whole witness \(b\). It makes no equivalence claim about \(Dq:DM_\square\to DQ\).

Duality alone need not preserve whole h-projectivity on the new opposite index. Before a whole Hom lift, take the B.ND5 right-module replacements there. Treat B.RD6–8 as the supplied strict base diagram, including the free inverse/coherence generators and their displayed differentials, and apply B.CE10 to retain them on the selected receiving resolutions. The checked \(d^2=0\) identities make this a specified relative free boundary, not an unspecified lift of relations. After any subsequent restriction use B.CE11 again.

4. Connect to the existing right-kernel words without discarding data

At vertex \(i\), let \(E_i:K_i\to DW_i\) denote a collapsed representative of the recorded B.KC12–15 zigzag for that geometric word, with every original leg and inverse-cancellation witness kept. Its new receiving map is the actual composite

\[ \begin{gathered} \widetilde E_i=(Dp_i)E_i\\ :K_i\to DR_i. \end{gathered}\tag{B.RD9} \]

For the elementary factors these are exactly the original \(H_f,P_g\) roofs. For words use B.RK3's evaluation with \((-1)^{|u|(|v|+|x|)}\), and B.RK4's all-length associator compatibility. Do not replace a word evaluation by an unsigned identification.

There is a useful exact rule for an already supplied old right edge. Suppose \(B_e:K_i\to K_j\) is closed and its retained roof witness is

\[ E_j B_e-(D\mathcal W)(e)E_i=dA_e. \]

The strict naturality of \(p\), dualized by B.RD1, then gives

\[ \begin{gathered} \widetilde E_jB_e-(DR)(e)\widetilde E_i\\ =d\bigl((Dp_j)A_e\bigr). \end{gathered}\tag{B.RD10} \]

Thus no additional unspecified homotopy is needed merely for composing that given edge witness with the whole bar roof. The degree-zero \(Dp_j\) retains the order of its factors.

For a homogeneous higher graph arrow use B.RD2–3 on the full triple and the actual graph product, not B.RD10 stripped of its differential term. If only the lower right edges have already been supplied, B.CE10 may lift the actual strict \(DR(c)\) boundary to the selected whole right-kernel resolutions; its base is given by B.RD5, not guessed. A prescribed full higher cell can be compared through the zero-base difference only when its base and boundary agree with those of the displayed cell. This agreement is a separate hypothesis.

5. The remaining geometric identification

The dual MX graph, its signs, the whole inverse span and transfer of a prescribed edge witness do not by themselves identify the geometric comparison. That identification requires the actual \(E_i,A_e\) for the factorized \(L S,V L_0\) endpoint routes on the same opposite parameter index, with their endpoint-comparison displacements. B.RCmp1–11 require a primitive of B.IW1 evaluated on those choices.

Neither the span nor its acyclic resolution kernels imply exactness of the fixed closed endpoint displacement, as the IW counterexample shows. A coherent replacement route and an independently prescribed alternative route can be identified only through their full comparison.

The actual geometric \(J_H\), the degree-minus-five triangle comparison, all-array coherence, nearby-cycle descent and coefficient completion remain additional proof obligations.

Compare whole inverses on the dual mixed diagram

Proposition B.1bg (a homogeneous inverse comparison). On the actual dual mixed diagram of B.1bf, two whole-diagram resolution roofs admit a comparison of their inverse maps with a degree-minus-two component on the mixed generator. This component has the full endpoint boundary. The construction gives compatible endpoint choices; a comparison with independently prescribed endpoint homotopies retains the explicit obstruction described below.

The preceding constructions are whole natural resolutions, the mixed bar roof, its signed dual, and the full record comparison.

The coefficient and geometric hypotheses are those of B.1af. Let \(\mathcal I=\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}\) for the six-vertex free category of B.MP1, and let \[ N_i=DR_i,\qquad N(t^{\mathrm{op}})=D(R(t)). \tag{B.WI1} \] Here \(R\) is the actual whole bar resolution in B.MP6–7. The dg-opposite signs are B.RD1. Thus \(N\) is a strict diagram of right kernels, with the original endpoint variables retained. Its distinguished arrow \(c^\vee:0\to3\) has degree \(-1\) and differential \[ dc^\vee=T^\vee-B^\vee, \quad T^\vee=e_{23}^{\mathrm{op}}e_{12}^{\mathrm{op}}e_{01}^{\mathrm{op}}, \quad B^\vee=e_{53}^{\mathrm{op}}e_{45}^{\mathrm{op}}e_{04}^{\mathrm{op}}. \tag{B.WI2} \] The edges have degree zero, so reversing their words introduces no additional sign. This diagram retains its maps \(Dp\), \(D\beta\) and its comparison witness \(Db\) from B.RD6–8. In particular the length-one coefficient \(-K\) of B.MP5 remains in \(\Psi\) and in that comparison. No inverse of the raw map \(Dq\) is used.

1. Two roofs and a comparison in the full natural Hom complex

Apply B.ND5 over \(\mathcal I\) and both endpoint categories. For each \(\sigma=d,o\), choose whole h-projective resolutions \[ a_\sigma:A_\sigma\longrightarrow N, \qquad b_\sigma:B_\sigma\longrightarrow N. \tag{B.WI3} \] Both arrows are closed quasi-isomorphisms of the entire diagrams. The letters \(d,o\) distinguish these two resolution choices. Identifying them with specified factorized geometric routes requires the additional comparison stated in paragraph 4 below. Existence here needs no h-projectivity of the dual diagram \(N\): it is the target of the resolutions. The free opposite index has the path filtration used in B.ND2, and B.ND6 makes their values h-projective as well.

B.ND7 gives closed natural maps \(\beta_\sigma:A_\sigma\to B_\sigma\) and natural degree-minus-one maps \(t_\sigma:A_\sigma\to N\) such that \[ b_\sigma\beta_\sigma-a_\sigma=dt_\sigma. \tag{B.WI4} \] It also gives closed natural maps \(X:A_d\to A_o\), \(Y:B_d\to B_o\) with witnesses \[ a_oX-a_d=du, \qquad b_oY-b_d=dv. \tag{B.WI5} \] These choices take place before evaluation at a vertex. Their comparison square is \[ \begin{array}{ccc} A_d&\xrightarrow{\ X\ }&A_o\\ {\scriptstyle\beta_d}\downarrow&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle\beta_o}\\ B_d&\xrightarrow{\ Y\ }&B_o. \end{array} \qquad \Delta=\beta_oX-Y\beta_d. \tag{B.WI6} \] Set \[ K=u+t_oX-t_d-v\beta_d. \tag{B.WI7} \] All four terms map \(A_d\) to \(N\) in degree \(-1\). Substitution of B.WI4–5 gives \[ \begin{aligned} dK &=a_oX-a_d+(b_o\beta_o-a_o)X\\ &\quad-(b_d\beta_d-a_d)-(b_oY-b_d)\beta_d\\ &=b_o\Delta. \end{aligned} \tag{B.WI8} \] Since \(A_d\) is whole h-projective, postcomposition by \(b_o\) is a quasi-isomorphism on its natural Hom complex. In particular \(\Delta\) is a boundary. Choose \(H_0\) with \(dH_0=\Delta\). The closed map \(b_oH_0-K\) has a degree-minus-one cohomology class lifted by a closed map \(Z:A_d\to B_o[-1]\). Subtracting \(Z\) gives maps \(H,V\) satisfying \[ dH=\Delta, \qquad b_oH-K=dV, \qquad |H|=-1,\quad |V|=-2. \tag{B.WI9} \] Thus the comparison retains all four witnesses in B.WI7. The second equation is part of the construction, not a consequence of the first alone.

Each \(\beta_\sigma\) is a quasi-isomorphism between whole h-projectives. To obtain its inverse, lift \(1_{B_\sigma}\) through \(\operatorname{Hom}(B_\sigma,\beta_\sigma)\), giving a closed \(\vartheta_\sigma\) and a homotopy for \(\beta_\sigma\vartheta_\sigma-1\). Postcomposing \(\vartheta_\sigma\beta_\sigma-1\) by \(\beta_\sigma\) then gives a boundary. Injectivity on cohomology of \(\operatorname{Hom}(A_\sigma,\beta_\sigma)\) supplies the other homotopy. Retain both whole witnesses: \[ d\ell_\sigma=\vartheta_\sigma\beta_\sigma-1, \qquad dr_\sigma=\beta_\sigma\vartheta_\sigma-1. \tag{B.WI10} \] No compatibility is inferred from separately chosen vertex inverses.

2. The inverse homotopy and its value on a nonclosed record

Define a degree-minus-one natural map \(J:B_d\to A_o\) by \[ J=-\vartheta_oH\vartheta_d +\ell_oX\vartheta_d -\vartheta_oYr_d. \tag{B.WI11} \] The Leibniz rule gives \[ \begin{aligned} dJ &=-\vartheta_o(\beta_oX-Y\beta_d)\vartheta_d\\ &\quad+(\vartheta_o\beta_o-1)X\vartheta_d -\vartheta_oY(\beta_d\vartheta_d-1)\\ &=\vartheta_oY-X\vartheta_d. \end{aligned} \tag{B.WI12} \] Every term is a map of the whole diagrams of the indicated degree. In particular, B.ND4 applies to \(J\) on arrows of nonzero degree.

For a homogeneous arrow \(f:i\to j\) in \(\mathcal I\), of degree \(n\), set \[ \begin{aligned} \Theta_\sigma(f) &=\vartheta_{\sigma,j}B_\sigma(f) =A_\sigma(f)\vartheta_{\sigma,i},\\ \mathcal J(f)&=J_j B_d(f) =(-1)^n A_o(f)J_i. \end{aligned} \tag{B.WI13} \] The degrees are \(n\) and \(n-1\), respectively. The two equalities are the graded naturality identities, rather than choices of additional arrow homotopies. Differentiation, including the sign from \(|J|=-1\), yields \[ \begin{aligned} d\mathcal J(f)+\mathcal J(df) &= (dJ_j)B_d(f)\\ &=\Theta_o(f)Y_i-X_j\Theta_d(f). \end{aligned} \tag{B.WI14} \] For the last equality use the closed naturality of \(Y\), and then that of \(\vartheta_d\). This proves the identity on every homogeneous arrow and every finite linear combination of paths. The term \(\mathcal J(df)\) is essential when the record is not closed. Formula B.WI13 is a degree-minus-one map on the arrow complexes; no assertion that it is a derivation on path products is needed for B.WI14.

For the actual mixed generator in B.WI2, put \[ \mathcal J_H=J_3B_d(c^\vee),\qquad \mathcal J_T=J_3B_d(T^\vee),\qquad \mathcal J_B=J_3B_d(B^\vee). \tag{B.WI15} \] The first has degree \(-2\); the other two have degree \(-1\). The explicit higher boundary is \[ d\mathcal J_H =\Theta_o(c^\vee)Y_0-X_3\Theta_d(c^\vee) -\mathcal J_T+\mathcal J_B. \tag{B.WI16} \] Thus a higher comparison exists on these particular coherent whole roofs of the geometric mixed diagram. Its existence does not require vanishing of an arbitrary negative Hom group. It follows from the actual component B.WI15 of the whole map B.WI11.

3. Prescribed endpoint choices and their exact obstruction

Suppose \(\mathcal J'_T,\mathcal J'_B\) are other endpoint homotopies on these same objects, with the same endpoint differentials as B.WI15. Set \[ C_T=\mathcal J'_T-\mathcal J_T, \qquad C_B=\mathcal J'_B-\mathcal J_B. \tag{B.WI17} \] Both are closed. Keeping \(\Theta_o(c^\vee),\Theta_d(c^\vee),X,Y\) fixed, the obstruction with the primed endpoints is \[ \mathcal O' =d\mathcal J_H-C_T+C_B. \tag{B.WI18} \] Consequently it has a primitive if and only if \([C_T-C_B]=0\) in the degree-minus-one whole endpoint-bimodule Hom group from \(B_d(0)\) to \(A_o(3)\). If \(dZ=C_T-C_B\), the primitive is exactly \(\mathcal J_H-Z\). Conversely any primitive \(J'_H\) gives \(d(\mathcal J_H-J'_H)=C_T-C_B\). This proves both directions and retains the original endpoint homotopies as distinct data. The nonzero class in the B.IW counterexample therefore remains an obstruction for its prescribed endpoints.

4. Factorized geometric routes

The result supplies a homogeneous inverse comparison on the fixed dual mixed diagram, with explicit formulas for its endpoint displacements. It is the required form of input for B.RCmp1 when whole comparison maps identify \(Y_i\) with the appropriate \(L s\), \(X_j\) with \(vL_0\), and the two \(\Theta\)-families with the geometric cells on the same model. Those identifications must retain the KC signed evaluation roofs, the HN nested coefficient \(K_2\), and the original unit and triangle witnesses. B.WI3 alone does not establish them. In particular the letters \(d,o\) in B.WI3 are not an identification of the direct and ordered factorized functors.

After those maps and their full comparisons are supplied, B.RCmp2–11 transport B.WI14 through the resolved mate and target calculations, including its nonclosed-record differential. An independently prescribed endpoint route additionally requires the comparison of B.WI17–18 on those actual transported objects. Changes of parameter index require the re-resolution in B.CE11. The simultaneous factorized transport, degree-minus-five triangle comparison, changing-array coherence, geometric nearby-cycle descent and normalized coefficient completion remain separate obligations. \(\square\)

Transport the mixed diagram through its factorized right kernels

Proposition B.1bh (the factorized mixed-kernel diagram). The actual six-vertex diagram B.MX3 has right-kernel models given by the six ordered factorizations below. Its elementary edges can be taken factor by factor. They admit a comparison with the fixed dual mixed diagram, including the specified original edge homotopies and the higher mixed cell. The resulting higher right-kernel map compares the two actual factorized paths, and has a second witness in the dual mixed target.

Use the Noetherian separated finite-type geometry, ordinary unbounded torsion coefficients and locally semifree endpoint categories of B.1af. All resolutions in this proof concern both endpoint variables. The comparison uses the signed right-kernel evaluations, the KC roofs, and the whole mixed bar model and its dual. The arbitrary commutative coefficient ring in the module calculations does not enlarge the geometric proper-base-change hypothesis.

1. The six factorizations and their actual evaluation maps

Write \(a_T:T'\to T\), for \(T=U,Y,C,D\), for the vertical maps in the pullback of B.GC1. Let \(P_{a_T}\) denote its inverse-image right kernel. For an open or proper map \(t\), write \(H_t\) for the original compact-support right kernel, with its identity open or proper factor included. Thus \(H_h,H_p\) represent proper images and \(H_i,H_k\) represent extension by zero. This notation never identifies an unresolved proper image with its derived functor.

Choose whole h-projective factor models for these kernels, retaining their augmentation and comparison roofs to the original \(P\)'s and \(H\)'s. In the table the same symbols denote those chosen models; a repeated geometric factor uses the same model. Tensor order is right-module order, so the leftmost operation is applied first: \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c} v&F_v&K_v\\ \hline 0&A_D i_!h_*&H_h\otimes H_i\otimes P_{a_D}\\ 1&A_D p_*k_!&H_k\otimes H_p\otimes P_{a_D}\\ 2&p'_*A_C k_!&H_k\otimes P_{a_C}\otimes H_{p'}\\ 3&p'_*k'_!A_U&P_{a_U}\otimes H_{k'}\otimes H_{p'}\\ 4&i'_!A_Y h_*&H_h\otimes P_{a_Y}\otimes H_{i'}\\ 5&i'_!h'_*A_U&P_{a_U}\otimes H_{h'}\otimes H_{i'}. \end{array} \tag{B.FK1} \] All tensors are balanced over the displayed intermediate scheme's endpoint category. Canonical associators identify different parentheses; the factor order is fixed. These are whole h-projective kernels from \(\mathcal E_U\) to \(\mathcal E_{D'}\). Indeed the exterior-cell proof in B.KC2 applies to each factor and to each finite tensor. On an h-projective source module, the retained factor augmentations identify the corresponding tensor functors with the original sequence of geometric functors. This uses K-flatness of the resolved source at each step and the preservation of h-projectives by the kernels, as in B.RK10.

For an elementary left kernel \(L_F\), the factor comparison is a closed quasi-isomorphism from its chosen right model to \(DL_F\). For inverse image it is the right-model augmentation followed by \(DC_a\to DL_a\). The map \(L_a(-,I)\to C_a(-,I)\) is a homotopy equivalence of h-projective columns; its dual is therefore a homotopy equivalence. For open and proper maps use B.KC12–14 and double Yoneda, retaining the identity-factor evaluations. These are specified full Hom and bar maps connecting the original \(H_F\) to \(DL_F\).

To obtain a single receiving map from such a finite zigzag, resolve every intermediate whole bimodule. Lift each leg through its receiving quasi-isomorphism by B.ND7, keeping the lift homotopy. The lifted leg is a quasi-isomorphism between whole h-projectives, and hence has an inverse with both homotopies by the argument in B.WI10. Compose the oriented legs, retaining the unused reverse legs and their cancellation witnesses. Finally compose with the augmentation to \(DL_F\). This constructs a closed map rather than choosing a pointwise identification of represented objects. Dualization in this construction is applied only to the actual column homotopy equivalences or to the whole homotopy equivalences just described.

Compose these factor maps with B.RK3–4's ordered evaluation. For each row of B.FK1 this gives \[ E_v:K_v\longrightarrow DW_v, \tag{B.FK2} \] where \(W_v\) is exactly the left word of B.MX4. In particular a binary evaluation sends [ \nu(u\otimes v)(x\otimes y)

(-1)^{|u|(|v|+|x|)}v\bigl(xu(y)\bigr). \tag{B.FK3} ] For three factors the exponent and order are B.RK4. These formulas fix the maps and their naturality for homogeneous arguments.

Each \(E_v\) is a quasi-isomorphism. Fix the input endpoint. The first left column is homotopy corepresentable; substituting its actual homotopy equivalence to a corepresentable reduces evaluation to co-Yoneda. Continue with the next factor. Tensor and Hom preserve these homotopies, so the argument works through the three factors and proves the claim in every degree. The maps themselves are whole bimodule maps, hence the columnwise quasi-isomorphism is a quasi-isomorphism of whole bimodules. This proof does not tensor arbitrary unresolved quasi-isomorphisms or dualize a general quasi-isomorphism without its homotopy-equivalence justification.

2. Factorized edges, with the original left-edge choices retained

The six right edges follow the geometric orientation \(0\to1\to2\to3\) and \(0\to4\to5\to3\). Their affected blocks are \[ \begin{array}{c|c} \text{edge}&\text{block comparison, with other factors retained}\\ \hline 01&H_h\otimes H_i\longrightarrow H_k\otimes H_p\\ 12&H_p\otimes P_{a_D}\longrightarrow P_{a_C}\otimes H_{p'}\\ 23&H_k\otimes P_{a_C}\longrightarrow P_{a_U}\otimes H_{k'}\\ 04&H_i\otimes P_{a_D}\longrightarrow P_{a_Y}\otimes H_{i'}\\ 45&H_h\otimes P_{a_Y}\longrightarrow P_{a_U}\otimes H_{h'}\\ 53&H_{h'}\otimes H_{i'}\longrightarrow H_{k'}\otimes H_{p'}. \end{array} \tag{B.FK4} \] The first and last are the proper–open exchange, the second and fifth proper base change, and the third and fourth open base change. Use the actual left block maps and witnesses of B.MX2, B.KC5 and B.KC7. They have the sheaf-level identifications proved there. Lift their signed duals through the receiving right-block comparison by B.ND7. This gives a closed right-block map and its degree-minus-one evaluation witness. It is a quasi-isomorphism: the two receiving evaluations are quasi-isomorphisms and the dualized block map is a homotopy equivalence. If such a block map and its full witness have already been chosen with these comparison roofs, they are admissible inputs to this construction.

Whisker the block maps by the remaining factors in B.FK1. Denote the resulting map by \(B_e:K_i\to K_j\). On left kernels let \(\lambda_e^{\mathrm f}:W_j\to W_i\) be the corresponding factorized edge.
